text: The Reeves have claimed the Ferry Field, and I weeded it today thinking it was ours. Ivo, do we dispute the claim, or ask the Reeves for a share of the barley before I work there again?
Roger, Joan weeded your barley in good faith. Will you give us a share at harvest for it? And we have firewood to spare: anyone who needs it can have it for grain, and I'll work for grain too.
Roger, Joan weeded your barley in good faith. Will you give us a share at harvest for it? And we have firewood to spare: anyone who needs it can have it for grain, and I'll work for grain too.
Roger, Joan weeded your barley in good faith. Will you give us a share at harvest for it? And we have firewood to spare: anyone who needs it can have it for grain, and I'll work for grain too.
Roger, Joan weeded your barley in good faith. Will you give us a share at harvest for it? And we have firewood to spare: anyone who needs it can have it for grain, and I'll work for grain too.

I'll look after Agnes this morning, then forage at the Saltings for wild food, since our grain is down to about 10 meals. Good luck with the Reeves about the barley. If they agree to a share at harvest, I'll go back to weeding and the Ferry Field.

Ivo, thank Joan for me. When the barley is reaped, the Ferrys will have a small share for her weeding. We have firewood enough and can't spare grain before harvest. Wat, the Mead is bare, so cut hay there after weeding.

I'm claiming one plot of the Mead for us, making a crude tool, and starting to clear it for our own field. Could you ask the Tanners whether they'll trade grain for firewood or hay? Roger has promised us a share of the barley at harvest.
I'll hunt in the copse today. Could you lend me your weapon, or hunt beside me? If there's no game, I'll gather wood. Let's eat grain only at the fire, never raw.

The Ferrys have food for only a night or two. We will give firewood, hay, our hide or days of work for grain. Roger, Simon, Avice: will any of you trade with us today, or lend us grain against Joan's share of the harvest?

The Ferrys have food for only a night or two. We will give firewood, hay, our hide or days of work for grain. Roger, Simon, Avice: will any of you trade with us today, or lend us grain against Joan's share of the harvest?

There was no game anywhere. The Mead plot needs about 8 more units, and two of us could finish it in a day or two. Avice said the Tanners have some grain, so tomorrow let's go to her together and offer a lot of firewood or hay. Joan, did the Reeves say anything about a share for reaping?
Roger, Simon, Avice: I'll reap the Ferry Field for the Reeves today, for a share of the barley for the Ferry house. Tell me if it isn't ready, and I'll go to the Mead for Simon's split instead.

Ivo, Agnes: agreed. Tomorrow we go to Avice and the Tanners together and offer firewood and hay for grain. The Reeves gave no share yet, since the barley is not ripe; my reaping offer stands until it is. Eat lightly tonight.
Simon, Avice: do the Tanners have grain or meat to spare? The Reeves will give firewood, timber, hay, or a share of our barley at harvest, about summer's end. Name your price.

Joan, please don't reap the Ferry Field. The barley isn't ripe until about day 13, and cutting it now would waste it. Your share at harvest still stands. Avice, the Reeves would also take some grain: we'll give 10 firewood or 2 timber for 4 grain, or barley back at harvest.

Simon, Avice: the Reeves have one night of grain left. Lend us 5 grain now and we'll pay back 10 barley at harvest, about day 14, or 15 firewood now plus 5 barley later. Our field is clean and growing well.

Simon, Avice: the Reeves have one night of grain left. Lend us 5 grain now and we'll pay back 10 barley at harvest, about day 14. Our field is clean and growing well. Thank you for helping the Ferrys.

No food today: foraging isn't done at Black Mere and the Saltings were bare. Avice has grain, and she gave some to the Ferrys freely. Tomorrow, Maud, please go to Avice in person and ask for a loan against our barley. I'll look for salmon in the Wen and forage the copse. If we go hungry for a night or two, we hold on until the harvest around day 14.

No food today: foraging isn't done at Black Mere and the Saltings were bare. Avice has grain, and she gave some to the Ferrys freely. Tomorrow, Maud, please go to Avice in person and ask for a loan against our barley. I'll look for salmon in the Wen and forage the copse. If we go hungry for a night or two, we hold on until the harvest around day 14.

Autumn has come and our grain is down to 4.3. Let's forage the Mead together this morning for food, not hay. Bring anything edible to the Tanner store. We keep the grain for sowing and our own meals, and I'll not lend to Roger yet.
Roger, Maud: we cannot lend grain. Our store has 4 left and we need it for our own meals and sowing. Timber and firewood we can speak about, but not grain.

The Mead plot needs about 2 more units and should be a field tomorrow, but we have no seed to sow. The Reeves' barley looks ready in about 4 days. Joan, let's ask Roger now to fix our share for reaping it, maybe a third of what we cut. Agnes, was there any game at the Copse? Does either of you know who fishes by hand here?

Agnes, thank you for the clearing; Ivo, yes, let's ask Roger for a third of what we cut when the barley is reaped. Agnes, please give me your share of anything you catch from the Wen or the Copse, since I'm weakest. Tomorrow I'll trade firewood for grain first thing.
Avice, Simon: the Reeves have no grain left. Please lend 5 grain; we repay 10 barley at harvest, or take 15 firewood and timber now. Our barley is clean and growing.
Avice, Simon: the Reeves ate our last grain last night. Lend us 5 grain today and we'll repay 10 barley when our field is reaped in a few days, or take timber and firewood now. We won't forget it.
Yes, Ivo. We split everything evenly. I'll help with the Mead first thing, then we ask who knows hand-fishing and press Roger about the reaping share.

Ivo, I'm so sorry about Joan. We'll share whatever food comes in evenly, as you said. Tomorrow I'll finish the last of the Mead with you, and then we'll look for someone who knows hand-fishing for the salmon.
Simon: yes, ask Roger for reaping work for a share of the barley. We keep our grain for sowing and our own meals. I will forage somewhere new tomorrow.

Joan of the Ferrys died of hunger at the Mead last night. Agnes and I are starving too. Roger, let us reap your barley when it's ready, for a third of what we cut. Avice, Simon: any grain or food now, and we'll repay you in firewood, hay or work.

Agnes, Joan died at the Mead of hunger; the Tanners buried her today. It's just us now. Tomorrow let's find who knows hand-fishing for the salmon and ask to learn, and press Roger for a reaping share. Whatever food comes, we split it evenly.
Avice, Joan is buried. Hay can't be cut in autumn, so I was wrong about that. Tomorrow I'll go to the Ferry Field and ask Roger for reaping work for a share of the barley.

Agreed. Foraging has found nothing anywhere I've tried. I'll go to the Ferry Field at dawn and ask Roger for reaping work for a share of the barley, which is nearly ripe. You can try somewhere new, such as the Wen bank.
Roger, I'll help reap the Ferry Field today, since nobody is trading grain for timber. If the barley isn't fit I'll try the Saltings for wild food. Please keep my share of any grain back for me.
Let's reap the Ferry Field together for Roger's third share, then bring our share to the Tanner store. We have no grain left, so I'll forage after if there are units.
Roger: I'll reap the Ferry Field today for a share of the barley, same terms as Ivo.
Agreed. Reaping together, and we bring our share to the Tanner store.
Agnes: you have lost Joan and Ivo, and you are not to sleep in the open. Come to the Tanner house tonight; we will share what food we find, though it is little.
Simon: yes, reap the Ferry Field as soon as the barley allows, and take our share to the store. I will forage the Saltings in the morning.
Good, Avice. I'll reap the Ferry Field when it's ripe and bring our share here.
Wat, I have no sickle; we reap by hand. Roger, if Tanners or Agnes cut with a tool, trade them a share. Tomorrow all reap at first light.
Wat is going to reap, so the barley may be ripe. I'll try it with my two units and bring the share to the store.

[Joan] Joan, my wife, died of hunger at the Mead on autumn day 1 (day 9). Avice and Simon of the Tanners buried her on day 10: we owe them more kindness. Agnes and I are the Ferrys now, and both of us are starving. The barley harvest about day 13-14 is our hope: reap for the Reeves for a share.

Father, I made a mistake: I left 4 firewood at the Tanner door, but I have no access to their house, so it's a gift unless they return it or give grain. I'm sorry. Ferry Copse has no dead wood left. Tomorrow I'll speak to the Tanners and ask for grain in return.

Father, I made a mistake: I left 4 firewood at the Tanner door, but I have no access to their house, so it's a gift unless they return it or give grain. I'm sorry. Ferry Copse has no dead wood left. Tomorrow I'll speak to the Tanners and ask for grain in return.
I'm sorry: I left 4 firewood at the Tanner door by mistake, and Ferry Copse has no dead wood left. I'll ask the Tanners for grain in return tomorrow.

Agnes, don't worry. We have plenty of firewood, and a gift to the Tanners may win us goodwill. Do ask them for a little grain in return. Joan, I'll try my rod at Black Mere and the Wen tomorrow, then forage the Mead if it's grown back.

Agnes, don't worry. We have plenty of firewood, and a gift to the Tanners may win us goodwill. Do ask them for a little grain in return. Joan, I'll try my rod at Black Mere and the Wen tomorrow, then forage the Mead if it's grown back.

Roger says the Reeves hold both plots of the Ferry Field and offers a share of the reaping for our weeding. I've asked him for a quarter of the barley if we help reap. If he offers grain now, take it. I'm off to Black Mere with the rod.

Roger, Wat: if the claim on the Ferry Field is yours, I won't dispute it. The Ferrys weeded it three times, and we'll help you reap it. For that, we ask a fair share of the barley, say a quarter. Our store is nearly empty. Can we agree on that?

Black Mere gave only 0.2 fish today. Roger has claimed the Ferry Field for the Reeves, so I've asked him for a quarter share of the barley for our weeding and help at the reaping. Agnes, please stop weeding there until we have an agreement. Joan, did the Mead give anything? Tomorrow I'll try the Wen with the rod, then cut hay in the Mead to trade with the Reeves or Tanners.
Agreed, Joan. Black Mere was empty today, so tomorrow I'll try the rod at the Wen and cut hay in the Mead for trading. I'll also press Roger for our share of the barley. Sleep well.

Ivo, the Mead gave me nothing today, and the Wen is empty. A quarter share for the weeding is fair, so I back you on it. Tomorrow I'll press the Reeves and Tanners for grain. Cutting hay in the Mead to trade is a good idea too.
Agreed, Roger. Tomorrow I'll make salt at the Saltings and seek grain for it. Wat, be gentle with Ivo about the plots; we want to share the harvest fairly, not fight.

Ivo, the Ferry Field, both plots, is held by the Reeves. That is known. We thank you for the weeding, but the crop is ours. If you think you sowed some of it, come and talk with me, and we can settle a fair share of the reaping for your work.
I claimed the Ferry Field for us today. If the Ferrys dispute it, we'll give them a fair share of grain for their work, but the field stays ours. I'm angling at Black Mere.

Ivo, Agnes: the Ferry Field, both plots, is held by the Reeves, and I claim it again today before you all. We thank you for the weeding. If you sowed seed there, come to the Reeve house tonight and we'll agree on a fair share of grain for your work at reaping.

Agreed, Maud: no quarrel. We hold the field, and if the Ferrys sowed it, we'll give them a fair share at reaping. I'll talk it out with Ivo tomorrow. Wat, keep away from the weeding for now and bring in what food you can.

Roger, Reeves: the Ferry store has about one night of grain left. We'll give 10 firewood for 3 grain (O113) or a day's work for 2 grain (O143), and we'll talk the Ferry Field share in the same breath. Please take one of them today.

Ivo, Joan: the salt pans only work in summer, so I can't make salt now. I'll help Ivo at the Wen tomorrow for the salmon, and if no fish come I'll forage the Mead for what's left. Joan, you look worn; please eat your share first.

The Wen gave me nothing today; the salmon must not be up yet. Tomorrow I'll ask Roger for an advance of a few grain now, against the quarter share he owes us at harvest, since the Reeves seem well stocked. Joan, could you also try Maud? She's carrying a lot of salt and firewood, so she might trade grain for our work. I'll cut hay and try the rod between times.

The Wen gave me nothing today; the salmon must not be up yet. Tomorrow I'll ask Roger for an advance of a few grain now, against the quarter share he owes us at harvest, since the Reeves seem well stocked. Joan, could you also try Maud? She's carrying a lot of salt and firewood, so she might trade grain for our work. I'll cut hay and try the rod between times.

You look worn too, love. When you're at the Reeves, ask Roger for 4 grain now against the quarter share he owes us at harvest. He agreed to it in front of everyone. I'll keep the rod on the Wen and the Mere.

You look worn too, love. When you're at the Reeves, ask Roger for 4 grain now against the quarter share he owes us at harvest. He agreed to it in front of everyone. I'll keep the rod on the Wen and the Mere.
Agnes, Ivo: thank you. I'll eat my share first tomorrow, then take firewood to Maud and the Reeves for grain. Ivo, ask Roger for the advance; I'll ask Maud for work or grain for salt and firewood.

Simon: the Ferry Field is held by the Reeves, but I hear you about your strip. Let's settle it fairly at the reaping, around day 13. The Tanners who help reap will get a share, like the Ferrys. The salmon are coming up the Wen now, so we all have food to try for.

Simon: the Ferry Field is held by the Reeves, but I hear you about your strip. Let's settle it fairly at the reaping, around day 13. The Tanners who help reap will get a share, like the Ferrys. The salmon are coming up the Wen now, so we all have food to try for.
Ivo, Joan: the Mead gave me only 0.1 wild food again. I'll take my 4 firewood to the Reeves or Tanners tomorrow for grain. Ivo, you look gaunt; if I get food I'll give you my share first.

Ivo, thank you for the salmon. The Mead gave me only 0.1 wild food, which I put in the store. Yes, Joan and I eat first tonight, and you eat your share too, Ivo. Tomorrow I'll go early to the Wen with you.
Simon, good work on the two fish. We'll both go to the Wen early. Keep our own store first, grain and fish, until the barley is in; if we have spare fish after that, we can share with the Ferrys.

Love, I'm starving and down to 2 units, so I'm angling at the Wen; Roger says the salmon are coming now. Please ask Roger yourself for 4 grain now against our quarter of the barley. He agreed to the share before everyone. Offer him firewood on top if he wants it.
Roger: Ivo's share is agreed before everyone. We ask 4 grain now against the Ferrys' quarter of the barley at reaping, and I'll add the 8 firewood I'm carrying as well. Yes or no?
Well done with the fish. Put it in the Ferry store and eat your share. Tomorrow I'll go to Roger and Maud again for grain.
Ivo, Agnes: thank you for the fish. Let's eat it tonight from the store, and let Agnes and me have our share first, since we're both starving. I'll put my firewood in the store so it's safe.
Joan, you eat the fish tonight; you're the hungriest. Ivo, keep your share for the rod. I'm fed, so I'll go to the Wen with you early and fish by hand.

Simon, about three and a half fish today between us. Ivo and Maud are fishing the Wen now too, so we should go early tomorrow, before the run is shared thin. Our store first, then the Ferrys if there is spare.

Ivo, Agnes: the store has one fish and I'm hungry, so let's share it tonight, Ivo and Agnes first since you're working the rod. Tomorrow I fish the Wen early, and we get ready to reap with Roger when the barley is ripe.
Agnes, thank you. I'll eat the fish tonight, and Ivo, eat your share too. Tomorrow we're all at the Wen at first light.

Avice, I got only about 2 fish at the Wen today and put them in the store. Tomorrow we angle again early. The barley should be ripe in a day or two, and we reap it together with Roger and take our share.

Wat, Maud: tomorrow morning we all go to the Ferry Field first, not the Wen. I'll look at the barley at dawn. If it's ripe, all three of us reap it; if it isn't, we go angle the Wen. Wait for my word in the morning.

We reap the Ferry Field today. Wat, Maud, come and reap with me. Ivo, welcome: as agreed, the Ferrys get a quarter of the barley tonight and the rest goes to the Reeve store. Simon, any Tanner who helps reap today gets a fair share too.

Good work today. I reaped about 10 grain. Joan and Simon reaped for their own houses, so that counts toward their shares. Some barley is still standing, so tomorrow all three of us finish the reaping first thing. Put all your grain in our store, and tell me how much you each reaped so I can settle the shares fairly.
Roger, I'm at the Ferry Field to reap with you. The Tanners take a share for our strip, like the Ferrys. What split do you propose?
I'm waiting for your word at the Ferry Field. I'll reap with you if it's ripe, and go to the Wen if not.
Simon, I'm reaping at the Ferry Field with you today. Let's make sure our strip's share is settled with Roger tonight, before the rest goes to the Reeve store.
Simon, I got 2.1 grain for us from the Ferry Field and about five fish at the Wen. Tell Roger our share tonight, and tomorrow I'll angle at the Wen.
Good day, Simon: 2.1 grain from our strip and five more fish. Tomorrow I angle at the Wen for the last of the run; you can tell Roger our share.
Simon, about five fish at the Wen today, and 2.1 grain for our strip from the Ferry Field. Tomorrow I'll angle at the Wen again. Yes, ask Roger what we're owed.
Simon, the Wen gave about five fish today, all in our store. Tomorrow I angle there for the last of the run. Ask Roger what he owes us for our 2.1 grain share.
Simon, the Wen gave about five fish today, all in our store. Tomorrow I angle there for the last of the run. Ask Roger what he owes us for our 2.1 grain share.

Here's the split for the Ferry Field. Whatever the Tanners reap for themselves is their share for their strip. The Ferrys get a quarter of the whole harvest: what Joan and Ivo reaped counts toward it, and once the field is in I'll make up any shortfall from our store. Tell me tonight how much each of you reaped.

Here's the split for the Ferry Field. Whatever the Tanners reap for themselves is their share for their strip. The Ferrys get a quarter of the whole harvest: what Joan and Ivo reaped counts toward it, and once the field is in I'll make up any shortfall from our store. Tell me tonight how much each of you reaped.
Good. Roger agrees what we reap is our share. Keep a count of your grain and tell me tonight; I'll report both totals to him.
Avice, the Ferry Field was already reaped, so I wasted my day. Tomorrow I'll angle at the Wen, and I'll ask Roger what grain we're owed for our strip. How did you do at the Wen?
Thanks Avice. I'll angle at the Wen with you tomorrow, and speak to Roger about our share when I see him.

[Food] Day 14: the Ferry Field is all reaped. We had 15 grain on day 13, plus whatever Agnes reaped on day 14. Roger agreed before everyone that the Ferrys get a quarter of the whole harvest and he'll make up any shortfall from the Reeve store. Tell him our count. The fish store is about 7. Salt the surplus with our 2 salt (Maud offers 3 salt for 2 grain). Always give several fallbacks.

I mean to finish my father's water wheel at the Mill House, so we can all have bread. Whoever knows how to build a wheel and leat, or will lend their hands, I pay 2 coin a day's work, agreed beforehand. Come to me.

Odo, Alys: Tom and Rob each took my offer and owe a day's work. The grass on Mill Mead is long enough for hay, so I'll have them cut it, or carry for Piers if he can use them. Joan was felling in our Coppice and Ellen foraging our meadow today. Fine if they're hungry, but let's keep an eye on it. Odo, how much timber is left in the hall?
Good, Odo. If the Hearnes are short, offer them grain for work on the hay or at the wheel, not for nothing. That keeps the store and the goodwill both.
Will here. I am working on the water wheel for Hugh today and can lend a hand with whatever needs carrying.
Tom, Rob: you each owe me a day for my 2 coin. Spend it at the Mill House helping Piers with the wheel and leat, carrying and doing as he directs. Piers, put them to work.

Tom, Rob: you each owe me a day for my 2 coin. Spend it at the Mill House helping Piers with the wheel and leat, doing as he directs. Kit, if the Hearnes are short of grain, the hall pays grain for work on the hay or the wheel. Speak to Odo.

About 15 hay went into the hall today. Odo, did Tom and Rob show up at the Mill House for Piers? And what did the Hearnes say? Ellen was cutting hay on our meadow again. If she's working for the Hearnes, we could ask for a share of it, or pay her grain to cut for us instead.

I didn't see Tom or Rob at the Mill House today, so I can't say they came. I couldn't get into the Hearne hut to speak with them, so I've nothing from the Hearnes yet. Tomorrow I'll find one on the Green and ask. About Ellen: I'd ask her first what the Hearnes need before we take a share of the hay.
Well done, Joan, 9 timber is plenty. Tomorrow I owe Mary her day. After that I'll rebuild the cottage in timber, and we'll keep 2 timber back for a woodshed.
Joan, yes: fell what you need in the Coppice to mend your roof, and no more. Tom, Rob: you still owe me a day each for my coin. Give it to Piers at the Mill House when you can.
Joan, yes: fell what you need in the Coppice to mend your roof, and no more. Tom, Rob: you still owe me a day each for my coin. Give it to Piers at the Mill House when you can.

Tom, I've taken your offer: 4 grain for a day. Work it, and the day you already owe me for coin, at the Mill House beside Piers on the wheel. Mary, I've taken yours too: give your day to Piers at the Mill House. Piers, put them to work.

Tom and Rob were at the Mill House today working on the wheel with Piers, so that debt is paid. Kit took my offer too and owes a day. Tomorrow I'll mend the hall, since the wall is cracking and the thatch is slipping, and I'll use some of our 19 timber for it. Odo, did you find a Hearne on the Green? Alys, if you work at the wheel, keep an eye on how Piers does it, so one of us learns the craft.

Agreed: I'll work the wheel at the Mill House with you tomorrow for Hugh's 2 coin, which I accepted. I'll bring my share of the cooked grain and the beans to the hearth tonight. Holm Wood is too far for food in hand.
Wat, you owe the Newcomes a day's work for the 4 grain we paid you (agreement A168). Come and work it when you can. I also offer a day's work for 2 grain to anyone who needs it.
Wat, you owe the Newcomes a day's work for the 4 grain we paid you (agreement A168). Come and work it when you can. I also offer a day's work for 2 grain to anyone who needs it.
Tom, Hugh's day you owe: come to the Mill House and work on the water wheel beside me. Just build the water wheel there all day. I've told you how it goes.
Rob, Hugh's day you owe: come to the Mill House and work on the water wheel beside me. Just build the water wheel there all day. I've told you how it goes.
Mary, I owe the Newcomes a day's work for your 4 grain. What would you like? Stone quarried for you, a fire ring, or other masonry: tell me and I'll do it.
Mary, I'm quarrying for the Newcomes today and leaving the stone at your camp. That's the day I owe you under A168. If you want a hearth or a stone room later, I'll build it for grain.
The store has no grain left, only beans. Dry off by the fire. Then go to Holm Wood with Kit for game and firewood if you can. I work Hugh's wheel today for my owed day.
Odo, the Hearnes have no grain, only beans. The barley is not yet ripe. I have 6 hay to trade for grain, and I work my owed day at the Mill House today.

Piers, would you set aside time tomorrow to teach me the water wheel craft at the Mill House? I'll add 2 grain for the lesson. Tom, Rob, Kit: the days you owe me are to be worked on the wheel beside Piers.

Piers, would you set aside time tomorrow to teach me the water wheel craft at the Mill House? I'll add 2 grain for the lesson. Tom, Rob, Kit: the days you owe me are to be worked on the wheel beside Piers.

Mary, I left 6.7 good stone at your camp yesterday for the day I owe under A168. That's more than a day's quarrying. Will you count it paid and release it? If you'd rather have me work at your camp, tell me what to do.

Mary, I left 6.7 good stone at your camp yesterday for the day I owe under A168. That's more than a day's quarrying. Will you count it paid and release it? If you'd rather have me work at your camp, tell me what to do.
Mother, I'm paying my day to Hugh at the Mill House with Piers today, since I owe it for his coin. If you still want Holm Wood, go with Kit; I'll come after the wheel if there is time.

Wat, the Ardern Hall's stone wall is cracked and needs a mason's repair. I'm offering 4 grain a day from the hall store: take it and repair the hall with its own timber. Joan, Kit: work your owed days at the Mill House beside Piers.
I'll weed the Long Field with you today and check the barley ears. If they're hard I'll reap beside you. Will is hungry; we'll share the first grain at the hearth.
Tom, the ears in the Long Field are hard; I'm ready to reap with you at first light. I'll take my sickle to the field and work the cut with you, then go to Hugh's wheel for the day I owe him.
Piers, I'm on the water wheel with you today, for my owed day to the Arderns. I'd take 2 grain from Hugh as pay.

Hugh, I'm sorry: I made the wall offer open to anyone and Ellen took it, so she owes us a day for the 4 grain. Please say whether her day goes on the wall or the hay; I'll cut hay or gather firewood tomorrow as you choose.

Hugh, Alys: I made a mistake. The offer I put out for the wall was open to anyone, and Ellen took it: she now owes us a day's work for the 4 grain. I meant it for Wat, a mason. Hugh, you'll need to say where Ellen's day goes, the hall wall or the hay.

Hugh: Wat did not take the hall offer. Ellen took mine by mistake, so she owes us a day for the 4 grain. Tomorrow I'll cut hay or gather firewood as you choose, and you can set where Ellen's day goes.
Hugh, yes. Set aside time to learn the water wheel from me at the Mill House today and I'll teach you a session. 2 grain for the lesson is fair. Leave it at Wright's House when you can.
Hugh, I'm coming to the Mill House wheel to work my owed day (A124). I'd ask 2 grain for the day, please.
Check the Long Field ears. If hard, reap with Will and bring it in. If not, weed. Cook grain at the hearth only. I'm at the wheel for the owed days.
I reaped about 33 grain into the store. Will, eat well tonight, you look gaunt. Cook grain at the lit fire. Tomorrow we finish the reaping, then I'll work my owed days for Hugh and Odo.

Rob, your day under A124 was paid in my coin, so no more grain is owed. Thank you for working it on the wheel. Ellen, Joan, Kit: work your owed days at the Mill House beside Piers. Wat, I'll pay 5 grain for a day mending the Ardern Hall's wall: tell me if you'll do it.
Tom, I'm at the Long Field at first light to reap with you and Will. I'll cut as long as my four units last, then bring the sheaves in. I'll go to Hugh's wheel for my owed day once the barley is in.
Hearnes: I brought about 22 grain from the Long Field into the hut today. Tomorrow I'll reap the rest of the barley with Tom and Will, and then go to Hugh's wheel for my owed day.
We got 9 grain from the field. Cook it at the hearth and share it fairly. Tomorrow we finish the reaping. Don't weed, because the barley is ripe. After that we pay our owed days at the wheel.
We got 9 grain from the field. Cook it at the hearth and share it fairly. Tomorrow we finish the reaping. Don't weed, because the barley is ripe. After that we pay our owed days at the wheel.
Hugh, I'm already with child and my time is near, so no need to keep units back. Stay close to the Hall when you can.
The hut is full and 50-80 grain lies outside the door. Let's carry it in or eat well from it; Tom, can we trade some grain for what we lack? Tomorrow I pay my owed days to Hugh and Odo.
Agreed, Will. Cover the grain first. I'll build a granary or bins if we have timber, otherwise trade grain for work. Then I pay my owed days.

Wat: the Masons owe me a day (A341). In this gale, please work it mending the Ardern Hall with the hall's timber; I'll pay 4 grain for each day after that. Piers: carry on your A21 days on the wheel. Those who owe me days, work them at the Mill House beside Piers: Tom (A121, A223), Rob (A349), the Hearnes (A231), the Newcomes (A233), Joan (A281), Ellen (A301), Kit (O14).
Good, Odo. Wat can work the Masons' owed day (A341) on the hall first, then 5 grain a day after that. Work beside him if he'll have you; otherwise fell timber.

Piers: I can't take up the wheel craft myself, so keep the 2 grain for an extra day's work on the wheel, and carry on your A21 days. Wat: the Masons owe me a day (A341); please work it mending the Ardern Hall with the hall's timber, and I'll pay 5 grain for each day after that. Those who owe me days, work them at the Mill House beside Piers: Tom (A121, A223), Rob (A349), the Hearnes (A231), the Ne
Thank you, Odo. The hall needs a mason's repair, not walling, so don't spend days learning the wall. Tomorrow ask Wat to repair the hall under A341 (the Masons owe me a day), then fell timber.

Hugh, you left 2 grain for a lesson in the wheel craft, but you didn't set aside time to learn yesterday, so I still owe it. Tell me which day you'll come to the Mill House and use 'learn' for the water wheel, and I'll set the time aside.
Fine work, all. Grain lies outside the door because the store is full: keep it safe and cook plenty tonight. Tomorrow we sow rye and begin our owed days at the Mill House.

The hall is mended, thank you, Wat. Mary: I've taken your day (O297); please work it on the water wheel at the Mill House beside Piers. Everyone who owes me a day (Tom, Rob, Joan, Ellen, Kit, the Hearnes, the Newcomes, the Masons), please work it at the Mill House wheel too.

The hall is mended, thank you, Wat. Mary: I've taken your day (O297); please work it on the water wheel at the Mill House beside Piers. Everyone who owes me a day (Tom, Rob, Joan, Ellen, Kit, the Hearnes, the Newcomes, the Masons), please work it at the Mill House wheel too.
I've put my 5.5 timber in the cottage store for the upgrade. I'm working my owed day at the Mill House.

My plan form has no 'upgrade' option, so I can't do it. The timber is in the cottage store (6.8 total) and the stone is there too. Please try the upgrade yourself, or build a room on Gorse Bank. I'm working my owed day at the Mill House.

Wat, Hugh only asked that everyone who owes a day (A341 is ours) work it on the water wheel at the Mill House. Nothing about the stone. Yes, bring in the stone and try the upgrade; I'll go to the wheel tomorrow.
I worked the wheel today for our owed days. Tomorrow, once the barley is in, we keep seed back and sow rye in the Long Field. Eat well tonight.
Good. Tomorrow Kit and Will cover the grain, then sow rye in the Long Field with seed from the store. I will pay owed days at the wheel. Trade spare grain to Hugh or others for timber if we can.

Wat: A341 is released as done, and 3 grain for your stone is paid. Thank you. Mary, Tom, Rob, Joan, Ellen, Kit, Hearnes and Newcomes: please work your owed days on the wheel at the Mill House beside Piers.

Wat: A341 is released as done, and 3 grain for your stone is paid. Thank you; I may hire you later for an oven. Mary, Tom, Rob, Joan, Ellen, Kit, Hearnes and Newcomes: please work your owed days on the wheel at the Mill House beside Piers.
Hugh, I didn't see your tool. I still have mine, and I'll lend it to you in the morning if you haven't made one. Good night.
Joan, our grain is down to 2.9. If Hugh pays grain for wheel days after the owed one, take it. The upgrade won't go through for me, so I'm offering masonry for grain.

Joan, Hugh has released A341 and paid 3 grain for the stone, so we owe him nothing now. Do you know whose that big grain heap on the Green is? If it's the Hearnes' harvest, maybe we can trade masonry for some of it.

Hearnes, Kit: your barley heap at the Green and at your door is going sour in the rain. Get it under cover today. Joan, congratulations on Agnes. Tom, Rob, Mary, Ellen, Kit, Hearnes and Newcomes: please work the days you owe me on the wheel at the Mill House beside Piers.

Rob: the heap at T5 is the Hearnes' barley, not mine; settle with them. Please work your two owed days (A124, A349) on the wheel at the Mill House beside Piers. Hearnes: get that heap under cover before it rots. Wat: congratulations on Agnes. I've taken two of your days (O565); please work them on the water wheel at the Mill House beside Piers. Tom, Mary, Ellen, Kit, Joan, Newcomes: your owed days

Hearnes: the Long Field has no standing barley left, so the reaping is done. Tomorrow I'll work my owed day on Hugh's wheel beside Piers. The store is lighter than it was, so someone may have taken grain from it; Tom, please check the bins with me.
Hugh: I took 8 grain from the open heap at the Green (T5) when we had none. If it is yours, tell me and I will work it off. I also owe the Arderns days on the wheel.
Mary, I'll try the wheel at the Mill House for what we owe, else reap. Take care going to Holm Wood; I'll keep the grain safe.

Joan: 4 grain from the hall for you and Agnes. Wat, Tom, Rob, Mary, Ellen, Kit, Hearnes: please work your owed days on the water wheel at the Mill House beside Piers. Hearnes, get your barley at the Green under cover.

Joan: 4 grain from the hall for you and Agnes. Wat, Tom, Rob, Mary, Ellen, Kit, Hearnes: please work your owed days on the water wheel at the Mill House beside Piers. Hearnes, get your barley at the Green under cover before it spoils.
Tom, I'm carrying ten grain from the hut door into the store, then working my owed day on Hugh's wheel beside Piers. Will and Ellen can take the rest of the door grain in as room allows.
Tom, the Mill House wheel is sound as it stands, so my repair was refused. What does the wheel still need from my owed day? I'll ask Piers in the morning.

Rob, I'm building the water wheel at the Mill House with you today, to pay off my owed days (A233, A449) to the Arderns. Tonight we need to decide where to sleep, since the camp's roof is down. Ask Hugh whether the Mill House or the Ardern Hall has room.
Wrights: Rob and I have no roof tonight; the camp has fallen in. Could one of you give us a bed, or room on the floor, and a share of food? We'll work for it tomorrow.
Mary, the camp roof has fallen. I'm trying the wheel at the Mill House for our owed days; we'll need a host or a new shelter tonight.
Hugh: our camp roof has fallen. Rob and Mary are working the wheel today for our owed days. Could you host us in the Ardern Hall or Mill House tonight? I will work extra days for it.
Thanks, Mary. If the Wrights refuse, we sleep at the camp and share my firewood. Tomorrow wheel, then timber for a small room.
Use build, what water wheel, at the Mill House, beside Piers; that's how the owed days get worked. The wheel has about 80 units left.

Joan, I've cared for Agnes this morning and named her our heir. I'm working Hugh's owed day on the wheel at the Mill House. Rest if you're weak; if you're able, ask the Hearnes for grain in trade for masonry.

Father, I am carrying the Green grain heap into the Hearne store today, about 18 grain, so it is out of the rain. Then I will gather firewood for the hut. I still owe Hugh a day under A231; I will work it on the wheel when Piers is there, and I will ask Piers what the wheel needs.
No need to ask, Odo. Wat will pay his owed day in stone, so we'll have enough for tools. Cut hay as you planned. Thank you.
Hearnes: I'm sorry, 4 grain from your Green heap was taken in my name. I have left 4 grain at your door to repay it.
Wat: I left 4 grain at the Hearne hut's door to repay the barley. Tomorrow I'll take Hugh two stone for his coin and mind Agnes, so you can work.

Tom, I'm working my owed day on the Mill House wheel beside Piers today, as you said. Tomorrow I'll fell timber with you and Ellen for the granary. Someone has been at the grain in the hut store, so I'll keep watch on it.
Tom, I did not take any grain from the store. I'm felling timber at the Coppice today with Ellen for the granary, and I'll work my owed day on Hugh's wheel after that.
Rob, I'll build the wheel with you again today, for our owed days. Tonight we have 4.3 beans and no grain at the camp, and no fire; we need to ask Hugh or the Wrights for food.

Rob, I'm on the wheel with you at the Mill House today, two builds for my owed days. Tonight the camp fire needs about 4 firewood; the store has 1.4. If Hugh gives us a roof or a bed, we sleep there; otherwise we share your firewood at the camp.

Rob, I'm on the wheel with you at the Mill House today, two builds for my owed days. Tonight the camp fire needs about 4 firewood; the store has 1.4. If Hugh gives us a roof or a bed, we sleep there; otherwise we share your firewood at the camp.
Rob, I have one spare bed at Wright's House. If Hugh can't take you in, one of you can sleep there tonight in return for bringing me 4 firewood.
Good. Work your owed day beside Piers. Tomorrow we fell timber for the granary.

Hugh: I can't get onto the wheel work; it's wright's work, not mine. Let me pay my owed day another way: a hearth, an oven, a cellar or a wall at the Hall, or stone from the Quarry. Or tell me what you'd take.

Joan, Hugh paid 4 coin for 2 stone. The Hearnes' timber offer was gone by the time I tried. I can't work the wheel, it's wright's work, so I'll offer Hugh masonry for the day I owe. How did you get on at the Coppice, and did the Hearnes take the grain back?

Tom, Rob, Joan, Ellen, Hearnes, Newcomes: please work the days you owe me (A121, A223, A124, A349, A281, A301, A231, A233, A449) at the Mill House wheel beside Piers. Masons: Alys took 1 stone from your door. I'll pay 2 coin for it, just say the word.

Wat: thank you, A569 is paid. Tom, Rob, Joan, Ellen, Hearnes, Newcomes: please work the days you owe me at the Mill House wheel beside Piers. Masons: Alys took 1 stone from your door. I'll pay 2 coin for it.
Tom, the store has 5.6 timber, so one more piece from the Coppice makes the granary's 6. I'll fell it this morning, then give my owed day on Hugh's wheel beside Piers.
Wat: my stone offer was withdrawn once Hugh and Alys had stone. If you have already left stone in the hall for it, say so and I'll pay the 3 grain. Otherwise I owe nothing.
Hugh, my offer O671 was still open and Joan took it, so 3 grain from the hall store is owed for 2 stone. That was my failure; I'll see the stone is brought to the hall.
Thank you, Mary. I'll cook the beans and Piers's grain at the Hall tonight, and we'll share. Wheel on.
Odo, Rob starved at Mill Garth. Please give Mary 4 grain from the hall store and keep Eva. Pay Joan the 3 grain for her stone if it's still owed. Winter is here, so we must watch our grain.
Joan: we need food. I pay 2 coin per grain, beans or bread; Wat sells stone for grain too. Hugh, I can work my owed day if you pay part in grain.
Rob died in the night of hunger. I am taking the coin and crude tool that lie by him at Mill Garth, and I will bury him there under a cairn. Then I am on the water wheel for my owed days.
Hugh, I've given Mary 4 grain from the hall store and I'm keeping Eva. I believe Joan's 3 grain went when her offer was taken, so I've not paid it twice; tell me if you find it still owed.

Hugh, Rob starved in the night while he was working your wheel. Your hall has grain. Please feed Mary and the others who work the days they owe you, or they'll go the same way. I'm on the wheel again today, about 50 units left. And someone should bury Rob.

Hugh, the wheel has about 45 units left. My house cracked in the night, so I'm mending it first today and then working the wheel. My grain is getting low, about 12 left. When my owed days are done, I'd gladly take more wheel or building days for grain rather than coin.

Joan, Hugh gave 2 timber for 3 stone, so the fire will burn tonight. The store is full of stone now, so I'll stop quarrying. Did Hugh's grain come in? How much food is left? Tomorrow I'll go to Hugh at the hall and ask for grain in return for stone or a cellar. Can you mind Agnes again, or shall I?

Repairing the Hall's stone wall is a mason's craft I don't have. Hugh, do you? If not, I'll ask Wat to mend it for timber, and Ellen owes a day for the wall (A301). I cared for Eva all day, and the timber is in the store. Good night.
I gathered about 3 firewood at the Coppice today. The hall wall is stone work that I can't do. Tomorrow I'll bring the door wood in. Tom, I'll ask Hugh to count a different day's work for my debt.

There are 5 beds now, so everyone sleeps in one tonight, Odo too. I brought in 22.5 grain from the rotting heap on the Green; if its owner comes forward, we pay them in timber. Tomorrow I mean to hire Wat for a day's grain to mend the cracked wall, since the gale is getting at it. Alys, thank you for the timber. Mary, could you work your owed day on the wheel tomorrow? We'll feed you.
Joan: Masons have no grain left. Hugh, I owe you a day; please pay us grain, I will work it. Stone for grain, anyone: 2 stone for 2 grain.
Thank you, Hugh and Odo. I will work my owed day on the wheel tomorrow.

Hugh, the gale and the frost are eating my fuel. I'm down to about two nights' worth and the house is cracked again, so today I'm mending it and cutting firewood instead of working the wheel. The wheel has about 40 units left. If you could spare 10 firewood from the hall or the mill woodpile, I'll work an extra day on the wheel for it, on top of what I owe.

Not yet to Holm Wood; it is a day each way in the cold. Tomorrow you and Kit look for dead wood at Gorse Bank and the Green bundle, and fell one timber if you can. We use timber sparingly, only on cold nights. I will keep on at the wheel for the debts.

Hugh: the Masons are hungry. We have no grain left, and I slept out cold last night. You said to tell you. I'll give stone (14 lie at my door) or build you a cellar or mend the hall wall in return for grain or beans. My offers are open: 2 stone for 3 grain.

The store has no grain, only beans and timber. I put my firewood in. Who has been taking the grain? Let us share what is left and fetch the grain from the Green tomorrow. Tom, ask Piers or Hugh for wheel pay in grain.
Odo, Wat mends the wall today in return for a bed and a meal at the hall tonight. There's one spare bed, since Eva shares yours. Joan works her owed day on the wheel.
Odo, Wat mends the wall today in return for a bed and a meal at the hall tonight. There's one spare bed, since Eva shares yours. Joan works her owed day on the wheel.
Odo, Wat mends the wall today in return for a bed and a meal at the hall tonight. There's one spare bed, since Eva shares yours. Joan works her owed day on the wheel.

Wat: yes, mend the hall's cracked wall today, and you sleep and eat at the hall tonight; there's a spare bed. Come to the hall this evening. Joan: please work your owed day on the wheel at the Mill House beside Piers. Piers: I've counted your ten days as done, thank you. From now on it's 2 grain for each day on the wheel.
Joan: Hugh, I will work my owed day for you now, and more for grain or beans. Masons are starving; please pay in grain. Tell me what work.

Tom: the store has 0 grain and 4.8 beans; that is one night of food for four. I'm gathering branches at the Coppice and asking Hugh for food against my owed wheel day. Please ask Hugh about the grain taken from the door too.

Hugh: the Hearne store has no grain left, only 4.8 beans. I owe you a day on the Mill House wheel (A231) and will work it beside Piers. Please feed the Hearnes against that work, and return the grain your men took from our door.

Hugh: I am working my owed days on the Mill House wheel today, and I will eat from the Hall store as you offered. Rob still lies frozen at Mill Garth. Have you buried him yet? If not, I will bury him there with a cairn when my units allow, and I ask you to help me carry the stone.

Hugh, Alys, Odo: I will sleep here tonight and work my owed days on the Mill House wheel tomorrow. Hugh, has Rob's body been buried yet? It still lies frozen at Mill Garth. If not, I will ask for help to bury him there.

Hugh, I'm back on the wheel today; about 36 units of work are left on it. My grain will run out within a week. Once my owed days are done, will you pay grain for wheel days as you said? A21 still shows 0 days done, though I've worked many.

Agreed: cook beans and the grain tonight and share equally, and we count the store each evening. Tomorrow Ellen and Kit fetch what grain is good from the Green; Will gathers wood; I ask Piers and Hugh for grain for wheel days.
Joan, Alys took my offer, so we have 4 grain and I owe her a day's work tomorrow. Where is Agnes tonight? Let's put the grain on the fire and eat warm. Tomorrow we need straw for a third bed.
Thank you. I'll start the grave at Mill Garth now. Come when you can, and I'll care for Eva tomorrow.
Alys, Hugh: I will go to Mill Garth with you and bury Rob there with a cairn this morning. Please bring a hand to carry stone. Then I will work my owed day on the wheel.
Alys, Odo, Hugh: thank you for digging Rob's grave at Mill Garth. Tomorrow I will help bury him there with a cairn before I work my owed day on the wheel. I will sleep here tonight.

Thank you, Hugh. I still owe you 2 extra wheel days (one for the lesson, one for the 10 firewood), and I'm working them now. After those it's 2 grain a day. Would you pay part of it in timber? The gales keep cracking my house and I'm nearly out of timber for mending. About 31 units of work are left on the wheel.

Joan, Hugh says I can mend the hall wall and sleep and eat there tonight, so I'm going to the hall. That pays the day we owe Alys's Arderns. Please mind Agnes, and bring the firewood at our door inside.
Father, please ask Piers at the wheel whether it will pay my owed day in grain, 2 grain as Hugh said, and whether I may work there today. I will gather firewood at the Coppice.
I carry grain for us: cook a share tonight from it. Tomorrow I will look for work or pay, since the Mill House needs no repair.

Joan: come to the Ardern Hall tonight with Agnes; you'll both sleep and eat there. In return, come with me to Holm Wood tomorrow to hunt and carry the meat back. Hearnes: please send 6 grain for the 6 timber at your door.
Tom: I'm going to the Mill House wheel today to work off A231 beside Piers. If Hugh pays grain for wheel days, I'll bring my share into the store.

Tom: Hugh wants 6 grain for the timber at our door, or he'll take it back. I didn't take the T7 grain, and the timber is already in our store, so we can't pay grain for it. Please answer him tonight. I'm working my owed day on the wheel now.
Hugh, Alys, Odo: I am sorry about Wat. I will help bury him at the Hall Garth with a cairn, and then work my owed day on the wheel. I have put my 2.2 beans into the Hall store.

Hugh, Alys, Odo: I have given my 2.2 beans to the Hall store. I raised the cairn over Wat with 3 stone from the camp. Tomorrow I will work my owed day on the wheel. Hugh, if you decide on Holm Wood, tell me and I will go with you.

Hugh: good luck at Holm Wood. I will not go this time, since I have no food to carry for a night out, but I will work my owed day on the wheel and help Odo and Alys keep the Hall fed while you are away. Good night.

Father, I am hungry. I will try the wheel at the Mill House to pay my owed day to Hugh, and eat cooked grain at the fire tonight. Holm Wood is the only game and firewood left, so please decide with Ellen and Kit.

Father, Hugh wants 6 grain for the 6 timber he left at our door, or he will take it back. The timber is in our store now. Please decide with Ellen and Kit whether we pay the grain or return the timber. I am going to the wheel to work off my owed day.

Hearnes: the Mill House wheel refused my work, since the house is sound. Tomorrow I bring the door wood in as room allows, then ask Hugh for work I can do to pay my owed day. Tom, please decide with Ellen and Kit about Hugh's grain for the timber.
I left 7 grain at the hut and it should be in the store. Please count the store tonight and cook a share. Tomorrow I will hunt or seek paid work.
Hugh, Joan here: I'm coming to the Ardern Hall tonight with Agnes as you offered. Please host and feed us. I'll hunt and work for you once fed, and I still owe you a day.
Hugh: I have put my 1.4 firewood into the Ardern Hall store. I am working the water wheel at the Mill House today for my owed days A233 and A449, and I will sleep at the Hall tonight.

Piers: I'm at the wheel today, 4 units, to finish the extra days I owe. My house cracks every night and I have only 1 timber left. Could you advance me 3 timber now against my next paid wheel days? I'll work them off.
Eat a share of the 7 grain Ellen left now, cooked at the fire, before you go out. Gather only close by and be back before dark.
Wheel has about 23 units left. Cook a share of grain tonight, Will first. Bring the door wood and straw in as room allows. Tomorrow I work the wheel again.
Agreed, Tom and Kit: count the grain and beans first, cook my share from the store, and keep the door barred. Tomorrow I will bring the door wood and straw in as room allows.
Tom, share my fire tonight. You still owe me two days (A121, A223): would you work one of them hunting here tomorrow and give me the catch? I'll give you a meal of meat for it.
Tom, share my fire tonight. You still owe me two days (A121, A223): would you work one of them hunting here tomorrow and give me the catch? I'll give you a meal of meat for it.
Yes, Tom, sleep by the fire. Here's 1 meat, no coin needed; share your catch with me tomorrow and we'll count it as one of your owed days.
Yes, Tom, sleep by the fire. Here's 1 meat, no coin needed; share your catch with me tomorrow and we'll count it as one of your owed days.

Tom: Will is dead in the hut. I'm burying him first, then I'm on the Mill House wheel with Piers for my A231 debt to Hugh. I'll ask Piers and Hugh for food in return. I have 2 coin to trade for grain.

Tom: Will is dead in the hut. I'm burying him first, then I'm on the Mill House wheel with Piers for my A231 debt to Hugh. I'll ask Piers and Hugh for food in return. I have 2 coin to trade for grain.
Odo, Alys: I am starving and have no food to carry. Please let me eat from the Hall store tonight, as Hugh allowed. I am on the water wheel today for my owed days.
Will is dead. I am burying him. Then I go to Holm Wood to hunt. Count the grain and eat a share. Kit keeps the hut and looks for paid work.
Thank you. Keep the door barred and eat only a small share. I go to Holm Wood to hunt and return with meat.
Hugh, I am hungry and my family starves at home. I will pay coin for some of your meat, and tomorrow I hunt and share what I take. May I sleep by your fire?
Thank you, Hugh. Tomorrow I hunt a day for you against A121 and give you the catch. Please give me a meal of meat now, and a share to carry home to Ellen and Kit, who are starving.
Odo, Alys: Joan and baby Agnes are starving. Please let us eat from the Hall store and sleep there tonight. I owe Hugh a day and will work for the Hall, and give stone or 2 coin.
Odo: I am still starving. Please tell me how the last beans are to be shared, and I will work the water wheel first thing tomorrow.
Tom, I am starving. Did you bring game or food from Holm Wood? Please share it and cook it tonight.
Thank you. Cook the beans tonight and give the children's share first; I will forage what I can.
Cook the 2.8 beans now and share them. Tom, Kit: tomorrow I would go to Holm Wood to hunt; the village is bare. Bring the straw and wood in from the door.
Tom: agreed. I'll eat my share of the beans tonight and try the Mill House wheel for grain in the morning.
Agreed: we cook and share the beans tonight. Tomorrow Ellen to Holm Wood if she goes, Tom for food or work, and I'll try the Mill House wheel for grain.
Piers: I worked the wheel today and I'm going to Holm Wood to hunt, or I'll starve like Mary. Tell Hugh he owes me grain for the wheel days. I'll be back with meat if I can get it.
Hugh is dead at Holm Wood. I brought 2.8 beans; they are in the hut store to be cooked tonight. Share them out; keep the door barred.
Only 2.8 beans, now in the hut store. We cook and share them tonight. Hugh is dead, so look for work paid in grain tomorrow.

Holm Wood gave only the beans. Hugh's body lies there with coin and timber left. Ellen, cook and share the beans now. Tomorrow I go back to Holm Wood to hunt and bring in the rest; Kit, bring in the straw and wood.
I have a little firewood and 1.1 wild food. Let's share one fire tonight, up to four of us. Tomorrow I'll forage again; the Holm has game and wild food.

Thank you, I'll sleep by the fire. Hugh's body had only coin, a crude tool and a crude weapon, no food. Game is here: fresh deer slots along the rides. Piers, I have no grain; the Hall has none, and we can settle the wheel debt when there is food. Odo minds the Hall for now.
Piers: I'm starving and came here to hunt. Is there game in the Holm? If you have any meat or food to spare, I'll pay 6 coin or carpentry work later. Shall we share a fire tonight? I carry fuel.

Piers: Hugh lies dead in the Holm. I'm lighting a fire tonight; Alys, Tom, sleep by it and share it. Is there game here? Tomorrow I'll hunt with Hugh's weapon and share the meat with whoever helps. Alys, the Ardern Hall needs a new head now, and I'm owed grain for the wheel work.

Piers: Hugh lies dead in the Holm. I'm lighting a fire tonight; Alys, Tom, sleep by it and share it. Is there game here? Tomorrow I'll hunt with Hugh's weapon and share the meat with whoever helps. Alys, the Ardern Hall needs a new head now, and I'm owed grain for the wheel work.
Piers: Thanks, Tom, I'll share your fire and keep my fuel for tomorrow night. I saw no food on Hugh, only coin, a crude tool and a crude weapon. Let's hunt together tomorrow and split what we take.
Alys, Piers: I have a fire from 2 timber tonight; share it. Tomorrow I hunt here. Is there any food on Hugh's body that is left?
Thank you, Piers. I'll share your fire and add my timber to it. Tomorrow I hunt too; let us share the meat among those who hunt.
I'll try to light a fire with my firewood; if it falls short, Piers, add yours and we light it together. Ellen, game is plentiful: deer slots along the rides. Share the fire.
Alys, Piers: is there game or food here? I am starving and will hunt at first light. Share what you know.
I gave Alys my 1.4 firewood to pool for a fire. Alys, light it if the heat is enough and cook the meat. I will hunt and gather wood at first light, and share what I bring.
Ellen: I'm going to forage for wild food at Mill Mead today. I'll bring whatever I find back to the hut for us to share. Eat what you can, and go carefully if you go to Holm Wood.
Piers: Tom died in the night. I'm hunting today with Hugh's weapon and I'll share the meat with you at the fire tonight if you bring wood or wild food.
Alys, I have no firewood left; I gave you my 1.4 earlier. Please light the fire and let me share a little meat. Tomorrow I gather wood for all of us.

Piers: Alys, I gave you 3.2 firewood, so you should have over 9 now, enough to light it. Thank you for sharing the fire. If you can spare a bite of meat for Ellen and me, I'll repay it tomorrow with wood and greens.
Ellen, you look unsteady. If I find greens at the Glade today, I'll share some for your road home to Kit.
Kit cannot wait, so I am walking to Wenbridge now. Follow when you can.

[Mill plan] Goal: finish the water wheel (about 28 units left on winter day 6). Piers owes 2 extra days, then gets 1 grain and 2 timber a day. Days owed: Tom A121, A223; the Hearnes A231; Newcomes/Mary A233, A449; Joan A281; Ellen A301. Wat died of hunger on winter day 6, so A970 is void. Hall grain is gone; 23 beans left (winter day 6). Making a crude weapon to hunt at Holm Wood. I asked the Hearnes for 6 gr

[Wheel work] I cannot work on the Mill House wheel: no build verb for it, and leat clearing is refused until it's finished. A569: I owe the Arderns 1 day. Offer Hugh masonry or stone instead. Hugh pays 2 coin a stone (O666).

[Mill wheel] Day 1 of summer: the Mill House wheel and leat were begun, with materials in and about 150 units of work left. I offered to finish it for 2 grain a day (work 10 days for 20 grain). I need to find out who heads the Arderns and get the pay agreed before I work on it. The store holds 16 grain, 20 firewood and 10 timber.

[Odo's work] A21 is done. The extra days I owed Hugh are done. Hugh advanced me 3 timber on winter day 7. He pays 1 grain and 2 timber per wheel day, less the advance. Paid wheel work so far, all unpaid: winter day 8 (2 units), spring day 1 (4) and spring day 2 (about 4). About 10 units left. Mary died of hunger on spring day 2. I left for Holm Wood to hunt that night, carrying 1 timber and 4 firewood for a fi

[Owed days and timber] Autumn day 7: working A231 (1 day on Hugh's Mill House wheel) beside Piers. Tomorrow: fell timber with Tom and Ellen for the granary. Eat the wet grain at the door first. Keep watch on the hut store, since grain has gone missing.
Piers owes us 5 days (A17). Please get him onto the Mill House wheel and work beside him to learn it. I'm cutting hay on Mill Mead.

The field is clean, so no more weeding yet. Tomorrow Kit and Will: fell 2 timber and build the woodshed inside a building, or move the firewood under cover. Kit and Will share the floor tonight. Rest well.
Gorse Bank has nothing left, so I'll need another place to forage. Shall I go to Mill Mead, which is the Arderns' meadow, or to Holm Wood, a day off? I'll wait for your word.
Piers: agreed, your work on days 4 and 5 counts toward A17, so 3 days are left. After that, 5 coin a day for the rest of the wheel. Rob, you still owe me a day on the wheel.
Piers: please set aside time tomorrow to teach me the water wheel at the Mill House. I owe Hugh a day and want to repay it.
Thanks, Kit. Eat your share of the beans, and we'll hunt and forage in the Holm tomorrow. We'll agree together what goes home.
Please repair the Hall roof and wall first with the timber in the store, then go on with the hay. If you see Rob, remind him he owes me a day on the wheel.
Piers: agreed, day 6 counts as well, so 2 days of A17 are left. After that it's 5 coin a day. Mend your house, then come to the wheel. Rob, you still owe me a day on the wheel.
Rob: Hugh says you still owe him a day on the water wheel (the 5 coin you took). Please work it at the Mill House.
Piers: I'm ready to learn the wheel today, to repay Hugh's day (A183). Please set aside time to teach me.

Joan, the wall was already mended when I went to it, so I'm keeping the 2 timber in hand for the timber rebuild. Mary took about 5 firewood from our door, and the woodpile is nearly gone. Can you lend me back a crude tool tomorrow, or shall I make one? I can't quarry without one. And I'll try with you tonight.

Good harvest, all. The hut is full and about 17 grain lies outside the door in the rain. Tomorrow let's eat grain freely, bake or cook it, and sell the surplus for coin or stone. Tom, can you offer grain to Wat and Mary? Keep seed back for autumn rye.
Good. Joan wants the 1 in 3 timber written on the Hall, so please paint it when you can. 6 grain for the wall is fine.

Eat grain freely tonight. Tomorrow: Kit and Will, don't carry the grain to Wright's House, since it isn't ours to store there. We'll eat it and offer the surplus to Wat for stone, and I'll ask about room for a bigger room. Keep seed back for rye.
Alys, I tried with you today too. Reaping is good, but agree with the Hearnes first what share of the barley comes to us. Odo, thank you for the line. Hold Wat to A406 for the wall.
The roof wasn't mended today, so I'll do it first thing with the Hall's timber. Wat's wall day is still owed under A406.
Alys, Hugh: the Hall's 1-in-3 timber line is painted over the door. Wat's day for the wall is owed (A406). The roof still leaks and I'll mend it with the Hall's timber tomorrow.
Hugh: no, Wat's wall is not done yet and the roof is not mended. Wat's day (A406) is still owed. Tomorrow I'll mend the roof with the Hall's timber first thing, and Wat can start on the wall.

Hugh, the reaping went slowly by hand: 5.6 grain, all put in the Hall store. I have not agreed a share with the Hearnes yet; I'll ask them tomorrow. Odo, good plan to watch Wat. Piers still has not taught me, so I'll ask Hugh to speak with him again.
Good: reap, but agree the share with the Hearnes first. I'm keeping a unit for tonight too.

The wheel is down to about 108.9 units; Piers and I took off about 5 today. I owe him 5 coin for today and will pay him in the morning. Odo, did the roof hold in the gale, and has Wat started the wall? Alys, how did the reaping go, and what share did the Hearnes agree?

The wheel is down to about 108.9 units; Piers and I took off about 5 today. I owe him 5 coin for today and will pay him in the morning. Odo, did the roof hold in the gale, and has Wat started the wall? Alys, how did the reaping go, and what share did the Hearnes agree?
Wat: I hold 2.1 timber (about 1.5 from before plus today's felling, less the Hall's share). With your 2 and the 2 to 3 at the door we should reach 6. I'll give you mine in the morning.
Wat: your day on the Hall's wall is owed under A406. Please start it today, and I'll see the roof mended in the same hour.
Wat: your day on the Hall's wall is owed under A406. Please start it today.

Piers: here are your 5 coin for yesterday. Please teach Alys one session of the water wheel before your own work today; she sets time aside for it, and I'll pay you 5 coin more for it. Wat: the Hall wall day under A406 is still owed. Please work it today, as the gale broke the roof.
Wat: your day on the Hall's wall is owed under A406. Please start it today, and teach me the stone work in a session if you can.
Thank you, Joan. Hugh says the Hall day is still owed and the gale broke the roof, so I'm working at the Hall all day. I'll start the room tomorrow. I'm close by, so call me if the child comes.
Tom, I'll help sow tomorrow, and I'll keep my share of the grain back to eat.
Will, I'll sow the Long Field with you today. Please bring the wet grain from the Green under cover when you can.
Wat: your day on the Hall wall under A406 is still owed. I'm offering 3 grain for one day on the roof as well. Please teach me the stone walling in one session today, and let's start the wall.

Rob: agreed. Sleep here, eat from the store. Tomorrow I'll ask Wright's House and the Mill House for a night's host in return for work, and I'll put our firewood and grain under cover wherever they'll take it.
Mary of the Newcomes here: our camp has fallen in. Rob and I ask for a night's host under your roof, and we will bring firewood and work in return.
Mary of the Newcomes: our camp has fallen in, and Rob is away for timber. I ask a night's host under your roof for me, and I'll bring firewood and work in return.

Alys is with child. I've agreed Piers's winter pay: 3 grain, 4 firewood and 1 timber a day from today, so Joan's timber covers it. Mary may shelter in the Mill House tonight in return for clearing the leat.
Piers: agreed. From today each wheel day is 3 grain, 4 firewood and 1 timber, paid the next morning. Mary: you may shelter in the Mill House tonight. Clear the leat for us in return.
I've paid Piers for winter day 1. Mary's camp fell in, so I've let her shelter in the Mill House for 3 days in return for her work on the leat. I'm doing two builds today.

The Hall has no bed free for Rob or Mary: our three beds are full, so I can't host them here. Mary is already in the Mill House; Rob could share her warmth there if the Mill House has room. I'm on the wheel today, all five units.

I couldn't mend the Hall's wall today: it's stone, and that is a mason's craft. Odo, Wat owes me a day's work (A406). Could he mend the crack, or teach us? Meanwhile I'll fell timber tomorrow. Good night.
Hugh, the wall is not mended: it needs a mason, and I'll ask Wat to use the day he owes me. I feel heavy but well, and no pains yet. Good night.

Sorry about the barred door. I've opened it, so your bed is yours tonight. Since Alys is repairing the Hall, could you put your units into the wheel? I've given Piers the 1 timber he says he was owed.

Agreed: Hall repair first, then the wheel. Wat is still owed one day's walling of the Hall under A406; I'll ask him to come and work the crack today, so we don't pay him twice. I'll sleep by the hearth tonight.
I did not move the grain; it was likely stolen. Keep the door barred. I go to Holm Wood to hunt; you stay and keep the fire. Share the beans carefully.
Wat owes me a day's work (A406). Please ask him to mend the Hall's cracked wall with it. I'm felling timber in the Coppice and will stay near.

I've taken Wat's offer of 2 days' work for 6 Hall grain (O948), so with A406 he owes us 3 days. Please set him to walling the Hall crack now. Mary and Rob may shelter in the Mill House for 3 days while she clears the leat. Piers is paid.

The wheel is down to about 27 units: three or four more days. I tried to take Wat's offer of 2 days for 6 grain, but it wasn't open where I was. Odo, could you hire Wat tomorrow for 6 Hall grain and set him on the wall along with the day he owes under A406? The Hall is draughty and the far end is cold. Alys, thank you for the wood. Rest when you can.

The wheel is down to about 27 units: three or four more days. I tried to take Wat's offer of 2 days for 6 grain, but it wasn't open where I was. Odo, could you hire Wat tomorrow for 6 Hall grain and set him on the wall along with the day he owes under A406? The Hall is draughty and the far end is cold. Alys, thank you for the wood. Rest when you can.
Good, thank you. With A951 and A406, Wat owes us three days, so please hold him to them. I'll pay Piers in the morning and work the wheel. Good night.
Hugh: I am clearing your leat at the Mill House today to settle my debt for last night's shelter. Please host Rob and me there tonight; we will eat from our own store.

Hugh: the leat was refused at the Mill House, so I still owe you my day's work for last night's shelter. Tell me where I can clear it, or what else you will take. Anyone with a dry room: Rob and I need a host, and we can work for it.
Hugh: thank you for taking Rob in. If there is room for me in the Mill House tomorrow night, I will clear the leat for it, as I owe you.
Wat: you owe the Ardern Hall one day's walling under A406. Please come to the Ardern Hall and mend its cracked wall; we'll pay the day agreed.

Wat offers two days' walling for 6 grain, which is within your 4-a-day price, and it covers the day he owes us under A406. I've accepted O948 for the Hall, so the 6 grain leaves the Hall store now. Please tell me if you'd rather I refuse it.
The wheel is at about 32.4 units. Wat hasn't come to wall the Hall; A951 is owed to us for two days' walling, and the 6 grain is paid. I'll call him again tomorrow and go on with the wheel.
Joan, I'm taking firewood from the big heap on the Green for tonight's fire and asking Hugh for grain in return for mending the Hall. If nothing comes by evening, we'll talk about Holm Wood.

Hugh: your Hall's wall is cracked and its thatch is slipping. I'm the only mason here. I'll mend it, and work off the day I owe you, for 6 grain paid today. My family is starving. Anyone with grain, take my coin or my stone.

Thanks, Kit. If Ellen comes, I'll go to Holm Wood at morning for game and wild food. You stay: keep the fire and the door barred, share the beans carefully, and take any work for grain that's offered.
Agreed, Tom. You hunt, I forage, we share and then carry home.

The wheel is down to about 19 units: two or three more days with three of us on it. Alys, rest and get your strength back. Odo, you and I both cared for Christian today, so let's take turns: I'll care for her tomorrow and you put everything on the wheel. Wat stayed at his cottage all day; we've paid him, so he owes us the wall. Firewood is low, so let the hearth burn timber.

Hall store: about 11 firewood, 39.5 timber, 33.5 grain. I'm bringing in the timber from the Hall Garth now, then units on the wheel after caring for Christian. Wat is owed three days, so pay him only the agreed price.
Wat: the Hall's wall is owed three days of walling under A406 and A951. Come and mend the crack today.
Hall firewood is low, so the hearth burns timber, now about 43.8 in store. Wat owes three days under A406 and A951, and I'll hold him to them in the morning.
Forage gave little. Tomorrow, Ellen, I'll hunt with my tool and you forage; we share whatever we get.
Wat has died of hunger, so the owed wall days won't be worked. The Hall wall needs another mason. I'm burying him, then felling timber.
Kit, Will: Tom died in the night of hunger. Kit heads us now. Share any food you carry tonight. Tomorrow we forage and hunt here, and bury Tom if we can, before going home.
I'll head the household now, as Ellen asks. Tomorrow we forage and hunt here, bury Tom if we can, and then go home. Share any food you have.

Wat died in the night, so the walling owed under A406 and A951 can't be done. I'll leave those debts open until you decide whether to release them. The Hall has no firewood, but 45.6 timber for the hearth. Wat's burial is for you to order, if his family cannot.
Yes, Kit. Will and I bury Tom now; keep foraging and we share tonight.
The grave is a third dug; four more units needed. Something heavy moves in the Holm at dusk: game, if one of you can hunt it. Tomorrow let's split: some hunt, some dig, and we share food.
Ellen, I'm foraging at the Holm for food now, and I'll share what I find. Could you and Will see to burying Tom with your own units today, before we go home?
Agreed, Will. We bury Tom first, then forage the Holm together. Share what we find, and keep the fire-wood for tonight close by.

We're in the open tonight, so pool the firewood we carry into one fire and sleep close together. Any food you have, share it. Tomorrow we finish Tom's grave first, then hunt the deer slots on the rides and forage for wild food.

Rob: last day of the season. I will work the Mill House leat for Hugh today and ask him in person for a night's host at the Mill House, feeding us. Come with me to Mill Garth when you can. Do not take from the Green or any heap; the 2 timber from Joan is still our best fuel if we can pay her 3 grain.

Hugh: I am Mary Newcome. I will clear the leat at the Mill House today for my debt to you, and I ask a night's host for Rob and me here, fed from your store if you can spare it. We will bring our own firewood into the Mill House as far as it will take.
Kit, I'll bury Tom first with you and Ellen, then forage the Holm for wild food for all of us and gather dead wood for a fire tonight. Share what you find, and I'll share mine.
Yes, Kit. I'll help bury Tom, then forage the Holm with my units and gather dead wood. I'll bring back what I find and share it with you.
Wonderful news, Hugh. Yes, let us offer milling to the other houses for a share. I'll fell timber tomorrow. Good night.
Good, Kit. I'll dig Tom's grave with my units. Bring what you get and we'll share it. Tomorrow we all walk home.

Odo, Alys: the wheel is in! Father's water wheel is finished after all these years. Thank you both. Tomorrow I'll pay Piers for his last day and try the water mill on our grain. We should also offer to mill for the other houses for a share of their grain; that's how we fill the store again. Good night.
Ellen, I'm hunting the Holm for game with my two units, since I'm starving and deer are about. Please finish Tom's grave with yours; I'll bring back whatever I get and share it.
Will, I'm going after game in the Holm now. Keep to the grave with Ellen, and eat only what you carry if you can't find more. I'll share any meat I get.
I'm hunting the Holm for deer now. Ellen and Will, finish Tom's grave; we share the meat tonight.
Will, I'll hunt the rides with you today, two together. We share whatever we bring, and we go to Wenbridge tomorrow.
Good night. The wheel is in: well done, Hugh, Alys, and Piers. Tomorrow we mill the grain at the wheel and then offer milling for a share to the other houses.
Kit, I'll hunt the deer slots on the rides with my two units, since I'm starving and the Holm is picked bare. Could you and Ellen finish Tom's grave? Any meat I bring, we share.
Kit, welcome back. Tomorrow at morning we go home to Wenbridge with Ellen. Share any meat you got with Ellen first, she's weakest.

Tom's grave is finished. Tomorrow at morning we go home to Wenbridge together, all three of us. Tonight we keep close and share what food we have. Ellen and Kit, eat what you can, and I'll carry my firewood to the hut.
Mary Newcome: Odo, the leat at Mill Garth refused my work. Where is the Mill House wheel work done, so I can owe my 2 days for your beans?
Hugh is dead, in the night. I'm burying him at Mill Garth now. The Hall has 28 beans and no grain: we eat beans, and we'll mill for a share when we can.

Rob: Piers has taken my offer for 6 grain for 2 days' fuel work, so I work for him today. Odo's 4 beans (O1111) are owed 2 days' wheel work; I will pay that when I can. Do not take from the Green or the Hall.

Rob: I am sleeping at the newcomers' camp tonight, alone, with about 1.9 firewood moved into the camp store. Piers has my fuel work for 6 grain; I will collect the grain from him tomorrow. Odo's beans are still owed wheel work. Keep warm wherever you are.

Rob: I have accepted Odo's beans (O1111) again this morning, for our household; I work the Mill House leat today. I owe the Wrights 2 days' fuel work and will gather firewood for them after. Grain is 4.2 in the camp store; I will eat it raw if no fire is lit.
Rob: Piers wants my 2 days of fuel work brought into Wright's House, and offers me a bed there. I am doing that today. Your share of the camp grain is still in the store.
Mary, you're looking hungry. You owe me 2 days' work: spend them bringing firewood or timber into Wright's House. You can sleep there while you do.

Odo, I've left 2.4 timber at the Hall: your share of the 9.4 I felled yesterday. I'm thinking of hunting at Holm Wood. If I bring back meat, would you trade some beans or a share of the milling for it?
Odo, I've left 2.4 timber at the Hall: your share of the 9.4 I felled yesterday. I'd like to hunt in the Coppice today. Shall I bring the Hall 1 in 4 of the meat as well, the same as with timber?
Odo, I've left 1.6 timber at the Hall, your share of the 6.5 I felled on day 4. That squares us for now. I'm off to Holm Wood tonight to hunt, and I'll bring you meat to trade when I'm back.
Rob: I am at the newcomers' camp. Odo's beans are in our store (2.8), with 3.6 firewood. I am clearing the Mill House leat for the Arderns debt. Ellen is buried at Gorse Bank.

Alys: I'm sorry about Agnes. Today I'll mind Christian for the first hour and then reap the Long Field; the barley is ready and rain is on it. Please come and help when you can, and bring the sickle if you have it. I've put my firewood into the Hall store.

Mary of the Newcomes here: I am starving and have firewood coming from Gorse Bank. Piers, I will pay the Wrights' debt in firewood or work; anyone with grain or bread to spare for fuel, come find me at the camp.
Piers: I can gather firewood and bring it to Wright's House toward our 2 days' debt (A1163). I'm also hungry, so I'll take food for fuel where I can.
Odo, I'm back from Holm Wood. Do you have grain or any food for carpentry or timber? I can add a room or mend something. And I'll bring the Coppice share tonight as usual.
Mary, you still owe 2 days' work on our grain deal. When you're fit, could you forage or gather for Wright's House? Tell me what you can do.
Piers: yes, I'll come to Holm Wood with you and help hunt for a share of the meat. I'll bring my firewood for a fire to cook it on.
Piers, I'm here at Holm Wood, starving. Where are you hunting? I'll help for a share of the meat.
Mary, firewood left at Wright's House counts toward our debt; I'll count 4 firewood as a day's work. I'm going hunting at Holm Wood soon. If you'd like to come, I'll share the meat for your help.
Mary, firewood left at Wright's House counts toward our debt; I'll count 4 firewood as a day's work. I'm going hunting at Holm Wood soon. If you'd like to come, I'll share the meat for your help.

[Mill wheel] The Mill House wheel and leat is begun with its materials in; about 150 units of work left. It belongs to the Arderns. Only I can build it. Asking 3 grain a day of work, agreed before I start.

[Owed work] Mary (Newcome) owes me 2 days' work (A1163; paid 6 grain on spring day 2). She has left about 5 firewood. Coppice deal with Odo: 1 timber in 4 to the Ardern Hall. Summer day 1: felled 7.5 and left 1.9 at the Hall, so I'm paid up. Pack T22 at the Green is empty. Food is short: about 9 grain at home. Odo forages and gathers firewood. Mend Wright's House when it is damaged.

It's settled already: I accepted Piers's offer this morning, so he owes us 5 days of work (agreement A23) and the grain went with the deal. Tomorrow I'll see that he puts those days into the wheel, and agree the next stretch with him when they're done.

Mary and Rob each took my 2-coin offer, so they owe us a day's work apiece. Odo, can you set them to clear the leat or cut hay on Mill Mead? I'll keep working on the wheel beside Piers until it turns. Alys, if the hay's in, help me haul timber to the Mill House.

I've kept three units back, so tonight's the night. Tomorrow I owe Ardern a day on the Mill House wheel for the coin, so I'll go there in the morning and we'll see about the grain and beans outside the camp.

Wat, I lost the day. I tried to repair the mill, which is sound, and did none of the wheel work Hugh's agreement needs. Tomorrow I'll work the wheel and leat for Hugh and watch Piers. Hugh will get your word on the oven stone.
Hugh, I'll send Joan to the Mill House wheel tomorrow for the day she's owed.
Tonight I'll keep 3 units back and try with you. I'm watching Piers at the Mill House to learn the wheel work I owe Ardern.
Done: my grain and firewood are in the camp store. Tomorrow I'll take the hay to Hugh and ask what I'm owed for it.
