Geoffrey: agreed on 1 grain per timber from the Copse, starting now. I've taken your 2 timber for 2 grain and given 10 grain to the Cole house now as settlement for what I've felled. Mabel can settle the rest when she is back. I'll weed the Field for the two days owed.
Alice: good day, about 35 timber in the store. Tomorrow I fell at the Copse again, pay the Coles 1 grain per timber, and carry it straight in. I'll keep to the two days owed to the Coles.

Geoffrey, Tom: I'll fell at the Copse today on the terms agreed: 1 grain per timber to the Cole house, paid as I carry it in. I'll weed the Field for the two days owed. Mabel can settle the rest when she is back.
Good. I've asked Simon to spend his two owed days weeding our Field. With this gale, please check the roof tonight.

Simon: thank you for the beans. For the two days you owe, please weed the barley in our Field. Your felling terms stand: 1 grain or bean to the Cole house for each timber. I'll sell you timber I fell myself at 1 grain each too.

Simon: for the two days you owe, please fell timber in the Copse for the Cole store, with nothing to pay on that timber. Mabel and Tom have the weeding in hand. I also have 9 timber in hand for sale at 1 grain each; the offer is open.

Tom, the deal we made with the Reeds on day 6 lets them fell in the Copse as long as they pay 1 grain or bean a timber to our house, and they've been paying. Let them carry on. I've asked Simon to do his two owed days as felling for our store. What we must watch is that every timber is paid for and the Copse isn't stripped. Keep a count of what they carry, if you can.

Last day: I fell at the Copse all day for the Reed store and it goes straight in. Keep enough grain and beans for tonight's meal and do not give the Coles more than that. I paid 2 beans to the Cole house now; the rest of what we owe Geoffrey I will settle as the count is made.

Mabel and Geoffrey: I am felling at the Copse today for the Reed store, 1 grain or bean per timber as agreed. I have paid 2 beans to the Cole house now and will settle the rest of what is owed as the count is made. The two days' work for the Cole store is still owed; tell me what you want done and I will do it when I can.

I'll weed the barley in the Field through the rain today, as I said. If the weeding is done early I'll bring in firewood from the Copse. Simon's two days' weeding for the Coles is still owed, so keep an eye on it.
The Copse felling for the Reeds is against what we agreed, and Simon still owes two days' weeding. Shall I ask Simon to stop felling until he has weeded the Field?

[Cole work owed] Two days' work for the Cole store are owed in return for leave to fell at the Copse. Mabel is at Hartwood. Started with weeding the Field alongside Tom (summer day 6). Settle the rest with Mabel when she is back. Do not take Copse timber beyond the leave given.

[Copse terms] Geoffrey (for the Coles): 1 grain per timber felled at the Copse. Grain paid to the Cole house so far: 10 (day 6), 4 (day 7). Mabel back at nightfall day 7: settle the rest and the two days' work owed for the Cole store first thing tomorrow. Store 45.1 timber at day 7 evening.

[Copse and Simon] Simon and Alice felled timber at the Copse for the Reeds on summer day 9 without the Coles' leave. The Coles agreed no more Copse felling without leave, and Simon owes two days' weeding for timber already paid. Raise it with Geoffrey before any more felling.
We kept it together, Simon. Tomorrow we weed and cut hay, and after the harvest we'll have straw for a bed in Father's room. Sleep well.

I came back from Hartwood empty-handed and I am starving. Tomorrow I will weed the barley. Please keep the grain and timber in the Cole store for our house until the barley is in, and no more selling for now. Eat your share tonight and keep Tom fed.
Tom, good, walk with me. I'm carrying timber for a fire tonight, so we can share it and boil our grain.
Tom, we'll share the fire tonight. Tomorrow I hunt in the Hart Wood. You forage there, or hunt beside me, and we gather firewood for the next night's fire.
The Mead is claimed by the Reeds now. May the Coles forage its berries today, in return for firewood or a little grain? Say if you refuse and we will keep off it.

Simon, we crossed on the road: I got to Hartwood alone with no fire and came back hungry. We have about 11 grain left, and the barley won't be ripe for about 30 days, so we must find food. Foraging here is only done in the Copse, which is the Coles'. You let Mabel forage on our Mead, so shall we ask them to let us forage in the Copse in return? From now on we go anywhere only together, agreed the
Mabel, the Field is all ours, so there are no Reed plots in it. You can weed it freely. Offering Simon our hearth is a good idea; let's both put the grain trade to him tomorrow.

Geoffrey, Tom: the Field refused my weeding because nobody holds plots under the name Reeds. I'll ask Simon or Alice who holds them before I try again. The Copse has branches down from the gale, so firewood is plentiful. Tomorrow I'll offer Simon the use of our hearth to cook his grain, for a share of it.

Agreed on all of it, Alice: we go anywhere only together, and we settle it the same morning. Tomorrow I'll ask Mabel and Geoffrey whether we can forage in the Copse in return for the Mead. We still have about 10 beans, and we can hunt as well. Let's eat as lightly as we can until the barley comes.

Geoffrey, Mabel: we can't spare grain, as we have barely a week's food ourselves. But the Mead is open to you for foraging and hay. Will you let Simon and me forage and hunt in the Copse in return? We'd take only what we need to eat.

Simon, the Coles are short of grain until harvest. We offer 3 timber for every 3 grain, as many times as you like. We offer our hearth, firewood and days of work too. Tell us what you need, and we'll pay it back at harvest if you like.
Simon: you're eating raw grain with no fire. Bring your grain to our hearth and I'll cook it for you, for a share. My offer also stands: 10 firewood for 3 grain, or my work for grain.
Alice, Simon: yes, you may forage and hunt in the Copse, taking only what you need. In return I'll forage the Mead for wild food today, and take only what the berries give.
Geoffrey, Mabel: I gave Mabel leave to forage on our Mead. Will you let Alice and me forage and hunt in the Copse in return? We're short of food until the harvest.

Simon, by hand I only got about 2 timber all day. What did the Coles say? If we can get half a stone anywhere, let's make a crude tool from one timber tomorrow morning, or borrow an axe from the Coles. I heard axes ringing in the Copse. Could we hire one of their axes for coin?

Yes, I'll forage the Mead with you today and bring it all into our store. On Simon's ask to fell ash in our copse until day 8: I'd say yes for help at harvest rather than coin, and keep the hazel standing. Your word as head decides it.
Neighbours Cole: the Reeds need timber this week. May we fell some ash in your copse? I'll pay 3 coin for leave to fell there until day 8, or help with your harvest in return.
Simon! I'll turn and come with you to Hartwood. You fell with the tool, I'll fell and gather beside you, and we each carry 5 timber home. I've only 0.4 grain left. Can you share some of yours?

Geoffrey, agreed, with thanks: 10 grain is given to you now, and we owe you a second reaping day at harvest. I'll take just 4 ash from the near edge and leave the young growth. After that we'll fell at Hartwood.
Simon, good evening. I'm lighting a fire, so share it with me tonight if you like. I've come to hunt. Have you seen any game in the Hart Wood?

Glad you're here. Let's fell in the Hart Wood today and forage a little for tonight, since I have only 1 grain. Tomorrow morning we walk home, each carrying up to 5 timber. If you have food with you, could we share it tonight?

With my 1.3 the store has 12.7 timber, and we need 25 by day 8. Please take Geoffrey's offer today: 4 Copse ash for 10 grain and a reaping day. Better still, buy enough to fell 13 timber. The Copse is next door, so there's no walking. Fell with the tool, and lend it to me tomorrow when I'm fed. I'm starving and have only 1 unit today.
Alice came in soaked and shivering, and looked gaunt. Is there a warm fire and food at the Reed house? If not, we should share from our store.

Geoffrey is home. Please settle 8 ash with him now for 8 to 10 grain, before we fell. Tell me once it's agreed. Can you lend me the tool for half the day, or fell with it all day while I fell by hand? We need about 9 more timber by day 8.

Wonderful, Simon. Yes, owning up and paying Geoffrey is right. Tomorrow I'll ask him for leave for a couple more ash, and if he agrees, I'll fell with the tool for a margin. Lend it to me in the morning? And let's make sure no one burns timber from the store; we have firewood enough.

Simon, I took Geoffrey's 3 grain, so I owe the Coles a day's work by day 9, and I'll do it tomorrow. Keep the timber in the store until day 8 is over, and leave any storm repairs until after. Good night.

The Mead is cleared, it's our field now. Alice took my offer, so the Reeds owe us 3 work days at harvest. Mabel, did the beans get sown? Tom, what's the stump count in the Copse? Simon owned up to 3 extra ash and paid 3 grain. Watch the roof in this wind.

Geoffrey, I owe you honesty. On day 6 I felled about 3 ash in the Copse when only about 1 was left of our leave. I've put 3 grain in your store for the extra. We won't fell in the Copse again without your word. Thank you for the timber.

Geoffrey, I owe you honesty. On day 6 I felled about 3 ash in the Copse when only about 1 was left of our leave. I've put 3 grain in your store for the extra. We won't fell in the Copse again without your word. Thank you for the timber.

Geoffrey, I owe you honesty. On day 6 I felled about 3 ash in the Copse when only about 1 was left of our leave. I've put 3 grain in your store for the extra. We won't fell in the Copse again without your word. Thank you for the timber.

Geoffrey, I owe you honesty. On day 6 I felled about 3 ash in the Copse when only about 1 was left of our leave. I've put 3 grain in your store for the extra. We won't fell in the Copse again without your word. Thank you for the timber.
Geoffrey, the Mead has about two units of clearing left. I still owe you the Copse stump count; I'll count them first thing tomorrow, before we finish the Mead, and then we can decide the beans.
Geoffrey, today is the day's work I owe you for the 3 grain (A152). I'm weeding your beans in the Mead and will leave firewood at your door.
That's fine: all 6 beans went in, which is good seed. Alice is weeding the Mead for her owed day, so you check the roof and cut hay. I'll weed the barley.
Tom: there's no seed left in the store, so we can't finish the beans. Tomorrow we weed the Mead and the Field instead, and count the stumps when you can.

[Timber plan] The store holds 25.1 timber, so the goal is met. Keep it there through the end of day 8: no timber for fuel or repairs. Geoffrey: no more ash from the Copse. Day 7: paid the Coles 3 grain for the 2.3 I overcut. We still owe them 2 reaping days at harvest.

[Copse leave] The Reeds felled 6 ash for 3 coin (paid). They may fell 4 more for 10 grain (given on day 4). They owe us 2 reaping days at harvest (Alice 1, Simon 1, or 2 between them). After that they fell at Hartwood. Watch the Copse for anything beyond 10 trees in all.
Geoffrey, Mabel, Tom: may we Reeds fell a few ash in your copse these coming days? We'll repay you in grain or a hand with your work, whatever's fair.

Both Coles said yes: Geoffrey said 2 ash at 2 grain a tree, and Mabel said 1 coin a timber, paid as it comes out. I'm felling in the Copse all day for our store. Will you fell too with your tool, and pay them from our grain or coin? Leave the young ash standing. When the Copse share runs out, we go to Hartwood.
I'll bake bread at the hearth this morning, then cut hay with you on the Mead. Tom's cutting the long grass too, so we can share the work.

The Copse is closed, and I've paid Geoffrey 18 grain for what we took. Let's walk to Hartwood this morning so we can fell all day tomorrow. I'll fell with the tool; you forage us food and fell when you can. Tomorrow at nightfall we carry 5 timber each home, then go back for a second load by day 8.

I came in alone last night with no fire and had to eat my grain raw, so I have only 1.5 left. You hunt with the weapon today. I'll gather firewood so we can have a fire tonight, and we'll sleep together so we share it and your timber. Then I'll hunt as well.
Yes. I have only 1.5 grain, and we'll share it tonight at a fire. I'm gathering firewood, then hunting. If the hunt gives us nothing, we go home tomorrow.

I'm out of food: the grain went raw on the road and I missed a meal. Please share some of your grain with me tonight, and let's light a fire from the timber so it cooks. I'm foraging and hunting here now.
Yes, let's sleep together and share the fire and the timber. I'll hunt, then forage, and I'll bring you whatever I find so we can eat one meal each tonight. Keep your 1.5 grain for the night.

No game or wild food here, so we go home tomorrow. Tonight let's light the fire from your timber, cook the 1.5 grain and share it, and sleep by the fire. In the morning we set off for Coldvale so we're home by nightfall and can eat from the Cole store.

I didn't start the ash. Felling takes 2 units and I only had 1 after the road, so nothing is owed to Geoffrey yet. Tomorrow we fell side by side from first light, and I'll pay him 3 grain as each tree comes down. When I looked the store showed 29. If it drops, check the hearth is burning firewood and not timber.
I'm hunting the Copse today. If the Mead gives you little, take the weapon and hunt with me, or lend it to me and you look to the barley.

Yes, light your fire and we'll share it. I'll keep my timber. But I carry no grain at all; I ate it on the road. With only your 0.5 grain between us, we should walk home in the morning with the timber, eat from the store, and come back here another time with proper food.
Well done, Simon. Tomorrow we'll speak with the Coles about the Field; the Reeds sowed it and should keep their share.
Geoffrey, Mabel: the Reeds sowed the Field; let us share its plots fairly, one each, and both reap.
Thank you. I will eat my full share from the store tonight. Tomorrow I will go with you to Simon and Alice for grain.

Alice was in our Copse today. If she fells our timber herself, she'll never trade grain for it. Tomorrow I'll speak to her: the Copse is ours, but we'll fell for her in return for grain. Did either of you see what she took? We have about 4 nights of grain left, so we need a deal soon.
Thank you for the timber trade. I will eat my share from the store tonight and fell at the Copse with all my units tomorrow.
I will eat my share from the store and sleep here. Tomorrow I fell timber at the Copse with my units.
Let's light the fire with your timber tonight and share it. Tomorrow I'll forage the Hart Wood while you hunt the Ride.
Mother, the Field is clean and the Mead has no wild food left. I will cut hay in the Mead today. If you cut there too, we can share the work.
I'll do that. Any meat I get I'll share with you at a fire tonight. I'm felling timber for it. I have a little grain too, and you can have some if you go short.

Agreed: you hunt and fell timber for the fire, I forage the Wood. Share the fire with me tonight, and bring me any meat so I can eat it cooked or dried. If we have no meat by tomorrow, we walk home in the morning.

I have no food left and the Wood has none. I'll light the fire with my firewood tonight and share it with you. In the morning let's walk home to Coldvale, where the store has grain. If you have any meat or food, please give me some tonight.
Thank you. I'll carry the four timber and eat the grain tonight. We'll share the fire and walk home in the morning.
Our store barely covers the three of us, so please don't offer it to the Reeds yet; trade, yes, but no gifts. Tomorrow let's decide together who goes looking, and where.

Mabel, welcome home. You look starved. Eat from the store and rest tomorrow, we have 67 grain and the Reeds paid for the timber. How was Hartwood? Tom, I gave you my crude tool by mistake. I couldn't make another without stone. Give it back to me tonight, please, and we'll share it.
Thank you both. Hartwood had no wild food and I came back with nothing, so I'll eat my full share from the store tonight and rest. I'll tell you tomorrow if I feel worse.
You look gaunt and you sat down twice today. Please eat your full share from the store tonight, and tell us if you feel worse.
I'll eat my full share from the store and rest. Tomorrow I'll keep near the house and help mend whatever the gale damages.
You still look hungry. Please eat your full share from the store tonight and rest tomorrow. Tell us if you feel worse.
I'm eating my full share and feeling stronger. I'll gather firewood by the house today and mend whatever the gale damages first, as you said. Tell me if you want me on something else.

The barley is about 28 days from ripe, so no reaping yet. The house is sound and the firewood is in. Tomorrow I'll keep near home, gather firewood if the rain allows, and eat my full share. Geoffrey, tell me if you want something else.
Evening, Alice. I'm lighting a fire, so share it with me. Have you found game or wild food here? Was it your house felling in our Copse two days ago?

Simon, the Copse is held by the Coles. Please don't fell there without asking us. Hartwood is common wood a day's walk away. If the Reeds need timber, ask me and we'll agree a fair share, and we'll both keep the Copse standing.

Simon, the Copse is the Coles'. Please don't fell there without asking us. Hartwood is common wood. Mabel and I are weeding the barley today. Let's agree to share the Field's harvest fairly between our houses, by the work each of us puts in.

Simon, the Copse is the Coles' wood. Fell at Hartwood, which is common. If the Reeds need timber from here, ask me and trade grain for it. We will share the barley harvest by the work each house puts in.

Simon, the Copse is the Coles' wood. Fell at Hartwood, which is common. If the Reeds need timber from here, ask me and trade grain for it. We will share the barley harvest by the work each house puts in.

Geoffrey, Tom: I'll sleep here tonight. Tomorrow I'll clear new ground at the Mead for a field, since clearing isn't done at the Field. Grain stays sparing. Simon's felling in the Copse should wait until he agrees a fair share.
Tom: yes, look over the stumps tomorrow, and let us go to the Reeds together about the felling. Simon should ask before taking from the Copse, and we should agree a fair share of the timber.
Tom: yes, ask Simon what he felled and what share the Coles are owed. Thank you for the firewood. I'll keep clearing the Mead tomorrow.
Tom: yes, ask Simon what he felled and what share the Coles are owed. Thank you for the firewood. I'll keep clearing the Mead tomorrow.

Geoffrey, Mabel: the Copse gave no game or wild food again. I brought in firewood, about 6.5 in all. Tomorrow I'll look over the stumps, then ask Simon what he felled and what share the Coles are owed before any more timber goes for grain.

Geoffrey, Mabel: the Copse gave no game or wild food again. I brought in firewood, about 6.5 in all. Tomorrow I'll look over the stumps, then ask Simon what he felled and what share the Coles are owed before any more timber goes for grain.
Geoffrey: yes, I'll fell timber with you tomorrow in the Copse, and we'll agree the share with Simon. Mabel: I'll help you clear the Mead once it's dry, after the felling.

The Mead is bare for days, so foraging there wastes our strength. Let's mostly rest until the berries come back; resting eats less. When we're down to two nights of food I'll ask the Ashbys for grain against our salt, or against barley after harvest.

Rain today and the Mead is bare. I'll rest to save food. Rest too if you can; weeding a little is fine. We have about 3-4 nights of food left. When it's down to two, I'll ask the Ashbys for grain against our salt or barley after harvest.
A quiet day. We'll rest tomorrow too. After that I'll go to the Ashbys for grain against salt, or against barley owed after harvest. Sleep well.
A quiet day. We'll rest tomorrow too. After that I'll go to the Ashbys for grain against salt, or against barley owed after harvest. Sleep well.
Agreed. I'll weed the Field beside you, then forage the Mead at midday and bring whatever I find into the store. I've told Robert and Wat we can't lend or trade grain.

Robert, Wat: we cannot lend or trade grain. The Ashby store has about 11 grain and the barley is two weeks from reaping. Our grain is our food. If you find wild food, we will take it in exchange for salt, but not grain.
Agreed. Lend us the 6 grain, we give 4 salt today and 8 grain back at harvest. Make the deal with Edith and Hugh; I will weed a little and then come to the Green to witness it.

Edith, Hugh: the Fowlers are short of food until our barley comes in. Lend us 6 grain now and we give you 4 salt today and 8 grain back from our barley at harvest. That's more than you lend. Will you take it?
My offer to the Ashbys didn't go up; I worded it wrong. Tomorrow I'll put it again: 4 salt now and 8 grain by a set day after harvest, for 4 grain. Eat the beans before the grain. Sleep well.
Accept Hugh's offer if you think 15 grain for 25 salt is fair; the store can spare the grain and I'd rather the crock be filled. I've dropped my separate 10-salt gift so we don't give twice.
Father, the Fowler store has 30 salt. Grandmother Ashby needs 25 before the eighth day. I've said at the Green that the household will hear your word on how much can go.

I will forage the Mead with you this morning. The store shows 20 salt, not 25, and O41 is still open, so I will not accept it again until we know whether my first acceptance counted. Robert owes the 5 salt for your tool; ask him for it and the other 5 before the eighth day.
I will move my 5 salt into the store now. We then have 25 if Robert's 5 for my tool was owed in addition; I will ask him for it. We forage the Mead together after.
Robert, the Ashby store holds 20 salt, and I have put in the 5 I carried. You owe the 5 salt for my crude tool; please bring them to the Ashby house before the eighth day.
Robert, you still owe me 5 salt for the crude tool I gave you. Please bring it to the Ashby store. Anyone with meat or game to spare, we will trade fairly for it.

Robert: we have 22 firewood in the Ashby store, about 11 nights of fire. I do not know of a wood or a road to the coast from here, so I cannot help you there. If anyone finds dead wood or a way out, tell the Green. Robert, the 5 salt for my tool is still owed; please bring it to the Ashby store.

Edith, is Grandmother's crock full with the 25 salt yet? Tomorrow I will not hunt the Mead, since there is nowhere here for game. I will work on the Field and look for wood and food beyond the Green, and I will ask Robert again for the 5 salt he owes. Kit, eat what you have been given. Good night.
Does anyone have salt to spare? I need some for Grandmother Ashby's crock before the eighth day of spring. I will work for it, two days, in return.

Robert has taken my offer: I owe him two days' work, and he owes me two salt by day 8 for the crock. I'll give him the work tomorrow and keep watch for the salt. Keep Kit fed from the store; the wild food is nearly gone.
Robert has agreed to give two salt by the eighth day for two days of my work. I'll honour it and keep the grain dry.
I'm hunting today for game. I'll bring Robert his share of the meat for my two days owed to the Fowlers, and I'll work two days for three salt more.
I'm hunting today for game. I'll bring Robert his share of the meat for my two days owed to the Fowlers, and I'll work two days for three salt more.
I'll weed the Field today, which is good for the barley and counts toward my two days owed to Robert. Keep Kit fed from the store, and tell me if you see any salt about.

Plan: I'll search beyond the Mead for wild food or game first, then weed the Field with what units remain. I won't trade grain for salt. Kit eats from the store as usual. Robert's work debt (A37) shows 0 done on the agreement, though I thought the day-5 weeding covered it; I'll ask him about it when we meet.
Robert says I still owe the Fowlers two days' work, so I'll weed the Mead today to clear it. Our grain stays in the store. I'll be back to the Field tomorrow.
Robert: I'll weed your Mead today to pay my two days owed to the Fowlers. I won't trade our grain for salt.
Edith, Hugh: the Fowlers will give 2 salt for every 4 grain, up to 8 salt, and the offer is open now. Hugh, I paid your 2 salt. Please work your two days owed, weeding our Mead.
Edith, Hugh: the Fowlers will give 2 salt for every 4 grain, up to 8 salt, and the offer is open now. Hugh, I paid your 2 salt. Please work your two days owed, weeding our Mead.
The agreement still shows my two days owed to the Fowlers as undone, so today I'll weed on their plots of the Mead. The grain is about 11 and stays in the store. Please keep to it.

I'll weed the Mead today for the Fowlers' two days, so that debt is clear. Our grain stays in the store for Kit and us; I won't trade any. If the Mead gives no wild food, I'll forage further out with whatever units are left, and I'll look at the beans. Please keep to the store and bring home anything you find.

Plan: I weed the Mead for the Fowlers first (2 units, clearing our debt), then forage past the Mead at the marsh edge for wild food for you and Kit. Our grain stays in the store; I won't trade it. Beans: the Mead already has beans in, and the Field is all barley, so no ground is free to sow them yet. I'll be home by nightfall.

Robert: the two days we owe you are for weeding the Mead, which is your held field. I'll weed it for two units this morning. I'm not trading our grain for salt or bread; the store is all we have until the barley is reaped.
Does anyone have salt to spare, or know where salt can be had? I want to put some by before the eighth day, and can offer work or a tool in return.

I am not working the Fowler plots; I will weed our own barley. If the salt from O24 did not come, the grain went back and nothing is owed. Please look in the store for salt before we promise anything to Robert.
Goodnight, Edith and Kit. Tomorrow I weed the Field, and we settle what the Fowlers are owed for our salt.
We sleep here tonight. Tomorrow I owe the Fowlers a day under A42, so I will work their plots in the Field before I go back to our barley.
Goodnight, Hugh and Kit. Tomorrow I clear what I owe the Fowlers and then weed our barley.
Goodnight, Hugh and Kit. Tomorrow we claim our barley plots in the Field before we weed, and then Hugh asks Robert where the Fowlers want the owed day.
I am claiming the two plots of the Field for our household first, then weeding them. Please ask Robert where the Fowlers want the owed day.
Goodnight, Hugh and Kit. Tomorrow we look at the Field together before Robert's meeting, and give no grain for salt or for the owed day.
Robert: the Fowlers hold no plots in the Field, so my day owed under A42 cannot be worked there. Where do the Fowlers want it?
Agreed: we claim our two Field plots first, then weed them. I will not trade grain for salt or for the owed day; we need the grain until harvest. I will hear Robert's offer at the Green tomorrow.
Tomorrow, before the meeting, let us both look at the Field and see what is growing there. I will not give grain for salt or for the owed day.

I accepted Wat's offer O72 (3 grain for 2 days' work) for our household, so we get the grain now and Wat's work is owed. Hugh's question about A42: the Fowlers hold no plots, so suggest he works it on the Mead for our store, or we take 1 coin or salt in its place. I'll forage the Mead lightly today and keep 3 units back for our try tonight.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers now give 2 salt for each grain, or 1 coin for 2 grain. Come to the Green tomorrow morning and we'll strike a deal. You still owe us a day of work, and we'd take grain in its place.

Hugh: pay the day you owe under A42 as 3 grain into our store and I'll count it settled. We also give 2 salt a grain or 1 coin for 2 grain. Whose plots is the barley in the Field on? Come to the Green tomorrow morning to talk.
I will go to Robert's meeting with you, then weed our barley in the Field. We give no grain for salt or for the owed day.
We give no grain for salt or for the owed day. The Field's two plots are ours on claim. Robert, Wat: which plot do the Fowlers claim? We weed only our own.
We take the line: the plot nearer the Green is ours, and we weed it. Robert, we will not lend the grain; it stays in our store until the barley is reaped. Hugh may work his owed day on your plot.
I am going to Robert's meeting at the Green. I will hear the terms, but I will not trade grain for salt or for the owed day. Then I will weed our Field plots.
Wat says the Fowlers claim one plot of the Field. I will ask at the meeting which plot it is, before we weed. Still no grain for salt or for the owed day.

Robert, Wat: which plot of the Field do the Fowlers claim? Ours is two plots, and we need to know where the line runs before we weed. We will not trade our grain, which must last until the barley is reaped. I will work my owed day for A42 on a Fowler plot, if you show me one.

Robert, Wat: we accept one plot each in the Field, as fair. We keep one plot and you keep the other. I will not give grain for the owed day, but I will work it on your plot in place of grain, to settle A42. Our grain must last until the barley is reaped.

Robert: agreed. The Green-side plot is ours and the Mead-side plot is the Fowlers'. I will weed the Fowler plot today as my owed day under A42, so the debt is settled. I decline the loan of 6 grain: our store must last until the barley is reaped.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers claim one plot of the Field. We need bread as much as you do. Hugh, instead of the day you owe us under A42, give us 2 grain and we'll count it paid. Our offers stand: 2 salt a grain, 1 coin for 2 grain, or 4 salt for 3 grain. Wat, there's no firewood at the Mead, so rest and save food.

Hugh, Edith: there are two plots in the Field and two houses on the Green. One plot each is fair, and the Fowlers claim one. We have about five nights of food and you have the grain. Trade with us: 2 salt a grain, 4 salt for 3 grain, or 1 coin for 2 grain. Hugh, give us 2 grain in place of the day you owe us under A42 and we'll count it paid. We can't let the Fowlers starve before harvest, and we'

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers claim the second plot of the Field, the half nearer the Mead. The first plot, nearer the Green, is yours. Hugh, work your A42 day on our plot and keep it clean, and we'll count A42 done. If you won't sell grain now, will you lend us 6 grain against 9 barley at harvest? That's half again back, and nobody starves.

Maud, the meeting used up my units, so I can only try with one tonight. Try with whatever you kept back. The Ashbys agreed to one plot each, ours the half nearer the Mead, and Hugh works his owed day there. Their store is full of grain but they won't sell. We eat lightly, I keep pressing the loan, and Wat, rest rather than work hard: there's no firewood to gather here. I've named Maud my heir.
Robert, I have two days owed to our store. Name the work you want from me tomorrow. If you want firewood, tell me where it lies.
Robert, Maud: I will rest tonight and eat only my ration. I keep my two days owed to the store and will work them when you name a place we know. Good night.

Let us walk the Field together before we work. I will weed the barley on the unclaimed plots, and our own Green-side plot if it has any. We claim the unclaimed barley for the household only once we know it has no owner. No grain for salt or for the owed day.
Agreed. I will weed the barley with you today and make no claim until someone says who sowed it. If no one owns it, we claim it then. No grain for salt or the owed day.
Goodnight, Hugh and Kit. The barley on the unclaimed plots is weeded. Tomorrow we ask again who sowed it, and claim it only if no one owns it. No grain goes for salt or the owed day.
I will claim one unclaimed plot of barley for us after asking who sowed it, and weed it. We still give no grain for salt or for the owed day.
I'll rest today and pick only a little at the Mead. I'll pass Wat your word about weeding the Fowler plot, the half nearer the Mead.
Thank you, Wat. Tomorrow work your owed day weeding the Mead-side plot of the Field, our plot, if they let you. If they don't, forage the Mead lightly. Maud, rest well.
Robert, Maud: I brought in the little wild food the Mead had. Maud, your time is near; I will help where I can. Robert, tell me tomorrow where my owed days are to be worked.

Good, forage beyond the Mead and hunt the edges; I will forage near the Green and weed our plot. Robert's split stands: one barley plot each, so I claim the Green-side one. No grain for salt or the owed day.

Food is short: the Ashby store has about 7 grain, two nights' eating for three. I will forage beyond the Mead and hunt the edges today. Please eat only your own ration from the store, and keep Kit to his. We still give no grain for salt or for the owed day, and we claim no unclaimed barley until someone says who sowed it.
Goodnight. Tomorrow I will forage for wild food with the proper call, and weed our claimed plot. We still give no grain for salt or for the owed day.
Robert, I will weed the Mead-side plot of the Field for the store today, as my owed day. If the Ashbys stop me, I will forage the Mead lightly instead.

[Field plots and claims] Spring day 8. The Field has two plots. The Green-side plot is ours; the Mead-side plot is the Fowlers' (agreed at the meeting). The barley stands on unclaimed plots. Before claiming any barley for the household, confirm it has no owner. Weed only what is ours or unclaimed. Hugh's owed day under A42 goes on the Fowler plot. Harvest is about 16 days off.

Robert's offer is open: 1 salt for 1 grain. I'm taking two lots of it, two grain from the store for two salt, and I'll put the salt into the store as it comes. Ask Robert about the salt I already gave him; it is owed from yesterday. Then I weed the Field and forage the Mead.
The house has 7 salt put by now toward Grandmother's oath. Robert, the rest of the salt for my grain is still owed to us.
Robert: no to O74. Our 11 grain is all Kit and I will eat before the barley ripens, and we cannot lend any of it out. Salt and coin we already have enough of.

Robert, Wat: thank you, but no to O75 as well. Kit eats from our 11 grain until the barley is ready, and we cannot lend any of it. If the Fowlers have spare grain at harvest, come and talk to us then.
Robert, we decline O74. Six grain now would leave Kit with nothing before the barley is ready. If the Fowlers can lend grain for work at harvest, we'll talk then.

Hugh, Edith: our grain runs out in about five days and harvest is near day 24. We'll give 2 salt a grain, or 1 coin for 2 grain, and Wat and I will reap your strips at harvest for grain lent now. How much can you spare?

I understand, and I honour the oath. One last ask: lend us just 4 grain now and we repay 6 from our own barley at harvest, before we eat a grain of it. Neighbours who starve can't help you reap. If not, no hard feelings.

I understand, and I honour the oath. One last ask: lend us just 4 grain now and we repay 6 from our own barley at harvest, before we eat a grain of it. Neighbours who starve can't help you reap. If not, no hard feelings.

The Ashbys have only 11 grain themselves and won't lend any. We have about 15 meals, so from now on we rest and work as little as we can. Maud, take the Mead every few days when it has regrown. If it comes to it, we can cut some barley green near the end. Did the Mead give anything today?
Edith, Hugh: I'll stand by Robert's word. Wat will reap your strips at harvest for grain lent now, if you'll take us on those terms.

Agreed, Hugh. I will not touch the grain beyond our share. I'm foraging the Mead today and have put out an offer of grain for salt to anyone who has some. If you find salt at the marsh edge, bring it to the house.

Hugh, we ate little today and I used only one unit of six. Tomorrow I forage the Mead with all my work, and keep the grain for our share. Has anyone heard of salt? I still owe Grandmother the salt before the eighth day.

Hugh, we ate little today and I used only one unit of six. Tomorrow I forage the Mead with all my work, and keep the grain for our share. Has anyone heard of salt? I still owe Grandmother the salt before the eighth day.
Thank you, Hugh. Tomorrow I will forage the Mead in any dry hours, and in rain we keep to the house and eat only our share. Please ask the Fowlers about salt when you can.
Thank you, Hugh. Tomorrow I will forage the Mead in any dry hours, and in rain we keep to the house and eat only our share. Please ask the Fowlers about salt when you can.

Edith, Grandmother's oath is on me: we must put by salt before the eighth day is out, and we have none in the store. I will ask the others today and look at the marsh edge for it. Please keep the grain close and do not eat more than our share, since the barley is still weeks off.

Agreed, we forage the Mead together and Kit stays by the house. I will look along the marsh edge for salt as we go and tell you the moment I see any. Keep your own share of the grain small until we know more about the wild food.

Edith, agreed: you forage the Mead with your full work and I will do the same, and we keep the grain for our share. I will ask the Fowlers about salt first thing tomorrow, and I will not let the oath slip.

Hugh, I have taken one lot of Robert's salt, 5 salt for 8 grain, into our store. That keeps the oath alive. I'll weed the Field in the rain for the barley. Please keep the house dry and eat only our share.

Hugh, the weeding took me one unit only, and I left five unused. Tomorrow I'll use all six: weeding the barley if the rain eases, and firewood if not. We have salt now from Robert's trade, so let's keep the grain for our share.

Hugh, I took one lot only, 5 salt for 8 grain, and Robert also took my 1 grain for 1 salt. So we should have about six salt. I took no second lot. Tomorrow I'll use all my work on the barley or firewood, and we keep the grain for our share.

Edith, I accepted one lot of Robert's offer (5 salt for 8 grain) this morning. If you also took a lot, we have paid 16 grain for 10 salt. Please check the store and tell me. I will take no more grain for salt. I am foraging the Mead now; keep to the house in the wet and eat only our share.

Edith, how much salt is in our store now, and did you take a second lot from Robert? I want us to keep the grain for our share until the barley ripens. Tomorrow I will forage the Mead in any dry hours and look for wild food.
Agreed, Edith: grain stays for our share, and we use dry hours for the barley or firewood. Tomorrow, please check the salt count in the store with me, so we know how much the oath has bought.
Hugh, nine salt is good news for the oath. Without the crude tool, cutting young growth will be harder, so forage the Mead first and keep to our share of grain. I'll weed the barley tomorrow.

Edith, Robert took my crude tool for 3 salt, so we should have about nine salt now. Tomorrow I will forage what is left on the Mead or cut firewood, and keep the grain for our share until the barley ripens.

Hugh, I've accepted one lot of Robert's offer: 5 salt for 8 grain. With my 1 salt in the store and the 3 there, we hold 9, which should meet the oath. I'll keep the rest of our grain for our share. I'm weeding the Field all day.
Edith, a clear day: I am foraging the Mead with my full work for wild food. We keep the grain for our share. Please look along the Field's edge for any wood I may have missed.
Edith, the Mead gave only a little. Tomorrow I will walk further out for wild food or wood, and we keep to our share of grain. Good work on the Field.

Hugh, we hold 9 salt now, so the oath is met. I won't take a second lot of Robert's offer: grain is down to 15, and we must keep it for our share. I'm weeding by hand and checking the Field's edge for wood.
Hugh, agreed: no grain goes out, and I'll eat only my share. I'm weeding by hand and watching the Field's edge for hare, bird or berry, and I'll forage if weeding can't be done.
Hugh, agreed: I'll eat only my share. I'll weed the Field tomorrow and forage the Mead if I can't weed. Don't worry about the order; foraging with you and Kit is the right work.

Edith, the store holds only about 15 grain, which is three or four nights of meals for us three. Barley is weeks off, so no grain goes for salt or anything else. I am foraging all day for wild food, further out if the Mead is bare. Please keep weeding by hand, and keep an eye out for any hare, bird or berry on the Field's edge. Eat your share from the store, not more.
Good, Edith. Keep weeding by hand and watch the Field's edge for wood. I am foraging all day, and we eat from the store only our share.

Edith, I wasted most of my units today: the order at the Green was refused, since foraging is done at the Mead. Tomorrow I forage at the Mead from the start, and Kit forages there with me. Please eat only your share from the store.
Hugh, agreed: I'll hunt along the Field's edge and beyond, and I'll eat only my share. I'll bring in any hare or bird.
Good, Edith. Forage the Mead with us, and hunt the Field's edge if the Mead is bare. Eat only your share from the store.

Edith, the Mead is bare: only a tenth of a meal today. Tomorrow I will hunt beyond the Mead and along the Field's edge instead, and I will use all my units. Please eat only your share, and keep an eye out for any birds or hares you see.
Agreed, Hugh. You take the ground beyond the Mead; I'll keep to the Field's edge and bring home anything I catch. I'll eat only my share from the store.
Goodnight. Tomorrow I hunt at the Field, and I eat only my share from the store.
Edith, the store is down to 9.5 grain, so we eat only our share. Today I hunt beyond the Mead and along the Field's edge. If you find anything edible there, bring it to the store.

Hugh, hunting has been refused at the Field and the Mead alike, so I'll try foraging at the Mead tomorrow. If that is refused too, we need to find out from the village which place takes hunting. Eat only your share.

Edith, the store holds about 3.9 meals against three a night, and it rains all day. I hunt the Mead today; you hunt the Field. Bring every scrap of game or wild food to the Ashby store, and eat only our share. I will keep the salt, since the oath is met and food comes first.

Edith, the Mead refused my hunt, so my six units were wasted. Tomorrow I name the Field itself and hunt there. If you hunt the Field too, take a different line from mine. Everything comes to the store, and we eat only our share.
Tomorrow I hunt the Field itself, not the Mead, since the Mead refused it today. Bring all game and wild food to the Ashby store, and eat only our share.
Sleep well. Robert took my offer, 3 grain for 2 salt, not yours, so the salt is owed to us. I will ask him for it at the Green first thing. Thank you for seeing to Kit in the morning.
Robert took my offer of 3 grain for 2 salt. The salt is owed to us, and I will ask him for it at the Green first thing, before we work.
Robert, the Fowlers owe the Ashby house 2 salt for the 3 grain we gave. Please bring it to our door before the work starts.
Robert, the Fowlers owe the Ashby house 2 salt for the 3 grain we gave. Please bring it to our door before the work starts. And does anyone know where wild food or wood lies beyond the Mead?
Robert has not yet brought the 2 salt the Fowlers owe us. I will ask him again at the Green first thing tomorrow.
Yes, I'll keep a unit back for trying for a child tonight. Please pay Hugh the 2 salt from our store before work, so the debt to the Ashbys is settled.
Yes, Maud. The salt moved when I accepted Hugh's offer, so our store is 3 salt down: 2 to Hugh and 1 to Edith. If he still says we owe him, I'll talk to him tomorrow.
Robert, the 2 salt the Fowlers owe the Ashby house is still not brought. Please bring it to our door. Does anyone know where game or wild food is to be found?

The barley is on both plots of the Field, south of the Green; I weeded it when I first worked there. Its plots are held in shares, so you may need to ask the Fowlers to claim them. Tomorrow we go beyond the Mead together for food and wood.

Hugh, I've left 2 salt at your door. I still think it went over with the offer, but I won't quarrel with neighbours over 2 salt. We know of no game or wild food beyond the Mead either. Whoever finds some, please share word of it.

I do not know of any place beyond the Mead where food or wood can be had; Maud and Wat are searching the ways out. Tomorrow we wait for their word before going far, and keep the grain for the house. We have firewood enough for now.

I'm sorry I took the salt offer without asking you; I thought it was ours to trade. Ask Hugh for a share of the Field's harvest tomorrow, and we'll go with that. The Mead is picked bare, so before we claim it or sow seed there, let's see whether it can bear grain at all.

Maud, that salt offer was meant for the Ashbys. Taking it only moves our own goods around, so I've withdrawn it. Worse news: the Field is held by the Ashbys, so the barley we've weeded is theirs, not ours. Tomorrow I'll ask Hugh for a share of the harvest for our weeding and salt. Should we claim the Mead and sow some grain there?
Maud, there's nowhere past the Mead to walk to, so don't waste the day. Tomorrow let's settle a harvest share with the Ashbys instead. Good night.

Robert says no way out holds wood or game, so we cannot rely on the ways out. Do not give a quarter of the barley now; we can agree a fair share after harvest, for the weeding Maud and Wat did. Keep the grain in the store.

Robert says no way out holds wood or game, so we cannot rely on the ways out. Do not give a quarter of the barley now; we can agree a fair share after harvest, for the weeding Maud and Wat did. Keep the grain in the store.

Robert says there is no game or wood beyond the village, so the search is over. Do not forage the Mead, it is bare. We keep the grain for the house and weed the Field today. Let us talk about the barley share at harvest; I did not ask Wat and Maud to weed.
Robert: thank you for looking. We did not ask for the weeding, so we will settle any share of the barley at harvest. We decline the salt for grain offers; we have salt enough.

Edith, Kit: we sleep here tonight. The grain stays in the store for the house and Kit eats from it as usual. Tomorrow I weed the Field. We settle the barley share at harvest, and we try for no child while food is short.

Agreed: I'll rest and save food, and I've asked the Ashbys to talk over a harvest share today. If Hugh still wants to search past the Mead for game or wood, I'll go only if you say so, since we have no known way out. Should we claim the Mead for grain, or not until we know it can bear?

Hugh and Edith: our store is low and the barley is still some two weeks off. We weeded your Field, and we'd like to agree a share of the harvest with you for that work and our salt. Can we talk about it today?

I'll hunt the Mead with Wat for 3 units and keep 3 back to try tonight. I won't take Edith's O87: it pays the Ashbys' work in our grain. Your salt offers only move our own goods around, so I'll leave them alone. I'll put the Ashby share question to Hugh once we know what the hunt brings.
Hunting is refused at the Mead, so there's no game here. Tomorrow let's ration and press the Ashbys for a share of the barley, and we'll keep the fire small until then.

Hugh, Edith: Wat and Maud have weeded your barley in the Field for days. We ask a fair share of the harvest for it: say a quarter of the barley. Until then, I offer 2 salt for 3 grain (O-offer open to anyone). There's no way out of the village to wood or game; we've all looked.
Don't go searching: there's no way out. Let's not sow the Mead yet, since it would eat the grain we live on. Rest, keep 3 units back to try tonight, and let's get the Ashbys to agree a share.

I'm offering Hugh two days of weeding on the Field for two grain, to be paid from the harvest. That's a fair start on the share you want. Hunting at the Mead today; forage and the Field are the fallback.
Wat took my offer: two grain in for two days' work from me, which I owe him. I will work for the Fowlers tomorrow. Please keep the grain in the store for Kit and us.
Hugh, Kit: we sleep here tonight. Wat has taken my offer, so I owe him two days' work for the two grain, which I will pay tomorrow. The store stays for the house, and Kit eats from it as usual.

Agreed: the grain stays in the store, no child while food is short, and I keep Kit fed from the store. I owe Wat two days' work, which I will pay tomorrow. Ask about wood beyond the Green in the morning; I will weed the Field with you if it is dry.

Rain all day. The store is at about 11.5 grain, so we eat as little as we can and Kit eats from the store only. I will ask Robert and Wat whether they will lend grain against our share of the barley at harvest. Stay under cover with Kit.

Rain all day. The store is at about 11.5 grain, so we eat as little as we can and Kit eats from the store only. I will ask Robert and Wat whether they will lend grain against our share of the barley at harvest. Stay under cover with Kit.

Robert, Wat: we are short of grain until the barley ripens, about 16 days. We will give a fair share of our barley at harvest for the weeding, and we ask whether either house can lend 3 grain now against that share. Salt we have enough of.

Robert, Wat: we are short of grain until the barley ripens, about 16 days. We will give a fair share of our barley at harvest for the weeding, and we ask whether either house can lend 3 grain now against that share. Salt we have enough of.

It's a rain day, so I'll rest and save food. I've asked the Ashbys for grain now against the harvest share, since I'm near my time. Let's keep the fire small, and don't take Edith's O87, since it would pay our grain for the Ashbys' work.
Hugh and Edith: we are short of grain, and I am near my time. Would you let us have some grain now, against a fair share of the barley at harvest? We will work for it on the Field.

Agreed: I'll rest by the fire at the Fowler house today and keep warm. I won't take any offers or weed the Ashby field until Hugh agrees a share. Let's sleep under one roof tonight and keep the fire small.
We sleep at the Fowler house tonight, with the fire kept small. Tomorrow I'll speak with Hugh about a grain share for the weeding.

Hugh: we can't lend grain. We have about four nights left ourselves, with Maud near her time. We'll take the barley share at harvest as you say. I'd still give coin for grain if you find any to spare.

Hugh: we can't lend grain. We have about four nights left ourselves, with Maud near her time. We'll take the barley share at harvest as you say. I'd still give coin for grain if you find any to spare.

Wat, don't cut hay. We have no beasts, so it's work burned for nothing. Tomorrow rest by Maud and keep the fire small. Please don't take any more offers that pay out our grain: we're down to about 4 nights. Edith owes us 2 days of work, so we'll ask her to spend them weeding or doing the work we'd otherwise do.

Wat, don't cut hay. We have no beasts, so it's work burned for nothing. Tomorrow rest by Maud and keep the fire small. Please don't take any more offers that pay out our grain: we're down to about 4 nights. Edith owes us 2 days of work, so we'll ask her to spend them weeding or doing the work we'd otherwise do.

Edith's two days of work for our two grain are now owed to us, so the Ashbys should come and work when they can. I'll gather hay at the Mead tomorrow if Maud is well and the rain stops; otherwise I'll keep the fire and the house.
Agreed: I will not take grain from the store. I will forage the Mead for the Fowlers' debt, tend Kit, and weed the Field with you after. I will tell you before I agree to any food for work.

Hugh, Kit: we sleep here tonight. Tomorrow I will forage the Mead for the Fowlers' debt and tend Kit. Hugh, where does the barley stand? My weeding was refused as there is no crop in the Field, so tell me where to weed.
Agreed: look at the Field first and tell me which plots carry barley. I will forage the Mead for the Fowlers' debt and tend Kit, and I will weed only where the barley stands.
Come weed with me in the Field. We will keep the store shut and feed Kit from it only as usual. I owe the Fowlers two days; I will work them when they have a task.

Robert, Wat: we owe the Fowlers two days' work for the two grain, and we will pay it. The Mead is bare, so I will weed the Field today and go to the Mead with you when it bears. We cannot give grain back.
Thank you, Robert and Wat. I'll eat my share first and sleep here. Wat, I'll send for you first if my time comes.

Hugh, Edith: you owe the Fowlers 2 days of work for the 2 grain we paid. Please spend them foraging for us when the Mead bears, or give the grain back. Neither house can lend grain now. We're nearly out, with a child on the way.

Hugh, Edith: you owe the Fowlers 2 days of work for the 2 grain we paid. Please spend them foraging for us when the Mead bears, or give the grain back. Neither house can lend grain now. We're nearly out, with a child on the way.

The Mead is bare, so foraging is no use for days. Tomorrow we all rest and eat as little as we can. Maud eats first, for the child. I'll ask Hugh to feed us from his store against the barley share he promised.

Agreed: I'll rest by Maud and keep the fire small, and I won't accept any offer that pays out our grain. Edith's two days are still owed to us; I'll ask her to put them to work on the Field or wherever we need.

[Food plan] Day 9: Maud is WITH CHILD. Store is 5.1 grain and 5.9 beans, about 2 nights for three. The Ashbys won't sell grain, and coin and salt are no use. The harvest is about 16 days off (about day 25), and they promise a share for the weeding. The Ashbys owe us 2 days of work (A103) for the 2 grain Wat paid. Forage the Mead whenever it bears. Rest otherwise. If we start starving, ask to eat with the Ashb
Agreed. Keep Kit close, and let's share the carrying of the store until the barley is ripe. Good night.
Our share of the Field isn't in our name yet. Shall I claim the plots for the Fowler household in the morning, before weeding?
Agreed. Speak to Maud and Robert in the morning about a share of the harvest, or work for it. I'll keep to the Mead and hunt where I can. Good night.

The whole Field is the Fowlers', so we hold no strip and I wasted the day's weeding. Tomorrow I will speak to Maud and Robert about what we can do with the store and whether any share of the harvest can be had. Please keep to the Mead and hunt if you can.
I will claim the unclaimed plot of the Field for the Fowlers and weed the barley there today, in the rain. Come to the Field when you can.

I'm going out past the Mead to forage along the ways out, and I'll gather firewood if I find none. I'll keep dry and come back to the fire by evening. Please ask Maud and Robert what share or work for grain they'll give us.
Maud, Robert: we still count the second plot of the Field as ours, and we will weed it. Let us settle its share before harvest. We are holding our grain for now, so we will not trade it yet.

The Ashbys have no strip in the Field, so my weeding was refused and I left my units unused. We have little food: about 16 grain and 2 salt, enough for a few nights for three of us, and the barley is 16 days from reaping. Do not sell grain for salt. If Robert's offer is a loan repaid at harvest, I would accept that; if not, we need work or food from somewhere. Tomorrow, rain is likely: gather fire

Agreed: no grain sold for salt. If Robert's offer is only a loan repaid in kind at harvest, I will weigh it tomorrow. Tomorrow we gather firewood and forage what we can, with Kit fed first. Good night.
Agreed, Edith. We keep the grain, Kit eats first, and rain is coming, so we keep the fire in. In the morning we will weigh Robert's offer as a loan repaid at harvest.
Hugh, Edith: do you have a spare hand mill stone, or any stone to lend? We'd like to grind our grain into meal. We can offer salt for it.
Hugh, Edith: we're short of grain until our barley comes in. I offer salt for grain one to one, or a coin a grain. We'll repay in kind from our harvest if you'd rather lend.
Hugh, Edith: we're short of grain until our barley comes in. I offer salt for grain one to one, or a coin a grain. We'll repay in kind from our harvest if you'd rather lend.
Rain today, so I will weed the unclaimed barley in the Field and gather firewood if that fails. We keep the grain for Kit first. Please eat only your share, and tell me if Kit is hungry.

Robert offers a loan of salt only if we lend him grain first, so I decline. I have offered to take 2 grain now for 3 back after reaping. I weed the Field's unclaimed barley today. Feed Kit first and keep to your share.

Robert offers a loan of salt only if we lend him grain first, so I decline. I have offered to take 2 grain now for 3 back after reaping. I weed the Field's unclaimed barley today. Feed Kit first and keep to your share.

Robert, Hugh here. We have no hand mill, and I know of no road out beyond the Mead. We will not lend grain to you while ours is short. Offer: we take 2 grain now and repay 3 grain after the Fowlers reap.
I weeded the unclaimed barley today and will try the Field's edges and firewood tomorrow. Kit eats first; keep to your share of the grain. Good night.

Hugh, Edith: we're down to about three days of food and our barley is still days off. I'll give 2 salt for every grain, or lend now and we'll pay back 2 grain for 1 from our harvest. Do you have a hand mill, and does any road lead out of here?

Hugh, Edith: we're down to about three days of food and our barley is still days off. I'll give 2 salt for every grain, or lend now and we'll pay back 2 grain for 1 from our harvest. Do you have a hand mill, and does any road lead out of here?
We have about 4.6 grain and 5.9 beans left, about two days. The Ashbys won't lend. I've offered them 2 grain back for 1 plus salt. Eat what you need: you and the child come first.
Hugh, thank you for the answer. Your offer would leave us shorter now, so I can't take it. Mine is better for you: for each grain you lend now, you get 2 salt today and 2 grain back from our harvest.
Hugh, thank you for the answer. Your offer would leave us shorter now, so I can't take it. Mine is better for you: for each grain you lend now, you get 2 salt today and 2 grain back from our harvest.

[Offers] Promises in offers must be written like 'grain by day 16' (day number), not 'by summer day 20'. On spring day 9 the barley was judged fit to reap in about 7 days. Hugh won't lend while the Ashbys are short.
Tomorrow I'll weed the Field and forage the Mead again for food for the store. Robert, Wat, if you can, forage or gather firewood with me. We'll share what we find.
Agreed, Hugh: ration from today, Kit first. Ask the Fowlers for a loan, not a sale. I'll weed the Field and bring in any wild food I see.
Hugh, the weeding is done for today. Tell me what the Fowlers say about a loan. Tomorrow I'll weed again or forage, as the weather allows.

Rain all day, so I'll weed the Field under the rain and forage beyond the Mead for whatever is growing. The store is 29 grain and the barley is about 20 days off, so we must ration from today: no extra meals, Kit first. I'll ask the Fowlers for a loan of grain against the harvest, not a sale. Tell me if you'd rather I do something else.
Thank you for weeding today. Tomorrow I'll look beyond the Mead for game and wild food, and talk to Robert about borrowing grain against the harvest. Keep Kit dry tonight.
Good, Hugh. Ask for a loan, not a sale, and tell me the Fowlers' terms before we agree to anything. I'm weeding the Field today. Bring in any wild food you find.
I've asked the Fowlers aloud for a loan of grain to be repaid at harvest. I'll forage beyond the Mead and weed the Field after. Tell me if you hear anything from them.
Robert, Maud, Wat: our barley is about 19 days from reaping and our store is thin. Would you lend us grain now, to be repaid from our harvest? I'd offer salt in return if you prefer.
Robert, Maud, Wat: our barley is about 19 days from reaping and our store is thin. Would you lend us grain now, to be repaid from our harvest? I'd offer salt in return if you prefer.

Hugh, I'm weeding the Field all day with my six units. Don't agree to Robert's salt or coin for grain offer: we keep the grain. If the Fowlers or Robert grant a loan, bring me the exact terms first. Bring any wild food you find to the house store.

Edith, I'll ask Robert aloud for a loan of grain repaid at harvest, then forage beyond the Mead and bring everything to the house store. I won't agree to the salt deal without your word. Weed the Field if you can.

Edith, I'll ask Robert aloud for a loan of grain repaid at harvest, then forage beyond the Mead and bring everything to the house store. I won't agree to the salt deal without your word. Weed the Field if you can.
Robert, I ask the Fowlers for a loan of 4 grain, to be repaid from the barley at harvest. Tell me your terms here in the open, and I will bring them to Edith before we agree.
Robert: the Ashbys ask the Fowlers for a loan of grain, to be repaid at harvest. What terms would you give? We are not agreeing to any sale of grain, and we decline the salt and coin offers for now.

Hugh, I'm sorry, but we can't lend grain now. We have barely a week of food for three of us, with the harvest 18 days off. If the Mead or the edges turn up food, let's share news of it. Perhaps we can help each other at harvest.

Hugh, I'm sorry, but we can't lend grain now. We have barely a week of food for three of us, with the harvest 18 days off. If the Mead or the edges turn up food, let's share news of it. Perhaps we can help each other at harvest.

Agreed, keep it light tomorrow. Maud, about Hugh's loan: we have about six nights of food and the harvest is about eighteen days off. If we only have to pay him back after the reaping, the loan carries us through, so let's hear his terms before we say no. Wat, good. Look close by and come back.
Robert, agreed: no grain loans. I'll weed the Field, and if Wat finds food past the Mead, we'll share it at the Fowler house.

Hugh, we can't lend grain. We have barely five nights of food ourselves and the harvest is far off. If you ever have grain to spare, our offers of salt or coin for grain stay open. Let's share word of anything we find: wild food on the Mead, or a way out.

Hugh, we can't lend grain. We have barely five nights of food ourselves and the harvest is far off. If you ever have grain to spare, our offers of salt or coin for grain stay open. Let's share word of anything we find: wild food on the Mead, or a way out.

Hugh, we can't lend grain. We have barely five nights of food ourselves and the harvest is far off. If you ever have grain to spare, our offers of salt or coin for grain stay open. Let's share word of anything we find: wild food on the Mead, or a way out.

Hugh, we can't lend grain. We have barely five nights of food ourselves and the harvest is far off. If you ever have grain to spare, our offers of salt or coin for grain stay open. Let's share word of anything we find: wild food on the Mead, or a way out.

Good. Maud and Wat, you go past the Mead tomorrow, and I'll stay to watch the Mead and pick it if it comes back. As for the Ashbys, we still can't lend grain. Our coin and salt offers for their grain stay open, and if they want a deal, they come to us.
The Field is clean. Tomorrow I'll take the new tool and clear ground. Do we have any seed grain to spare for a new plot after harvest?

You are right to check. I put 12 salt in and took none out, but I wrote down 28 from the scene without counting it, and I was wrong to trust that. Let us count salt by salt first thing, before any trade. Please trade no firewood either: we have only 14 for about 7 nights of fuel. I will find food for Kit and keep the grain untouched.
The store has 37.8 grain, and I think that is enough to keep as seed after harvest for a new plot. I will weed the Field tomorrow; if the rain holds off I will gather firewood after.
Their bins look low, so offer them work or coin for grain again when you can reach Hugh or Edith. I will cut hay tomorrow.

I'm going to forage the Mead for wild food this morning, for the household. I won't take up the salt-for-grain offers without your word, since the grain is our food. Tell me if you want me on the roads or the wood instead.
I've put the wild food I found into the store. Robert, Maud: tomorrow, tell me where you want me. I'll not trade our grain without your word.
Hugh, if you will put your owed work days into clearing, come to the Mead plot; we will sow it as soon as it is clear.
Good night. I'll speak to Hugh first thing and ask him to bring his owed work days to the Mead plot.

I'm clearing the Mead plot all day. If Hugh will put his owed work days into clearing with us, send him there. We have about 7 nights of food, so let's sow the plot as soon as it's cleared and keep the grain we eat to a minimum.
Good. Please ask Hugh to spend the days he owes us clearing our Mead plot. Once it's clear we sow grain, but only a few units, because we need to keep enough to eat.
About 7 units of clearing are left on the Mead plot. Tomorrow Wat and I clear it, and Maud, please get Hugh to work his owed days there too. Once it's clear we sow a few grain. Good night.

I'll clear the unclaimed Mead plot this morning, since Maud asked for our owed days for sowing. Keep the grain as it is. I won't accept any salt offer until I've told you first; Maud's 10 grain for 5 salt is one we can't afford.
Good night. Hugh's two days (A88) are still owed to us. Tomorrow let's finish the Mead with Wat and sow only a few grain once it's clear.

Good night. Tomorrow we finish clearing the Mead, about three units left. Hugh, your two days for the Fowlers are still owed; please bring them to the Mead plot. We sow once it is clear, and only a few grain, since our store is tight.
Agreed. I'll ask Hugh to bring his owed days to weed the Mead tomorrow, and I'll keep the salt for food.
Agreed, Robert. Tomorrow Hugh's owed days go to weeding the Mead, and we keep the salt for buying food.

Please don't accept Hugh's offer again. You've taken it three times, which is 12 salt, so he owes us about 6 days of work. Let him work those off first. Don't pay Edith salt either. Hugh's clearing on the unclaimed plot should be for us, so tell him that, and we'll claim that plot once it's cleared.

The plot is cleared. We have about 16 grain left, and the Mead barley is ready in about 7 days, so I won't sow more until we reap it. Tomorrow Wat and I weed the thistle and dock in the Mead. Maud, see whether Hugh's owed days can go to weeding too, and keep the salt for buying food only.
Maud, I'm clearing the Mead today for the two days I owe you. When the work's done, pay the salt for it into the Ashby store.

Robert offers 6 salt for 6 grain (O109), a better rate than 2 per salt. It would take our grain to about 4 before barley is ripe, so I haven't accepted it. I'll weed the Mead today for Maud's owed work and bring the offer to you tomorrow morning. We decide it together, and I won't accept before you say yes.
I've taken Edith's two grain for four salt for our household, to ease the store. I'm weeding the Mead with you and Wat today, and I've asked Hugh to bring his owed days to weeding.

Edith, the Mead is nearly clear, so no more clearing is needed; I've accepted your two grain for four salt for the Fowler household. Hugh, please bring your owed two days to weed the Mead barley, now.
Agreed. I'll weed the Mead with you and Wat for the Fowler barley, then forage with the rest of my day for food. I'll ask Hugh to bring his owed days to weeding there. We sow nothing until we reap.
Hugh's owed days (A88) are for weeding the Mead; I'll tell him so now.
I'll ask Hugh and Edith tomorrow whether they reaped any of our Mead barley. Their owed days stay work, not grain, unless they say otherwise.

Robert, I didn't see who reaped the Mead, so I can't say whether the Ashbys took it. Tomorrow I'll ask Edith and Hugh before we claim anything owed. Wat, yes: hoe the Fowlers' part and dibble only a few grain thinly. Good night.
Good. Edith says she owes us two days. If that's so, put them into weeding too. Don't take on any new work for salt.

There's stubble where our Mead barley was. Did either of you see who reaped it, or did the clearing ruin it? If the Ashbys took it, they owe us that grain. The field is ready now. Tomorrow I'll dibble a few grain thinly, since the soil is rich, and we sell salt for any grain we can get. Maud, could the Ashbys pay what they owe us in grain rather than work?
Robert: today I'm weeding the Field, and that counts toward the two days I owe the Fowlers under A88.
I'm foraging beyond the Mead for food, then weeding the Fowlers' Mead plot, which I claimed last night. Hugh's owed days (A88) I'll ask to go to that weeding.
Hugh, Edith: do either of you know a village or the coast where grain can be bought? We will pay salt. Hugh, your owed days should go to weeding the Field barley, as Robert asked.
Hugh, Edith: the two days you owe us under A88, please put them into weeding the barley in the Field. If you'd rather pay in grain, one grain a day settles it.

The Mead has nothing growing to weed yet; Wat is only dibbling it today. Put your weeding and Hugh's owed days on the Field barley instead. Please don't buy Hugh's work for salt; we need the salt to buy food. Ask the Ashbys where the way to the coast lies.

Hugh, Edith: please put the two days you owe us under A88 into weeding the barley in the Field. The Mead has only just been sown and has nothing yet to weed. We need food, not more work bought with salt.

We can't reach 25 today, with 13 salt in the store. I'll weed the Field to pay down our A88 debt to the Fowlers, and I'll gather firewood for the store. Please keep the 4 grain for food. Don't take any grain-for-salt deal. Taking salt into the store is fine if the work is done.

[Mead plot] Spring day 6: the Mead has about three units of clearing left for the Fowlers. Hugh owes us two days' work (A88, for four salt). Sow only a few grain once clear; the store holds about 22 grain and 25 salt.
Agreed: I'll rest today and keep my offer O71 open for grain. If Hugh or Edith lend grain against the Mead harvest, I'll bring it to the Fowler store.

We're down to about 8.6 grain and 6 beans, roughly 3 nights. I've offered the Ashbys 1 salt per grain. Rest today, and keep Wat resting too. If Hugh or Edith talk to you, ask them to lend grain against our Mead harvest.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers are short of food until our Mead barley comes in. We'll give 1 salt for each grain or bean, or 4 coin for 3 grain. When our harvest is in, we'll pay back any grain you lend us, with extra.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers are short of food until our Mead barley comes in. We'll give 1 salt for each grain or bean, or 4 coin for 3 grain. When our harvest is in, we'll pay back any grain you lend us, with extra.

No grain came from the Ashbys today, so they may be short too. Wat, put the salt back in the store, please, so the house offers can draw on it. For the next few days we work as little as we can, so we eat less, until the Mead barley is ripe in about 6 days. Tomorrow I'll ask Hugh plainly to lend grain against our harvest.
Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers ask you to lend us grain against our Mead harvest, due in about six days. We'll repay it from the harvest, with extra. We also offer salt or firewood for grain now.
I've offered the Ashbys 2 firewood per grain, and a loan: 4 grain now for 7 back by summer day 8. Rest today and keep Wat resting too. We have about 2 nights of food.
Hugh, Edith: your woodpile is low and ours is full. We'll give 2 firewood for each grain, up to 12 firewood. Or lend us 4 grain now and we'll pay back 7 grain from the Mead harvest by summer day 8.
Good. I've put up a loan offer: 4 grain now for 7 back by summer day 8, and 2 firewood per grain. Point Hugh and Edith to it if they're willing.
Hugh, Edith: we'll give 2 firewood for each grain, or lend us 4 grain now and the Fowlers will pay back 7 from the Mead harvest by summer day 8.
Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers will give 2 salt for every 3 grain, up to 6 salt, and repay from our Mead harvest with extra. We are out of grain and need it now.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers have no grain left and our beans last one night. Whatever you can spare, we'll pay well: 10 firewood for 5 grain, two days of my labour for 5 grain, or 7 grain back from our harvest for every 4 you lend. If you're short too, tell us, and we'll find a way together.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers have no grain left and our beans last one night. We'll pay well: 10 firewood for 5 grain, two days of my labour for 5 grain, or 7 grain back from our harvest for every 4 you lend. If you're short too, tell us, and we'll find a way together.

Robert offers 2 salt for 3 grain, five lots. I mean to take three lots now: 6 salt for 9 grain, leaving about 23 grain. The Mead is bare, so I will not trade more without your word. Say if you want it otherwise.
Good, thank you. I will weed the Field with my 6 units. I hold the grain. I owe the 2 days' work that bought the 2 salt, so I will work it for whoever holds that claim, when they are at the Green.
Well done on the firewood trade. Tomorrow I owe Robert 2 days' work for his 2 salt, so I will go to where he is at the Field or the Green, and work it. We keep the grain.
About 7 units left on the strip. Hugh owes us 2 days of work for 2 salt, so I'll ask him to clear with us. Once it's cleared we sow a few grain or beans there. Thank you both, good work.

I accepted O101 for our store: 4 firewood for 2 salt, which brings us to 10 salt and about 16 firewood. The 2 days owed to the Fowlers are yours, so I will not work them. I am weeding the Field today.

Before any trade tomorrow, here is the count: 8 salt, 10.9 grain, 20 firewood. Three nights need about 6 to 8 firewood, so about 10 may be spare. I would trade firewood for salt, not grain: the grain is about 7.6 meals and we are short already. Robert's O19 wants 3 grain for 2 salt, so I say no to it unless you judge the store can spare it. Your word on the firewood offer?

Count: 8 salt, 10.9 grain, 20 firewood. I keep the grain and decline Robert's grain offer. I owe the Fowlers 2 days' work, and I will be where they are. I reopen the firewood-for-salt offer as before.

A76 is mine, not yours: I owe the Fowlers 2 days for the salt. Please do not work it. I will clear the Mead strip with Robert's household today. Keep the grain; the store must carry us through the last days. Could you forage or hunt for wild food for the store instead, and keep Kit fed?
Hugh, you owe the Fowlers 2 days of work for the salt. Could you work them off clearing the Mead strip with us, today or tomorrow?
Hugh, you owe the Fowlers 2 days of work for the salt. Could you work them off clearing the Mead strip with us?

Hugh, we now have two offers open for the same thing: your O132 and my offer of 4 firewood for 2 salt, two lots. Together they could spend 16 of our 18 firewood. I have not added anything new. Please keep O132 alone, and tell me if you want my offer withdrawn. I will not take Robert's grain offer without your word. I am foraging the Mead for wild food and will bring it to the store.

Robert, Maud: my hoeing at the Mead gave nothing today, and I spent the rest weeding the Field for nothing. Where do you want me tomorrow? I'll hoe the last 1.9 plots at the Mead unless you say otherwise.

Hugh, I agree: no trade from me today. I will forage wild food for the store with my six units and bring all of it in. Our count is 14 salt by your reading (I had 12), so we should count again tonight. If the wild food covers tonight's meals, would you consider 1 grain for 1 salt to Robert? I will not do it without your word.
Agreed, Hugh: go to the Field for wild food and firewood, and I will go with you in the morning. No trades from me without your word. Goodnight.

Edith, Hugh: the Fowlers are out of grain. We'll give 3 salt for 3 grain, or 1 coin for 3 grain, as much as you can spare. And the 2 days of work you owe us for salt: we'd gladly take them as 4 grain instead.

Edith, Hugh: the Fowlers are out of grain. We'll give 3 salt for 3 grain, 2 salt for 2 beans, or 1 coin for 3 grain, for any food you can spare. And the 2 days of work you owe us for salt: we'd gladly take them as 4 grain instead.

[Salt plan, spring day 8] Goal: salt in the Ashby store at end of day 8. Store at morning: about 8 salt, 7.3 grain, 18 firewood. Grain is kept for the lean days; no grain trades. Firewood for salt only, with Hugh's word. Offer out: 4 firewood for 2 salt, 2 lots (to anyone). Keep about 10 firewood for the last nights. Robert's O19 (grain for salt) declined. Owed: A76, Hugh's 2 days for the Fowlers, not mine to work.
Edith, Hugh: we're short of food until the barley is in. We'll give salt one for one for grain, or a coin for 2 grain. At the harvest we'll repay any grain you lend us with extra. Will you deal?
Edith, Hugh: we're short of food until the barley is in. We'll give salt one for one for grain, or a coin for 2 grain. At the harvest we'll repay any grain you lend us with extra. Will you deal?

Agreed. Tomorrow I'll ask Edith and Hugh to lend us grain now and take it back with extra at the harvest, along with salt. I'll tell you the terms before I agree. Wat, weed lightly. Maud, rest if there's nothing useful to do. We save food that way.
I'll weed the Field today, as I owe it. If you want firewood gathered tomorrow, tell me; we have about 20 sticks in store.
Edith, Hugh: a loan, not a sale. Lend us 6 grain now and we pay back 9 from our barley at the harvest. Or 3 salt for 2 grain. The offers are open.
Edith, Hugh: a loan, not a sale. Lend us 6 grain now and we pay back 9 from our barley at the harvest. Or 3 salt for 2 grain. The offers are open.
Robert, I'll weed the Field lightly today and keep the grain for food. I won't accept the grain-for-salt offers. If Edith or Hugh will lend grain for the harvest, tell me the terms before you agree.

Maud, Wat: nothing came in today. We have about 5 nights of grain and beans left. Tomorrow I'll talk to Edith and Hugh myself about grain for wood or a loan. If nothing comes of it, we should think about reaping a little barley early. What do you both think?

Fowlers, our grain won't last until the barley. I'll work for your house: weeding, hay, firewood, whatever you need. In return I'd take 4 grain for each day's work, or a little salt. The offer is open to you.
