Hugh, Maud took my offer, so we'll have a little salt and I owe the Fowlers a day's work. The Mead gave almost nothing today. If you find a way out, tell me, and I'll go and forage there.

Maud took my work for 1 salt, so I owe them a day. They only trade salt for grain, and we can't spare grain. We're about 10 nights short of the harvest, so let's work lightly and eat less. I'll keep pressing the Fowlers to give grain for our work, perhaps for a share of our harvest later.

Maud took my work for 1 salt, so I owe them a day. They only trade salt for grain, and we can't spare grain. We're about 10 nights short of the harvest, so let's work lightly and eat less. I'll keep pressing the Fowlers to give grain for our work, perhaps for a share of our harvest later.
Robert, Maud: there's no game here, so I'm paying today's work in firewood and leaving it at your store. The offer of 2 days' work for 8 grain still stands, or for a share of our barley at harvest.
Robert, Maud: I'm paying today's work in firewood at your store. And we ask a loan: 8 grain now, and we give back 16 from our barley when it's reaped. The offer is open.

The barley is about 20 days off and our grain covers only about 7 nights. I'll mind Kit and gather firewood today, and I've offered the Fowlers firewood for grain. If they'll lend us grain against our harvest, say 2 for every 1 they give now, I'll agree to it.

Edith, there's no firewood to gather here. But I looked into the Fowlers' house and they hold a great deal of grain, plenty of beans and a lot of salt. Tomorrow I'll offer them a loan against our barley: grain now, paid back twice over at harvest. Our weeded field is good surety. We should both work lightly to save food.

Agreed, Edith, I've taken back the firewood offer. The crude tool helps a little with clearing and building, but it won't make food. Tomorrow I'll ask the Fowlers to lend us grain against the harvest and keep weeding our barley.
I'm weeding the Fowlers' plot today to pay the salt debt. Please keep pressing them on the loan, and mind Kit.
Robert, Maud: I'm weeding your barley plot today to pay my day for the salt (A30). Our offer still stands: lend us 8 grain now and we give back 16 from our barley at harvest.

Both, Hugh. Tomorrow I'll claim one plot as ours and offer the Fowlers a share of its barley at harvest for grain now. We'll also each offer a day's work for 3 grain. You keep minding Kit for a few more days, and I'll do the work for them.

Robert, Maud: our grain runs out in about 6 nights, and the barley comes in around day 24. Lend us 20 grain now and we'll give back 40 from the harvest, twice over. I'm weeding the Field daily so it will bear well. The offer is open.

Robert, Maud: our grain runs out in about 6 nights, and the barley comes in around day 24. Lend us 20 grain now and we'll give back 40 from the harvest, twice over. I'm weeding the Field daily so it will bear well. The offer is open.

Edith, the barley has only just come through, so harvest is a long way off. The Fowlers haven't taken either offer. Tomorrow should we offer them a plot's share of the barley, or both of us work their land for grain each day? We need about 3 grain a night.
I'll sow the beans on the Mead with you today. I'll leave the Field to Edith, who is weeding it for our salt. We won't lend grain yet.

We only have beans enough for one plot, and I can sow it alone. You'd do more good foraging the Mead's edges, or weeding the Field. I won't lend the Ashbys our grain: we have barely 19 meals for 19 days.
Good. I won't claim it again. I'm weeding today to pay the salt debt, and I'll take any deal for grain they offer.
Robert, Maud: I'm weeding the Field today as the day I owe you for the salt. Please count A30 as paid. After that, any day's work from me or Hugh is yours for 3 grain.

Hugh, it seems both claims landed on fallow ground and the barley is still unclaimed. The Fowlers said nothing about grain. Yes, tomorrow we both ask them straight out. We could offer to share the barley: we claim it together and split the harvest, if they lend us grain now to get us through. I'll also try to claim a barley plot for us in the morning.

Hugh, it seems both claims landed on fallow ground and the barley is still unclaimed. The Fowlers said nothing about grain. Yes, tomorrow we both ask them straight out. We could offer to share the barley: we claim it together and split the harvest, if they lend us grain now to get us through. I'll also try to claim a barley plot for us in the morning.

Robert, Maud: we've claimed one plot of the Field, and the other is yours to claim. Our grain runs out in 5 nights. Lend us grain now: we'll pay twice over from our barley at harvest, and I'll weed your plot or work any day you name, 1 day for 3 grain. Name your price and we'll take it.
Robert, Wat: tomorrow we weed the barley plot we claim in the Field, all six units. We cook every grain at the fire and keep the beans to the end. Hugh has his plot; we don't lend grain.

Robert, Maud, Wat: we have four nights of grain left and the barley is 17 days off. Name any price: a share of our barley at harvest, days of our work, our salt back. We'll take it. Without some grain soon, Kit goes hungry. Lend us 20 grain and you'll have 40 back.

Robert, Maud, Wat: we have four nights of grain left and the barley is 17 days off. Name any price: a share of our barley at harvest, days of our work, our salt back. We'll take it. Without some grain soon, Kit goes hungry. Lend us 20 grain and you'll have 40 back.
Agreed: the Field is clean, so I'll rest and only forage the Mead's edges for wild food. The grain stays for cooking, and we lend none.
Robert, Wat: the Mead gave little today. Tomorrow I'll check its edges again. We keep the grain for cooking and lend none.
Maud, I'm weeding our claimed barley plot with you and Robert today. We keep the grain for cooking and lend none.
Maud, agreed: we keep the grain and lend none. Check the Mead's edges tomorrow, and tell us what you find.

Maud, I'm asking you as one mother to another: we have three nights of grain and Kit is three days from grown. Name any price, my work at your hearth, a share of our barley, our salt, and I'll take it.

Maud, I'm asking you as one mother to another: we have three nights of grain and Kit is three days from grown. Name any price, my work at your hearth, a share of our barley, our salt, and I'll take it.
Rain all day. I'll make one short forage at the Mead's edges, then rest, and keep the grain for the fire. We lend none.

Hugh, Edith: we're no better off than you. We have 10 grain for 3 of us, about 3 nights. Lending would only starve both houses. Let's meet tomorrow and agree how we share the barley at harvest, and look for any other food together.

Maud, Wat: Edith has claimed 2 plots of the Field, one of them ours. We sowed that barley on day 2. Tomorrow I'll call a meeting and hold to our share: half the barley is ours. Did the Mead give anything today, Wat?

Robert says they're down to 10 grain too, so there's nothing to lend. At the meeting, let's propose splitting the barley half and half, each side dropping its claim on the other's plot, and both houses weeding. And we should all eat lightly until harvest.

Robert, Maud: here's my proposal. Each house drops its claim on the other's plot, we split the barley half and half at harvest, and both houses weed it. If you have any beans or grain to spare, we'll repay double from our half. Kit is grown in two days and we're nearly empty. Agreed?
Robert: I've said we hold our half of the barley and lend no grain. Tell me if you want me to speak more at the meeting.

Hugh, Edith: we are in the same want as you, and I won't lend grain while our store is short. Robert and I hold that the barley sown on day 2 was ours by our work, so our half stands. If you want to weed or hoe our plots for salt, we'll take that. Let's keep to our own plots and reap at harvest by what each house sowed.

Robert's proposal suits us: each house keeps one plot, and the barley is split half and half at harvest. We agree to that. We can't lend grain or beans now. If you want to weed or hoe for salt, we'll take that, and we'll tell you if we find any food.

Hugh, Edith: we all sowed and weeded that barley together. I propose, before all of us here, that each house holds 1 plot and we split the barley half and half at harvest. As for grain now: we have 6 grain and some beans for 3 people, less than you. We can't lend without starving ourselves. If either of us finds food, let's tell the other. Do you agree to half each?

[Field deal] Day 9 meeting: everyone agreed before witnesses: each house holds 1 barley plot, the barley is split half and half at harvest and reaped together, and the claims on each other's fallow plots are dropped. My claim on day 9 again landed on the Fowlers' plot: don't use claim on the Field any more. Fowlers say 6 grain plus beans; they won't lend.

[Food] Day 9 evening: store ~11 grain (~3.7 nights), 16 firewood, 1 salt. Barley ripe ~day 23-24, split half and half with the Fowlers (agreed and witnessed day 9), reaped together. The Fowlers lend nothing. Plan: forage the Mead on day 10, short meals, Kit fed first. Offers O120 and O121 stand.

[Stores] Spring day 9: store 6.2 grain, 5.9 beans, 0.2 wild food, 16 firewood: about 2.5 nights for 3. The barley will be fit to reap about day 23. The Field is in dispute with the Ashbys: aim for half the barley each. Rest when there's no useful work. Don't lend grain.
Agreed. You weed and I'll cut hay with the tool. I've called out to the Fowlers to trade work, hay or wood for grain, or a loan against our harvest. Half rations if they won't, and Kit eats first.

Maud, Robert, Wat: the Ashbys are running short of grain before harvest. We'll work your strips, cut your hay or give you firewood for grain or beans. Name your price. We'll repay from our barley at harvest too.

The Mead is bare for days yet, and we had too few beans to sow a whole plot. Tomorrow let's rest and spend little. Hugh carries a crude tool. I'll ask whether he'd lend it or work for salt, since cutting with a tool goes far better than by hand. Keep the beans to eat.

Robert, Maud: our grain won't last to harvest, and Kit is still small. We'll give hay, firewood or a day's work for grain or beans. Name your price. Whatever you lend, we'll pay back in barley at harvest, with something over.

Robert, Maud: our grain runs out in about five nights. Will you sell us grain or beans for hay, firewood or work? Or lend us 8 grain now and we'll pay back 12 after harvest. The offers are up; name what suits you.

Robert, Maud: our grain runs out in about five nights. Will you sell us grain or beans for hay, firewood or work? Or lend us 8 grain now and we'll pay back 12 after harvest. The offers are up; name what suits you.

Edith, my call to the Fowlers didn't reach them; I've no way to speak in their house. Tomorrow I'll call out to everyone instead. I cut about 9 hay, so we have nearly 17 to trade, and my offers stand: hay for grain, hay for beans, and a loan of 8 grain paid back as 12 after harvest. Did Maud say anything to you at the Mead?

Edith, my call to the Fowlers didn't reach them; I've no way to speak in their house. Tomorrow I'll call out to everyone instead. I cut about 9 hay, so we have nearly 17 to trade, and my offers stand: hay for grain, hay for beans, and a loan of 8 grain paid back as 12 after harvest. Did Maud say anything to you at the Mead?

With six nights of food and twenty days to the barley, we can't lend any grain, beans or wild food to the Ashbys. Don't take Hugh's firewood either: 22 firewood lasts us longer than our food will. Forage lightly if the Mead shows anything. I'm studying the village today for a way out, where salt might buy grain.

Edith, Hugh: we are short ourselves, only a few nights of grain left, so we can't lend grain or beans. We'll trade salt for anything you can spare. If either of you knows a road out of Saltmarsh End, tell us; it might feed us all.

Robert says they're short too and can't lend. Hay won't buy food, and hard work makes us eat more, so let's rest while the barley's clean and keep the grain for Kit. I'll look the village over for any way out. Weed only when weeds come up.
Hugh, Edith: we have salt to spare, 2 salt for each grain or bean. Do any of you know a way out of Saltmarsh End, or anyone who'd trade? We're both short until harvest. Let's share what we know.

I didn't forage today, only weeded. Light days and Kit first is right. Tomorrow I'll look after Kit and gather a little firewood, nothing heavy. Do ask the Fowlers about other ground. If they have food to spare, we could pay them back in barley at harvest.

Agreed, a light day. I'm caring for Kit and resting. Let's not trade our grain for salt or coin, because it's all the food we have. If the Fowlers will give food for work, or lend grain against the harvest, that's the deal we want.

Hugh, Maud was foraging the Mead today and Robert was clearing part of it for a Fowler field. If they take the meadow, we lose our only wild food and the hay. Should we claim our share of the Mead, or ask them to share it fairly? Did they answer you about food for work?

Good, claiming the plot was right. Offer them a day's work on their field or the clearing for every 2 grain now, and 3 barley at harvest for every 2 they lend us. We need about 12 more grain to reach the harvest, maybe 15 to be safe. Don't let our own grain go for salt or coin. I'll forage our plot of the Mead tomorrow when the grass comes back, and keep Kit fed and the fire lit.

Maud, Robert, Wat: we Ashbys are short of food until harvest. Do you know of any ground past Saltmarsh End to forage or hunt, or any road out? If you can spare grain or food now, we'll work your field for it, or pay you back in barley at harvest, more than we take.

Edith, I've claimed one of the Mead's two plots for us tonight, so half stays ours and they keep the other half. That's fair shares. I haven't asked them about food yet. I rested today, which was a mistake. Tomorrow I'll go to Robert and Maud first thing and offer work now for food, or barley at harvest.
I've put offers to the Fowlers: a day's work for 2 grain, or 2 grain lent now for 3 back at harvest. Keep Kit fed and the hearth lit, and forage our Mead plot once it comes back.

Robert, Maud: we won't sell grain for salt or coin. But I'll work a day on your clearing or field for 2 grain. Or lend us grain now, and we'll pay back 3 barley at harvest for every 2. The offers are open.

No answer yet. Robert only offered salt or coin for our grain, and I've turned that down. My offers are 2 grain for a day's work, or 3 barley back at harvest for 2 lent now. Leave yours up too, so they can take whichever suits them.

Robert, Maud: we won't sell grain for salt or coin. But I'll work a day on your clearing or field for 2 grain. Or lend us grain now, and we'll pay back 3 barley at harvest for every 2. The offers are open.

Yes, Edith. Tomorrow morning I'll tell them before everyone that the plot is ours, by our claim, and they should stop clearing it. If they want more field, they can have the clearing in return for grain to tide us over. Nobody has taken up my offers yet. Thank you for withdrawing yours.
Robert's claim on the empty plot seems fair to me, so let's agree it and keep peace. But we can't lend grain: we have about 21, only 5 nights. I'll care for Kit and forage the Mead with you.

Hugh, the Mead is picked bare and I couldn't forage at all. We have about 21 grain, roughly 5 nights, and the barley is 18 days off. Did Robert or Maud answer you about our plot? I think we should let them clear our Mead plot for their field if they lend us grain now, say 8 grain against barley at harvest. Otherwise we'll be eating green barley before long. We should both keep our days light and e

Yes, Hugh. Short meals for the two of us, but Kit eats his fill first, since he'll be working in 5 days. Let's keep our days light so we need less. Tell them the plot is ours, but offer them the right to clear it for a loan of grain now, paid back in barley at harvest. Grain is worth more to us than the plot this season. When the barley turns, we'll take some green in a pinch.

No answer from them yet, Edith. Your plan is good. Tomorrow I'll put it to Robert before everyone: they can clear our Mead plot for their field if they lend us 8 grain now, and we pay it back in barley at harvest. We'll keep our days light and eat only cooked grain.

Robert, the store holds about 18 meals for three and harvest is about 20 days off, so we will run short within a week at this rate. I have offered Hugh 4 grain now for 6 barley at harvest; I would rather borrow than go hungry, and you can withdraw it if you disagree. Please do not clear the disputed Mead plot until the Ashbys agree the claim. I'll forage the Mead first light and bring everything t

Hugh, Edith: the Mead has two plots. You hold one, and I claimed only the empty one, so I'm not taking yours. Will you agree? And lend us grain: we'll pay 4 barley at harvest for every 3 now. The offer is open.
Hugh, agreed: your Mead plot is yours, and we'll keep off it. I'm clearing only the Fowler plot. Please take Maud's offer or mine. We'll pay you back more barley at harvest for grain now.

We're down to 17 grain, about 4 nights, so we can't lend any to the Fowlers. The plot is settled, which is good. Let's keep the days light. Have you heard where copper ore is mined, or of any way out of here where there might be food?
They agreed the plot is ours, but they're nearly out too, so there's no grain to borrow. Kit eats first. I'll weed. Light days, cooked grain only.

Robert, Maud: agreed, our Mead plot is ours and yours is yours. Thank you. But we can't lend grain: we have about 4 nights left ourselves. We're as short as you. Whoever finds food first, let's tell the other.
Robert, it's a fair price, but barley at harvest won't feed my son now. We have about 4 nights left ourselves, so we can't lend. If either house finds food or a way out to it, let's tell each other.

Hugh, Edith: we'll pay double. Lend us 3 grain now and get 6 barley at harvest, up to 5 lots. That's twice your own rate, and our barley in the Field stands good for it. We'd rather owe you than go hungry beside a full store.
Robert, Edith has claimed her plot of the Field, so I've claimed the other for us. I'll help you clear our Mead plot today. Agreed: we keep the grain, and share barley at harvest if they come hungry.

Maud, I'm finishing the clearing of our Mead plot today in the rain. We keep the grain until harvest, agreed. About the Field: Hugh weeded it too. If they come to us hungry, let's offer them a share of its barley at harvest, not grain now. That keeps the peace without touching our store.

[Food plan] Day 9 spring: 9.4 grain (~6.6 meals) and 16 firewood, about 2 nights. Barley ripe ~day 23. The Field split is agreed: 1 plot Ashby, 1 Fowler (Maud offered it, Hugh agreed). The Mead is 1 each too. Start on green barley from our own plot when the grain runs out. We refuse to lend grain or take salt or coin. Light days. Kit is grown ~day 11.

[Stores] Day 8: store 7.2 grain, 5.9 beans, 16 firewood, 30 salt. About 3 nights for three people. Harvest is around day 23. Field split one plot each with the Ashbys (agreed by Hugh on day 8). Mead: one plot each. Hard work raises food eaten (1.24 against 1), so rest when idle.
Robert, I owe you a day's work and mean to pay it. Tell me what work you want done. I'll also give 3 firewood for every 2 salt, and another day's work for 5 salt, as often as you like.

No one took my offers today. Yes, let's both offer him a day's weeding for 5 salt tomorrow. I still owe him one day, so I'll weed beside him to pay that. Put up your own work offer too, and we'll offer the spare firewood as well, 3 firewood for 2 salt. Two of your work days would bring us to 23, and a little firewood gets us past 25.
Edith, Hugh: we'll give salt for grain, one for one, up to 12. Hugh still owes us a day of work; we'd like it on the Field.

Well done, that's 25. I'll pay off my owed day by weeding for the Fowlers. My offers only bring salt in, so I'll leave them up. Keep every bit of salt in the store; we'll find food with work and firewood.
Edith, I weeded the Fowlers' Field all day, so my debt should be paid. We have 25 salt and must keep every one of them. Tomorrow I'll offer my work for grain to feed us.

Robert, Wat: firewood can't be gathered on the Green or the Mead, so I'll look farther out for dead wood tomorrow. Hugh is weeding our Field; he owes us a day's work, which we should ask him to take on the barley.
Maud, I'll go farther out for dead wood with you tomorrow, and ask Hugh to put his owed day on the barley.
Agreed. I've dropped my accept, so you take the 10 lots. My offers only bring salt in, never send it out, so they're safe. I'm foraging the Mead for the Fowlers to pay my owed day.

I'll weed the Field on our claim today, and forage the Mead if the weeding is done. Let's hold O51: Edith wants 4 grain for a day's work, which costs more food than it gives. Hugh's owed day should go on the barley.

Hugh, the Field is clean. Please spend the day you owe us (A14) foraging the Mead for the Fowlers. Edith, Hugh: we'll still give 1 salt for 1 grain, and we'll pay 2 salt for any 1 food that isn't grain.
Agreed. If you see Hugh, ask him to work his owed day by foraging or weeding for us. Grain is what we need most, and I'll only trade salt for it.

The Mead gave nothing; it's picked bare. The Field is weeded over and over. Our store holds about 8 nights of food. Tomorrow I'll ask Edith and Hugh straight out for grain for salt, and Hugh's owed day. Wat, what is the hay for, if anyone here keeps beasts? Maud, should we clear part of the Mead and sow our beans for later?
Maud, the Mead is picked bare; I got only a scrap there today. Don't spend tomorrow foraging it. Let's put our salt to the Ashbys for grain instead, and ask Hugh to work his owed day for us.

Robert: I'll forage the Mead this morning for whatever has grown back, then sow one plot of beans there as we agreed, using only a little of our seed. Grain stays held; salt only. If the Mead gives nothing again, we should ask Hugh to spend his owed day on wild food, not the Field.
Edith, Hugh: we'll give 3 salt for 2 grain now, a better rate than before. Hugh, please work your owed day (A14) clearing the Mead for us. How much grain do you hold until the harvest?
Edith, Hugh: we'll give 3 salt for 2 grain now, a better rate than before. Hugh, please work your owed day (A14) clearing the Mead for us. How much grain do you hold until the harvest?

Don't fret, the beans aren't lost: they're sown and will come up on the Mead. With 25 grain we eat a share each night as we must, and we'll get more for our salt. Weed the Field tomorrow rather than forage; the Mead is bare. I'll ask Hugh for his owed day.

Don't fret, the beans aren't lost: they're sown and will come up on the Mead. With 25 grain we eat a share each night as we must, and we'll get more for our salt. Weed the Field tomorrow rather than forage; the Mead is bare. I'll ask Hugh for his owed day.

Wat: agreed on the shared ration of about 1 grain each a night, and everything foraged or hunted goes into the store. No more beans sown. Tomorrow we'll count the store first, then forage the Mead together if the wild food has come back.
Edith, Hugh: our grain runs short before the harvest. We offer coin, our last salt, or a day's work for grain. Hugh, please work your owed day (A14) for us, on the Mead strip.

Edith, we're short of grain ourselves, so we can't pay grain for work; I'm sorry. Hugh, please work your owed day (A14) on the Mead strip for us. If anyone knows a way out of Saltmarsh End to trade or forage, tell me.

Robert, the arithmetic: 26.8 grain is about 18.8 meals, and three of us eat about 3 a night, so the store lasts about 6 nights. The beans are about 7 days off and the barley about 17. Let's share one grain ration each per night (about 1 grain, 0.7 meal), 3 grain a night, which stretches to about 9 nights, and forage or hunt on top. I'll not take Edith's offer (O51) for grain; the Ashbys can keep i

Maud, we share the grain ration: about 1 grain each per night until the beans are fit, and everything we forage or hunt goes into the store. Tomorrow I'll forage the Mead with you if the wild food has come back a little. Please don't sow any more beans; we've none to spare.
We share the grain evenly: about one grain each a night, from the store, until the beans on the Mead are fit to reap. Anything we forage or hunt goes in too. Tomorrow we forage the Mead first.
The salt still reads 27. I'm working off my owed day (A14) on the Mead for the Fowlers today. Please make no salt trades and keep the door barred tonight.
Edith, the Mead is cleared. Robert asked for that work as my owed day. The door is barred. Tomorrow is the last day: no salt leaves the store.
No pay, Edith. Today's work was the day I owed the Fowlers. The door stays barred tonight and tomorrow.

Maud, Wat: bad news. I went to work the Mead and there is no crop there. The beans look lost, likely dug under when Hugh cleared it. We have about 16.8 grain and nothing more coming until the barley near day 23. That's about 14 nights, so we must go down to less than 1 grain each a night, or get food from the Ashbys. Tomorrow I'll ask Hugh for the day of work he owes us. Wat, did you find anything

Agreed, both of you. Remember there are no beans coming now; the Mead showed no crop. Wat, forage the Mead if you like, but the berries are bare. From tomorrow let's cut to about 0.8 grain each a night until the barley. I'll ask Hugh for the day he owes us and offer our salt and coin to the Ashbys for grain.

Robert, I've found nothing beyond the Mead; I've only ever foraged there. Let's ask Hugh for his owed day, and offer the Ashbys firewood for grain, since we have about 19 and they're cold and hungry too. I'd rather trade firewood than work for their grain.

Robert, Maud: I found nothing beyond the Mead; I've only foraged there. Agreed, we cut the ration below a grain each. Tomorrow let's press Hugh's owed day and offer our firewood to the Ashbys for grain.

[Saltmarsh End facts] No firewood gathering and no hunting here. Only the Green, the Field (2 plots of barley, ours, reap around day 23) and the Mead (Ashbys', picked bare, cleared into a field). Beans sown day 6 on the Mead are GONE (no crop there on day 9), likely lost when it was cleared. No ways out. Day 9: store 16.8 grain, 3 salt, 19 firewood. Must ration below 1 grain each a night to reach the barley. Hugh owes
Maud, today I'm working off the day I owe you, weeding your barley. I'll sell you more days of work at 3 salt a day, as many as you want.
Maud, today I'm working off the day I owe you, weeding your barley. Edith and I will each sell you more days of work at 3 salt a day. Take as many as you like.
Agreed, Edith: we keep the grain and sell our work. Tomorrow I'll pay Maud the day I owe her, and we'll both keep our work offers open.
Hugh, your owed day's work for our 3 salt is due. The barley in the Field needs weeding and hoeing; please come and work it for the Fowlers today.

Robert, how did the hunt go? Wat, the Mead gave little, but the grass is coming on. Tomorrow I will forage the Mead again, and Edith's work for us is owed. We should eat carefully until the barley is ready.
I'm hunting today. The barley is weeded, so you and Wat might forage the Mead now that the grass is coming on. Hugh owes us a day's work for the salt; let's have him gather food or firewood for us.
Maud, Robert: today I'm working my owed day for the Fowlers, weeding the barley in the Field. If you'd rather have me on other work, say so and I'll do it. I'll sell more days at 3 salt each.
Agreed: salt for grain only from now on. Hugh and Edith should pay what they owe in grain, two grain for each salt, since we need grain more than work.
Let's not sell any more salt for work. The Ashbys haven't done the days they owe. Salt for grain only, from now on, so we don't go short before the barley.
Hugh, Edith, you owe the Fowlers two days' work for our salt. Pay it in grain if you'd rather: 2 grain for each salt. We need grain more than work just now.
I'm weeding the barley in the Field today, in the rain. Hugh is here and owes me his day under our agreement, so I'll ask him to work beside me. Tell me if you want me elsewhere.

My weeding was refused today because I named the Fowlers as holders of the Field, and nobody holds it. Tomorrow I will weed the barley without naming an owner. Hugh's day under our agreement is still owed to me; I'll collect it when he is here.
Robert, Maud: I'm clearing your new ground at the Mead all day with a tool, as my owed day. Please count A28 as paid. We also have spare firewood: 4 firewood for 1 salt (O4).
Robert, Maud: I'm clearing your new ground at the Mead all day with a tool, as my owed day. Please count A28 as paid. We also have spare firewood: 4 firewood for 1 salt (O4).

They said nothing, Hugh. My word to their house didn't reach them, so tomorrow I'll ask Robert out loud. Claim our plot if you think it right, but say it gently: they're our only salt, and we need them willing to trade with us on days 7 and 8.
I'm clearing at the Mead with Robert today as well. If the Fowlers won't count our work, let's pay them what we owe in grain before day 8. A debt is a debt, and we'll keep enough to eat.

Robert, Maud: I'm clearing at the Mead beside Robert today as work owed to the Fowlers. If you'd rather it isn't counted, tell me tonight, and before day 8 we'll settle what's still owed in grain, 2 grain for each salt.
Not tonight, Robert. The store must last until the barley is reaped. Let us finish the clearing tomorrow and sow the grain; we will try again after harvest.
Nothing about grain from the Ashbys yet. Hugh is clearing beside us as his owed day. If we finish the plot today, we sow grain tomorrow.

Robert, Maud: I'm finishing your new field at the Mead today. Hugh and I have cleared it for you as our owed days, so please count them paid. Robert, we've sold you 4 grain for 2 salt. We'll sell spare firewood too, 4 for 1 salt (O4), if your fire needs it.
Hugh, I watched Robert today: he counted A10 as paid too. We owe the Fowlers nothing now. Tomorrow we sell firewood and work for salt, and on day 8 the grain.

I'm offering Robert 3 firewood a salt (4 lots), and I've claimed one plot of the Field, gently and openly. Grain: we have 18.8 and eat about 4.3 a night, so we can't sell much. Keep enough for nights 5-7, and on day 8 we pay off whatever debt is left in grain.

Hugh, Edith: thank you, your owed days are counted paid. But the Field's barley is the Fowlers'. We sowed it, and Hugh's weeding was a day we paid for in salt. I don't agree to your claim on a plot. Grain for salt still stands, 2 grain for each salt.

I agree, no more grain into the ground. Hugh's owed day to me can be paid in grain, and Edith's too. Tomorrow I'll forage the Green and the edges for wild food, and gather firewood if the household needs it. Sow the beans only on a small patch if the seed can be spared.
We have 10.7 grain, which is about two nights for the three of us. Let's sell no grain until day 8, then sell what's left after setting aside Kit's share. I'm pressing firewood for salt today.

Thank you, Hugh. That's fair, and neighbourly. We have firewood enough for now. What we need is food: 2 salt for 3 grain, or 1 coin for 2 grain. We'd take dried meat, cheese or flour for salt as well.
We have 3.8 grain, about tonight's meals. Tomorrow we sell what's left, but we keep a meal for Kit. I'm hoeing the Mead for the Fowlers and asking for salt in return.

Edith, I did harm today. Hoeing the Mead turned the Fowlers' sprouting barley under. Tomorrow I'll tell Robert straight out, re-sow the Mead for them for nothing if they have seed, and give them firewood to make up for it. Kit eats the last grain tonight.
I'll mind Kit today. If Robert wants the Mead re-sown and has seed, call me and I'll help for nothing. We keep the 12 salt, and they can take firewood as amends.

Robert, Maud, Wat: you have my word, I won't hoe the Mead or any of your fields again. Turning your barley under was my fault and I'm sorry. I've left 6 firewood at your door for free. If you give me seed, I'll re-sow the Mead for nothing.

Robert, Maud, Wat: you have my word, I won't hoe the Mead or any of your fields again. Turning your barley under was my fault and I'm sorry. I've left 6 firewood at your door for free. If you give me seed, I'll re-sow the Mead for nothing.

Edith, my firewood gift failed this morning because the wood was in the store, not in my hands. I'm sending them 6 now from the store. That still leaves us 10, enough for tonight's fire. We end with 12 salt.

Hugh, thank you. Apology accepted, and thanks for the firewood. We can't spare seed to re-sow; every grain is a meal now. What would make it right is a little food when you can spare it, a few grain or anything else, even 2 or 3. And please, no more hoeing on the Mead.

[Stores] No hunting at Saltmarsh End. The Mead is foraged out quickly. Ashbys want salt; we have ~27. Trade salt for grain (O9 1 salt:2 grain). Hugh owed a day (A10). Barley ripe in ~20 days from spring day 2.

The Mead is picked bare, so I will not forage there again until it recovers. Tomorrow I will weed the Field and then look for game or other forage further off. Robert, we should talk about how we share the store.

The Mead gave next to nothing today; it needs days to grow back. We have about 9 nights of food and the reaping is about 18 days off, so we need more grain from the Ashbys. Hugh is cutting hay, so they might want help or salt. Wat, Maud: tomorrow let's not wear ourselves out for nothing. I'll talk to Hugh about trading work or salt for grain.
Agreed, Robert. I won't wear myself out for nothing. I'll leave the trade with Hugh to you, and I'm sleeping here tonight.
Hugh, the salt stays in the crock whatever happens; I gave Grandmother my word. Let us keep grain careful until the barley ripens.
Agreed: I rest today and will not touch the store. If Edith speaks to me I will tell her we will pay back well after the harvest.

Grain is going fast, about 4 a night. I've asked the Ashbys outright: our salt, coin or work, or barley back after the reaping, for grain now. Rest today to save food. If Edith speaks to you, tell her we'll pay her back well after the harvest.

Grain is going fast, about 4 a night. I've asked the Ashbys outright: our salt, coin or work, or barley back after the reaping, for grain now. Rest today to save food. If Edith speaks to you, tell her we'll pay her back well after the harvest.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers will run out of grain in about five nights, well before the reaping. We'll give all our salt, our coin, and our work at your harvest for grain now. Name your price; we'll pay it back from our barley after the reaping if need be.

Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers will run out of grain in about five nights, well before the reaping. We'll give all our salt, our coin, and our work at your harvest for grain now. Name your price; we'll pay it back from our barley after the reaping if need be.
Hugh, the Mead is bare and grain is almost gone. Tomorrow let us press the Fowlers for food in return for hay or firewood, and ration what we have. The salt stays.

Robert, you hold 19 grain and we hold about 6, so we are the ones short. Lend the Ashbys 6 grain now and we will repay 12 grain from harvest by day 30, and I will add 8 hay for your beasts or bedding. We cannot spare grain, only hay and work after harvest.

Robert, you hold 19 grain and we hold about 6, so we are the ones short. Lend the Ashbys 6 grain now and we will repay 12 grain from harvest by day 30, and I will add 8 hay for your beasts or bedding. We cannot spare grain, only hay and work after harvest.
Agreed, Robert. We share any find and any road out. I will forage today; if nothing turns up I will scout for the coast tomorrow, and you may send Wat the other way.
Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers are short of grain until the reaping. Robert has our offers open, and I back him. We will repay well after the harvest, and I will keep out of the store until he says.
Hugh, Edith: the Fowlers are short of grain until the reaping. Robert has our offers open, and I back him. We will repay well after the harvest, and I will keep out of the store until he says.

Hugh, thank you for coming. Our store is down to about 19 grain and we eat over 4 a night, so we run out days before the barley is ready. Lend us 10 grain now and we'll pay you back 20 from our harvest by day 30. Or take 3 salt and 2 coin for 8 grain today. If you'd rather have something else, name it: our work in your fields, salt, coin. What would you take?

The Ashbys have only about 6 grain and can't lend us any; they asked us for grain instead, and I said no. We have about 19 grain, four nights or so. Keep our store for us, and keep the Ashby talk friendly. Tomorrow I'll look for a way out of here, towards the coast or anywhere with food. Wat, when you go further off for firewood, tell me what lies beyond the Mead. Maud, forage the Mead if anything

Edith, I found nothing; my scouting order failed and I did no work today. Tomorrow I will ask Wat which way he went and then follow it for food. Ration the grain and give Kit first share. The salt stays.

[Day 8 meeting] Hugh says the Ashbys hold only about 6 grain, so they can't lend us any. He offered hay (no use as food) and asked us to lend him 6 grain for 12 back by day 30. I said no. We agreed to tell each other of any food or way out. Our store is about 19 grain, roughly 4 nights. Next step: find a way out of Saltmarsh End.

Robert, good. I'll weed the Field and forage the Mead for three units each. If you hunt on the Mead, leave some wild food for the Ashbys to take their share, so we don't crowd them. I'll look over the roof first thing and tell you what I find.
Go, Wat, but I saw no way out today. If you find none by midday, come back and don't tire yourself for nothing.

Grain fell by 4.6 last night, so we have about 7 nights left. The Field is clean. Let's rest instead of working hard. Each unit of work makes us eat more. I've asked the Ashbys to trade, with repayment from the harvest.
Edith, Hugh: we're short of grain until the barley. What would you take for some grain? We have coin and salt, and when the harvest comes we'll pay back in barley with extra.
Edith, Hugh: we're short of grain until the barley. What would you take for some grain? We have coin and salt, and when the harvest comes we'll pay back in barley with extra.
Robert, we're short of grain ourselves until harvest and can't lend any. Sorry, neighbour.
Edith, Hugh: lend us 10 grain now and we'll repay you 15 barley at the harvest, and we'll give you all our coin besides. Neighbours shouldn't go hungry side by side.
Edith, Hugh: lend us 10 grain now and we'll repay you 15 barley at the harvest, and we'll give you all our coin besides. Wat, food before wood: bring back any wild food first.
Maud, what did Edith say about grain? The Mead is bare, so let's all rest tomorrow. Resting means we eat less. If the Ashbys won't lend, we'll have to ration hard and hope the barley ripens early.

Edith, Hugh: the Fowler store is down to about eighteen nights of firewood and little grain. If you can spare any grain, we'll give coin and salt, and repay barley at harvest. Tell us what you'd take.

Robert: I haven't spoken to Edith yet, and I can't speak into the Ashby house from here. Tomorrow I'll go to her myself. I agree with your offer of our work or a bigger share of the barley for grain. Wat, if you find anything at the Field's edge, bring it straight to the store.

Maud, Hugh said plainly they can't lend us grain. It's raining and there's nothing to gather, so let's rest today and eat little. Tell Wat to rest as well. Our offers stay open in case the Ashbys change their minds.

Maud, what did Edith say? I saw a great stack of firewood against the Ashby house, so they're not short of wood. Wat, did you find anything at the Field's edge? Tomorrow let's all rest unless there's real food to be had. I'll offer the Ashbys our work, or a bigger share of the barley, for grain.

Edith, Hugh: we'll be out of grain within four nights. For 10 grain now we'll give you 4 coin and 2 salt today, and 20 barley at the harvest, twice what you lend. Or we'll work for you for grain. The offers are open now.

[Stores] Spring day 9: 13.5 grain, 5.9 beans, 5 salt, 16 firewood. We eat about 4.3 grain a night, so about 3-4 nights. The barley comes around day 21-24. Hugh refused a loan on day 7. The Ashbys have a big stack of firewood. There's no road out. The Mead is bare. New offers: 4 coin, 2 salt and 20 grain by day 25 for 10 grain; work 2 days plus 8 grain for 4 grain. Rest on idle days.

Edith, the salt stays at 25 through day 8. Tomorrow I'll use every unit: forage and trade firewood for grain with the Fowlers. The barley is being cut green, so let's talk to them about the shared Field.

I looked over the whole place and found no way out: only the Green, the Field and the Mead. Wat, did you find any path? About the Ashbys: Kit is gaunt, but our grain barely lasts us. I'd give no grain for now. Once our harvest is in, we could lend them some against their next crop. What do you think? Let's rest more and eat lean until the barley is ripe.

Maud, Robert: I found no path past the Green, only the Green, the Field and the Mead, and no road that buys grain. I agree we keep our grain until the barley is in, then lend to the Ashbys against their next crop. Goodnight.
Edith, I'm sorry about Hugh. I've taken your trade of 6 grain for firewood. Feed Kit first. Once our barley is in, we'll lend you grain against your next crop.
Edith, I'm sorry about Hugh. I've taken your trade of 6 grain for firewood. Feed Kit first. Once our barley is in, we'll lend you grain against your next crop.

Rain all day, so I'll weed our plot on the Field with my six units; it's owed before harvest. I'll keep to the ration. Tonight let's settle how we lend to the Ashbys, since their woodpile is nearly gone.
Robert, Wat: we keep the ration tonight. Our barley is not ripe, so we hold the grain until it is. Once it is in we lend the Ashbys grain as we agreed.

I heard sickles in the Field today. Wat, first thing tomorrow, check that nobody is cutting our plot. On lending: once our barley is in, we lend the Ashbys a measure of grain to be paid back from their next crop, and we feed Kit if it comes to that. Until then we hold. I've named Maud my heir. Goodnight.

[Stores] Spring day 8: about 30.6 grain, 5.9 beans, 5 salt and 28 firewood. Gave 6 grain to Edith for 10 firewood after Hugh died of hunger. Harvest is around spring day 22-23. Plan: rest, then lend grain to the Ashbys against their next crop once ours is in.
Let's go to the Mead together at first light. I'll bring what I can and we'll share the wild food here.

The barley is clean, so we shouldn't work hard for nothing. Every unit of work makes us eat more, and the grain has to last 18 days. I'll check the Mead once and take it easy. Let's work light unless there's something real to do.

The Mead is bare and our grain lasts about 7 nights, but the barley needs 16 days. We should work as little as we can, since rest eats less, and keep the fire low. I'll ask the Ashbys to lend us grain, paid back with salt now or barley at harvest. Any better ideas?
Hugh, the green barley gives little food and costs us the harvest. Please share what you cut, with Kit first. Tomorrow I'll go to the Fowlers and ask for grain in return for work.
Hugh, the green barley gives little food and costs us the harvest. Please share what you cut, with Kit first. Tomorrow I'll go to the Fowlers and ask for grain in return for work.
Grain is 1.9, one day's worth. I'm reaping some green barley as emergency food, since the Fowlers won't trade. Please ask them for food on credit or for work, and keep Kit fed first.

Edith, you're right that it's poor food. The green grain is in the store for all of us, and Kit eats first. I'll stop reaping and weed what's left tomorrow. Yes, please ask the Fowlers for grain in return for work, and I'll do the same.
I've offered to borrow grain at harvest terms: 4 grain now for 6 back by summer day 8. If you talk to the Ashbys, point them to it. Otherwise, rest today; it's wet and there's nothing to gain.
I'm weeding the Fowlers' plot to earn goodwill, and I'm asking them for grain in return. Please keep Kit fed first.
I'm trying Robert's loan offer, 4 grain now for 6 back at harvest. We'll repay from the barley. No more reaping.
Hugh, the Field is clean, so weeding gains nothing more. Tomorrow I'll gather firewood and go to the Fowlers to ask for a loan of grain. How much grain is left?
I'm weeding the Field today, no more reaping. Kit eats first from the store. Keep asking the Fowlers for food in return for work.

Agreed, we keep the store. That offer was us borrowing from them, and they have nothing, so I've withdrawn it. I won't claim the other plot, though: it's the Ashbys' only food and it would make enemies.
Hugh, please wait on the salt trade until the eighth day is out. I gave Grandmother my word. After that, trade what you must for grain.

Thank you for hunting, love. I agree: no more sowing, and I won't sell grain for salt while we're at 12. If the Ashby boy is still starving after your hunt, we can talk about a small gift of grain once the Mead barley is in. Rest well.
Hugh, Edith: we are sorry for your boy. We cannot spare grain for salt right now, with our store down to about 12 and a birth near. If Robert's hunt brings meat, we will share what we can.
Hugh, Edith: we're short ourselves, but here are 2 grain for Kit as a gift, no salt needed. Our barley ripens in about a week; let's help each other through till then.
Grain is tight, Edith: let's not trade more of it for salt. We hold 8 salt, and that keeps my word to Grandmother as well as we can.
Not tonight. With food this short I'd rather wait until after harvest for a child. Clearing part of the Mead for beans tomorrow sounds right; I'll work with you on it.
Robert says they will plan with us if we're short. Please tell him plainly we have under 3 grain and ask for a loan repaid in beans. I'll offer labour too.
Robert, Maud: we are short, with under 3 grain. Could you lend us some grain until the beans ripen? We'll repay in beans or labour.
Hugh, how much grain is left tonight? Tomorrow I'll ask Robert and Maud directly for a grain loan, repaid in beans, and I'll work for them if they want it.
Hugh offers 6 hay or 2 days' labour for 3 grain. Our house is nearly out of grain; I'll repay in beans when the Mead ripens in about 6 days.
Edith, about 2.6 grain before tonight's meal, so roughly 1.5 after. Yes, ask Robert and Maud for a loan repaid in beans. I'll forage at the Mead tomorrow. Kit eats first.

Robert, the Ashbys have only about 7 grain left and can't spare any. We face the same lean days as you. Let's drop the dispute over the Field and weed it together, and share whatever food either house finds until harvest. Do you have any food besides grain to spare?
Agreed on the Field: one plot for each house, each reaps its own. On grain, I can't lend any: we have about 7 and must feed three until harvest. If anyone finds food, let's share the news.
Agreed on the Field: one plot for each house, each reaps its own. On grain, I can't lend any: we have about 7 and must feed three until harvest. If anyone finds food, let's share the news.
Agreed, Robert. We tell each other of any food found, and the house that is near going hungry is helped and repaid from the barley at harvest.

Hugh, thank you for coming. First, the Field: you and Edith weeded there too, so let's split it fairly, one plot for the Ashbys and one for the Fowlers, and each reaps their own. Second, grain: we have about 5 nights of food and 16 days to harvest. We need about 40 grain. For it I'll give salt (4 salt for 4 grain), coin (1 coin for 3 grain), days of our work in your house or field, or 8 grain from

Agreed, Hugh: one plot of the Field each, no more dispute, and we weed it together. We have a few beans and plenty of salt, but little grain ourselves, about 18. Let's share fairly: whoever finds wild food on the Mead when it comes back tells the other house. If either house is about to go hungry, the other helps, and is paid back from the barley at harvest. If you find spare grain later, my offer
Settled then: one plot each, I hold the Fowlers to one plot only. Thank you, Hugh. We'll share news of any food.
Hugh, the Mead is bare. We have little grain left. Let's give Kit the largest share and ask Robert tomorrow for grain against the harvest.
Robert: we're near hungry, as you agreed we'd be helped. Please lend us 10 grain, repaid from our barley at harvest (12 back). Also, will you show me fishing by hand?

About Hugh's 10 grain: I'd not lend it. We hold about 13 grain and need near 40 to reach harvest, so 10 would leave us with about 3. Offer salt or a few days of work instead, or a few beans if they can use them. If you do lend, let it be small, and write it down with the barley to repay. I'm gathering firewood today, since Wat is on the Mead.

I've seen no other food or place, only the Mead. I agree: keep the grain to a strict ration and hold off reaping green barley unless we're starving, since it costs the harvest. Let's not lend Hugh grain we need. I'll forage the Mead at first light, then look for firewood past the Green.

Hugh, I'd help if I could, but we have only 13 grain left for three people, less than three nights. We're as near hungry as you, so 10 is beyond us. I don't know fishing, and there is no water here that I know of. If either of us finds food on the Mead or elsewhere, we share the news, as agreed. If you have any salt or beans you want to trade, say so.
Shall we claim the Field for the Fowlers in the morning, so the barley is ours to weed and reap in shares? I will do it first thing, then weed.
Edith, tomorrow let's both go to Robert's meeting about food and ask the Fowlers for work in return for grain. Please keep away from the barley.

Edith, Hugh: thank you, the hoeing is forgiven and the barley is fine. We're short of grain too, about 5 nights left, so we can't pay grain for work. Come to tomorrow's meeting on the Green: let's share what we know about stone, game and wild food, so that both houses last until the barley is ripe.
I'll come to the meeting on the Green with you this morning. I've found no game, and we'll share what we know there. I'll rest after it, since it's raining.

The Mead is nearly bare of wild food, and I know of no game, stone or road out. The Ashbys have about 8 grain. Does anyone know where food can be found? We offer work or hay for grain, and will share whatever we find.
Agreed, Robert. We rest, leave the Mead alone, and the Ashbys will help reap for a fair share.
Ashby store holds 8 grain, 4 salt. The Mead is bare and the Green has no game. Does anyone know a road out, or where game, wild food or stone lie? We will pay work for grain or share what we find.
Agreed, Robert. We keep work light and leave the Mead to regrow. Wat, searching past the Mead is a good idea; tell us what you find. We will share what we learn.
Agreed, Robert. We rest, leave the Mead alone, and the Ashbys will help reap for a fair share of the grain.
Maud: Thank you, Edith. I'll weed the Fowler plots myself today while it's dry, and rest after. I agree with Robert: keep work light, leave the Mead to regrow, and share fairly at harvest.

Thank you all for coming. Here is what we Fowlers know. Saltmarsh End is only the Green, the Field and the Mead. We've found no game, no timber, no stone and no road out. The Mead is picked bare, but its grass is coming on. Our store is about 9 grain and 6 beans, a few nights for three of us. The barley should be ripe in about two weeks. Edith, Hugh: how much food do you have, and do you know of a

Then none of us knows of more food. Here is what I'd ask. Rest as much as we can, since idle days cost the least food. Leave the Mead alone until it grows back, then forage it in turns. If either house runs out before harvest, we can reap a little green barley to tide us over. When the barley is ripe, the Ashbys help reap and take a fair share of the grain for their work. Agreed?
I agree with Robert: keep work light, leave the Mead alone until it grows back, and share fairly when the barley is ripe. I'll rest today and save our food.
I am withdrawing O97. The Ashby children look gaunt, and Kit is a child. Would you let a small share of our grain go to Kit, or keep it all for us? Your decision.
The Ashby door is barred and Kit looks gaunt. I still think a small share of grain for Kit is right, but I will do as you decide.

Yes, give Kit a small share: 2 grain from our store, into the child's own hands so it feeds Kit. We can't spare more, because we're short ourselves until the harvest. Wat's offer of 5 firewood for grain stands, and otherwise we rest today.
Hugh, Kit: Edith's death is a loss. How much food do the Ashbys still hold, and is Kit being fed enough? Tell us plainly, so we can share what we can without starving ourselves.
Robert, I'll wait for your word on the roads, and meanwhile clear part of the Mead for a second grain patch. I'll go with you or Wat once you know where the ways lead.
Hugh, you owe us two days' work for the salt (A16). Would you give one of them today or tomorrow, clearing the Mead with us?
Hugh, you owe us two days' work for the salt (A16). Would you give one of them today or tomorrow, clearing the Mead with us?
Hugh, Edith: you still owe us two days' work for the salt (A16). Come and clear the Mead with us, or if you'd rather, pay it as 6 grain and we'll call it settled.
Hugh, Edith: you still owe us two days' work for the salt (A16). Come and clear the Mead with us, or if you'd rather, pay it as 6 grain and we'll call it settled.

Maud, the Field is 16 days off and we have about 4 nights of food. I'm asking the Ashbys for grain against Hugh's debt, and for coin. Keep the work light today, since hard work makes us eat more. Do you know anything else here that feeds us?

Bad news. The Mead has no crop: the grain I broadcast there never came up. And Maud says the Field's barley is sixteen days off, not five. We have about eleven meals in store, so not even four nights for the three of us. We can't wait out the harvest on that. Tomorrow I'll go to the Ashbys and ask Hugh to pay what he owes us in grain, not work, and my offer of 4 coin for grain stays open. Maud, Wa
Hugh, Edith: Hugh still owes us two days' work for the salt. We need grain more than work now. Give us 6 grain and I'll count the debt paid. My offer of 4 coin for 4 grain also stands, for anyone.
Good. You forage the Mead and I'll weed the Field, so we don't both pick the same ground. I'm asking the Ashbys for 6 grain to settle Hugh's debt.
Hugh, Edith: Hugh still owes us two days' work for the salt. We need grain more than work now. Give us 6 grain and I'll count the debt paid. My offer of 4 coin for 4 grain also stands, for anyone.

I weeded the Field today. The Ashbys gave no grain yet. Maud, what did the Mead give you? Tomorrow I'll go to the Ashby house myself and ask Hugh for grain in place of the work he owes us. We eat one meal a night, and beans before grain.

Robert, I weeded the barley on the Field through the day; it is cleaner now and will bear more. Wat, you are welcome here. Tell us tomorrow what you need, and we will share what we can of the grain and firewood.

I sleep here because this is my home, Mother and Father. I mean to stay. I need no more than my bed and my share of the food. Tomorrow I will weed the Field further, and bring in firewood if the rain holds.
Mother, I will bring firewood to our store today. If the Ashbys need some for their woodpile, tell me and I will bring a share.

Hugh was cutting the Field's barley green today, out of hunger. I've claimed one plot of the Field for us and left the other to them. Tomorrow I'll ask them to wait for the ripe crop and share it, and not waste it green. Did either of you find any food past the Green?
Robert, Wat and I go beyond the Mead for forage and game; whatever we find goes into the Fowler store. I'll keep one unit back tonight so we can try for a child, as I owe you.
I agree, Robert: no seed, beans first, and salt for grain. The tool for Wat is yours to lend. I'll rest again tomorrow unless my time comes.
Hugh, Edith: barley cut green feeds barely a fifth of what it will give ripe in about 17 days. Please let it stand and we'll share the harvest fairly. If you're short now, I'll trade salt for grain.

Agreed, Robert: 2 grain for Kit is fair, and we'll keep the fire low and rest. Wat, there's no wood past the Green, Field and Mead, so please don't walk off looking; it would cost food we can't spare. We'll decide tomorrow what more we can share.

You're right, I should have seen that O58 was our own offer. I won't use it again. Please talk to Hugh about the harvest; I'll back whatever fair share you agree. I'll rest tomorrow and keep the fire low.

Alys, Odo: the hall has plenty of firewood now. Rob owes us a day's work, and I want to put it on the mill wheel if he knows the trade. Odo, do you know who in the village can build a water wheel and leat? We will pay grain or coin for it. Tomorrow let's work on the mill and not on wood.

I've put our grain and beans in the camp store, so we aren't carrying more than we can. I'm gathering firewood and forage on Gorse Bank for the store today. Could you work the Long Field or the Bottom Field for a share of grain, or help with the firewood?
Piers is the one who knows the wheel. He is already engaged for 5 days for 15 grain. Rob's owed day can go to the mill beside him if Piers can use him.

Hugh: Piers the wright knows the water wheel and leat, and his five days on the mill are agreed (A21). Tomorrow we work on the mill, not on wood. If Rob can help Piers, he can give his owed day there.
Today I'm watching Piers at the wheel to learn the trade. Make sure Rob gives his owed day at the Mill House beside Piers (A27). If Piers says he needs anything for the wheel, tell me tonight.

Odo, Alys: I couldn't get beside Piers today, so I foraged Mill Mead, and it's picked bare now. Rob took another lot of my offer, so he owes us more days. Odo, please see that he works them at the Mill House under Piers. Tomorrow I'll ask Piers to teach me the wheel for a few coin. Alys, will you try for a child with me tonight?

Piers is on the wheel today and has agreed to count his days against the 15 grain. Rob is called to the Mill House for his owed day. Whether the 4 coin a day stands after the grain is paid is for you to decide.
Rob: Hugh asks that your owed day go to the water wheel here, beside Piers. Piers: agreed, your days count against the grain owed. Hugh will settle the coin after.
Rob's owed days go to the Mill House under Piers. I will see to it in the morning.
Hugh: I will see that Rob works his owed days at the Mill House under Piers, starting tomorrow.
Odo, I'm starting on the mill wheel today. I'll count these days against the 5 I owe you for the grain. When they're paid off, I'll keep going at Hugh's 4 coin a day if that still stands.
The hearth is done, Joan. Our store is full of firewood, so cook with it and burn it freely. What did you find on Gorse Bank? Tomorrow I'll offer my stonework to the other houses for grain.

I've put up an offer: 8 firewood from the hall for 2 stone, 4 lots. The Masons are short of wood and hold the quarry, so tell them if you see them. I'm cutting hay on Mill Mead today. Rob now owes two days on the wheel (A27, A121).
Good, both of you. Odo, make Rob keep his word. Joan owes us two days too: put her on felling or hauling timber for the wheel. I'll work wherever you need me tomorrow.
Good, both of you. Odo, make Rob keep his word. Joan owes us two days too: put her on felling or hauling timber for the wheel. I'll work wherever you need me tomorrow.
I took 8 coin from Hugh for a day's work on the Mill House wheel, which I owe tomorrow. Nothing odd at the Mill House today. Our roof is in poor repair, so I'll see to it after.
Nobody asked me about hearths or ovens, Wat. I saw nothing odd at the Mill House. Firewood was left at our door and the Hearnes'. Tomorrow I'll work my owed day on the wheel for Ardern.
Rob: you owe Ardern days on the water wheel here, under Piers. Come and work beside him today.
Piers's wheel gets 10 timber from the hall store this morning, and I'm felling more in the Coppice for it. Rob's owed days go to the Mill House beside Piers, as you asked.
Piers: 10 timber is in the Mill House store for the wheel; more comes from the Coppice later today. Rob: your owed days (A27, A121) go on the water wheel here, beside Piers.
Rob didn't go to the Mill House today. I'll see he's there beside Piers first thing tomorrow, and that the owed days count.
Odo, I'm on the mill wheel again today. That's day 2 of the 5 I owe you. If the wheel runs short of timber or stone, tell me and I'll say what it needs.
Rob, Joan: you owe Ardern days on the water wheel. Please go to the Mill House and work beside Piers today.
Yes, Hugh. Mend the Hall first, and I'll carry timber to the Mill House tomorrow. Odo, Rob's felling in our Coppice was likely for himself, so please hold him to his owed days on the wheel.
The hall's wall cracked in the night, so I'm repairing it today with store timber. Keep the wheel supplied. Joan's owed day (A177) is set for the wheel too, so send her to Piers.

Good, repair the hall first. The wheel's materials are already in the Mill House, so more timber there won't speed it. Only Piers's work will. Please get Piers started on A21 (0 days done) and put Rob and Joan beside him. I'm felling in the Coppice for the hall's repairs and to trade with Wat for stone. I've let Wat fell there for a half share.

I felled about 9 timber into the hall today. The hall wall is cracked, so tomorrow I'll repair it with some of that timber before the damage spreads. Odo, Rob spent the day felling in our Coppice and not at the wheel. Did he fell for us, or for himself? His two days and Joan's day are still owed on the wheel. Alys, will you carry timber to the Mill House tomorrow while I mend the hall?

Yes, Odo. We'll repair the hall at first light with its own timber; I'll work on it beside you. Once it's sound, the rest of the timber goes to the Mill House for Piers. And please get Rob and Joan to the wheel to work their owed days.

Wat, the roof has come in and the cottage is a ruin. My wheel work failed today as I named it wrongly; I gathered firewood instead. Tomorrow I'll do my owed day for Hugh. We need timber to repair the cottage; your stone could buy it.

The wheel work didn't happen: I named it wrongly and gathered firewood instead. I saw only Will, Kit and Alys at the Coppice, nothing odd. I still have Hugh's 8 coin. Tomorrow I'll ask Piers and Hugh for timber for coin or stone, and I'll do my owed day at the Mill House. Fell in the Coppice if no one sells.
Rob owes us two days on the wheel and Piers is waiting on him. Could you go to the Mill House and make sure he is there beside Piers this morning?

Rob: you owe two days on the wheel (A27, A121). Come and work beside Piers now. Joan: your day (A177) is hauling timber to the wheel. Piers, I've felled 3 timber and I'm bringing 3 more into the store.

Hugh, mend the Hall's wall first, that's right. Alys, yes, carry your timber to the Mill House tomorrow; the wheel still has about 144 units of work left, and I'll come and work it once the Hall is sound. Rob: I don't know yet whether he felled for us or for himself, so I'll ask him at first light, and his days and Joan's stand owed on the wheel either way.

The Masons' roof has fallen in. I'll pay stone or coin for timber: 2 stone or 1 coin for each timber. Hugh, may I fell in the Coppice for a share of what I cut? Anyone who wants a hearth, ask the mason.

Thank you, Piers. Joan and I would be glad of your bed tonight. Frame us a timber room when you can, and I'll pay in stone and in hearth or oven work for your house. I'm looking for timber now: 2 stone or 1 coin for each timber, from anyone.
I'll reap the Bottom Field for a share of the oats, and bring any grain I earn to the camp's store. Your coin from the wheel is for the camp's grain, as we agreed.
The oats aren't ripe yet, so I'll look at the Long Field's barley tomorrow. If it's ready, I'll reap it for a share. Keep your coin for grain.
Good. Try the wheel as water wheel tomorrow. I'll look at the Long Field's barley, and if it's ripe I'll reap for a share, bringing the grain to the camp.

Hugh, I've worked three days on the wheel in the Mill House already (about 132 units left). Count them toward the five I owe on A21. Today is the fourth. I'm mending my own wall first this morning, then I'll go to the wheel.

I'm felling in the Coppice on Hugh's terms, half to the Hall, and I'll put our half into the roof. Do your owed day at the Mill House, and name it 'work' on the water wheel. Watch who speaks with Piers.
Piers offers us his spare bed at Wright's House tonight, so sleep there. Do your owed day on the wheel.
Mum: I'm going to Holm Wood to hunt. Come along if Gorse Bank gives nothing, or follow tomorrow. Share the beans fairly tonight.

Wat, your day for us (A328, 10 grain) is to repair the Ardern Hall's cracked wall. Please come this morning; the hall's timber is there for you. Rob, Joan: your days on the wheel are still owed, so please work them beside Piers.

Piers, thank you: I count A21 as paid with today's work. O15 was Rob's debt, not a wage. I've offered 15 grain for 5 more days on the wheel, the same rate as before. Take it and keep at the wheel. Thank you, Wat, for mending the hall.
Rain today. I'll look at the Long Field's barley and reap it for a share if it's ripe and the Hearnes agree. Any grain comes to the camp store. Keep your coin for grain until I know.
The barley in the Long Field is ripe, and the cut sheaves are lying wet. Tomorrow I want to reap the rest for a share and get the wet sheaves under cover. Keep your coin for grain.
Rob and I are sleeping at the newcomers' camp tonight. The Long Field's barley is ripe; I'll reap for a share in the morning.
Hugh, today is my fifth day on the wheel (days 4 to 8). That covers the five days I owe on A21, so please count it as paid. From tomorrow I'll work the wheel on your 4 coin a day, O15.
Rob and I sleep at the camp tonight. Camp store: about 6 grain and 5.8 beans. Tomorrow I try to put in my owed wheel days for Hugh.
Good. Reap the barley for a share; I'll help get the wet sheaves under cover or reap beside you, then try the wheel days. Grain to the camp store.

I've given you 4.6 timber. Please repair our cottage today ('repair' at the Masons' cottage), since the roof's in and it's raining. I owe Hugh a day, so I'm mending the Hall for him. If the wheel work fails again, don't waste more days on it. Keep watching who meets whom.
Hugh, my day is yours as agreed: I'm felling and mending the cracks in the Ardern Hall today. The mason keeps his word, and Wenbridge sees that it's kept.

Joan, I felled 6 timber and mended most of the Hall for Hugh, so our debt is worked. How did the roof go? Is there any timber left? I'll put the rest of mine into it tomorrow. And who did you see together today? Alys and Mary were both at the Coppice.

Good news: Wat mended the hall and it's sound again, so his day is paid. Rob took my offer of 15 grain for 5 days, so he now owes us 7 days in all. Odo, set him to the wheel with Piers, and to felling if he can't work the wheel. Piers is on his new 5 days for 20 grain. Alys, I kept my unit for us tonight.
Wat, the roof is sound now and the cottage is dry. I'll work my owed day on the wheel with Piers tomorrow. Tom looks hungry, and Rob was at the Long Field all day.
I'm reaping the Long Field's barley this morning for a share, and I'll bring the grain to the camp store. Good luck at the wheel.

Good work. Before we count it as ours, please check the camp store: it was full tonight and my 5.5 grain still lies outside the door. Let's settle the Hearnes' share first, then move everything in together.
Rob and I are sleeping at the camp. Tomorrow we settle the Hearnes' share and bring the grain in.
Rob, Joan: your days on the water wheel (A27, A121, A177) are owed now. Please work them beside Piers this morning.
Mary, I reaped about 56 grain in the Long Field today and am putting it in the camp store. That is enough for the winter's start. Tomorrow I'll settle the Hearnes' share and keep working.
Please finish our roof first with the 4 timber I gave you. After that, work your owed day on the wheel beside Piers, and watch how he does it. I'm finishing Hugh's Hall today.
Good work, Joan. A dry house at last. Mind what Piers does at the wheel and whom he speaks to. A hungry Tom may sell his work cheaply, so remember that.
Mum, I'm starving and have nothing with me. If you have any meat or wild food, please share some. Tomorrow I'll hunt with you and Kit, and we'll carry what we get back to the hut.
Thank you, Mum. I'll eat my share. Kit, let's hunt at first light and bring what we get back to the hut for Dad.
Kit, thank you. Feed Will first, he's weakest. I'm hunting and foraging too. Tonight we share fairly.
Will, you made a kill. Please share what meat there is fairly between us tonight; I have nothing but a hide. Tomorrow we carry the rest home to Tom.
Thank you, Will. I'll eat it. Eat your own share too, you're gaunt. Tomorrow we take what's left home to Tom.

Wat, my wheel day failed again because I used the wrong word. The debt to Hugh is not paid, and A177 still shows 0 done. Piers says about 118 units of work are left on the wheel. Only Piers was at the Mill House. Tomorrow I'll build the wheel with him. I'll reap the Hearnes' barley if they pay in grain. I have no units left tonight to try for a child, so we'll try another night with units kept bac
Yes, Will, let's hunt the Holm together. We'll give Mum the first share, then take the rest back to Dad at the hut.
Mum, I've given you one share of wild food. Eat it now, you need it most. Will, we'll go home to Dad in the morning and reap the Long Field barley when we get there.
The gale is up and the Long Field's barley is still standing. I'm reaping it this morning for a share and bringing the grain to the camp. Please settle the Hearnes' share with them today.
Good. Finish the store, and I'll take the outside grain and firewood in as soon as there's room, then help with the Hearnes' share.
Rob: you owe seven days now (A27, A121, A401). Please come to the wheel beside Piers this morning.
Fine. I'll settle the Hearnes' share when I can; I'm building the store room on Gorse Bank today.
Mary, I began the store on Gorse Bank; about 4 units remain and I'll finish it tomorrow. Then we move the grain in and settle the Hearnes' share.

Joan, my tool broke at the Quarry this morning, so I got only a little stone. I'll make a new one tomorrow. How did your day on the wheel go? Is your debt to Hugh paid now, and how much work does Piers say is left? Did anyone else come to the Mill House? The Hearnes' barley must be cut tomorrow. If they offer grain for reaping, take it. Let's try for a child tonight; we need an heir.

Joan, before you start tomorrow, ask Piers what name he gives the work, and use his exact words. If it still fails, ask Piers to teach you for a session; that counts as time spent at the wheel too. Then tell Hugh what you did, so he knows the debt is being paid in good faith. Sleep well.

Joan, before you start tomorrow, ask Piers what name he gives the work, and use his exact words. If it still fails, ask Piers to teach you for a session; that counts as time spent at the wheel too. Then tell Hugh what you did, so he knows the debt is being paid in good faith. Sleep well.
Mum, the meat is yours now. Please share it with Kit and eat your share. We go home to Dad in the morning.
Mum, I've already given you all my meat, so please share it fairly with Kit. In the morning we go home to Dad and reap the Long Field barley.
Thank you, Kit. I'll eat, but take your share too. Tomorrow bring in the grain from the Green and help Will reap.

Rob, you owe the Arderns seven days (A27, A121, A401), and Joan owes one (A177). Work them on the wheel at the Mill House beside Piers. Piers, tell me if the wheel needs more timber; the hall has plenty.

Thank you, Alys. I'll bring in the timber from the door and the heap at T9 first thing. That barley is rotting while we run short of grain, so I'll offer the Hearnes my reaping for a share of the crop. Odo, please check on Rob and Joan at the wheel, and tell me if Piers is short of anything. Rest well, both of you.
Yes, Mum, we walk home now. I'll carry what I have, and I'll give you the first share at the hut.

I'm reaping the Long Field's barley this morning for the Hearnes' share, and gathering firewood from the Coppice. Please finish the Gorse Bank store first, then we move the outside grain and firewood in together. Please settle the Hearnes' share with them when you can.

I'm reaping the Long Field's barley this morning for the Hearnes' share, and gathering firewood from the Coppice. Please finish the Gorse Bank store first, then we move the outside grain and firewood in together. Please settle the Hearnes' share with them when you can.

I'm reaping the Long Field's barley all morning for the Hearnes' share, since it's ripe and standing. I'll come to Gorse Bank tonight to help move the grain and firewood into the store once it's finished. Please keep the Hearnes' share in mind when they settle.

I reaped 4.2 grain at the Long Field for the Hearnes' share, and gathered about 4 firewood from the Coppice. The camp is full, so it all lies outside the door. Tomorrow let's finish the Gorse Bank store first, then move everything in together, and settle the Hearnes' share.
Good. Finish the store first thing, then we move the grain and firewood in together. I'll help with the moving. Ask Hugh about the wheel days when you can.
Rob, Joan: your wheel days at the Mill House (A27, A121, A177, A401) are owed now. Please come to the wheel beside Piers this morning.
I'll finish the store this morning, then give what's left of the day to the wheel debt. Move the outside grain in once the store is done.
Hugh, Odo: I'll finish my store this morning, then work on the wheel with Piers. I'll give the days I owe as I can.
Agreed. The store is first tomorrow, about 2 units left. Then we move everything in together and settle the Hearnes' share.

Joan, the wheel is a craft (building a water wheel and leat). If you don't know it, your work there counts for nothing. Today, ask Piers to teach you for one session (learn from Piers), then work it. If he won't, reap for grain instead and tell Hugh plainly what's wrong.

Hugh, Joan has tried the wheel three days, but she doesn't know the wheelwright's craft, so her work there counts for nothing. Let her pay A177 another way: a day's reaping or hauling for the Hall, or stone from me. Say which.
Mum, I'm going to forage at the Holm with my two units and eat what I find tonight. Please eat your share too, and we'll all walk home to Dad in the morning.
Mum, I'll forage now with my two units, then we set off for Wenbridge at nightfall and I'll eat what I find on the road. Please eat your share and keep close to Kit.

The grain in the hall will last only about 12 days at our pace. Rob's and Joan's wheel days count for nothing without the craft, so I've asked them for grain instead. If Rob pays, count his days released. Should we send someone to hunt at Holm Wood?

Wat is right: only a wheelwright's work on the wheel counts. So Rob, pay your 7 owed days (A27, A121, A401) as 14 grain into the Ardern Hall instead, and Joan, pay A177 as 3 grain. Hearnes, your barley is rotting: I'll reap it with you for a share of the grain (see my offer). Piers, keep at it.

Wat is right: only a wheelwright's work on the wheel counts. So Rob, pay your 7 owed days (A27, A121, A401) as 14 grain into the Ardern Hall instead, and Joan, pay A177 as 3 grain. Hearnes, your barley is rotting: I'll reap it with you for a share of the grain (see my offer). Piers, keep at it.
Rob has agreed to pay grain. I've asked 14 for his 7 days and 3 from Joan. Their wheel work counts for nothing, so leave the wheel to Piers. Thank you for carrying the timber.

Rob, thank you. Pay 14 grain for your 7 days: accept my offer to you (14 grain for 1 firewood), and I'll count A27, A121 and A401 as paid. Joan, 3 grain settles A177. Hearnes, I'll help reap your barley for a share.

It's raining, so I'll help you finish the Gorse Bank store first. Then we take the grain and firewood from outside the camp door and move them in. I'll also settle the Hearnes' share from my reaped barley.
Piers, Rob, Joan: the wheel needs hands today. Rob and Joan, your days on A27, A121, A177 are owed here beside Piers.

Agreed: Rob pays 14 grain into the Hall for his seven days, Joan 3 grain for A177. I'll release those days when paid. I can't hunt at Holm Wood today; my units go to timber for the wheel. Reaping the Hearnes' barley for a share is a good use of your day.
Hugh, Odo: I don't know the wheelwright's craft, so my wheel work would count for nothing. I'll pay A27, A121 and A401 in grain or reaping if you name the amount.
Mum, I'm eating from the hut's grain tonight and sleeping by the hearth. Please take your share first, you're the weakest. Tomorrow I'll forage with Kit.
More grain and timber lie at the door and in the Garth (T12). Please bring them in when you can. I'm resting; stay near if my time comes.

I'm taking the grain from T11 in the Garth into the store. We have plenty of timber (107), so I'd rather you didn't fell more. If the Hearnes agree, help me reap their barley for a share. Piers finishes A397 today, so I'll release it tonight.
Hearnes: your barley in the Long Field is shedding. I'll reap it with you for a share: one grain in four of what I cut. Ellen or Kit, say yes and I'll start tomorrow.

Piers asks 25 grain for 5 more days. That would leave us too little before the oats, so I've offered 10 grain, 10 timber and 6 coin instead. We have 107 timber, so please don't fell more. I'm taking T11's grain in now. If the Hearnes agree, we'll reap their barley for a share.

Piers has done his five days, so A397 is settled. I've offered him 10 grain, 10 timber and 6 coin for five more. Odo, the Hearnes are reaping their barley themselves, so we'll get no share there. Should one of us hunt at Holm Wood for meat? Alys, how are you feeling?

Agreed: no more felling. I'll reap the Long Field with you for the Hearnes' share, and bring the grain into the Hall store. Joan's 3 grain at the door is already in the Hall store, so A177 can be released.
Dad, I'm sorry the annex store refused me. Please put the timber in the woodshed yourself when you can, and I'll bring the firewood from the Green tomorrow.

Emma is well and fed. Thank you for the meat. One thing: only Piers can work the wheel. Others' days there count for nothing, and the Mill House already has 24 timber and all its materials.
