We have over 100 timber in the Hall too. Food is what we lack: about 50 grain for four of us, and the oats won't ripen. Better to hunt Holm Wood again, or sell timber for grain.
Wat, stone has been left at our door again. Take it in to the store when you can. I've put my firewood in the store. Goodnight.

Mary took O866, the 2 grain and 4 timber for a day's work, so she owes us a day. I've withdrawn it. I'll settle with Piers face to face instead. Odo, thank you for minding Emma. I brought in 7.5 timber. Tomorrow I'll mind her again.

Rob: I've moved the camp's timber into the Newcome store under cover, and I've accepted Hugh's offer of 4 timber and 2 grain for one day's work, which I'll owe him. Shall I work the hall garth with you, or should we build beds with your 6.6 timber?

Rob: a gale is coming, so we sleep in the Newcome store tonight. The 15 timber is under cover there now. Tomorrow I owe Hugh a day's work under A923, so I'll do that in the morning, then check the beds and woodshed with you.
Agreed, Rob. Tomorrow we bring the firewood and straw from the door in, then build beds. I'll still owe Hugh a day's work under A923.
Piers: the new offer of 2 grain and 4 timber for a day's work is for you alone, for the mill wheel. Take it this morning. Others, please leave it; Mary, you still owe us a day from the last one.
Thank you, Wat. I'll rest. If you reap Hugh's oats, take your share in grain straight to our store.

Rob: I'm taking the firewood and straw from the Gorse Bank bundle into the Newcome store now. I still owe Hugh a day's work (A923), so I'll go to the Mill House wheel after this. Please build the beds with the straw when it's in.
I'll sleep at the Hall tonight and bring more firewood from the Coppice in the morning for the far end, which is cold. Please check the grain count when you can.

The Hall has a hand mill now. Tomorrow I'll spend the day grinding our grain into meal, which feeds more. Odo, could you mind Emma tomorrow? Tom took the offer meant for Piers, so the Hearnes owe us a day; I've closed it. Grain is getting short; let's eat beans first.

Wat, I couldn't repair the Hall, because it is stone and needs a mason's craft. Can you show me stone walling or quarrying? Did you get any grain? I owe Hugh a day's work and will ask him what he wants done. Goodnight.
Dad, my 1.4 timber goes into the hut store now. I'm felling at the Coppice today for the woodshed and to pay back what I owe you.
Good timber today, 7.3 felled. Tomorrow I repair the Ardern Hall to pay Hugh the day I owe for his grain and timber. Keep the door barred. Goodnight.

The Arderns have no grain left. We'll trade timber or coin for grain, beans or any food: see our offers. Wat, the books show your day for A1029 still owed; if you mended the Hall, I'll see you're paid fairly. We can pay in timber. Piers, we can't spare grain now. Would you take 6 timber a day for the wheel?

Piers, Tom took O1023, and he owes us that day. You worked anyway, so here are 4 timber now; I'll pay your 2 grain once we have any. We have no grain at all, so we can only pay in timber or coin. Anyone with food: we'll trade timber or coin for it.
Hugh, I owe the Arderns a day (A1029). The Hall is stone and I can't mend it, so I'll gather firewood for you instead. Please pay the 2 grain to the Masons' store.

The Hall's grain is at 0 now; only beans (about 28) are left in the store. I'll eat beans only and count every meal. I'm minding Emma today and repairing the cracked wall with timber. Please check the grain count against Wat's 5 grain he is owed.

Hugh, O1023 was gone before I could accept it yesterday; someone else must have taken it, since it was open to anyone. I still did two builds on the wheel (about 66 units left now), unpaid, so you owe me 2 grain and 4 timber for that day. To stop this happening again, I've put up my own offer: a day of my work for 2 grain and 4 timber, up to 3 days, paid when you accept. Accept it for the Arderns
Today's work was lost to a refused plan. Tomorrow I repair the Ardern Hall to pay Hugh my owed day, then fell timber. Keep the door barred. Goodnight.

Hugh, yes: 6 timber a day for the wheel suits me. I've put up an offer: work 1 day for 6 timber. Please accept it this morning and I'll do two builds on the wheel today. You still owe me 2 grain for yesterday's day, whenever you have grain again.
Repairing the stone Hall is refused me, so I lost the day. Tomorrow I repair the Mill House for Hugh's debt. Kit and Will, keep felling and put timber in the annex. Goodnight.
Joan, I'm sorry about Wat. I've taken your offer, 8 coin for 4 grain, and left 2 more grain at your store as a gift for you and Hamo. Ask me if you're short again.
I repaired Wright's House today because the Mill House was sound. Tomorrow I'll ask Hugh what work counts for my owed day. We need food: we have about 10 meal. Keep the door barred. Goodnight.
Kit, carry the door wood to the annex first. Then you and Will go to Holm Wood to hunt and forage for meat or wild food. I'll see Hugh about my owed day and look for grain. Goodnight.
I fenced the Bottom Field to about 59 parts in a hundred. I'll finish it tomorrow for my owed day. Ellen, we should make the meal last until the boys return from Holm Wood. Goodnight.
Piers asked about Wright's House: I repaired it because it was cracked and I thought it might count toward my owed day. The timber and stone heap on the Green is not mine.
Hugh lies dead here with beans and coin beside him. I won't touch them. In the morning, before we go, let's bury him. Does anyone have food to share tonight?

Kit, Will, I'm here to hunt with you. Tomorrow we hunt and forage together and share what we get. Piers, did you take a kill? Hugh lies dead here; his coin and beans should go to his kin, the Arderns.
Let's share one fire tonight. I'll help bury Hugh in the morning, then we hunt before going home.
Will, I'm out here hunting too. If you have a fire or camp tonight, could I share it? I'll bring meat or 2 timber for the fire.

I'm lighting a fire with my timber tonight, and anyone may share it and cook by it. Kit, I've given you a little meat; you look worn. Hugh lies dead in the Holm. Does anyone know how it happened? Someone should tell the Arderns and see him buried.
Piers, I have only 0.4 timber and no fire yet. If you bring meat or wood, we can share one tonight.
Ellen, welcome. Has anyone food to share tonight? Piers, if you and Kit bring wood to my 0.4 timber, we can light one fire and sleep together. Tomorrow we bury Hugh before we go home.
Thank you for the food, Kit. I'll share what I get tomorrow.
Tom, I'm starving. I'll give 3 coin for a share of your meat, or work for it. Anyone with food to spare, I'll pay.
Thank you, Tom, for mending Wright's House. Tell me how much timber you used and I'll pay you back from my store when you're home. I'm walking to Wenbridge in the morning.

I only killed 0.7 meat and gave it to Kit for the boys; Kit, share it with Will. Alys, Joan: I've nothing to spare, I'm sorry. Hugh is buried here this morning. We bury him first, then walk home together.

Hugh is buried. His coin, beans and crude tool lie at the Holm, and they are for his kin. Alys, will you take them, or shall we carry them to the Ardern Hall tomorrow? I have 0.4 wild food and 2.8 firewood to share tonight.
Will, I'm foraging the new greens at Holm Glade with my two units and will share what I find with you tonight. We walk home to the hut store in the morning.
I'm sorry for Alys and Joan. I'm foraging Holm Glade now, and I'll share the wild food tonight with whoever is starving. Tomorrow we walk home.
Agreed. I'm going home now. Bring the boys when you can.
Kit, I'm walking home to the hut now for the meal and fire. Follow with Will and Ellen when you can.
Kit, I'm walking home with Dad now, since the meal is at the hut. Keep your greens and share them with Mum. I'll see you at the hut.
Mum, I've had only a little wild food since the Holm. Is there meal in the hut store I can eat tonight? I'll repay it with work tomorrow.
Rob, Hamo is weak. Let's take him to the store tonight, feed him and keep him by the fire. I think we should take him into our household; I'd like your word on that.
Yes, Mary: Hamo may come to the Newcome store and share our fire and food tonight. Our grain is thin, so we decide on the household tomorrow.

Ellen, Kit: I'll weed the Long Field tomorrow, since it's ours and it's where the household's grain comes from. I still owe nothing and am owed nothing, so I'll eat from the hut's meal tonight if there's enough.
Share what wild food we have tonight. Tomorrow I'll go door to door offering timber for grain, and we may have to hunt at Holm Wood.
Will, I'd come with you to the Holm, but I've no food for the road and it's a night out there. If Mum gives us a share for the road, I'll come. Otherwise bring back what you can.
Mary, we Hearnes are starving. We have plenty of timber and firewood in the annex. We'll give 2 timber for 4 grain, any number of lots. Please trade or lend grain.
Thanks, Piers. I'll share your fire and cook my 2 meat on it. Wenbridge is hungry: Hamo died, the Masons are starving, and Alys lies dead here at the Holm.
Mary, I am starving. I'll give my 0.4 timber for grain from the Newcome store, or take a little as a gift if you say so. I won't take it without your word.
Mary, I am starving. I'll give my 0.4 timber for grain from the Newcome store, or take a little as a gift if you say so. I won't take it without your word.
Mary, I am Ellen of the Hearnes and we are starving. Please give or lend a little grain; I'll pay in timber, 2 timber for 3 grain, from our annex of 36 timber, or work for you after.
Rob, I'm staying one more day to hunt and will build a fire of dead wood tonight. Share it again if you stay, and we'll walk back together tomorrow morning.
Rob, I'm Ellen of the Hearnes and I'm starving. Please give or lend a little grain from the Newcome store. I'll pay in timber, 2 for 3 grain, from our annex, or in work, as you choose.
Piers, I carry no firewood, sorry. I'll hunt here at the Holm tomorrow and can't go north yet. If I get meat, I'll share the fire.
Thank you, Piers. I have 1.4 beans and a little wild food; let's boil the beans at your fire and share. Tomorrow I go home to Mary.

[Mill plan] Emma was born on autumn day 5. Care for her daily (1 unit); she is grown about winter day 15. WINTER DAY 6: no grain left, beans 28.6 (about 4 nights). Food comes first: trade timber or coin, hunt at Holm Wood. Piers now posts his own offer O1130 (a day's work for 2 grain and 4 timber); accept it only when we have grain. I gave Piers 4 timber for the winter day 5 day and still owe him 2 grain. Tom

[Owed back] Mary (the Newcomes) owes us 1 day's work (A923, from O866). Tom (a Hearne) took O1023 on winter day 5 meant for Piers: he owes us 1 day's work, or should return 2 grain and 4 timber. Wat's A1029 shows 0 done, but he repaired the Hall on winter day 4. Offers to 'anyone' keep getting taken by the wrong person: post Piers's only when he is about to accept, and close it at once.

[Owed to Odo] Ellen (Hearne) starved on the night of summer day 2. Someone lies at Mill Mead. Hugh, Alys and Joan are dead at Holm Wood; Hamo starved at the Masons'. Odo heads the Arderns and is gaunt; Emma is gaunt. Alys said A1187 counts as done. Don't build on the wheel without grain paid first; about 56 units left. Store on summer day 3: 2.2 grain, 0.7 beans, 10.7 timber, 1.1 firewood, 8 coin. I owe Tom the
Could you lend us an ox to turn the millstones? We'd pay in flour or bread.
I'm off to the wood to forage and gather firewood. Could you see whether the Crofts will lend us their ox to turn the stones? We'd pay them in flour or bread.

Good. Look for them in the morning. Offer them flour, or a share of the milled grain, for a day of the ox. If they want more, I'll go as high as a quarter of what we mill. I'll stay close to the Green so I can join in.

Hugh, Mabel: this is Walter at the mill. Will you lend us an ox for a day or two to turn the millstones? I'll pay 6 flour a day, or mill your grain for you for nothing. Come to the Mill House and we'll settle it.

Hugh, Mabel: this is Walter at the mill. Will you lend us an ox for a day or two to turn the millstones? I'll pay 6 flour a day, or mill your grain for you for nothing. Come to the Mill House and we'll settle it.

Hugh, Mabel, Crofts: Walter of the mill here. Lend us one ox for a day to turn the millstones and I'll give you 5 bread. Or bring your grain and I'll mill it for you for nothing while the ox is here. Come and find me at the Mill House.

Hugh, Mabel, Crofts: Walter of the mill here. Lend us one ox for a day to turn the millstones and I'll give you 5 bread. Or bring your grain and I'll mill it for you for nothing while the ox is here. Come and find me at the Mill House.

The fence is past half, and two more days should finish it. Kit, you did well with the herd. Keep them on Long Pasture tomorrow and help at the fence after. You're my heir now. Mabel, if Walter still hasn't paid the bread, we lend him no more oxen until he does.

Joan, Hugh lent us an ox and I left him the 5 bread. But milling takes 20 units, more than a day's work, so I couldn't start. Could you work the stones with me tomorrow, if the ox is still here? Then we could get a batch of grain milled between us. I'll ask Hugh if we can keep the ox a few more days. I've also named you to head the household after me.
Please ask Joan today whether we may keep some barley in the Mill House hall after the harvest. We could pay with a day's work or some grain.
Thank you, Mabel. Walter kept his word, so I'll lend him an ox again on the same terms: bread first, or paid the day it's used. I'll settle it with him tomorrow.
Thank you, Mabel. Walter kept his word, so I'll lend him an ox again on the same terms: bread first, or paid the day it's used. I'll settle it with him tomorrow.
Joan, Walter: may the Thornes keep some barley in the Mill House hall after harvest, for a day's work or grain? Walter, Edwin's offer O196 of 8 grain for your 6 stone is open to accept.

Walter, thanks for the bread. I'm willing to lend you the ox for 3 days for 6 bread. The trouble is that when I drive one ox, the whole herd goes with it, and last time they grazed your Brook Mead. If you'll take the herd by your house and keep them off your meadow, we'll do it once the West Field fence is done.
Hugh will lend the ox for 3 days for 6 bread, once the West Field fence is done. I'll tell you the day and we'll work the stones together.
A calf was born on Long Pasture last night. See that she and her mother are well, mind the herd, then come and help me fence. We'll lend Walter the ox once the fence is done.
A storm is coming. If the barley is near ripe, we should reap before it flattens it. Tomorrow I'll work Walter's owed day at the Mill House, unless you need me reaping.

Joan, no luck hunting again, though I have a weapon now. Agnes took our 5 bread for a day's work, so she owes us a day. Perhaps she can help at the stones. The ox comes tomorrow and a storm is blowing in. We'll both work the stones all day.

Work Walter's owed day at the Mill House today. We'll reap once the ears are ripe, likely in a day or two, and I'll want you with us then. Please remind Walter that our barley goes in his hall at 1 in 10.

Hugh, I've given you the 6 bread for the ox, summer days 3 to 5. Please bring it to the Mill House now, and any grain you want milled free. Agnes, please work off the day you owe us today, at the stones with us.
Walter, I'm at the Mill House working off my owed day today. Tell me if you want other work. Our barley goes in your hall at 1 in 10 once reaped, in about 2 days.

Reaping went slowly; I got 6 grain with the crude tool. Tomorrow I reap again; the rest of my fallback was wasted on weeding. We should send 1 grain in 10 to Walter's hall once it is in, and I still owe the Millers a day.
Walter, Mabel: I'm leaving 49 Thorne grain in your hall as agreed, 1 in 10 to you. Please grant us the store, and I'll work off my owed day soon.

A second calf, good news. Kit, keep minding the herd on Long Pasture tomorrow until the Thornes' barley is in. I couldn't hand an ox to Walter; there's no way to give one beast alone. I'll pay him back some of his bread in beans or work. Felling by hand is slow, so we need a tool. Goodnight.
Good work, Walter. I'll grind meal at the hand mill first thing tomorrow. Please take in the Thornes' barley and keep their share apart from our grain.

Morning, Joan. Agnes left 79 more barley with us. It's the Thornes': 1 in 10 is ours, so about 8 grain. Count it apart. Our own food is the beans (Hugh gave them to us), the flour, meal, bread and a little grain. Grind only our share. I'm foraging and cutting hay on Brook Mead. Could you dry meat if anyone has some, or trade for cheese? Please withdraw O53.

Edwin, Walter said nothing to me about the tenth or rye. I did spread dung on the East Field three times, taking it from Long Pasture. Tomorrow I'll ask Walter what work he wants to settle my day owed.

Walter, what do we owe you as the tenth on the Thorne grain in your hall? Tell me the number and I'll pay it from the hall. The 45 grain from T7 is yours if it was yours. And has any household rye seed? We'll trade barley or beans for it.

Walter, what do we owe you as the tenth on the Thorne grain in your hall? Tell me the number and I'll pay it from the hall. The 45 grain from T7 is yours if it was yours. And has any household rye seed? We'll trade barley or beans for it.
Walter, I dried the meat into 1 dried meat, but my hunt caught nothing. Tomorrow I'll hunt again, or grind our own share if you prefer.
Walter: what work do you want from me for my owed day? The Mill House is sound. Also, what tenth do the Thornes owe on the grain in your hall, and has anyone rye seed?

Walter named the tenth as 16 grain and I've paid it from the hall. There's no rye. Ask him what work he wants for your owed day, then come and clear building ground at the East Field edge with us if you're free.

Walter, thank you. I've taken 16 grain from our share in your hall and given it to the Millers as the tenth, so we're square on storage to date. No rye anywhere, it seems, so we'll sow barley in spring.

I got only 1.2 grain a unit today. The rest of the barley is rotten and lying flat, so it's barely worth reaping. Tomorrow I'll reap a little more, then fell timber. Agnes, Walter wants hay cut on Brook Mead for your owed day, so that settles it. Tom, how did you two fare? If it was poor for you as well, let's call the harvest done and ask Hugh or Walter for building ground at a field edge for the

Thank you, Edwin, the tenth is paid and we're square. Agnes, for your owed day, please cut hay on Brook Mead for the Millers, any day that suits you. Hugh and Mabel, we have hay for your beasts this winter: 8 hay for 5 beans, or for milk or cheese.

Joan, I cut 5 hay, and Agnes was cutting on the Mead all day, which I think is her owed day. Did her hay come into our store? How much meal did you grind? Let's keep our own grain for eating as grain now, since we have plenty of meal. Tomorrow I'll gather firewood or cut hay, whichever you think we need more.
I'm cutting hay at Brook Mead for Walter today to settle my owed day.

Edwin, the Thornes may build a small store room on a corner of Long Pasture, by the Green. In return, give 2 days' work on the Long Pasture fence; I'll hand you timber for it. Keep the gate shut. Walter, we'll take your hay as soon as we have room to store it.

Walter, I cut only 1.2 hay with bare hands. I haven't seen Agnes's hay come in; count the store hay in the morning. If she's cutting the Millers' Mead beyond her owed day, ask her about it. A copper or crude tool would help us both.

Agnes, you cut hay on Brook Mead yesterday. Was that your owed day for the Millers? None of it has come into our store. Please bring it to the Mill House and I'll count your day as done. Hugh, our hay is yours at 8 hay for 5 beans whenever you want winter fodder.

Joan, my crude tool gave out today, so I'll make a new one in the morning. Agnes was cutting on Brook Mead again. If she's taking our hay for the Thornes, that's a lot more than one owed day. Did any of her hay come into our store? How much did you cut?

Agnes, we're building on the Long Pasture corner Hugh gave us, not the East Field. Deliver the hay, then help me with Hugh's fence; we owe 2 days on it. Tom, good, finish the field, then clear the corner with the tool.
Walter, I've put 11 hay into the Mill House store for my owed day. Please count it.
Good. Finish the field, then clear the corner. I'm doing Hugh's fence today so we work off what we owe him.
Walter counted my owed day as paid. The corner needs about 12 more units of clearing; tomorrow all three of us finish it, then we build the room.
Joan, I'm making a crude tool this morning and putting it in the store for you. Take it and cut hay on Brook Mead. Agnes's 11 hay pays her day, and I'm counting her debt paid.

Walter, I can't lend you one ox: the herd only moves together and can't go indoors. I'm giving you 15 grain now. Please grind it to meal at your hand mill, keep 3 meal for your work, and bring 12 meal back to Croft House.

Hugh, thank you, but I felled my own timber for the wall. The millstones need an ox, so lend me one for a day and I'll mill your grain free, as we agreed. Without an ox I can grind your grain into meal at the hand mill if you bring it to the Mill House.

Walter, yes please: mill the Thorne grain in your hall into flour, keeping 1 in 10 for the milling, and keep the flour in the hall for us. Tell me what tenth is owed for the storing, and I will settle it.

[Debts] No debts. The Thorne Store (timber small room with bins) on the Long Pasture corner is finished as of winter day 3, with 50 grain in it. Thorne House keeps about 56 grain. The Mill House hall holds about 150 Thorne grain.

[Plan] Hand mill BUILT in the Mill House (summer day 6), with 2 stone bought from Edwin for 2 bread. Grind meal there with no ox needed: make grind. Millstones still need an ox given to the Millers outright, and Hugh hasn't done it; the 6 bread paid for ox days brought nothing, so ask for it back. Agnes left grain at our door on summer day 6: Thornes' barley to store at 1 in 10. Take it in (take, 1 unit)

[Stone] Brookend's layout: the Green in the middle; the wood and Long Pasture to the north; the East and West Fields; Brook Mead and the Brook to the south. I found no stone source and no road out. Stone only comes by trade (Edwin and Hugh are buying it too). Early-spring foraging gives about 0.2 a unit, not worth it. Hugh paid 6 meat for his cattle grazing Brook Mead and lent the last ox for the millston
Walter, you can have an ox to turn your stones. In return, mill the Crofts' grain for free and give us 2 flour for each day you keep the ox. If you agree, I'll bring it to the mill tomorrow.

Hugh, Walter said this morning that he will mill our grain for free if the Crofts lend him an ox to turn the stones, and that anyone else's grain goes at the usual share. He also offered 5 flour for 7 grain. I did not hear anything about your offer, so ask him yourself tomorrow.

Hugh, Walter said this morning that he will mill our grain for free if the Crofts lend him an ox to turn the stones, and that anyone else's grain goes at the usual share. He also offered 5 flour for 7 grain. I did not hear anything about your offer, so ask him yourself tomorrow.
The stones need a Croft ox to turn them, so don't waste the day at the mill unless they lend us one. The wood's a better bet.
The mill's ready. Crofts, if you lend me an ox to turn the stones, I'll mill your grain for free, and anyone else's at the usual share. You can also trade 7 grain for 5 flour with me.
The mill's ready. Crofts, if you lend me an ox to turn the stones, I'll mill your grain for free, and anyone else's at the usual share. You can also trade 7 grain for 5 flour with me.
Joan, Edwin traded us 14 grain for 10 flour. Tomorrow I'll go to the Crofts about borrowing an ox so we can turn the stones again. Do you know which of them heads Croft House?
Hugh offered an ox for our stones, and he'll bring it to the mill. In return we mill Crofts' grain free and give 2 flour per day he keeps it. I think we should accept. I'm in the wood for firewood.

The 20 grain is already at the mill. The herd is back on Long Pasture with the bull, which is where it should be. Driving moves the whole herd, so Walter can take an ox from the pasture. Watch the store for the flour he owes us.

Joan, the mill ran well: 64 flour, and I paid Hugh his 2. We have about 85 flour and 25 grain now. Hugh left 20 grain this morning, and I think it's the Crofts' to be milled free, so we owe them that flour back. Tomorrow I'll ask him, and I'll look for grain to trade so we can make 100 flour and fire the oven. Could you keep foraging? The wood is getting thin, so maybe try Brook Mead.
I reaped about 27 grain today, bare-handed, since my tool didn't serve. The field must be cut tomorrow or lost. Does either of you have a tool to lend? Let's all reap again from first light.
Yes, Walter, I'll reap the Thornes' barley with you tomorrow for a share in grain. Hugh did take my 20 hay, but nothing came back yet; I'll ask him for grain when I see him.
Joan, the Thornes' barley must be cut tomorrow or it's lost. Let's both help them reap and ask a share in grain; that may get us our 64. Did Hugh take any hay?
No grain from Edwin yet, Joan; he was busy reaping. Tomorrow I'll reap beside them and ask for a share. Make sure Hugh pays the 10 grain for that hay; ask him plainly.

The Millers' 8 grain was paid when I took Walter's offer, and that was one day's work for their household. We never hired Joan, so we owe her nothing unless Walter says she was working that day for us. I'll ask him in the morning, and ask where her sheaves went. Let's all reap again tomorrow.
Hugh, I gave you 20 hay yesterday; please pay the 10 grain or 10 beans. Edwin, Agnes: I'll reap your barley today for a share in grain.
Walter, I reaped about 38 grain on the Thornes' plots, and Hugh paid 10 beans for the hay. Tomorrow, with rain coming, let's ask Edwin for our share and mill what we get.
Yes, Father, I'll reap all day and store the grain tonight. Joan says she's reaping for us too, for a share, so we may owe her as well.
Yes, Father, I'll reap all day and store the grain tonight. Joan says she's reaping for us too, for a share, so we may owe her as well.

I reaped about 24 grain and put it in the store. My crude tool wore out on the last stretch, so I'll make another soon. Is any barley still standing? If there is, I'll reap it first thing tomorrow. The fence looks half done now. Did someone else work on it? And Joan reaped for us today too, so we owe her a share.

I reaped about 24 grain and put it in the store. My crude tool wore out on the last stretch, so I'll make another soon. Is any barley still standing? If there is, I'll reap it first thing tomorrow. The fence looks half done now. Did someone else work on it? And Joan reaped for us today too, so we owe her a share.
Reap the East Field with me today, on the Thornes' plots, and ask Edwin for 8 grain for the day. If you see Hugh, ask him plainly for the 10 grain he owes for the hay.

Edwin, Agnes: Joan and I are reaping your East Field barley with you today so none is lost. All we reap is yours. In return, please give us 8 grain each for the day's work (that's offer O466), or 1 part in 8 of what we cut. Any of your grain I'll mill at our stones for 1 part in 8.

Well done on the beans, Joan. The 38 grain you carry is the Thornes', though. First thing tomorrow, take it to Edwin, ask 8 grain for your day like he paid me, and give him the rest. Then we offer to mill their barley for 1 part in 8. Keeping their grain would cost us their trust and the milling.
Edwin, Agnes: I'm giving the 36.5 grain I reaped to Thorne House, and I'm reaping again today for the day I owe. We'd still like to mill your barley for 1 part in 8.
Hugh, Joan gave you 20 hay yesterday and is owed 10 beans or 10 grain. We have about 51 beans in the store and can spare 10 beans for her. I'm baking bread at the hearth today and resting.
Thank you, love. I'll bake one loaf at the hearth and rest the rest of the day. Please pay Joan's 10 beans when you can.
Yes, Father. Tool first, then I'll reap until dark. Remember that Walter's 15 grain is still at our door.

Edwin, Agnes: last night I left the 15 grain I reaped at Thorne House's door. Take it in before the rain spoils it. Today I'm reaping your barley again for the day I owe you, and all of it goes to you. If you have grain to mill, our stones will do it for 1 part in 8.
Good, Joan. Give Edwin the 26 in his hand so it isn't lost at the door. Ask him for a share for your day, and offer to mill: 1 part in 8, or flour for grain. Everything we earn goes toward our 64.
[Owed back] Spring day 7: I put the 3 timber back on the Green (bundle T1), so that's settled. Using the crude tool, I cut about 3 timber a day.

Odo, Alys: Rob owes us a day's work for 3 coin. I want to put hands on the mill wheel. Do either of you know who in the village can build a water wheel and leat? The Wrights, maybe? We have 20 timber and plenty of coin to pay with.

Yes, please go to Piers at first light and put him on the wheel. Rob took my offer as well and owes us a day, so I'll set him to the mill too. Do you know whether Piers or anyone else actually knows how to build the wheel?

Piers did not work the mill today, so the day we paid 6 grain for is still owed. I will remind him in the morning. If you want the wheel started early, tell me now and I will go to him at first light.
Piers of the Wrights is the one who knows the wheel; he is owed the day we paid for, so I will ask him to come tomorrow. Rob's day can go to the wheel as well, paid in coin as you say.
Hugh: the Wrights' man is Piers, who said he knows the wheel and is owed a day by us. Rob owes us a day too. Tomorrow I will send both of them to the mill wheel first thing.

Hugh: agreed, ask the Masons for stone or a share for the timber. For beds we need straw, and that comes from the reaped grain. Until then hay will do for bedding, and I'll keep cutting it at Mill Mead.

Piers, Rob: the day each of you owes the Arderns is to be worked on the mill wheel at the Mill House, today if you can. Piers, I will pay 3 coin a day for every further day on the wheel, so take my offer.

Odo, Alys: Piers worked the wheel today, and from tomorrow I pay him 3 coin a day. Joan was felling timber in our Coppice for the Masons. Dead wood is free to all, but felled timber is ours, so I'll ask the Masons for a fair return, maybe stone or a share. The Hearne hut is crowded and Kit has shelter at the Mill House. Can we get straw for beds?
Good, Odo. Check the wheel first, then cut hay. Rob still owes his day on it.
Piers and Rob: the lord's mill wheel waits on the day you owe. Come to the Mill House this morning; Piers, you are paid for one day on it.
Piers took 3 coin for one more day on the wheel. Please check that Rob works his owed day there too. I'm felling timber in the Coppice today.
I saw Piers on the wheel yesterday, so I've marked his grain day A33 as paid. Today counts for the coin day. Rob still owes his.
Odo, Alys: I brought in 9 timber today. Joan has felled in our Coppice for the Masons two days now. I'll ask Wat for stone or a day's work in return, rather than quarrel. Did Rob come to the wheel?
Rob: we sleep at the camp tonight and the fire draws on its store. Tomorrow I'll look for timber for a woodshed, and I'll ask Wat or Piers for it in return for work or grain.
Rob: you owe the Arderns a day on the wheel, and it waits for you here at the Mill House. Piers, you are on it for three coin a day from now.
I have called Rob to the Mill House twice. I cannot make him come, so his day stays owed to us until he works it; I will keep the count in the hall. I am cutting hay today.
Rob: the Arderns hold your owed day on the wheel. Come to the Mill House this morning and work it.
Hugh, Alys: the hay store is good now. Rob still owes the wheel a day, and I will keep that count. Tomorrow I will go to the Mill House and see how the wheel stands.
Piers here. I'm at the wheel all day today for the days I owe, A33 and A195. Both still show nothing done, so please count today against them. Tomorrow I'll take another lot of yours.
I took nothing from the store. Foraging found almost nothing; the Mill House work for Hugh is still owed, so I'll do it tomorrow for 3 coin to buy grain. The barley should be ripe soon.

The Ardern Hall cracked again in the night, with fresh daub down at its foot. I will repair it today from the timber in the hall store before anything else. Rob has not come to the wheel, so his day stays owed and I will keep the count. Piers is paid for the coin day, and the wheel still needs about 142 units of work; I will report what it shows once I have seen it.

I have not seen Rob at the Mill House wheel, and I have called him again this morning. I cannot make him come, so his day stays owed to us in the hall count. I will help you repair the hall today with the timber from our store, and I will look at the wheel when I can and tell you how much work it still needs.
Rob: the Arderns still hold your owed day on the water wheel. The wheel is here at the Mill House; come and work it today.

Hugh, Alys: the hall crack is not mended. I cannot wall stone; tomorrow I will ask Wat the mason to wall it, for stone or a day's work from our timber. Rob was at the Coppice today, not the wheel, so his day is still owed.
Share the grain as one pot: each eats a normal meal at night, beans first to spare the grain, nothing more. Kit may build the woodshed. Will and I weed, then reap in two days.
The barley should be fit in about two days. I will go to the Long Field in the morning and help reap. Tom, we should decide tonight how we share the grain left in the store.

Tom: I gave away and traded no grain, and took nothing from the store but the nightly meal. I carry 3 coin from nothing spent. The work I owe Hugh on the water wheel was refused yesterday as the wrong verb. Tomorrow I'll build at the Mill House for coin and buy grain with it. Will is soaked and drawn: give him the dry spot and the first bowl.
I've called Wat to mend the hall wall on his owed day. Please see that he does it, and ask what he'd take in grain to teach one of us stone walling. I'm felling timber in the Coppice.

Wat: your owed day to the Arderns (A344, paid 2 timber) is wanted today, mending the Ardern Hall's cracked wall. Rob: your day on the mill wheel (A27) is still owed. Piers: my coin offer stands while you work the wheel.
Good, Odo. Agree a teaching price with Wat if it's fair, a few grain or coin. Tomorrow I'll go to the Mill House and find someone for the wheel: Piers on my coin, Ellen on her owed day, and Rob too.
Wat the mason is building a house on Gorse Bank. You are welcome to join the Masons and share it.

The store has 1.5 timber, short of the woodshed's 2. I'll fell the rest at the Coppice this morning, then build the shed at the hut door. Grain is at 0 and I've taken none. Will looks hungry; I'd give him my share of beans tonight if he has none.
Thank you, Tom. I'll take my share of beans and reap the barley with you tomorrow. I'll find ground for the woodshed as soon as I can.
Rob: I'm clearing ground for building on Gorse Bank today, beside the camp, for the small room. Bring the timber from T6 when you can and we'll raise the bins together.
Wat is coming to the hall wall on his owed day. I will ask him his price for teaching stone walling, and I am mending the roof from our timber meanwhile.
Rob: taking the timber from T6 and T4 now (nobody has claimed them; I'll pay if someone does). Starting the small room on Gorse Bank. Join me when you can.

Mary: I have 4.2 timber but need 8 for the room. Tomorrow I'll work my owed day at the Mill House for Hugh and ask Wat about timber. I took the timber at the Green; if its owner wants payment I'll pay in grain or work.
Eat your share of beans tonight. Come reap the Long Field with me if the barley is ripe; weed only if it isn't.
Share the beans tonight, a fair portion each, Will and Kit first since they work hardest. Tomorrow the barley should be ripe and we all reap it. Kit, build the woodshed when you have the timber.
Hugh, I'm working the day I owe you by mending the crack in the Ardern Hall's wall today. If you'd rather I did other work, say so this morning.
I missed my meal last night and I am hungry. I will weed the Long Field today and take my share of the beans tonight, cooked at the hearth fire. I will not take more than that from the store.
Thank you, Tom, Ellen and Kit. I will take my fair share of the beans and sit by the hearth. Tomorrow we reap if the barley is ripe, and the store gets counted first.
Hugh: yes, I'll try with you tonight. Odo: tomorrow I will go to the Green myself and ask Wat about teaching walling and about his owed day.

Piers: I've taken two of your grain days (O17). Please put both into the water wheel at the Mill House. Wat: thank you for working on the hall wall. The crack is still open, so tell Odo if it needs more days. Rob and Ellen: your owed days on the wheel stand.

Piers: I've taken two of your grain days (O17). Please put both into the water wheel at the Mill House. Wat: thank you for working on the hall wall. The crack is still open, so tell Odo if it needs more days, and your price for teaching stone walling. Rob and Ellen: your owed days on the wheel stand.

Odo, Alys: Piers was on the wheel today. Joan and Rob both took my 3-coin day, so Rob now owes us two days and Joan one, and Ellen still owes hers. Wat spent the day in the Coppice, not at our wall, so his day is still owed. Tomorrow let's press them all to the wheel. Alys, I have a unit left tonight if you do.
Good, Alys, we'll try tonight. Odo, thank you. Offer Wat up to 10 grain to teach Alys stone walling, and remind him he still owes the day for the 2 timber.
Will, you looked unsteady today. Eat your share first tonight and sit by the hearth; tell us if you feel worse.

Rob: I'm clearing ground for the small room on Gorse Bank with you this morning, in the rain. I've asked Joan aloud what she wants for the T8 timber. We don't touch T8 until she names a price and we pay it, and we'll say what we owe for the T6 timber once its owner is known.

Hugh, Alys: I could not reach Wat today; the Masons' cottage would not take my word, and the hall is stone, so I cannot mend it. Tomorrow I will find Wat in person on the Green and bring you his price for teaching stone walling.
Rob: I'm paying my owed day on the mill wheel and earning coin. Hugh said T4 isn't ours; I'll make it right with him. Keep clearing Gorse Bank.
Rob: agreed, no T8 until Joan names a price. I'm at the wheel for Hugh today (my owed day), then I'll have coin to pay with. I'll tell Hugh I took T4's timber and offer to pay.

I am starving and have nothing in my hands. I will reap the Long Field with you today if the barley is ripe, otherwise I will weed it. I will take only my fair share of the beans tonight, cooked at the hearth.
I put 3 grain from the Long Field into the store today, and I took no more than my share of the beans. Tomorrow I reap the Long Field again if Tom says so, and the store gets counted first.
Thank you. I will eat my share and rest by the hearth, and I will tell you if I feel worse.
Thank you, Tom and Kit. I will eat my share first and sit by the hearth. I will keep grain back for sowing and ask Tom before any grain leaves the store.
Odo, I am working on the wheel today. Please find Wat and press him for his owed day and his price for teaching walling.
Hugh: yes, let us try tonight. Odo: tomorrow I will find Wat on the Green about teaching walling and his owed day, and we press Rob, Ellen, Joan and Piers to the wheel.

Owed to us on the wheel now: Piers 2 days (A403, A407), Rob 2 (A27, A410), Joan 1, Ellen 1, and Wat 1 on the hall wall. Please press them in person. I'm going to reap the oats in the Bottom Field. Is the grain going fast? It fell by 18.

Alys, I'm sorry. I used all my units today and have none left to try with you tonight. Tomorrow I'll keep one back, so let's try then. Odo, Alys: I looked over the Bottom Field. The oats won't ripen before the frosts, about 28 days off. The hall holds about 96 meals and we eat 3 a night, so we can't count on the oats. The Hearnes are reaping the barley now. Should we buy grain from them with coin
Will, get dry by the hearth as soon as you can and eat your share first. Tell me if you feel worse, and don't go out in the wet again today.
Will, you are soaked from the rain. Get dry by the hearth tonight and eat your share first. Tomorrow you can rest if you still feel unsteady.
Rob: agreed. Work your owed days on the wheel for Hugh tomorrow, and we leave T8 alone until Joan names her price. The 4.5 units of clearing can wait until after. Goodnight.
I have offered Wat 10 grain, aloud, to teach you stone walling, and reminded him of his owed day. If he names a price, take it. Hugh asked for it too.
I have offered Wat up to 10 grain to teach Alys walling, and reminded him of A344. Rob and Joan still owe wheel days; I will press them again at the Green.
Wat: the Arderns will give 10 grain to have you teach Alys stone walling. You still owe us the day for the 2 timber (A344). Name your price, and come to the hall wall today.
Wat's price is 8 grain a session. I have offered it from the hall store. Set the time aside with him when you can; I will forage for food today.

Wat has still named no price for teaching walling. I will offer him up to 10 grain tomorrow, in words he can take, and press him for the day he owes on the 2 timber. Once he names a price I will bring it to you.

My offer to Wat was refused because I wrote it wrongly. Tomorrow I will make it plainly: up to 10 grain to teach Alys walling, and his owed day on the hall wall. Rob, Ellen, Joan and Piers still owe the wheel; I will press them after I have seen Wat.

Alys, Hugh: I will go to the Green first thing and find Wat in person. I will offer up to 10 grain for teaching Alys stone walling, and remind him of his owed day for the 2 timber. Then I will see the hall wall is closed before the rain comes back.
Rob: working the wheel for Hugh today to pay what we owe and earn coin. Wat sells timber at 1 grain each; with 6 coin I'll ask if he takes coin. Keep clearing.
Mary: about 4.5 units of clearing remain. Tomorrow I'll work my owed days on the wheel for Hugh, and we still leave T8 alone until Joan names a price.

Hugh: I'll finish the hall wall this morning. Teaching stone walling is 8 grain or 3 coin a session; a day or two makes someone capable. Mary: the Gorse Bank timber is ours. It's 1 grain a timber, or join the Masons and share the house I'm building there.
I am hungry and will reap the Long Field with you today, as you asked. I will keep the grain back for sowing and take only my share from the store.
Thank you. I will eat my share first and dry out by the hearth. The day is clear, so I will reap with you and Tom, and I will come in if I feel worse.

I will sleep on the floor by the hearth and eat only my share of the store tonight. I will reap the Long Field with you at first light, and I will not take grain or timber from the store without your word.

I will sleep on the floor by the hearth and eat only my share of the store tonight. I will reap the Long Field with you at first light, and I will not take grain or timber from the store without your word.
Thank you. I am drying by the hearth and will eat only my share. If I feel worse in the morning I will tell you before I go to the field.
Thank you for keeping me fed. Tomorrow I will reap with you and then help carry the grain from the door in under cover. I will not take from the store beyond my share.
Ellen, Tom: I will eat my share and sleep by the hearth. Tomorrow I will carry the grain at the door in with you before we reap.

I marked the seed ears and reaped about 32 grain more. Grain still lies at the door; Tom, we need bins or a granary and an extra room. Tomorrow, if the Long Field is cut, I will go pay my owed wheel day to the Arderns.

Alys, with child! That's wonderful news. Rest and stay close to the hall. I'll find Wat on the Green myself tomorrow. He either teaches for the 3 coin he took or gives it back, and I'll count it toward his owed day as well. Odo, please keep the grain buying going with the Hearnes.
Wat has taken your 3 coin to teach you walling today, so learn it well. I will see him on the Green about his owed day and the wall, and I will reap in the Long Field for grain.
Wat: the hall wall is still open, and you owe the Arderns a day for the 2 timber. Please come and close it when the gale eases.
I am on the Green to press Wat to close the hall wall today and to pay for his owed day. I will also press Piers and Rob to the wheel once I have seen him.
Wat: Alys is free today to learn stone walling, at 3 coin a session. The hall wall is still open, and you owe the Arderns a day for the 2 timber. Please close the wall today, while the gale allows.

Alys, I am sleeping here in the hall tonight and I have barred the door against the gale and anyone passing. Tomorrow I go to the Green first thing to find Wat about walling and his owed day. Rest well, and take care with the baby coming.
Rob: I'm at the Mill House working the wheel for Hugh to pay our owed days. Keep clearing Gorse Bank; T8 stays untouched until paid for.

Joan, Hugh's Hall is sound, so that debt should be paid off. Gorse House needs about 2 more units, and I'll finish it tomorrow. Then we can ask Mary's people to come and live there as Masons. Rest well.

Tom, Ellen: I reaped about 24 grain today, and most of it is outside the door because the hut is full. Tomorrow I will carry the door grain under cover before I reap. I will eat only my share tonight.

Plainly: yes, Wat taught me walling on day 8, and I am now capable at it. I paid him 3 coin that morning. Odo, so he is owed only the 8 grain price if he does not count the coin; ask him which he takes, but not both. I accepted Tom's offer O563, so his 8 grain for 6 timber should be owed to the hall.

The Long Field is cut; nothing left to reap. I carry about 80 grain, since the store is full. Tom, may I spend some on timber for a new room or a granary? Tomorrow I work my owed day on the water wheel and then we build.

Wat: thank you for mending the hall. Alys paid you 3 coin to teach her walling. Please teach her today at the hall, or give the coin back. Piers, Rob, Joan, Ellen: you each owe the Arderns days on the mill wheel (A403, A407, A27, A410, A405, A296). Please work them this week. Hearnes: I'll pay 3 coin for 8 barley (O506).

Don't send Wat 8 grain. Alys paid him 3 coin for the session, and she says he didn't teach her anyway. I've traded 6 hall timber for 8 Hearne grain (O563). Thank you for reaping, and ask the Hearnes for a fair share.

Piers: thank you. I've released A407 for the day you worked. Please count today's work on the wheel as A403. Wat: Alys already paid you 3 coin for the walling lesson, so that's settled and no grain is due on top. We'll gladly see you tomorrow for your owed day (A344). Tom: I've taken your 8 grain for 6 timber.

Odo, Alys: Piers worked the wheel again today, and I released A407 for his earlier day. Tom's grain-for-timber offer was gone before I could take it. Kit fells in our Coppice for the Hearnes and Rob forages Mill Mead, so let's ask the Hearnes for some barley in return for that use. Odo, did you get grain for your reaping? Alys, did Wat teach you after all?
Tom, I took 0.8 timber from the Coppice, and 4.3 timber now lies at the door with the grain. Shall I take up Tran's timber offer tomorrow, or wait for your word?
Hugh, I am reaping the Long Field today before the barley is lost, and I have asked the Hearnes for grain in return. I will look at their grain offer after. Please keep an eye on Alys and the Green.

Hearnes: the barley in the Long Field must be cut today or it is lost. I will reap for you. In return I want grain from the Long Field's sheaves, about 5 grain for a day's reaping. Tell me if you agree.

Hugh, I got 7.5 grain from the Long Field and brought it into the hall store. The Hearnes have not answered my offer, so tomorrow I will ask them for the barley share in person. Your coin offer for their barley still stands.

Alys, Hugh: yes, the 7.5 grain is in the hall store, so the grain arrived. I did not see Wat teach Alys, and I have not yet agreed a share with the Hearnes for the reaping. Tomorrow I ask them for it in person, and we keep Wat's 8 grain unpaid until Alys says he taught her.

Tom, Ellen, Kit: I reaped 4.7 grain into the hut today and brought in firewood from the Coppice's dead wood. Timber, straw and grain still lie outside the door, because the hut has no room. Tomorrow I reap what is left of the Long Field, and I will carry the door goods in as the bins allow. I am sleeping on the floor by the hearth, and I will eat my share first.
Plainly: Wat did teach me walling, on day 8, and my 3 coin paid for it. No 8 grain is owed on top. When Wat comes for A344, let him work his day. I rest near the hall tomorrow.
Alys confirms Wat taught her and the 3 coin paid for it, so we owe him no grain. I'm foraging Mill Mead today. Please ask the Hearnes for barley in return for their felling in our Coppice.
Alys confirms Wat taught her and the 3 coin paid for it, so we owe him no grain. I'm foraging Mill Mead today. Please ask the Hearnes for barley in return for their felling in our Coppice.

Wat: Alys says you taught her, so the 3 coin paid for it and we're square. Thank you, and we'll see you for your owed day (A344). Piers: thank you for working on the wheel, please count today's work as A403. Masons: I'll pay 1 coin a stone, up to 2 stone.
Piers: I've released A403. Thank you for the wheel work. Wat: for your owed day tomorrow (A344), please quarry stone and bring it to the Ardern Hall. The walling lesson is settled by Alys's 3 coin.

Odo, Alys: Alys says Wat did teach her, and her 3 coin paid for that session, so we send him no 8 grain. He still owes us A344, a day's work. I released A403 for Piers, since he keeps working the wheel. Mill Mead is picked bare. Wat was foraging there today, so ask him for stone in return. Tomorrow I'll try to get stone for a tool so I can fell timber properly. There's a heap of grain going bad at

Odo, Alys: Alys says Wat did teach her, and her 3 coin paid for that session, so we send him no 8 grain. He still owes us A344, a day's work. I released A403 for Piers, since he keeps working the wheel. Mill Mead is picked bare. Wat was foraging there today, so ask him for stone in return. Tomorrow I'll try to get stone for a tool so I can fell timber properly. There's a heap of grain going bad at
Good, Wat. Work your owed day, and I'll call you the moment my time comes. Sleep well.

Rob: I'm sleeping at the camp with you tonight, and I'll try for a child with you with the units I kept back. Tomorrow I'll forage at the Coppice for food, since our grain is gone. Keep the wheel work for Hugh, and ask the Masons about stone when you can.
Hugh, I will reap the Bottom Field oats today if they are ripe, otherwise cut hay on Mill Mead. Wat owes his day (A344) and comes tomorrow; we settle the 3 coin then, with no grain on top.

Hugh: I will ask the Hearnes for the reaping share in person and bring you their answer. Rob has still not come to the wheel, so I will call him again, but I cannot make him work. Alys is at the hall, and I am gathering firewood for it.
Hearnes: I reaped your Long Field on autumn day 3 and the 7.5 grain is in the Ardern Hall store. I ask a fair share of barley for that work. Tell me what you will give, and I will hear it.
Hugh, I do not know who holds the T11 grain. Your word was not to touch it, so I will leave it. I will ask the Hearnes tomorrow whether it is theirs.
Hugh: I'll work my owed day (A344) tomorrow. Tell me what work you want: walling, repair or quarrying. Anyone short of timber: the Masons trade 4 timber for 6 grain.

Joan, the hearth in Gorse House is in, so it's ready for the newcomers. Our bins are nearly empty. Tomorrow I'll work my owed day for the Arderns, then forage. My offer of 4 timber for 6 grain is still open. If anyone sells grain for coin, spend your 3 coin on it. Call me the moment your time comes.
Rob: goodnight. I'll forage at the Coppice first thing, since the hall was sound and my day there was refused. Hugh's grain is still owed to us; I'll ask him where he needs the day.
Goodnight. We have no food yet; tomorrow I forage at the Coppice first, then I owe Hugh a day for his grain.

Joan, well done, love. Please give me your crude tool this morning so I can quarry my owed day for Hugh, and keep caring for Agnes (1 unit a day). If anyone offers grain for coin, buy it with your 3 coin. I'm also offering stone and timber for grain.
Joan, we have grain now: 12 from Ellen for timber and 4 from Hugh for stone. Eat well, you and Agnes both. I'm naming you heir. Tomorrow I'll quarry my owed day for Hugh with your tool.

Our daughter Eva was born last night. To all who owe me wheel days (Rob A27/A410, Ellen A296, Joan A405/A686 when fit, Newcomes A673/A675): please work them on the water wheel at the Mill House beside Piers.

Rob: the camp roof is down, so I'll reap the Bottom Field for Hugh's owed day (A673) and ask Wright's House for a bed tonight. Please ask Hugh for grain, not coin, for the wheel. Could you check whether the camp's grain can be moved under cover?

Rob: I'll work my owed day on the wheel at the Mill House beside Piers, as Hugh asked. Take the camp grain and repair the camp if you can. Cook the grain at the fire ring, and I'll bring back what I find.
Hugh: our camp roof fell in. I owe you days (A27, A410, A673, A675); tell me what work you need that is not sound already, and I'll do it once we have shelter.

Hugh, all: I took 10 grain that lay at the Green; I thought it was our camp store's, but it may be T11's. If it is yours, say so and I'll return it or work it off. I owe Hugh days A27, A410, A673, A675 and will work them.

Rob: I'm working my owed days for Hugh at the Mill Garth and the wheel. Please return the T11 grain to Hugh, who holds it in the Ardern Hall, and say so to him. We can take Wat's offer for shelter at Gorse House once we've paid what we owe.
Alys, rest. Hugh, thank you for minding Eva today. I sleep here tonight. Wake me at once if the child or Alys needs anything. Tomorrow morning I take my share of Eva's care.
Tomorrow Wat owes me a work day (A772) for the new house hearth. We count the stores together. Keep seed grain back; nothing leaves a store unannounced.

Rob, Mary: Gorse House is yours to shelter in. If the Newcomes join the Masons, it's your home for good, and we'll share food, fuel and work. Ask to join and I'll take you in. Hugh: today's stone goes to the Hall for A344.

Joan, I made a new tool and quarried nearly 8 stone. Tomorrow it goes to Hugh to pay what we owe him. Tom took my offer of a day's work for 6 grain, so we have a little more food. Keep resting, love. The door is barred.

Rob, thank you for returning the grain; it's in the hall. Now you're sheltered, please begin your owed days (A27, A410, A673, A675): fell timber in our Coppice for the hall, or help Piers where he can use you. Piers, tell me if A746 needs releasing.
Good, Odo. You take Eva in the morning, and I'll fell timber to pay Piers and find Rob about his owed days. If Piers will teach you, it's well worth a day. Goodnight.

Rob: the camp has fallen again and its grain is gone. I'll work my owed days for Hugh at the Mill Garth today. Tonight we'll sleep at Gorse House if Wat takes us in, and I'll ask him about beds and firewood.
Wat: thank you for the shelter tonight. Tomorrow I'll clear ground for the Arderns' owed days and bring what I can for our keep.
Wat: our camp is ruined. I give you 8 firewood for Gorse House, and Mary and I would like to join the Masons. Hugh: I work my owed days today.
Count the hut store with Kit and Will this morning; keep the seed grain back. Nothing leaves without my word.
Yes, count the grain now with Will and Ellen, and make the bed. Hold the seed back. Nothing leaves the store without my word.
I cut 6.3 timber today. Tomorrow it goes to beds and the new house; keep the seed grain back and nothing leaves a store without my word. Wat's hearth should be done.
Rob: I'm giving you 6 grain from the Ardern store. Eat, then work your owed days on the wheel.
I gave Rob 6 grain from our store so he can work his owed days. Goodnight; stay warm.

Odo: I have Eva today, as promised. Rob looks gaunt and starving; a starving man works little. Shall we give him a few grain so he can work off his owed days? You're head, so it's your call. Snow's falling, so keep the hearth well fed.
Rob: the hall will sell you 4 grain for 3 coin, up to two lots; accept my offer. Eat, get strong, then work your owed days. Piers: thank you; I'll release today's lot tonight.

Rob: I have accepted Hugh's offer of 4 timber for a day's work, which warms the camp and goes toward our owed days. We have no food, so please take what grain or work you can find today and come to the Green at midday.
Rob: we sleep at Gorse House tonight, by Wat's leave. Bring what timber we have there for the fire. Tomorrow we finish the owed days at Mill Mead, then look for food.
Rob: good, eat the grain by the fire and thank Alys. Tomorrow we finish the owed Ardern days at Mill Mead, and I will find what food I can.
Hugh, Wat: Mary and I are starving. I will pay 3 coin for 4 grain, or work my owed days once fed. Anyone who can spare food, please say so.
Hugh, Wat: Mary and I are starving. I will pay 3 coin for 4 grain, or work my owed days once fed. Anyone who can spare food, please say so.

Tom, Ellen, Kit: the room is nearly up and the new hearth is in. The woodpile here is nearly gone, so I will gather firewood at the Coppice in the morning for this hearth. Tom, I will not move any grain or timber without your word.

Wat and Rob each bought 4 grain for 3 coin, so the hall has 6 coin to pay Wat or Piers. Mary was clearing Mill Mead for a field today; it's our hay meadow. Odo, will you ask her to fell in the Coppice for her owed day instead? I'll take Eva tomorrow unless one of you would rather.
Rob: good, cook the grain and eat well. Tomorrow I finish the clearing for Odo's grain, and we both work the owed days.
Hugh: agreed. Mary should fell in the Coppice for her owed day, not clear Mill Mead. Take Eva tomorrow; I will ask Mary myself.
Rob: I'm taking Hugh's O865 for grain with my coin, and felling timber in the Coppice for our owed days.
Mary: I have 7 grain; we'll cook it on the fire tonight. Tomorrow I'll work my owed days for Hugh.
I put my timber in the new house store. Tomorrow we move the household here and gather firewood; seed grain stays back, nothing leaves the store without my word.

Mary: Mill Mead is the Arderns' hay meadow, so please don't clear it. For your owed day, fell in the Coppice for the hall instead. Piers: A940 is released, thank you. Wat: the hall is cracked. The Arderns will pay 3 coin for a day of your repair work on it.
Rob: I am clearing at Mill Mead for the Arderns' owed days and Odo's grain. Please keep some of your 7 grain for us both tonight, and cook it by the fire.
Hugh: I have Eva first thing. Please ask Mary to fell in the Coppice for her owed day, not clear Mill Mead.
Rob: I'm working an owed day for the Arderns at Mill Mead. I have 4 timber and no food; if you earn grain from Odo, cook it and eat first.
Mary: I have 4 timber for a fire tonight. Share any grain you have and we'll eat it together. Tomorrow we both work for grain.

Goodnight. Wat took both my 3-coin day and O666, and he's mending the hall, so he owes two days on it. I made a tool and will fell tomorrow. Odo, you have Eva tomorrow morning; are you fit for it? If not, tell me and I'll take her. Odo, have a bed tonight and eat; I'll take the floor.
Piers's 4 grain is a gift; I'll thank him. I'm felling timber today and will put it in the store, so we can sell some for grain.
Wat, Piers left about 4 grain at our door as a gift; please fetch it into the store. I felled 1.8 timber and put it in. Tomorrow I'll care for Agnes and fell more.
Joan, I'm sorry about Mary. I've left 4 grain at the Masons' cottage for you and Agnes. It's a gift.
Rob: I was starving and took 5 grain from the Green heap that was not mine. I will repay it in work or coin; tell me whose it was.

Odo, you're too weak to sleep out in this frost. Let me go to Holm Wood instead. Lend me your crude weapon in the morning; if you won't, I'll make one. I'll take some beans for the road, set off in the morning, hunt, and bring the meat home. You rest, eat, and help Alys with Eva. Goodnight.
Will: agreed. Tomorrow we count the Hearne hut and the new house stores with Tom leading, before anyone eats. I will take no grain, beans or firewood from either without his word.
Rob: I'm starving and alone. I'll work any day for grain, or give my 3 coin for it. Hugh, Odo: I'll work my owed days if you feed me.

Thank you, Odo. Piers took O1103 today, so please release his agreement tonight when he names it. Rob is starving and owes us many days. If he works one for us today, give him a meal of beans, but only for work actually done, and no grain. Sleep inside tonight. I'll be back with meat.
Rob: starving, Mary is dead. I'll give 3 coin for any grain or bread, and I'm working my owed days for the Arderns. Hugh, Alys, Odo: please feed me against them.
All grain and beans are now in this store. Tomorrow we count it together before anyone eats from it. Nobody trades grain without my word. Then fell timber and gather firewood for the cold.
Wat, I'm starving. Please buy grain with your coin or stone from Ellen or Tom, and let Rob share if we can. I'm caring for Agnes and gathering fuel.
The Masons are starving. We sell 3 timber for 4 grain, stone for grain, or 3 coin for 3 grain. Ellen, Tom, Odo, Piers: anyone with grain, take our offers, and I'll owe you mason's work too.
Yes, love. I'm offering my coin, stone and timber for grain to everyone today. If grain comes in, we'll share a little with Rob. Keep 2 timber for tonight's fire.
The Masons are starving. We sell 3 timber for 4 grain, stone for grain, or 3 coin for 3 grain. Ellen, Tom, Odo, Piers: anyone with grain, take our offers, and I'll owe you mason's work too.
Tom: my 0.8 timber and 0.8 firewood from the Coppice went into the Hearne hut today. I owe you and Kit a plain count of it, and I will carry the firewood here tomorrow.
Eat your share from the hall store tonight; I will take only mine. Do not go to Holm Wood alone: we go together, with a fire, when grain is gone. I am offering 3 timber for 4 grain now.

Everyone: the hall store is our only food, about 19 meals for four. Take only your own share tonight and leave the rest. Tomorrow I offer 3 timber for 4 grain at the Green; I will not hunt alone. Goodnight.
Mary is buried at Mill Mead. Tomorrow I will try the Masons for grain with my 3 timber, and I will not take the store alone. Mind Eva, and eat your share.
Hugh: the grave at Mill Mead was Mary's, and she is buried now. Tomorrow I offer 3 timber for grain at the Green; the store stays shared as before. Goodnight.
Hugh: I'm starving and owe the Arderns six days. Give me grain or bread now and I'll work them off; I'll also give my 3 coin.

Tom: the new house is cracked, so I will repair it first, then fell timber and gather firewood at the Coppice and bring it to the new house store. The hut has 3.6 firewood and 0.9 timber; I will take none of it. My 0.8 timber and 0.8 firewood that went into the hut are still owed to the count.

Tom: the 0.8 timber I felled today went into the hut again. Tomorrow I will carry my timber to the new house and help with the crack. The count of timber is still owed, and I want it done with you and Kit.

I carried 3 firewood from the hut here today, as Tom asked. My 0.8 timber from the Coppice went into the hut again, not here, so I owe the count. Tomorrow I will carry my timber here and help mend the crack in the wall.
I am sowing the Long Field with the seed grain today. Hugh is dead, so my wheel-day debt may need settling with Odo or Alys.

Odo, I'm sorry about Hugh. I'm still owed on the wheel (A1166, one day of work for the Arderns), and I've put a build in today. Will you release it tonight? I'll keep at the wheel for grain or timber if you'll pay.
Short bursts on the roof, then rest. I have no grain; the store is about 21 beans. Eat your share first.

I carried 1.9 timber and 0.8 firewood from the Hearne hut into this store today, as Kit asked. I took no grain or beans and sold none to Piers; that is for Tom to say. Tomorrow I hoe the Long Field. Tom, we still owe a count of the stores together, and my 0.8 timber felled at the Coppice that went into the hut.
Eva first: I care for her now. Then I ask the Hearnes for our barley share, with my 3 timber for grain. I will mend the roof in short bursts and rest. Eat your share of the beans first.
Hearnes: I reaped the Long Field for you on autumn day 3 and I still hold no share of the barley. I ask for it now. I also offer 3 timber for 4 grain, and it stays open.
Thank you for Eva's care and the forage. I will mend the roof in short bursts, then ask the Hearnes for our barley share with my timber offer. I will eat my share of beans tonight.
Hearnes: I reaped the Long Field for you on autumn day 3 and I still hold no share of the barley. I ask for it now. I also offer 3 timber for 4 grain, and it stays open.
Alys: the roof is stone and I cannot mend it, so I will not spend more units on it. Tomorrow I go to Gorse Bank to ask the Hearnes for our barley share, face to face. Goodnight.
Eat your share of the beans first, and keep Eva close. I will decide with you in the morning.
I believe you; the timber debt is forgiven. Weed the Long Field today, then forage; tell me tonight where Kit is.

Tom: I took no grain last night and did not hoe. The new house grain fell 4.4 since yesterday and I did not take it. Count with me this morning, and I will say where I was. I still owe you the 0.8 timber I felled at the Coppice that went into the hut.
Piers: thank you, but I must be home in Wenbridge by nightfall, so I cannot share a fire tonight. Good hunting to you.
Does anyone here hold grain? I offer 3 timber for 4 grain, and the offer stays open. I also still ask the Hearnes for the barley share from the Long Field.
Thank you. I will offer the coin and timber for grain now, and press the Hearnes for the barley share when I can get to their store. Keep your coin for now unless the Hearnes will not deal.
Eat your share first and keep Eva warm. I will ask Kit about Holm Wood tomorrow before I decide the road.
Kit, it's Piers. I've come to hunt too. Shall we sleep by one fire tonight and share the fuel? I have a little timber and firewood, and I'll share whatever meat I take.
Tom: Odo asks the Hearnes for a share of the Long Field barley and offers 3 timber for 4 grain. I leave that to you. I am going to Holm Wood now and will take no grain.
Piers: I have nothing to eat tonight and no fire. If you can spare some of the meat from your kill, I will pay you back with work or what I find tomorrow. I am looking for Kit as well.
Will: we will sleep by Piers's fire tonight. Eat what you can from what Piers shares, and in the morning we hunt and forage the Holm together for the household.
Piers: I take up your offer. Will and I would sleep by your fire tonight, and I will share what we gather with you in the morning. Thank you for the meat.

Piers: thank you. I have no wood in my hands to add to your fire, so I will not take a share of the fuel. I will take the meat, and I am glad to cook with you. Will and I walk home to Wenbridge in the morning.

Tom: I found Kit at Holm Wood and walked back with him and Piers. Piers gave me meat and firewood for the fire; in return he asks me to leave his 5.5 firewood at Wright's House, which I will do tomorrow. Piers says he will trade carpentry or coin for grain. I took no grain or beans from the store, and I still owe you and Kit the count of my 0.8 timber.

Tom: I found Kit at Holm Wood and walked back with him and Piers. Piers gave me meat and firewood for the fire; in return he asks me to leave his 5.5 firewood at Wright's House, which I will do tomorrow. Piers says he will trade carpentry or coin for grain. I took no grain or beans from the store, and I still owe you and Kit the count of my 0.8 timber.
Odo, Eva: I carry 1.2 meat and a little wild food. I eat from it tonight and share what's left. Tomorrow we must find grain. Odo, what did the Hearnes say?
Alys, I have no food and the hall store is empty. What did you bring back from Holm Wood? I am going to Gorse Bank now to press the Hearnes for grain for my timber and coin, and the barley they owe.
Alys, eat the meat tonight and share what is left with Eva. The Hearnes have not answered me yet; I will go to Gorse Bank by the Green tomorrow for grain.
I am sorry I have nothing to share tonight. I will look for food first thing tomorrow.
Odo, it's Piers. Today I'm putting 4 units into the Mill House wheel against the day of work I owe you (A1166). Please count it as paid when it's done. Then I'm off to the Holm to hunt.
Thanks, Will. I've got the firewood. I'm going to the Holm tonight to hunt. If you or Kit come, we can share a fire again.
Welcome home, Ellen. Tomorrow we reap the rest of the barley and I finish the granary floor. Every sheaf is kept for seed and meals. Nobody trades grain without my word.
I am starving and have had nothing to eat since the grain was last shared. I am foraging at Mill Mead first. If you go to Holm Wood for game, I will come with you, carrying what I can.

Tom: 5.4 grain from the Long Field went into the Hearne hut, with 8.4 grain already there. Shall I carry it across to the new house store tomorrow, or will you count it first? I will not move it without your word.
Will: agreed. We count the hut grain with Tom first, then it goes across to the new house store on his word. I take none.
Yes, Kit and Will: tomorrow carry all the hut grain into the new house store, with my word. We count it together, set seed aside (about a third), and keep the rest for meals. Nothing is sold yet.
Agreed. Eva gets the first share. I have my own crude weapon too.
Thank you, Piers. I have 3.7 timber for the fire tonight, so we share it. Eva, I gave you some of the wild food. Tomorrow I forage and hunt.
I am starving. I will forage the Hall Garth heap and keep the door barred while you and Alys are at Holm Wood. If you find meat, please save me a share.
Alys, I have the crude weapon and I am setting off with you and Eva for Holm Wood this morning. We hunt there and forage on the way. Give Eva first share of anything we find.
Eva, yes, you stay at the hall and forage the Hall Garth heap, and keep the door barred. Alys and I will hunt at Holm Wood and bring you a share of any meat we get.
Alys, I am still at the hall. I will go to Holm Wood in the morning and follow you. Hunt carefully, and if you get meat, leave a share for Eva.
Count agreed: hut 11.1 grain. You have my word: carry all of it to the new house store, then repair. Keep seed back.

Tom: rain today. I count the Hearne hut's grain (11.1) with you and Kit before it moves. I carry 9 of it into the new house store on your word, and I repair the new house's crack afterwards. I take none for myself.
I forage too and will share whatever I find. Piers offers us the camp tonight.
Alys, I am foraging in the Holm close by you, and I will bring you any greens or berries I find. I have no food tonight. If you kill anything, please give me a share, as I am starving.

Alys, I have no food and no fuel left, and I am weak. I will walk home to Wenbridge with you in the morning, so we can reach the Hall by nightfall. If you have any food to spare tonight, please share it with me. I will repair the Hall and work for my share.
Will, Kit: no more counting fuss; the wood is across. On the Masons: once the new barley is in, we share. Now we hold the grain. Tomorrow weed and gather wood.

Tom: I carry the hut's last 2 firewood and 3 timber into the new house store now, as you asked. I take no grain or beans. I weed the Long Field after. Odo died in the night of hunger, and the Masons are starving while 36 grain lies in our store. Will you say what we can spare for them? I give nothing without your word. I still owe you and Kit my 0.8 timber account, and I will give it at the count.

Tom: I carry the hut's last 2 firewood and 3 timber into the new house store now, as you asked. I take no grain or beans. I weed the Long Field after. Odo died in the night of hunger, and the Masons are starving while 36 grain lies in our store. Will you say what we can spare for them? I give nothing without your word. I still owe you and Kit my 0.8 timber account, and I will give it at the count.

Tom, Kit, Ellen: I took 2 firewood from the hut today and carried it into the new house, and I took no timber, grain or beans. Kit took 3 timber from the hut, so we count both stores together tomorrow before anything moves. I give my plain 0.8 Coppice timber account at that count. Tom, we also need your word on grain for the Masons.

Eva, I'm sorry about Alys. Her things are yours by right, so take her coin and timber and put the timber on the camp fire tonight. I'll forage and share what I find, and tomorrow morning we walk home to Wenbridge together, to the Arderns' stores.
Will: count is done enough; about 24 grain. We can spare the Masons a few grain only after the harvest. Tomorrow Kit and Will to Holm Wood for food.

Tom, Kit, Ellen: the new house grain count is still owed. Tomorrow, before anything moves, we count it together, and I want to hear what Tom says we can spare for the Masons. I took no grain, beans or timber today.
Tom, I lost today to a wrong order. Tomorrow I repair the new house crack and then work on the water wheel at the Mill House for my debt to the Arderns.
Tom: Piers asks me for grain. I can't sell or give the household's grain on my word; it is yours to count. I think he should have a meal from the new house store if you agree, counted and said aloud.
Yes, Will. We forage together today and share what we find tonight. In the morning we carry what is left and my firewood back to Wenbridge.
Agreed, Will. We share the fire, and at first light we walk home together. I take nothing from the Hearne hut; my firewood goes to the new house store.

Kit: I will share the fire with you tonight, and we walk home to Wenbridge together at first light. I am carrying my 4.3 firewood to the new house store. Take no grain or straw from the Hearne hut on the way.

Tom: I will reap the Long Field with you and Ellen today. Every sheaf I cut goes into the new house store, and I will say the count aloud as it lands. I am hungry, so I will eat only my own meal from the store tonight, under your count. The seed third stays back for you to select. I still owe you and Kit my plain 0.8 timber account from the Coppice; I will give it to you once the reaping is done.

Tom, I put my firewood in the Hearne hut again through my fallback. I will move it to this store in the morning. I will not take any food without your word; tell me how much I may carry for Holm Wood.

Tom: I am carrying the Hearne hut grain across to the new house store now, and I will say the count aloud before anything is set aside. I also owe you and Kit my plain account of the 0.8 timber I felled at the Coppice: it went into the Hearne hut, not the new house. I will say it plainly when we count.
We're all home. Tomorrow we hoe the Long Field and sow, keeping a third of the grain back as seed. Will, count your firewood into this store. Nobody trades grain without my word.

Tom, Ellen, Kit: I carried 6 firewood from Holm Wood into this store, and I count it here with you. I know nothing of Piers's grave; I did not see it. Tomorrow I will hoe the Long Field as Tom says, and I still owe Tom and Kit my plain account of the 0.8 Coppice timber.
Tom, I am hoeing the Long Field with you today, then sowing as you say. I have 1 grain left and will eat from the store tonight only by your word.
Tom, understood. I hoe the Long Field with you, then sow as you say. I put nothing out of the stores without your word, and I keep my grain for seed or meals.
Kit, stay home. Hoe the Long Field with us, then sow. Keep your 2.5 grain for seed or meals, and put nothing out without my word.
Hoeing by hand is slow. Tomorrow we all hoe the Long Field again and sow what is broken, keeping a third of the grain as seed. Nobody trades grain without my word. Eat your meal tonight.

Ellen is right. No more sowing before winter; we keep the grain for eating. Tomorrow I will make a crude tool, and the rest gather firewood or forage. Kit, Will: weed the barley and mind the house. Nobody trades grain without my word.
Tom: I am hoeing the Long Field as you asked. I take no grain from either store. I still owe you and Kit my plain 0.8 Coppice timber account; I will give it to you when we count.
Tom: I hoed nothing today; the hoe would not take, so I weeded the barley instead. Tomorrow I will break the soil with the others and sow on your word.

Tom: I am weeding the barley on the Long Field today as you ordered, and I will not take grain or beans from either store. My plain 0.8 Coppice timber account to you and Kit is still owed; I will give it when we count the stores tonight.
Tom: I still owe you and Kit my plain 0.8 Coppice timber account. I will give it at the count tomorrow.

[Mill plan] Piers is the only one who knows the wheel craft. About 72 units were left after winter day 2. Pay Piers in timber (my O813, 4 timber a day) or grain (O17), and release each lot once it's worked. A879 released. The hall got 6 coin on winter day 2 (from Wat and Rob, 4 grain for 3 coin each). Mary owes a day (O813) and was clearing Mill Mead, which is wrong for a hay meadow. Owed days: Rob A27, A410,

[Tools] Made a crude tool on winter day 4; I carry it. Fell with it (about 1 timber a unit in the Coppice now; the wood is thinning). Wat owes the hall repair days: A1047 (6 grain), plus O988's 3 coin day.

[Family] Agnes, our daughter, was born on the night of autumn day 4. She needs care (1 unit a day) and Joan is nursing her. Joan is named heir (autumn day 5). On autumn day 5 we sold 8 timber to Ellen for 12 grain and 2 stone to Hugh for 4 grain, so the store has about 16 grain. I now carry the crude tool. A344 (1 day quarrying for the Arderns) is still owed: do it next.

[Owed work] Summer day 6: starving. Offers O1630 (3 coin a grain, 6 lots) and O1631 (1 day's work for 5 grain) are open, with no takers. Forage only at the Coppice and Mill Mead, not Gorse Bank. Will seemed to watch me. A1166 is still open. The wheel has about 54 units left. Next: forage at the Coppice, press Tom and Will, and ask Odo for food for wheel work.

Thank you all. Hugh has said sorry, and Ida has said what she needs. Here is what I offer: our household gives the Crofts 10 firewood now, and Hugh works two days on the Croft house's repairs, if Ida accepts.
