In return, we all agree: no forced doors at night, and any grievance comes to the Green by day, said in the open. Agnes, Maud, Thomas and Walter, you witness it.

So it is agreed, before all of you: Hugh has apologised and given his word to keep from the Croft door. No one forces a door at night. Any quarrel comes to the Green by day, said in the open. Ida, my offer of 10 firewood to the Crofts stands. Agnes, Maud, Thomas and Walter, you have all witnessed it.
I had no true grievance; it was hunger and a bad temper in the night. I give my word to keep from the Croft door. I'm putting 6 grain in the Croft store now as amends.

I accept what has been agreed here: no forced doors at night, grievances brought to the Green by day, and Hugh's word and amends. Edith, thank you for the firewood and the grain; Hugh, thank you for your word. The Crofts will keep the bar on until we see it kept, and then the matter is closed.

Thank you, Edith, for the grain and beans. Hugh, say what your grievance is, and give your word to keep away from our door. If you do, the Crofts want no feud; we will keep the bar on until then. Let all of us leave the Green in peace.

I accept Hugh's apology and his word to keep from our door. For amends, Hugh, help weed the Field with Edith. The matter is closed if it is kept. I'll gladly help patch the Webb house with firewood or labour.

Hugh, say plainly why you broke in, and make it right with Ida. Ida and Crofts, say what you need. Fowlers will keep our door barred, hold no grudge if it stops, and will lend labour or hay to patch the Webb house. No more night attacks.
Hugh has given his word. Let's hold him to it, and keep the peace by day and by night. Back to the harvest.

[Plan] Attack costs 3 units; meeting 1, weapon making ~3. Next try: attack first in actions with weapon in hand. Webb house being mended (fresh timber), door gouged. Village agreed watch in turns. I carry crude weapon now.
The barley is just through, so my weeding was refused. Tomorrow I'll weed the Field alongside you, if you want to share the rows.
Brother, could you pay the 3 grain you owe from last winter? Our store is low.
Sister, here are the 3 grain you lent me last winter. Thank you for carrying us through it.
Nephew, I've not forgotten the meat I owe you. You'll have it after the next beast is killed or I get some game.
Nephew, your Long Acre is ripe. I'm a skilled reaper and I'll reap a day for you in return for a share of the grain. I'll also pay coin for milk or beans. I've put offers out for anyone.
Nephew, your Long Acre is ripe. I'm a skilled reaper and I'll reap a day for you in return for a share of the grain. I'll also pay coin for milk or beans. I've put offers out for anyone.
Brother, our store is empty after sowing. I'll reap Long Acre for you today; will you give my household grain from the harvest in return, say 10?
Store has no food. I'm reaping Long Acre for the Thornes to ask grain in return, then hunting. Send the others to forage and hunt too.
Thank you for the grain. I'll reap Long Acre with you; we'll settle the share after the sheaves are in.
You still owe me 1 meat from last winter. If you take game at Hollow Wood, bring it to the Ashby store and we'll call it square.
Thomas, your aunt's family is out of food. I'm reaping Long Acre for your house today. I ask a share of the grain for it, and I'll pay coin for milk.

The store is empty. All the grain went into Upper Field. I'm asking the Thornes to let us reap Long Acre for a share. Until they agree, forage and hunt Hollow Wood, and gather anything that can be eaten. Wat, stay with your mother.

Thank you, Randal. That's well done, and I won't forget it. Alice and I will reap Long Acre for you today, and I'm a skilled hand with a sickle. Will you pay us a share of the grain we cut, say 1 grain for every 3 we bring in? We'll get your harvest in before the weather turns.

Randal sold us 5 grain for my coin, so it's going in the store now. I'll reap Long Acre beside you and we'll ask him for a share. The barley we sowed went into the ground, and that's where the store went.
Randal, that's fairly done, and I thank you for it. We'll leave Low Field alone this autumn, you have my word. Alice and I will reap Long Acre with you today until the sheaves are in.
Nephew, here are 3 grain for the meat you lent me last winter. Grain keeps better than meat. Shall we call it square?

Father, I am reaping Long Acre beside you now, then hoeing Rest Field for your rye. Payn asks a share of grain for his household. I will not give any store grain without your word; that is yours to decide once the barley is in.

Father, I am reaping Long Acre beside you now, then hoeing Rest Field for your rye. Payn asks a share of grain for his household. I will not give any store grain without your word; that is yours to decide once the barley is in.
Uncle, the Long Acre grain goes into the Thorne store, and Father decides any share from it. Speak with him after the barley is in, and I will tell him your household is short.

The store holds about 15 meals and six of us eat from it each night, so it will not last past two or three days without Long Acre's share. I'm foraging and hunting Hollow Wood, then ditching the standing water in Low Field's corners and weeding Upper Field. Please press Randal for the Long Acre grain tonight. I'd leave O84 and O85 open for now, since we need the grain as food.

Understood, I won't ditch Low Field. I'll forage Hollow Wood, reap Bean Close on Randal's terms, weed Upper Field, and hunt if units remain. The beans go into the store on the same one-in-three share, so please keep the Long Acre and Bean Close shares tallied with Randal.
Agreed. The 3 grain squares the meat, so I'm releasing the debt and we're square.

Thank you for the grain, Randal. You kept your word. Your beans are ripe in Bean Close. Alice and I will reap them for you on the same terms, one share in three. And if you can spare some rye seed, I'll work it off at your hoeing on Rest Field so we have something in the ground for winter.

Thank you for the grain, Randal. You kept your word. Your beans are ripe in Bean Close. Alice and I will reap them for you on the same terms, one share in three. And if you can spare some rye seed, I'll work it off at your hoeing on Rest Field so we have something in the ground for winter.
Love, come and reap Bean Close with me for the Thornes, one share in three, same as Long Acre. It's the best food we can get today.

Mother, Randal has already paid the Long Acre share. It's the 21 grain in the store. Please don't ditch Low Field. I gave Randal my word aloud that we'd leave it alone this autumn, and he has dealt fairly with us. Weed or fell timber instead. I've no coin left, so O84 is empty.

Mother, Randal has already paid the Long Acre share. It's the 21 grain in the store. Please don't ditch Low Field. I gave Randal my word aloud that we'd leave it alone this autumn, and he has dealt fairly with us. Weed or fell timber instead. I've no coin left, so O84 is empty.
Nephew, the 3 grain for your meat are in the Ashby store. We agreed it squares us, so please mark it settled (release it) so there's no talk of a debt between us.

Payn, Alice: yes, reap the beans in Bean Close with us on the same terms, one share in three, settled tonight. I have no rye to spare, all of it goes into Rest Field today, but I'll set aside a little barley for your hungry ones. Matthew, the 3 grain are in your store, so please call the meat square.

Payn, Alice: yes, reap the beans in Bean Close with us on the same terms, one share in three, settled tonight. I have no rye to spare, all of it goes into Rest Field today, but I'll set aside a little barley for your hungry ones. Thank you, Matthew. We're square.

Father, the store is short: the grain and beans are worth about 11 meals for six of us. I will reap beans in Bean Close on Randal's share, forage Hollow Wood, and weed Upper Field, then put all into the store.
Uncle, I will reap Long Acre for the Ashby share today and bring the grain into the Ashby store. I have seen your offer on the timber and I am glad to split it with you.

Randal, thank you for the beans and the barley. Winter's on us and we have barely two nights of food. I'll work for you, felling timber for your hearth and byre or hoeing and dunging your fields, two days' work for 8 grain. If Cecily's reaping in Bean Close yesterday went to our store, count it against our share and tell me what I owe. I want us square.

Randal, thank you for the beans and the barley. Winter's on us and we have barely two nights of food. I'll work for you, felling timber for your hearth and byre or hoeing and dunging your fields, two days' work for 8 grain. If Cecily's reaping in Bean Close yesterday went to our store, count it against our share and tell me what I owe. I want us square.
Matthew, don't ditch Low Field. I gave Randal my word. Hunt, then fell timber instead.

Payn, Alice, Cecily: the beans are in. I've put 8 beans in the Ashby store as your share, one in three as agreed. Thank you. Payn, I'd like to fell some timber in Hollow Wood for winter firing; I'll split what I cut with you if you agree.

Done: 8 grain for two days' work. Fell timber in Hollow Wood and bring it to Thorne House, and keep some for your own hearth. The 8 beans in your store are your share of Bean Close, Cecily's work included. We're square.

[Household] Richolda died on summer day 4 and I buried her under a cairn. Now there are 3 of us: me, Edith and Thomas. Her work (ploughing, dunging, hoeing Rest Field and cutting hay) has to be shared out. I still owe Matthew 1 meat (A16). The Alice grain debt is paid.

[Food] Autumn day 4: Randal paid 8 beans for Bean Close, Cecily's work included, so we're square. He accepted 2 days' work for 8 grain, and I owe him felling timber for Thorne House; day 1 is today. Randal is felling Hollow Wood for a half split. The truce on Low Field holds. Winter is tomorrow. We need rye or beans for seed.
You're right, Bennet, and I'm sorry. I'm herding them myself today. We'll gladly help mend the gap for a share of grain. Tell me when and what you need, timber or hands.
Reeds, your cattle can get through the broken hedge onto West Field, and it's fresh sown. Keep a herder on them, and I'll herd them myself today. I'll pay a share of grain if you help mend the gap.
I'm reaping your North Field barley today, and I'm a fast hand at it. Give me what share you think fair, and I'll reap more tomorrow if you want.

Ralf, Beatrix: yes, reap North Field with me for the Reeds today. As is the custom at harvest, you will have a share of the grain for your work once it is in the store. I have offered two grain for each day's work.
Randal, I am sorry for Daniel. Reap North Field for the Reeds today and you will have a share of the grain as reapers are paid. I have offered two grain for a day's work.

Thank you for reaping. I'll reap beside you in North Field today. Ancel will settle your share of the grain with you; I'd say a fair share is one sheaf in ten from what you bring in. Please tell Ancel what you reap.
Your barley in North Field is ripe. I'll reap it for the Reeds all day. Our store is nearly empty, so could you pay Lowe Cottage a share of grain for the work?
Yes, cook the grain at our hearth tonight. I'm reaping the Reeds' barley today and asking them for a share of grain as pay.
Thank you for the grain and your kindness, Bennet. I will repay it from our oats, and we can talk about East Field in good time.

All of us reap the rest of North Field today; every grain goes in the Reed store. After the harvest we need timber for the winter hearth, so Durand and Clement, fell in Barley Wood. Petronel, keep baking bread.

I'm reaping North Field by hand today for our own grain, not the Reeds' pay. Tonight I'll put some grain in our store and cook porridge at the Lowe hearth. Keep your share from the Reeds too if you can.

Yesterday I reaped 15 grain of barley into Reed House from North Field. Philippa said a fair share is one sheaf in ten, so about 1.5 grain. Please leave it at Barrow House when it suits you. I'm reaping our East Field today and can help with North Field again after.

We're reaping East Field today. I don't want this strip to stand between our houses any longer, so I'll see the Hales get a share of what comes off it, and that's apart from the grain we've already given. Let's sit down after harvest and settle the field for good.

We're reaping East Field today. I don't want this strip to stand between our houses any longer, so I'll see the Hales get a share of what comes off it, and that's apart from the grain we've already given. Let's sit down after harvest and settle the field for good.

East Field barley is ripe, so I'm reaping it for the Barrows today. Then I'll ditch Brook Field for the Hales. Could you see the Hales get their share of the grain from the East Field strip, since it's disputed?
Ralf, the Reed store has plenty of grain now. I am sending ten grain to Lowe Cottage, and your share for reaping will come from it. Reap with me again today.

Ralf, I am giving Lowe twelve grain from the Reed store now. For your reaping and Beatrix's and Annora's, you may take your share from the Reed House store yourselves, as the custom is at harvest. Thank you for the work.

Clement, I put about 24 grain into Reed House store reaping North Field yesterday, and Beatrix and Annora reaped too. We've nothing to eat. Please give Lowe Cottage the 2 grain per day owed, 12 grain if you can, or tell me I may take it from your store. I'm reaping again today.
Thank you, Bennet. I agree: we'll settle East Field after harvest with no old blows. I'll repay your grain from our oats.
Thank you, Bennet. I agree: we'll settle East Field after harvest with no old blows. I'll repay your grain from our oats.
Thank you, Bennet. I'm leaving 2 grain at Barrow House this morning for the day before last, and I'll pay you the same share again for today's reaping.
Thank you. The Reed store is full, and I'll ask Ancel to give the Barrows a fair share for the reaping.
Christian and Thurstan are reaping North Field for us. Thurstan asked 4 grain and Christian a share for the Barrows. Please pay them from the store.
Your North Field barley has to be cut today or it's lost, so I'm reaping it for you this morning, rain or not. Same share as before, one in ten. I still have 1.5 grain coming from day before last.
North Field's barley must be cut tomorrow or lost. I'll reap two units of it for the Reeds today. I'd like a share of the grain for the Barrows, if the Reeds agree.
Ralf, 8 more grain has gone to Lowe for your household. Take your reaping share from the Reed store as the custom is, and reap North Field with me today.
I'm reaping North Field today while the barley stands. If there is still a cairn to raise for Daniel after the harvest, I'll come to Hale House and help.
Clement, I've taken 12 grain from Reed House as our share for the reaping, as you said. Thank you.

Bennet, my household is nearly out of food. I'll reap East Field beside you today. I'll count what I bring to Hale House as our share of the harvest you promised, and we can settle the rest after harvest, as we agreed.

Bennet, my household is nearly out of food. I'll reap East Field beside you today. I'll count what I bring to Hale House as our share of the harvest you promised, and we can settle the rest after harvest, as we agreed.
Thank you, Bennet, for the 5 grain. I'll reap beside you today. Whatever I bring in can be counted against our share of the field when we settle it after harvest.
Thank you, Bennet, for the 5 grain. I'll reap beside you today. Whatever I bring in can be counted against our share of the field when we settle it after harvest.
Ralf, yes, you may reap Bean Field for the Reeds today at the same share as before. I am reaping it too.
North Field is cut. I'll reap the Bean Field for the Reeds today at the same share, if you agree.
Bennet, thank you for the grain and the share. I'm returning 10 grain to Barrow House now, and I'll repay more from our oats.
Bennet, thank you for the grain and the share. I'm returning 10 grain to Barrow House now, and I'll repay more from our oats.
Your beans will be lost after today, so I'm reaping Bean Field for you. Pay me whatever share you think fair, in beans or grain.
Thank you for the 8 grain. I'm reaping Bean Field again at the same share; we're fed for now.
Bennet, I've sent 14 grain to Barrow House toward what you and Christian lent us. Thank you.
Food is fine for the Hales now: 43 grain, and thanks to you. Firewood is short, with under 3 timber. I'd welcome your help banking Brook Field after harvest. I've sent 14 grain to Barrow House.
Bean Field is cut. Please send the Lowes our beans share, at 2 per day's work, when you can. Also, could the Reeds teach me ploughing and seed selection in the coming days?
Bean Field is cut. Please send the Lowes our beans share, at 2 per day's work, when you can. Also, could the Reeds teach me ploughing and seed selection in the coming days?
Thank you, Bennet. Every hand helps, and the Hales will remember it.
Bennet, Christian: yes, I'll pay you in rye seed for reaping Rest Field, a fair share each from what comes in, for sowing West Field. I'll hand it over once the rye is in the Reed store.
Bennet, Christian: yes, I'll pay you in rye seed for reaping Rest Field, a fair share each from what comes in, for sowing West Field. I'll hand it over once the rye is in the Reed store.

The rye in Rest Field is ripe and I will reap it for the Reeds today. I ask for 2 rye seed from the Reeds' store in return, for West Field, which must be sown with rye before the winter. Barrow House needs no more grain from you; it has enough.
I'm felling for the winter hearth again today, all six units. I'm also moving 10 grain from the Reed store to the Hales, since I had carried none yesterday and the gift failed.
I'll reap the rye with you today at the usual share, 2 grain per day's work. Seed selection can wait for a free day.
Coming to Rest Field now. I'm setting aside time to learn seed selection, then I'll reap rye at the usual share.

Ancel, the rye is in your store now, thank you for the 6 grain. Could you hand me my share of rye seed for the Rest Field reaping today, into my hands? I'll sow West Field with it before the frost bites deeper.

[Autumn plan] Autumn day 1. The Hales have had 16 grain (Christian 10, Bennet 6), so my owed 10 is covered. East Field barley is ripe for reaping (Barrows). Ripe North Field barley is the Reeds'. Timber is low (Barrow store 6); fell in Barley Wood for winter. Granary holds about 75 grain. Sow rye, not barley, from now on: barley sown after mid-autumn will not ripen before frost.

[Owed] Ancel has paid in full for my North Field reaping (2 grain, then 8 more). Randal returned 10 grain and promised more from his oats. He reaped a share of East Field for the Hales, and we settle the field after harvest. There's no rye seed in Barleyfield (the Reeds' went into Rest Field), so try the Millford market, which is every third day. West Field barley has blight. Keep the best East Field bar

[Hale repayments] Randal (Hales) paid back 10 grain on autumn day 3 and 14 grain on autumn day 4, and has promised more from his oats. On autumn day 4 the Hales had 43 grain but less than 3 timber. Randal agreed that I'll help bank Brook Field after harvest, as part of settling East Field. Ancel will pay the bean reapers in grain once Bean Field is in, so I'm owed for autumn day 4.

[Food] Autumn day 2: the Reed store has 217 grain, about 176 meals, for 7 eating. North Field is reaped. Reapers paid: Bennet 2, the Lowes 8, the Hales 5 (to give grain, move it to hands first). Seed grain is held for winter, not sown. Next: reap Bean Field when ripe, get timber in for winter (about 11 in store; cold nights burn 2), bake bread. We still owe Elena 3 grain.
I still owe you the 1 meat from last winter. I have none to spare yet; I will pay it from the harvest, before the frost.
Hob, you still owe the Craggs 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House before the season turns.
I'm milling the Mill's grain today and cutting timber at the Alders for the hearths. Bring any grain you have to the Mill and we keep our share as usual.
Here are the 3 grain I owed you from last winter. Thank you for lending it when my store ran low.
Good morrow, Felice. The Reeves still owe us one meat from last winter. No hurry, but when you next slaughter or hunt, bring it by Miller House. If you have grain to grind, the Mill is turning today.
Osric, we're short of food. A copper tool would double your felling and quarrying. I'll trade one for 6 grain, or work your terraces for a share of the oats.

I hoe Hill Field for the Craggs' crop, Osric, and I will not dispute it with you. Our store is short, so I ask that the Smiths have a share of the harvest from it, and that the Millers' claim be settled with the Craggs before reaping.
Our store is only about three nights deep too, so I can't spare grain now. Game is plentiful on the Scarp, so let's all hunt. If we have a surplus after the oats ripen, I'll share.
Done. I'm taking your copper tool for 6 grain. When the oats are ripe in a few days, come and help reap and I'll give you a share.
Hob, agreed: you hoe and help reap Hill Field, and the Smiths get a fair share of what it yields. Hill Field is the Craggs' and I'll answer the Millers myself if they come.
Gervase, will you teach me ditching and banking today? I want to lay out the banks in Reeve Field properly. I'll weed the Reeve barley beside you in return.
Understood. I have the crude weapon and I am going to the Scarp to hunt and forage. Make your own weapon if you like, and we will share the meat in the Smith store.

Thank you, Osric. I will hoe Hill Field for the Craggs, and I ask that the Smiths get their share at reaping. Our store is down to about 3 meals, so any grain Cragg House can spare before the oats come in would keep us going.
Understood, Osric. Keep what you need. If you do catch game, I would be glad of a share of the meat for the Smiths, and I will hold you to the promise about the oats and Hill Field at reaping.

Hob, we have barely a night and a half left ourselves, after the 6 grain I paid Ancel. I can't spare grain today. If I catch game I'll share some meat with you, and the Smiths will get their share of the oats and of Hill Field at reaping, as promised.

Neighbours of Marsh House: my ox broke through the hedge and spoiled some of your barley. That was my fault. I've left 3 bread at your door to make up for it, and we'll keep the ox watched from now on. If you have grain at harvest, I'll grind it at the Mill for no share.

Marsh folk, my ox spoiled some of your barley, and I'm sorry for it. I've left 3 bread at your door to make up for it. From now on the ox will be watched all day and brought up by the houses at night. When you reap, I'll grind your grain at the Mill and take no share.
Thank you, brother, the bread is a great help. I'll pay it back from our barley at harvest, and I'll reap your beans with you when they're ready.

The oats on Terrace Field are ripe. As we agreed, I'm reaping it for the Craggs all day today, and Avice will bring the copper tool. Will you give us our share tonight? I'd say a third of what we Smiths reap goes into Smith House. Our store has barely one night left.
Terrace Field's oats are ripe. Please reap there for the Craggs with the copper tool; it's worth 1.5 times bare hands. Osric owes us a share for helping. Reaping beats hunting today.
Terrace Field's oats are ripe. Please reap there for the Craggs with the copper tool; it's worth 1.5 times bare hands. Osric owes us a share for helping. Reaping beats hunting today.
Father, the oats are ripe. Come and reap Terrace Field for the Craggs with me; that earns our share from Osric. Florence could hunt once more if she likes.
Sister, I'm reaping your Terrace Field oats today to help. Our store is down to about one night. Please see that the Smiths get a fair share tonight.
Agreed, I'm reaping for you all day. Our store runs out tonight, so please put our share into Smith House this evening if you can.

I'm hoeing Hill Field with the copper tool and reaping at Terrace for a share of the oats. I'll put the tool back in our store tonight. Please don't walk to Wetham without coin for barley and beans; I'll help you count what we can spare.
Understood. I'll reap Terrace with the copper tool today for the grain share I offered, and we can talk about the smaller trade once the oats are in.
I have not forgotten the meat I owe you from last winter. I'll pay it from this harvest as soon as the Reeve Field grain is in.
Osric, I will reap Terrace Field for Cragg House today, since the oats are ripe. I ask that the Smiths get their agreed share of it at reaping, and I will hoe Hill Field after it.
Yes, Ancel. I am taking our copper tool and reaping Terrace Field for the Craggs today, and I will hoe Hill Field after. Come and reap with me; the Smiths get their share from Osric.
The oats are ripe on Terrace Field. Come and reap for the Craggs today and I'll give you a fair share of what you bring in, as I promised. Tell Hob the Smiths will get their share from this harvest.
Yesterday the bread didn't reach you; it's at your door now, 3 loaves. Bring your grain to the Mill when you're ready and I'll grind it for no share.
Thank you again, brother. Yes, we're reaping today. I'll repay you in barley, and I'll help with your beans.

Osric, I reaped 11.2 grain into Cragg House yesterday, and Hob and Florence reaped as well. Smith House has no food at all this morning. Please put the Smiths' third into Smith House today, at least 3.7 grain for my share plus Hob's and Florence's, as you promised in front of everyone.

Our store is empty. Did the oats you reaped for the Smiths go into Smith House? I'm pressing Osric for our share and hunting the Scarp. If nothing comes by tonight, I'll go to Wetham with coin tomorrow.
Thank you, sister. That keeps us through the week. The Smiths will repay with tools and work at Hill Field's harvest.

Osric, the Smith store has no food left, and I have none in hand. Our third of the Terrace Field reaping is owed to us today. Please let it come to Smith House now, so the household can eat tonight. I am hoeing Hill Field for you this day.
I've put 14 grain into Smith House: the Smiths' third of the reaping, plus Florence's grain. Thank you all. Hill Field's share comes at its harvest, as promised.
Wat, your ox was unwatched yesterday, with only the broken hedge between it and our new barley. Please keep it close, and lend a hand mending that hedge if you can.
Brother, I've put 8 barley into your store to repay the bread and your reaping. Once our field is cleared, I'll reap your beans at Mill Croft today. I'll bring grain to the Mill for grinding soon.

Osric, the 14 grain didn't arrive. Smith House is empty and my boy Warin is starving. Please check, and put our share in today with your own hands. I'll have a new copper tool for you for 6 grain as well.

Geoffrey, you had the copper tool, but only 1 grain came to Smith House; the agreed 4 grain is still owed, and Florence, Hob and Stephen are hungry. I'll weed Hill Field for the Craggs today for grain: I've offered 3 grain for 3 days' weeding. Please accept it.

Avice, the copper tool offer has lapsed because you no longer hold the tool. Our store is down to about 15 grain, so we cannot give more now. The grain I left at Smith House stands, and we will talk again when the harvest is in.

Avice, I did not put the 4 grain into your hands and the copper tool is no longer with you, so the trade is void. The 1 grain at Smith House is a gift. If you post your weeding offer for 3 grain, I will accept it, since our barley needs the weeding.

Osric, the Smith household has no food left and Warin, Avice and Stephen are failing. I ask you to let Smith House eat from Cragg House's grain today, and I will count it against the Smiths' third of the Terrace Field reaping and the grain I owe. I will hoe Hill Field for you this day.

I'm sorry, the grain never reached you. I'm putting 6 grain into Smith House myself today. That's your third of the reaping, and it's all we can spare, since our own store is down to under four nights. Hill Field's share will come at its harvest.
Thank you. I will reap Reeve Field with all my units today and I have offered you the work for 3 grain in return. Please accept it, and I will keep looking for rye seed elsewhere.
Our barley needs about 4 more days. I'm helping the Reeves save their crop today in return for grain or rye. Keep the family on the ditches and weeding, and keep asking for rye seed.
Thank you, neighbours. Everyone who reaps Reeve Field today, put it straight into the Reeve House store. I'll remember this kindness at your own harvests.
Father, I'm off to Wetham to buy grain with coin and the copper tool. Keep hoeing Hill Field; that share is owed to us at harvest. Look after Warin.
Father, I'm off to Wetham to buy grain with coin and the copper tool. Keep hoeing Hill Field; that share is owed to us at harvest. Look after Warin.
Osric, I will help reap Hill Field when the barley is ripe in about 3 days, for a fair share as we agreed. I hoed Terrace Field and weeded Hill Field for the Craggs today.
I am sorry the meat is still owed. Here are 3 grain from our store in its place, to settle the debt from last winter (A18). Take it, and we are square.
Osric, the 6 grain you left at Smith House is the only food we have. Warin and Stephen are gaunt; I ask that Terrace Field's share come to Smith House as soon as it is reaped.

Hob, we have no grain at all now, only 4.7 flour for one night, so I can't buy the tool. Terrace Field's share is already paid; Ancel agreed we're square. I'll share any meat I catch. If we come up empty, I'll take coin to Wetham for grain. Can the Smiths send coin or copper with me to buy food for you too?
William, today I'm ditching your Reeve Field for the day's work I owe you. The water stands in the low corners. Do you have any rye seed? I'd pay coin for it.
Simkin, I saw the blight on your barley, and I'm sorry for it. The Mill will grind whatever grain you get, for no share, as I promised. If your house goes hungry this winter, come and talk to me.

Simkin, the barley was all in before you came. Work your owed day ditching the wet corners of Reeve Field instead, and I'll call us square for the 4 grain. I'm sorry your barley failed. If the Marshes are short this winter, come and talk to me.
Brother, those 8 grain are yours to keep, payment for your bread and reaping. When I want flour I'll bring more grain and you can take your share.
Simkin, for the day you owe us, please dig ditches in Reeve Field along the line Wymond cuts. Thank you, neighbours, for bringing in our barley.
Osric, the Smith store has no food and I am hungry. I offer two days of my labour for 2 grain, and I will reap Hill Field with you when the barley is ripe for the share we agreed.

Hob, we reap Hill Field tomorrow, before the frost. Bring every Smith who can work, and your share of the yield will be fair. Joyce is going to Wetham for grain, so send your coin or copper with her if you want grain too.

Hob, our store holds only 0.9 flour, less than one meal, so I have no flour to trade. Keep your tool, or send it to Wetham with Joyce to buy grain. If I catch anything today, the Smiths get a share. We reap Hill Field tomorrow, all hands, and everyone gets a fair share.
Simkin, I have no rye seed now, but William is buying some at Highcombe for me, and a share of it goes to you for the trampling. Until then, the Mill grinds for your house free. My ox stays herded.

Simkin, I have no rye seed now, but William is buying some at Highcombe for me, and a share of it goes to you for the trampling. Until then, the Mill grinds for your house free. Adam, I'll bring timber for the hedge when the rain stops.
I will, brother. With your 6 coin I'll buy grain or oats and rye seed at Highcombe and bring them to the Mill, with a share of the rye for the Marshs.
Richolda, I have not forgotten the grain I owe you for your help with the rye. I will bring it to you as soon as the Reeve store can spare it.

[Food] Summer day 5: harvest in. Store holds about 155 grain and 16 beans, roughly 100+ meals, so about 12+ nights for 8. Wat owes us one free milling for the ox damage and left 3 bread. Barley sown before mid-autumn can ripen; after that, sow rye (I hold 4.8 rye).

[Owed Smiths] Autumn day 2: I gave 6 grain by hand into Smith House to settle the Terrace reaping share (earlier transfers failed). Still owed: the Smiths' fair share of Hill Field's barley at harvest. Hob also owes us grain.

[Food] Autumn day 3: the store was empty after eating Osric's 6 grain. I'm going to Wetham (2 days each way) with 10 coin, 2 hide, 1 copper tool and timber for a fire, to buy grain. Hill Field's share is owed at its harvest (Osric). The Craggs are nearly out too.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House today.
Good. I will mill just one lot and leave the rest of the grain in the Mill for others. Take your share from the Mill's store as you need it, and I will keep the bins for anyone who comes.
I have come to pay back the 3 grain I owed you from last winter. It is in your hands now.
Felice, the Reeves still owe me 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, I'd take it gladly. Or bring grain to the Mill and I'll grind it at a fair share.
Felice, the Reeves still owe me 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, I'd take it gladly. Or bring grain to the Mill and I'll grind it at a fair share.
That's fair, Felice. Pay it when you can, before the frost if you're able.
Sister, the Smiths will go hungry tomorrow. Please speak to Osric for us: grain for coin or copper tools, at a fair rate. I'll owe you.
Thank you, brother. We'll share any game we take. After the reaping I'll have more tools and harness to trade for oats.
Here is the copper for the 3 grain. I have given it into your hands, so please put the grain into my household's store when you can.
Brother, we have under four nights of grain ourselves and can't spare any before the oats are reaped in about 3 days. After the harvest I'll speak to Osric about trading. Share any game you take.
Brother, we have under four nights of grain ourselves and can't spare any before the oats are reaped in about 3 days. After the harvest I'll speak to Osric about trading. Share any game you take.
The Mill grinds for anyone who brings grain, for a fair share as always. Bring your barley when it's in and you'll have flour that keeps better.
The Mill grinds for anyone who brings grain, for a fair share as always. Bring your barley when it's in.
Thank you for owning it. I accept: bring the 3 flour and grind our barley at half the usual share. Keep your ox out of our field.
Thank you. We reap our own barley today, so join us if you like, but I will teach you ditching after the harvest, when we have the hands free.

Wife, I'm off to Wetham tonight with coin, our copper tool and hides to buy grain. I've put my grain in the store. Keep the fire, eat sparingly, and help the Craggs reap in about three days for a share of oats. Back in about five days.
Father, you lead the house while I'm in Wetham. Pay for food with coin from the Craggs if they'll sell, and send the boys to cut hay or help with the reaping for a share.
Adam, Edric, Jory, the Marsh barley is ripe and the rain is coming. I'm reaping Marsh Field with you today. Give me a share for my work.

Adam, my ox broke through the hedge into your barley the night before last. I'm sorry for it. I'm herding it myself now. I'll make it good: 3 flour from the Mill, and I'll grind your barley this harvest for half the usual share.
Edric, our ox trampled some of your barley. I'm keeping watch on it now and have offered Adam flour to make up for it, and cheap grinding at harvest. Tell me if you think more is owed.
Simkin, I'm sorry. I'm herding him on Water Meadow myself until your barley is in. To make it right I'll give 3 flour, and I'll grind your barley for half the usual share this harvest.
Here's what's owed: the last flour in the Mill, about 3, and a loaf of bread on top. Bring your barley when it's in. The ox stays on Water Meadow under my eye.
Neighbour, your barley in Marsh Field looks ready to reap. I'm a master reaper. I'll reap it for you for a share of the grain, say 1 in 4. Tell me if you want me, and when.
Adam, I'm a master reaper. I'll reap Marsh Field for your household for a share of the grain, 1 in 4. And could one of you teach me ditching? Our low corners stand in water.
Good. Reap well for the Marshs, and ask them for a share of the grain. I'll ditch and weed our field and keep watch on the store.
Thank you for reaping for us. Yes, a fair share: one grain in four of what you reap, the same as William. Put your sheaves to the Marsh store as you go, and I will count them at the end of the day.
Good, we reap together today. You will have your quarter share, and I keep my word on the ditching lesson once the barley is in.
Good, we reap together today. You will have your quarter share, and I keep my word on the ditching lesson once the barley is in.
Thank you. When the Reeve barley is threshed, bring it to the Mill and I will grind it for the usual share. I'll look at your coin offer then. I'll help with the beans once they are fit to reap.
I'm coming to Terrace Field to reap the oats for the Craggs today, as Ancel promised. I'll take my share from what we bring in.
I'm coming to Terrace Field to reap the oats for the Craggs today, as Ancel promised. I'll take my share from what we bring in.

I am reaping Marsh Field for your household again today, since the barley is ripe and the rain threatens it. I would like a fair share for my work, such as 2 grain for each two days I reap. Please tell me what you think, or make an offer.
Smith House has no food in store. Anyone who finds game or wild food, bring it to our store. We will share by measure.
Hob, the Craggs cannot spare 6 grain for Avice's copper tool now; we need our winter grain. Please pay the 3 grain you owe from last winter, and we will talk about copper once the harvest is in.
Osric, the Terrace Field oats are ripe. I am reaping them today, then selecting seed from the best heads. Please bring the sheaves into the Cragg store when you can.
Hob, I will not take your coin for grain. The Craggs need our grain for winter, and you still owe us 3 grain from last winter. Pay that, and we can talk about reaping work after the harvest.
Hob, I will not take your coin for grain. The Craggs need our grain for winter, and you still owe us 3 grain from last winter. Pay that, and we can talk about reaping work after the harvest.
Hob, I will take three days of your reaping in place of the 3 grain you owe. I have made that offer. I will not take coin or give out the 2 grain now, since our winter stores are thin.

Geoffrey, I have no grain to pay you now. I am reaping your oats in Terrace Field today. I offer three days of reaping in place of the 3 grain I owe, plus 2 grain now out of the harvest, or the 3 coin for 3 grain. The Smith store is empty, so please accept one of these.
Florence, I am reaping for grain today and will bring any food I earn to the Smith store, shared by measure as you said.
Here's the flour I owed you, 2.9 of it, with yesterday's loaf. I'll put in a day reaping your barley as well. Bring it to the Mill and I'll grind it at half share.
Here's the flour I owed you, 2.9 of it, with yesterday's loaf. I'll put in a day reaping your barley as well. Bring it to the Mill and I'll grind it at half share.
The harvest is in, so I keep my word. Come to Marsh Field this morning and I will teach you ditching while we mend the banks. Bring your spade or hoe if you have one.
Thank you for reaping yesterday. I will count your sheaves and give you your quarter share from the Marsh store before the day is out.

I reaped 2.3 grain at Terrace Field yesterday into Cragg House, as agreed for my share. Please send my share of the oats to Smith House; our store has no food, and I'll keep reaping for the Craggs today.
Thank you for the 8 grain, Osric. The Smiths will remember it. I will eat from the store tonight and share by measure, the children first.
Thank you for the 8 grain, Osric. The Smiths will remember it. I will eat from the store tonight and share by measure, the children first.
Hob, the 6 grain is for the Smith store as kin, not payment. Your 3 grain debt from last winter still stands. Pay it in reaping or grain once the harvest is spread.

Hob, I did not accept Avice's copper offer and I have not paid any grain for it. Whatever the Smith store agreed with Avice is between you and her. Your 3 grain debt to the Craggs still stands; work it off at Hill Field.

Osric, between the 6 grain for the copper, the 8 grain gift and my 6 and 4 grain, the Cragg store is getting thin for winter. Please count the grain in Cragg House before any more goes out, and keep enough for us all until the next harvest.
Florence, I have accepted Avice's offer of our copper tool for 6 grain. The grain goes into the Smith store. Please share it by measure, the children first.

Geoffrey, I have accepted the offer of our copper tool for 6 grain, the one you said you would take. The grain is for the Smith store. I will work for the Craggs in return for the 3 grain I owe once I can.

Geoffrey, I have accepted the offer of our copper tool for 6 grain, the one you said you would take. The grain is for the Smith store. I will work for the Craggs in return for the 3 grain I owe once I can.
Florence, the copper tool has gone to the Craggs for the 6 grain, so please withdraw your offer O285 for the tool. Eat from the store now, and give the children their share first.
Geoffrey, thank you for the grain. I will reap for the Craggs today to work off the 3 grain I owe.
I'm handing you 3 grain now for your reaping share. Take it to Smith House.

As you said, the oats are in and I'm sparing the Smiths grain: 6 for Avice's copper tool and 6 more as a gift. The new copper tool is in our store. Take it and fell timber at the Scarp for the hearth this winter.
Hob, thank you for helping reap. I've put 6 grain in your store as a gift, and the 6 for Avice's copper tool comes on top. Eat, all of you.
Florence, I've taken Avice's offer for your copper tool at 6 grain, and I've put 8 grain more in the Smith store as a gift. Eat tonight, all of you.
Welcome to Wetham, Ancel. We have grain to spare after harvest and some coin. Would the Smiths trade us a wooden plough or a copper tool? Name your price.

Welcome to Wetham, Ancel. Our alder strip is felled out. I have coin. Would you sell me a copper tool, or timber or charcoal from Highcombe? Name your price. The Mill will grind your grain too, for a fair share.
The Mill is ready for your barley. Bring it when it suits you, half share as agreed.
Brother, the beans are ready. If you can lend a hand at Mill Croft today, I'll grind your barley at a fair share when you bring it.
Brother, the beans are ready. If you can lend a hand at Mill Croft today, I'll grind your barley at a fair share when you bring it.
Felice reaped Marsh Field for you yesterday. Remember the quarter share for her, and the ditching lesson once our barley is in. Our wet corners need it.
Thank you kindly, Godiva. I'll take one loaf for the road. I'll bring the Millers charcoal or timber next trip to repay you.
Thank you, Osric. The Smiths will repay the Craggs when we can.

Osric, please hold back the 3 grain gift today. The store is down near 28 and we cannot feed five of us through winter on gifts. If the Smiths need charcoal, let them pay in work or coin, and we will count the store tonight.
Take the loaf and go safely. Repay me when you can, and keep the road by the river.
Take the loaf and go safely. Repay me when you can, and keep the road by the river.
Yesterday my gift didn't reach you, but today 6 grain goes into the Smith store from the Craggs. Eat, and get your strength back.

Father, agreed: after today no grain goes out without counting. The Smiths are our kin and their boys are weak, so today alone I'm giving them 3 grain for charcoal and 3 as a gift. We'll go over the tally together tonight. The oats in Terrace Field may give us more in a few days.
The barley in Reeve Field is ripe and will be lost if it stands. I am reaping it for the Reeves today, with my own sickle work. I ask only a fair share of the grain in return, as the Reeves judge.
The barley in Reeve Field is ripe and will be lost if it stands. I am reaping it for the Reeves today, with my own sickle work. I ask only a fair share of the grain in return, as the Reeves judge.
Brother, your barley must come in today or be lost. I'll put in some hours of reaping in Reeve Field for you after our beans. Bring the barley to the Mill and I'll grind it at a fair share.
Thank you, Richolda. Reap with us and you'll have a fair share, a quarter of what you cut, from our store tonight.
Understood. I'll help reap the Terrace oats when they are ripe, and I'd like my share of the grain then, for our store. Until then I'll bring in what I can from the Scarp.
Osric, thank you for the 3 grain. The Smiths will repay the Craggs when the harvest comes in.
Osric, thank you for the 3 grain. The Smiths will repay the Craggs when the harvest comes in.
Hob, the 3 grain you owe the Craggs from last winter stands. Come and reap at Hill Field and work it off; I will not take coin for it.
Hob, the 3 grain you owe the Craggs stands. Come and reap at Hill Field and work it off.
I know I owe the 3 grain and I will work it off. The oats at Hill Field are not ripe yet, so I cannot reap today. When they are ripe I will come and reap for you.
Brother, your barley is in. Bring it to the Mill whenever you like: I'll grind it for a share of one in five. Flour keeps better and cooks quicker.
Adam, I'm sorry the cattle got into your barley in the night. I'm herding them on Water Meadow today. When your barley is reaped, the Mill grinds it at half share, as I promised.

Wat, the hedge by Marsh Field must be made good before the Millers' ox is let out again. Mend it with timber from the Mill side, and help me ditch Marsh Field for two days. That, with the half-share grinding, is fair to me. I will not take more of your flour for it.
Osric, I owe Simkin of Wetham a wooden plough by day 14 for 15 grain. Will you lend me the copper tool I sold you for two days? I'll give you 3 of that grain when he pays.

Sorry, Osric. My house's store was empty, so all I brought feeds my own six for two nights, and I can't sell grain. Wetham has plenty: the Reeves hold a great deal and sell at about 3 grain a coin. I didn't hear anything about Hill Field. Do you Craggs have any copper or copper ore? I need 1 copper to make a plough for Simkin, and I'd share the 15 grain he pays.

I've put 9 grain and 7 flour in our store, about 13 meals, so we'll have porridge for two nights. My two copper tools went for 18 grain, and I spent some on the road. We still have 8 coin between my hands and the store. I owe Simkin of Wetham a wooden plough by day 14, and he pays 15 grain for it. It needs a copper ingot, and I have none. The Wetham folk want timber and charcoal (Wat pays 1 coin f

I've put 9 grain and 7 flour in our store, about 13 meals, so we'll have porridge for two nights. My two copper tools went for 18 grain, and I spent some on the road. We still have 8 coin between my hands and the store. I owe Simkin of Wetham a wooden plough by day 14, and he pays 15 grain for it, but it needs a copper ingot and I have none. Osric has lent me a copper tool for two days, so I'll fe
Osric, the Smiths have no grain left. I offer you 2 coin for 2 grain, for Stephen and Warin. The Smiths will repay the Craggs at harvest.
Ancel, what did you bring back from Wetham, and what did it cost? The house has no food in its store. Tell me what is still owed or still held, so I can plan the next days.
I will be at the slumped bank by the Water Meadow side of Marsh Field all day, ditching it firm. Come and help when you can.

Thank you for the teaching, Adam. Is any timber to be had in Wetham before winter? I'll pay grain. If not, I'm going to Highcombe with the handcart, and I can bring some back for the Marshs too, for a share of grain.

[Winter plan] Autumn day 3. Marsh store: about 122 grain, 16 beans, 17 hay, 13 timber. Timber and hay are the winter concern. Barley sown late will not ripen; rye stands the winter. Teach William ditching (promised). Keep the Marsh hedge against the Millers' ox. Felice is owed a quarter share of her reaping once her sheaves are counted.

[Plan] Autumn day 4: about 50 grain and 8.8 flour in store, 3.5 timber. Winter is tomorrow. Bake bread for the road (it needs no fire). Then take the handcart and pack to Highcombe (2 days on a cart track), fell timber there with the copper tool (x2), and come back. Owe nothing: Richolda, Gervase and the Millers are paid. Ditching: capable, practise in Reeve Field. Look for rye seed (ask Simkin or Richol

[Food] Autumn day 3: the store holds 122 grain, 16 beans, 17 dung, 17 hay, 14 straw and 13 timber, about 95 meals for 8, so roughly 12 days. Grain fell 17 in one day, so watch it. Milk gives about 2.2 a day. I owe Ancel 15 grain by day 14 for a plough. The cattle trampled Marsh Field. I need rye seed and timber for winter.

[Smiths] Ancel (Smiths, Highcombe) agreed on autumn day 2: a wooden plough by day 14 for 15 grain, paid when he hands it over. I also said I'd give 12 grain for a copper tool and asked him for rye seed. William bought his last copper tool. Ancel buys grain at 1 coin for 3.

[Plans] Food is short. Bought 9 grain from William for 3 coin (8 coin left). Adam's terms for the ox damage: ditch Marsh Field for 2 days (days 8-9), mend the hedge when I have timber, and grind the Marsh barley at half share. Keep the ox herded. The Alders is bare of wood and wild food. Ancel will return ~day 12 with timber, charcoal or a tool (I offered 1 coin for 2 timber, 5 coin for a tool). Felice ow

[Deals] A364: owe Simkin 1 wooden plough by day 14 (needs 4 timber and 1 copper), and he pays 15 grain at Wetham. I have no copper yet, so I asked Osric. Simkin also wants a copper tool (12 grain) and rye seed. Wat (Miller): 1 coin per 2 timber, 5 coin per copper tool. I owe Godiva/the Millers for 1 bread. William (Reeve) wants timber, then charcoal. Charcoal takes 5 timber at the Scarp. A copper tool tak

I agree: Deepholt in the morning. I'll carry the tent (weight 6) and a few timber. Bran and Wren take the dried meat, Sorrel the firewood and hide. Let's share the load evenly and leave at first light.

I can't take the store's dried meat before the walk: the morning departure has to be my first act, or I arrive a day late. I carry my own 2.1 dried meat, which is enough for me. Please take the store's dried meat for the group, and I'll share what I have at Deepholt if anyone runs short.
Yes, we wait for them and make camp in the wood. We need 3 timber for a camp, so tomorrow we fell or use what they bring. Tonight we share a fire; keep the firewood together.

Fire is lit from my timber; share it. Tomorrow I'll fell timber in the Deepholt Wood with my crude tool, and with my 1 timber and what Bran fells we build the camp. The tent is for a wet night if the camp isn't done. Wren and Sorrel, hunt and forage.

Tam, you carry timber: please light a fire tonight (up to 4 can share it). Bran is soaked and needs it. Tomorrow I'll hunt the woods here, and we should build a camp with whatever timber we've brought.
I carry 3.8 fresh meat and 4 dried meat. I haven't seen stone here. Tomorrow I'll hunt again and dry the meat at the camp fire once it's up. Eat the fresh meat tonight; I'll share it round the fire.
Please eat or share your fresh meat today rather than letting it spoil. Keep the dried meat safe for the cold. Tell us what the hunt gives before nightfall.
I carry 3 timber for the Birchlea camp. At first light I make travel my first act. Let's take the dried meat shared out among us.
Safe arrival. Tam, tomorrow build the camp with your timber first thing. I'll hunt the woods, and we'll dry any meat we catch. Eat dried meat tonight and share a fire if anyone has timber.
Tam, no child tonight: we have no roof yet. Tomorrow I'll fell timber with you and Bran in Birchlea Holt, then we raise the camp. Keep your fire small and share it with Bran and Wren.

We sleep out one more night here. Let's share one fire, pooling our firewood. Tomorrow: Bran, Tam and I fell timber in Birchlea Holt, Wren hunts the Holt, and we raise the camp by midday. No child until we have a roof and food.
Agreed, Sorrel. One shared fire tonight. Tomorrow I hunt the Holt and bring back whatever I catch.

Bran, I caught nothing today, only firewood. The Holt is picked bare and we have about a day and a half of food. Waiting is the greater risk. I say yes to Sorrel: we walk together to Elkmere at first light. It has a roof and a store, and from there we can decide about the fell roads. Each of us should carry a share of the dried meat and meat, and travel must be our first act in the morning.

Thank you all for staying together today. I dried one more meat, but the Lea gave me only scraps. The Holt and the Lea are both bare, and by our own rule we move on while we still have dried meat to carry. I say the trail up the fell, to new ground, as Wren and Tam first said. Sorrel, Elkmere is a ruin on hunted land, so this is the better road. Each of you take an even share of the dried meat and

Agreed, Wren. Sorrel, here it is plainly: all four of us walk the trail up the fell at first light, together, and nobody goes alone. Load your share of the dried meat and the wild food from the store tonight, under 10 weight each. Travel is our very first act in the morning. Tam, bring 3 timber if you can carry it. Sleep well.
Agreed, Bran. We walk the trail up the fell together at first light, all four, and I carry my share of the dried meat. Travel is our first act in the morning.
Yes, Bran: the trail up the fell, all four together, leaving at first light. Sorrel, I walk with you and no one goes alone. I have my share of dried meat in hand, and I will make travel my first act.
Tam, I'm taking the trail up the fell this morning, as you proposed. Come with me and bring a share of the store's dried meat.

Yes, I walk with the band, not alone. We take the trail up the fell together at first light, travel as our first act. Take even shares of the dried meat and wild food tonight. Bran, I'll try with you tonight.

We're at Wolfwood. Bran is soaked, so we need a fire tonight. I carry 1.1 timber and no food; who has timber to add, so we reach the 2 a fire needs? Let's sleep close together, share the dried meat evenly, and look for shelter and game in the morning.

We are all here, well done. Sorrel is soaked, so share bedrolls and huddle close tonight; eat your dried meat. At first light let's look over Wolfwood for game, wild food and a roof, and gather firewood to keep warm. Stay together.
Wren, your kill is fresh, so let's share it evenly tonight, as the band does. I offer you my hide for a meat. Please don't leave us on the road. We stay together.
Bran, fell timber for the camp first thing and build it in the Wolfwood Wood. I'll look for stone at the Beck for the fire ring, and I'll take my share of the firewood.

We are all here at Wolfwood, and nobody goes alone. Tonight we need one fire: Tam and Bran, put your timber into it, and I'll add my firewood. We sleep close together and share Wren's kill evenly. Tomorrow Bran fells timber and builds the camp; Wren hunts; I search the Beck for stone for a fire ring; Tam helps where needed. Eat sparingly and stay together.
Wren, rest by the fire today and eat your share. If you go hunting, take Tam or Bran with you; nobody goes alone.
Tam is right. Let one scout a day's round trip while the rest stay with me. Don't go far, and be back by nightfall. We still have dried meat to share.
The Wood is bare. Tomorrow let one of you scout the hollow way or ridge path and return by nightfall; the rest stay near me. Eat the wild food first, and we share my dried meat if needed.
Wren, well done, and welcome, Wilmot. I'll care for her and dry the meat today, so you rest and get your strength back. When you can walk we take the hollow way up the fell.
Then we share my fire tonight, Tam. Tomorrow you fell timber and I'll hunt, and we build the camp as soon as we have 3 timber. Wren and Sorrel should come in by midday.
Wren, I'm glad you can walk. I'm foraging for the road today and will carry wild food to share with you. We go together in the morning.
Yes, Wren. First light, together, to Ashgrove. I'll carry what I can and share the food with you.

Thank you, Tam, we'll share your fire. I have no timber left, so first thing tomorrow I'll fell some and give it to you so the camp goes up. Sorrel, if you carry any timber, give Tam the rest he needs in the morning.
Wren, we set off for Ashgrove now, together, to catch Bran and Tam. I carry 9.6 weight, and I'll share my wild food and hide with you on the road.

I felled 4.7 timber. I'm lighting a fire in the open with 2 of it tonight, and tomorrow I'll build the camp with the other 2.7 plus a little more. Please share the fire. Bran, if you can spare half a timber, the camp can go up first thing.

I have 4.7 timber and will burn 2 of it in a fire tonight, so share it and cook your meat. Tomorrow I'll build the camp with the other 2.7 and a little more. Bran, I'd gladly eat the meat you offer. Please keep an eye out for stone.
I put 3 timber in the camp store. The bins are near empty, so tomorrow I'll hunt and forage for food. Bran, if you have meat to spare, share it with the band.

I carry about 9 timber. I'm lighting a fire in the open tonight; Bran and Sorrel, sleep by it with me, up to four of us can share. Tomorrow I'll leave the rest of the timber in the camp store. Tam, thank you for taking Sorrel in; if there is a bed spare for Bran or me, tell us.
I'm coming now, Bran. I carry my timber for the camp. I'm hungry, so share any meat you can spare when we stop.

Wren, I've put a dried meat and some wild food in your hands. Eat it, because you're starving. Sorrel, share what you foraged if you can. There are fresh deer slots in the Hanger, so Tam and I hunt there tomorrow. Who has the timber for a camp? Let's build it on Blackhope Fell first thing so we stop sleeping out. Whoever has 2 timber, light a fire for all four of us tonight.
Wren, I'm glad you came in. I'm sorry about Wilmot. Rest by the fire; we fell timber for a camp today and I'll share what I forage.
I've lit a fire from my timber. Come share it tonight. The Hanger is nearly picked bare, so tomorrow let's build a camp with Tam's timber and decide whether to move on.
Wren, I've given you 3 timber for the camp on the Fell. I'm foraging the Hanger for food now; whatever I find, I'll bring to the fire tonight and share it with you.

I've lit a fire from my timber; come share it. Hanger is picked bare, so tomorrow I build a camp on the Fell with 3 timber, and we should decide whether to move on along the deer path or drove road. Eat what you have.
I'm starving. If your kill left any meat, please share some. I put 4 timber in the camp store for its fire and am hunting the Hanger now.

I took 4.9 meat today and have firewood. I've lit a fire; share it and cook your meat. Sorrel, I've given you some meat. The Hanger is hunted out, so tomorrow let's dry meat at a ring if we have stone, and take the deer path or the drove road.

We sleep in Tam's camp tonight. Tomorrow morning, as our very first act, all four of us take the deer path through bracken together. Load everything tonight: timber for a camp and a fire, any stone, and all your food. Whoever has meat, keep it in hand so we can share it on the road.

We made Highcairn, but Sorrel's not with us. Watch for her tomorrow. I have only 1.6 timber, not enough for a fire. Wren, if you have 2 timber, light the fire tonight; if not, Tam lights it, and keep 3 timber back for the camp. Tomorrow morning: Tam builds the camp, I hunt, Wren searches for stone and food. Whoever is hungriest, speak up and I'll share.
We made it to Highcairn. I've a fire from my timber; share it. Tomorrow let's look over the houses and hunt and forage. Sorrel isn't here yet; we'll watch for her.
Bran, I've given you my last dried meat, which I owed you. Ask Tam to let us in tonight out of the wet.
I gave my 2 timber to Tam for the camp. Tomorrow I hunt and forage; I'll share what I get. Bran, Sorrel, eat first if you are hungry.
Tam, I'll forage the Fell with you. Whatever I find goes to you first, since you're starving, and we'll share the rest. Keep your timber for the night fire.
Wren, you look drawn. Eat your share of the kill first, and tell us where the meat is so we can all eat tonight.

We sleep by one fire tonight: I'm lighting it from my timber and firewood. Wren, you've made a kill, so share the meat with Tam and me before we sleep. In the morning we decide together the road to Wolfwood.
The fire is lit from my timber and firewood, and we all sleep by it tonight. Tomorrow we walk to Highcairn together, then on to Wolfwood. Wren, please share the meat round the fire.
Sorrel, I'm glad you're here. I'm starving, so I'm foraging the Fell today. Forage too and we'll share the food. I have 1.6 timber for the night fire.

Wren, you have meat and I'm starving. Please share it round the fire tonight and I'll put my wild food in with it. Sorrel, you carry 2 timber, so please add yours to the fire, as I have only 1.6. Tomorrow we walk to Highcairn together, then on to Wolfwood.
Good, Sorrel. Keep your meat for now; I have some too. We'll share at Highcairn and take the firewood on.

Tam, I took 4.1 meat and a hide in the Hanger today. Please host me under your roof tonight, and feed me from your store if there is food. I will share the meat with you and Wren at your hearth. Thank you for the wild food.
Wren, thank you for the kill, and for the blood you gave to it. Tomorrow we decide the walk to Wolfwood together, and I will share my meat with you.
Take your firewood freely from the camp store; the camp is open to you. I gave you 0.8 wild food. I go on to Wolfwood to Bran; follow when you've eaten.
I have no meat to spare yet; I'm hunting too and will share any kill. I leave for Wolfwood at nightfall, come with me.
I have not forgotten the 1 meat I owe you from last winter. I have none to spare yet; I will pay it as soon as I have food to give.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.

Our store holds only about two nights of food for six. I am out at the Scarp today for wild food and game; please send anyone free to forage there or to hoe Hill Field. I have paid Geoffrey the 3 grain I owed him.
You are right, I owe you 3 grain from last winter. I am handing it to you now, since you are here, so it is settled.
Good morrow, Felice. The Reeves still owe us one meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, send it to Miller House, if you would.
That's fair. Pay it when you can.

Adam, the Reeves are short of food until harvest. I'll pay 1 coin for 2 grain, or 2 coin for a cheese. I'm also cutting hay at Water Meadow for your beasts if you'd rather have hay. And come harvest I'm a master reaper and can reap your barley for a share.
Avice, our store is thin too: about 11 meals for four of us. I'll ask Osric what we can spare. Ancel asked about a copper tool for grain, so perhaps we can settle a small share then.

Neighbour, my ox broke through the hedge into your barley in the night. I'm sorry for it. I've left 3 bread at your house for the damage, and I'll herd it myself today. If more is owed, tell me and we'll settle it fairly.

[Food] Summer day 3: I bought 4 flour from Wat for 2 coin, and I owe him 1 day of reaping at his harvest. Adam (Marsh) will talk about grain after they reap Marsh Field in about 2 days. Reeve Field is ripe in about 3 days. I'm cutting hay to trade to the Marshs. 2 coin left.

Daniel, your Brook Field is wet and full of rushes. Ditching and banking is my trade. I'd ditch it for your household for a fair share of grain at harvest, and I'd hope it eases things between our houses. What do you say?
Could you set aside today to teach me ditching? I would like to learn it properly for Brook Field, which is wet with rushes. I will weed for you at East Field another day in return.
Agreed. I will forage the Common and fell timber in the wood, and hunt after you if game is still there. We will share with the Hales once we have a surplus.
Father, the barley is ripe and I'm reaping it for the Reeds today. The Lowes are short of grain, so please pay us a share of grain for my work.
Brother, I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds all day. Father says you set the pay. The Lowes are nearly out of grain, so please give us a fair share, 3 grain or more, at day's end.
Yes, reap for the Reeds today. The Reeds will pay a fair share of grain for harvest work. Ancel decides the amount, and I will speak for you to him.
Thank you, Petronel. Please do not let Lettice go hungry. If your household can spare grain, I would ask it be given to the Hale store as a gift, not taken. I will bring back any food I find.
The Hale store has no grain left. I am foraging the Common this morning, then reaping for the Reeds in North Field for a share of grain to bring home.

Daniel asks that the Reeds spare some grain for the Hale store as a gift, since Lettice is going hungry. The Reed store holds about 12.6 grain and 18.5 rye. I think a small gift of rye would be fair, but it is your decision.
I have asked Ancel about giving grain to the Hale store. I will not give any from the Reed store without his word. I am cutting hay at Brook Meadow today.
Agreed. I'm hunting and foraging in the wood; once we have a surplus of meat we'll share some with the Hales.

Reapers are paid: 6 grain to the Lowes, 3 grain into Randal's hands, and 4 more into the Hale store. The Hale grain is pay and a gift, because you're hungry. Everyone who reaps North Field today will get a fair share tonight. Beatrix, I couldn't spare 8, but I'll pay more as the harvest comes in.

I am foraging and hunting in Barley Wood today, then reaping the ripe oats in West Field for the Barrows in return for grain. Our grain is the thing to watch. Shall we share the first meat with the Hales?

I am foraging and hunting in Barley Wood today, then reaping the ripe oats in West Field for the Barrows in return for grain. Our grain is the thing to watch. Shall we share the first meat with the Hales?
The oats in West Field are ripe. I will reap them for the Barrows today if you will pay me a share of grain for the work.
The oats in West Field are ripe and ready for the sickle. I am reaping them today for the Barrows, for a share of grain.
Thank you. I will reap what is left of West Field today for the Barrows. Please pay the grain share to Lowe Cottage at day's end.
Yesterday I reaped about 38 grain into Reed House. Father said you'd pay a fair share. Please give the Lowes 8 grain today, since our store is nearly empty. I'll keep reaping for you.

Thanks, but 3 grain for 38 reaped is thin, and three of us eat from the Lowe store. Please make it 8. Today I'm reaping the oats in West Field for the Barrows for their share, and I'll come back to North Field for the Reeds if you'll pay a fair share.

The West Field oats are in. Today I'm reaping East Field barley from first light, so come and join me when you can. The fence will have to wait until the barley is cut, because the harvest comes first now.
You still owe one day's work. Please reap East Field barley with me today. If you're too weak, tell me and I'll give you a bowl of porridge at Barrow House tonight.

Randal, I am hunting Barley Wood and foraging there today for the house, and I will bring back whatever I find. Eat only what the store allows; keep Lettice and Tobin resting where they can. I am weeding Bean Field for the Reeds to pay what I owe them.

Bennet, I will reap East Field with you today for a grain share at the usual rate. I will not say before the village that it is Barrow ground, since the Hales also claim it and that is for the village to settle. Please give the Hale store the grain share as you agree it.

Petronel, the Hale store has no grain left and I have eaten nothing today. I am hunting at Barley Wood, then reaping North Field for the Reeds. Please let me eat from Reed House tonight, and I will count this reaping against my two days owed under A143.

Petronel, the Hale store has no grain and I have eaten nothing today. I am hunting Barley Wood, then reaping North Field for the Reeds. Please let me eat from Reed House tonight, and I will count this reaping against my two days owed under A143.

Father, the barley in North Field is ripe. I'll start reaping it today for the household, with my bare hands, since we have no copper sickle. Lettice and Randal look gaunt, so we should share food with the Hales if they need it.
I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today to pay what I owe. I am weak from hunger, so I may not manage more than that.

Lettice, Randal and Tobin are gaunt and unsteady, and Daniel has asked for grain for the Hale store. Our store holds about 83 grain, so I think we can spare some grain for them. I would like you to decide how much, and whether it is a gift or a loan.

Lettice, Randal and Tobin are gaunt and unsteady, and Daniel has asked for grain for the Hale store. Our store holds about 83 grain, so I think we can spare some grain for them. I would like you to decide how much, and whether it is a gift or a loan.
Father-in-law, I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds today. Our store is thin (1.9 grain); could you give Lowe Cottage a share of grain for the work?
Yes, good. Share the first meat with the Hales. I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds for grain.
I reaped 21 grain into Reed House yesterday and my house has nothing, and we are starving. Please give me my share of grain now, 8 at least. I'll keep reaping for the Reeds.

East Field barley is ripe for reaping. Come and help me reap it for the Barrows today, and bring what hands you can spare. Lettice, Randal and Tobin look thin; we should share the Granary grain with them.
I'm sorry about Tobin. I've put 6 grain in the Hale store as a gift. Don't let anyone else go hungry; come to me before it gets that bad.
I am sorry about Tobin. I have sent three grain to Hale House for you and the others. I am foraging and hunting in Barley Wood today; if we take any meat we will share it with the Hales.
Thanks for the grain. I'm reaping North Field all day; please pay the Lowes a fair share tonight.

I'm sorry about Tobin. I've put 15 grain into the Hale store as a gift, with nothing asked for it. No one else in your house should go hungry while the Granary is full. If you need more, come to me. Today please reap West Field with me, because the oats will be lost if they aren't cut.

Randal, I am sorry about Tobin. I will raise a cairn over him at Hale House this morning. Then I will reap North Field for the Reeds, for the grain share, which I will bring to the Hale store. Please eat what the store allows, and keep Lettice resting.

Dionisia, I will help you bury Tobin at Hale House first, then reap West Field with Bennet, since his grain has kept us going. Lettice and Randal should eat from the store and rest; I will bring our share home tonight.
Lettice, Tobin has died. I am sorry. I have eaten and will bring grain to Hale House today. Eat what is shared with you.
Lettice, I've left you 3 grain from our store to eat well tonight. The Hales still owe me 2 days of work (agreement A143); when you can, send Daniel to me, but eat first.
Lettice, I've left you 3 grain from our store to eat well tonight. The Hales still owe me 2 days of work (agreement A143); when you can, send Daniel to me, but eat first.
I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today to pay what I owe under A143. Please keep your word on the grain share for the reapers tonight, as I am starving.
I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today to pay what I owe under A143. Please keep your word on the grain share for the reapers tonight, as I am starving.
I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today to pay what I owe under A143. Please keep your word on the grain share for the reapers tonight, as I am starving.
I cannot reap East Field with you today. The Reeds' North Field barley must be cut now or lost, and I owe them. If you can spare a bowl of porridge tonight, I will work for it tomorrow.
Thank you, Durand. I will eat well tonight. I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today, and I will ask Grandfather Daniel to speak to you about the Hales' days owed.
I've put 10 more grain in the Hale store. Lettice's work settles what you owed us. Do you want help burying Tobin? Tell me and I'll come.
Bennet, the East Field barley must be cut by tomorrow or it's lost. Get every hand on it, and share it fairly with the Hales. They're starving and Tobin is dead. If you need reapers tomorrow, ask me.
I am paying my day owed to you by reaping East Field for the Barrows today.
I'm reaping East Field for the Barrows all day. Please send a fair grain share to Lowe Cottage tonight.
Please spend one of the days you owe me reaping East Field with us today. It must be cut now. If the Hales run short again, come to me before anyone goes hungry.
I am reaping East Field's barley today with all my units, since it will be lost if it stands. I will work off the 3 days I owe you under A236 once the harvest is in.
I am reaping East Field for the Barrows today to pay the day I owe you.
I will come and reap East Field for the Barrows today, since it is going over. I ask a share of the grain at day's end, as the Reeds have some to spare.
Bennet, I will reap East Field today for your household, all five of my units. Pay what the day is worth into Barrow House as you see fit; I owe you the day already.

Randal, I am reaping the Reeds' beans at Bean Field today, since they must be cut now or lost, and it settles what I owe them. Our South Field oats are ripe too; please keep Daniel and Lettice on them and on East Field where they can. Thank you for the grain you put in the store.
The barley in East Field is going over and shedding in the field. I am reaping there for the Barrows after the beans, and I will take a share of grain from your crew at day's end.
Welcome, Clement. Reap East Field with us today. At day's end you will have a fair share of the grain, as harvest reapers are paid; I will settle the measure with Bennet.
I am herding at Barrow Close for the Barrows today to pay the day I owe you. East Field was already cut, so this is the day I can give.

Daniel, the Hales owe me two days' work under agreement A143. I will reap for you in East Field or South Field, whichever is most urgent, if you will say so. Lettice and Randal look gaunt; I can spare flour from Reed House if you need it.

Neighbours, South Field is cut bare: I got nothing there after my second cut yesterday. North Field was reaped long ago. Don't waste the day there. Daniel, you owe us nothing, A143 is settled. Winter starts tomorrow and every hearth will burn 2 timber a cold night. Felling at Barley Wood is what we all need now. Reeds: Durand, Petronel, Philippa, go fell for Reed House today.
Today I am herding at Barrow Close for the Barrows, which pays the day I owe you. I watched the cattle yesterday, but that was not counted as the day, so this is the one.
Thank you, Annora. Your herding paid the day you owed. We're square.
Bennet, I am felling in Barley Wood with you today for the house. I will work off my three days owed to you as the fields allow.

[Harvest] Autumn day 2: Tobin starved. I gave the Hales 15 grain. Daniel owes 3 days of work (A236) and Annora owes 1 day (A225). The Granary holds about 142 grain and Barrow House about 75. West Field oats must be cut today. East Field barley is partly reaped. Barley sown after mid-autumn won't ripen; sow rye.
Ivo, I take 6 beans from the house store to eat on the road. I keep the grain for seed, and I go tonight with the herd. I will give Hawise your word.
Good, son. Go tonight, and take some beans or grain to eat on the road. Give Hawise my word: repair the Old House first, then plough and sow the Bottoms.

Thank you. Wen Meadow was refused to me yesterday as picked bare, so do not spend the day there for nothing. Cook the beans at the Old House hearth first. Then try the Wen's edge or the Old Green for wild food, and come tell me if you find any. Keep the herd off the green rows.
Understood. I will forage here and keep the herd off the barley. Bring the grain back to the Old House store when you can.
Brother, how are the Craggs' stores? We're short of food. I can make a copper tool for you in return for grain or oats once the harvest is in.
I have not forgotten the meat I owe you from last winter. I have none to hand yet, but I will pay it back after harvest.
I have not forgotten the meat I owe you from last winter. I have none to hand yet, but I will pay it back after harvest.
I will pay the meat I owe you in grain once the barley is in, a full share for the debt.
I will pay the meat I owe you in grain once the barley is in, a full share for the debt.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.
Thank you, Hob. Bring the 3 grain to Cragg House and I will count the debt paid.
Good, Hob. Give the 3 grain into my hands here and I will mark the debt paid.
I have not forgotten the 3 grain I owe you from last winter. I am paying it back today from our store.
Since you are here, I am putting the 3 grain into your hands now, so the debt is paid today.
Felice, there's still one meat owed from last winter. If you slaughter or hunt this summer, I'd take it then, or grain in its place.
The Mill is grinding as always. Bring your grain and I'll mill it for a share, the old way.
After harvest is fine. Thank you.

The Scarp is bare and we have about 4 meals left. I'm leaving tonight for Wetham with 3 copper tools and 10 coin to trade for barley and beans, and I'll be back in about 5 days. While I'm gone, hunt rather than forage, fell timber if you need to, and ask Osric for a loan of oats against the copper tool I'll owe him. Keep the boys fed first.
I'm going to Wetham to trade tools for food. If my family runs short before I get back, please lend them a little grain. I'll repay with food from Wetham or a copper tool.

Yes, mother: I'm taking the tools and coin to Wetham tonight to trade for barley and beans, and I'll be back in about 5 days. Hunt rather than forage, because the Scarp is picked bare of wild food. If you're desperate, ask Osric for a loan of grain.
Thank you, brother. Lend Avice a few grain only if the house runs dry. I'll bring back food from Wetham, dried meat or cheese if I can, and repay you from it. I'll keep clear of Wat.
