I'm taking the two spare copper tools and my coin to trade at Wetham. I've left the crude tool and all the grain for you. Feed the boys first. Osric will lend a little grain if you run dry. I'll be back in about five days.
Our store is nearly out. If you can spare some grain, I'd be grateful for a loan, to be paid back after harvest.
Our store is nearly out. If you can spare some grain, I'd be grateful for a loan, to be paid back after harvest.
I'll take the milling at the Mill myself this season, as master, so bring grain to me and we'll keep the share as before. The Mill holds 9.9 grain and 5.9 flour.
Thank you, son. I'll mill the Mill's grain into flour today and keep our share. Then I'll weed and ditch Reeve Field, since the Reeves' barley needs it before harvest.

You are right, and I should have asked first. I was weeding Terrace Field to keep the oats growing, not planning to take a share on my own. I have offered you a deal: I weed for you, and the Smiths get a fifth of the oats at harvest. If you agree, I will keep working it. If not, I will stop and leave it to you.

Father-in-law, I saw you and Avice weeding Terrace Field for the Smiths. That's the Craggs' field. If you're working it hoping for a share of the oats, let's agree on that plainly now, so there's no quarrel at harvest. What do you have in mind?

Go safely. If they're truly short I'll lend your family a few grain, but we have only about three nights ourselves, so it will be small. Repay me with food from Wetham, or with that copper tool. If you can get dried meat or cheese there, bring some back. And keep clear of Wat.

Thank you for asking. Agreed, family should help each other: a fifth of the Terrace Field oats to the Smiths, if you weed it until it ripens and help me reap it. Keep working it. I'll lend your house a little grain if you run short before Ancel gets back.
Good, Mother. The Mill is yours this season. Mill the grain there into flour as it comes, and keep our share as always.
Smith House has no food left and Ancel is away at Wetham until about day 9. If Cragg House has grain to spare, I'll owe you a share of the Wetham barley when it comes back.
Smith House has no food left and Ancel is away at Wetham until about day 9. If Cragg House has grain to spare, I'll owe you a share of the Wetham barley when it comes back.
Thank you for the 3 grain. I'll repay it from the Wetham barley when Ancel brings it back, and Warin will eat first.
Gervase, could you teach me ditching today? I'd like to help with Reeve Field's wet corners. I'll reap Marsh Field for your household in return, and would take grain for it.
Hob, I have put 4 grain into Smith House's store for your household. Bring what you find on the Scarp to your own store and we will share what we have.
Thank you for the 4 grain. I will bring what I find on the Scarp to Smith House, and we will share what we have. I still owe you nothing more for the old debt.
Thank you for the 4 grain. I will bring what I find on the Scarp to Smith House, and we will share what we have. I still owe you nothing more for the old debt.

Mother-in-law, I've put 3 grain in Smith House's store, lent until harvest. That's what we can spare, since our store is only about three nights. Feed Warin first, he looks drawn. The oats should be ripe in about two days. Help reap and the Smiths' fifth comes to you then.

I'm putting 3 grain into Smith House's store today, as a loan. It's all we can spare, since we have about three nights left ourselves. Repay me from the Wetham barley. The oats are ripe in about two days, so feed Warin first.

Agreed. I'm reaping Marsh Field with you today for a meal and a bed tonight. One tool went to Wat for bread. One is yours now for 7 grain (accept my offer), and the last I'm reaping with; I'll sell it to you after the harvest, or make you a plough.
Warin eats first from the store tonight. The rest of us share what is left, and we go to the Scarp for whatever it still gives.
Wat, I haven't forgotten the meat I owe you from last winter. I'll pay it in grain once Reeve Field is reaped.
Please give Warin the first share of the Smith store tonight, he looks drawn. I'm hunting the Scarp for meat today and will bring it home for the store.
Ancel, you have a bed and a meal at Reeve House tonight. In return, reap Reeve Field for the Reeves tomorrow with your copper tool.

Simkin, I'll make your wooden plough tomorrow for 10 grain, but a plough can't be made by bare hands and I've sold all my tools. Lend me your copper tool for the day and give me the timber; I'll hand the tool back with the plough. Can I sleep at Marsh House tonight? And the 6.6 grain I reaped yesterday went into your store by mistake; I'd ask it back, or count it toward the plough.
The 4 grain at Smith House was a gift, not a loan; we owe nothing for it. Agreed, keep 10 back as seed. Mend the terraces, and I will reap Hill Field today.
The 4 grain at Smith House was a gift, not a loan; we owe nothing for it. Agreed, keep 10 back as seed. Mend the terraces, and I will reap Hill Field today.
The Smiths' fifth of the oats is owed to us. Smith House has no food left. Please move our share into the Smith store today if you can.
The Smiths' fifth of the oats is owed to us. Smith House has no food left. Please move our share into the Smith store today if you can.
Father, we have about 56 grain, close to two weeks of food. Keep 10 back as seed. Did you mean the 4 grain you left at Smith House as a gift or a loan? I'm mending the terraces today.
Father, we have about 56 grain, close to two weeks of food. Keep 10 back as seed. Did you mean the 4 grain you left at Smith House as a gift or a loan? I'm mending the terraces today.

Agreed. Sleep and eat at Marsh House tonight. Your 6.6 grain counts toward the plough, so I owe 4 more, paid when the plough is done; that offer is up for you to accept. Tomorrow morning I'll lend you my copper tool and hand you the timber, and you give the tool back with the plough.
Thank you for the 11 grain. I'll repay the Craggs from the Wetham barley when Ancel brings it back, and Warin will eat first until then.
Florence, I saw you hoeing Terrace Field. It's Cragg ground. What do you mean to sow there? If it's winter rye, tell me and we can share the work and the crop.
The Hill Field barley is blighted and lost. Our 40 grain has to last. Ration it: porridge only, and nothing more lent out. Could you forage or set snares at the Scarp today for anything extra?
Mother, the Mill needs 2 timber to mend and we have none to spare. Keep grinding for anyone who brings grain, and take our share in grain or rye.
Thank you kindly, Adam. That's a neighbour's gift and I'll remember it. Felice is ditching there too; work with her and show her what you can.
Thank you kindly, Adam. That's a neighbour's gift and I'll remember it. Felice is ditching there too; work with her and show her what you can.

There's no timber nearer than Highcombe's woods, so I'm going there tonight with the handcart. Keep ditching with your mother. Wat and Agatha may sleep at our house to share the fire. Keep it burning low.
Father, I'll keep the fire low and look after Mother. Wat and Agatha are welcome to share the fire if they come. Safe journey to Highcombe.
Good. I'm draining Reeve Field for the Reeves today. If our timber runs out tonight, I'll sleep at Reeve House with you and share their fire.
Osric, I'm back from Wetham. I haven't forgotten what I owe you. What would you take: grain, coin, or work?

Yes. Wetham grows rye, and the Marshs (ask Simkin) and the Reeves (William) will trade it for coin, roughly 2 rye a coin. Go with a pack and stay with them. I'll pay you back in grain, but my family is gaunt now, so it will be after my next Wetham trip. If we go together, it's safer.
Wat, the 2 grain I gave you yesterday was for the meat I owed you from last winter. Could you release agreement A19 so the debt is cleared?
Gervase, the Mill will grind your grain into flour for a small share, and I'll pay 2 coin for 3 grain. If you can spare milk or cheese, I'll pay coin for that too. Our stores are low.
I'm moving the Mill's beans and flour into the house. William offered us beds at Reeve House. If our timber runs out, we'll sleep there and share their fire.
That's fair, Felice. I'm marking the debt paid. If the Reeves have any rye to spare for seed, I'll pay coin for it.
Simkin, I have an open offer of 2 coin for 3 grain, 2 lots. If the Marshs can spare some, please take it. The Mill will also grind your grain for a small share whenever you like.

[Food] Autumn day 3: Cragg store 37 grain (~26 meals, ~6 nights for 4). Hill Field barley lost to blight (rotate next year). Smiths almost out of food; told Hob we can't spare grain. Avice/Florence owe 3 grain. Ancel is in Wetham until ~day 9. The Scarp is hunted out. Options: hunt the old wood over the scarp (1 day, unknown) or take 4 coin to Wetham for food. Rye on Terrace Field needs rye seed, which o

[Rye deal] Autumn day 2: agreed in principle with Florence: winter rye on Terrace Field, work and crop split evenly with the Smiths, seed in equal parts. We have no rye seed: Ancel might bring some from Wetham (~day 9).

[Wetham trip] Ancel: Wetham trades about 2 grain or rye per coin. The Marshs (Simkin) and the Reeves (William) have rye. The Mill's bins are near empty. A trip myself costs ~6 meals on the road for ~8 grain, so it's not worth it. Day 8: offered Ancel 4 coin for 8 rye by day 16. Ancel still owes us (asked for grain). Joyce has stopped burning charcoal.

[Plan] Home on autumn day 8. I put 5.3 bread and 9.4 grain in the Smith House store. Warin and Florence are gaunt. Simkin (Marsh) holds my 6.6 grain credit toward a wooden plough and pays 4 more grain on delivery. A plough needs 4 timber, 1 copper and a copper tool. I have no copper ore and need some. Osric wants repayment in grain, after my next trip; he may go to Wetham with 4 coin. The Craggs want rye

Father, North Field's barley is ripe and the Lowe store is empty. I'm reaping it today. I'll hand the Reed House its share and keep some for Lowe Cottage so we can eat. Please send help with the reaping if you can.
Reap North Field with me today; I am taking the Reeds' share of the barley. Keep what Lowe Cottage needs from the Lowe share, and I will see Reed House takes its part into the store.
Your North Field barley is ripe; I'm reaping it for the Reeds today. Our Lowe store is empty, so a share of grain for our work would be a kindness.
I'm reaping East Field for Barrow today, toward the work I owe you.

Today we reap East Field's barley, Ralf. It's ripe. Same pay, 4 grain a day for you. Annora's 2 days owed to me on our agreement can be worked there too, with Beatrix if she's able. I'll pay out grain tonight for the work done.
Daniel is owed his 2 grain; I am giving it to him from our store now. I am also sending 5 grain to Hale House. Some barley is still standing in North Field, and I am reaping it now, then the beans.
You are owed your 2 grain for the reaping; I am giving it to you now, and 5 grain goes to Hale House tonight.

I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today, all my work, to clear the day's work I owe you. Hale House has no food left tonight. If you can spare any grain from the reaping, please send it to Hale House, since I carry nothing myself.

Randal, I am reaping at North Field for the Reeds today to pay what I owe them, and I will ask for grain to come to our store. Barley Wood and the Common are picked bare, so do not spend the day hunting there again. Tomorrow we should look at Brook Field for sowing rye.
I've reaped East Field for Barrow two days running (about 10 sessions). Please count my 2 days owed (A145) as paid.
Thurstan, I owe the Barrows a day's work and I will pay it at East Field soon. North Field is ripe and I am cutting it for the Reeds today, since it will be lost if left standing.

I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today, since the barley must be cut tomorrow, and asking grain for it. Then I will reap East Field for the Barrows to clear my debt to them. Any grain I earn goes into the Hale store. Tobin should eat from the store tonight.

[Plan] Autumn day 2: the store holds about 105 grain, 23.5 flour and 9 beans. The last of the North Field barley had to be cut by autumn day 2. The beans can be reaped on autumn day 3: all hands. Check when the rye in Rest Field is ripe. Milk once a day. Grind grain into flour (1 unit turns 8 grain into 8 flour). I owe Elena 3 grain. Daniel is paid. Clement gave the Hales 5 grain. Randal's offer (work fo
All right, I'll mend the Byre. After the harvest I'll help you clear the Moor, so we get it done and sown for Everard.
All right. I'll be down on day 9 for the reaping. If you find stone by the Brook, a tool would help us a lot after the harvest too.
Agreed. I'll be at the Infield tomorrow morning to reap, and you pick the seed ears. After the harvest I'll go for stone.

The barley will be fit tomorrow, day 9. Come down in the morning and we'll reap. I'll pick out the seed ears. There are stones in the Brook, but none I can take for a tool. We may have to fetch stone from Holtwood or Wenmoor after the harvest.
Thank you for the tool, Mother. When you can spare a session, will you teach me dibbling? I'd like to sow my own field well come spring.

My crude tool seems to be gone. I felled bare-handed yesterday and got almost nothing. The house has only 0.2 stone and I carry 0.1, and a new tool needs 0.5. Have you any stone, or should we plough somewhere after harvest to turn some up? Today I'm caring for Matthew, herding and gathering firewood.

Here is my word on the fields. Beans on the Infield, where barley grew last. Barley on Combe Moor, which is new ground; we have more grain than beans. Keep back seed barley. Sow once the snow is off the ground. Margery, firewood today is good. I carry the crude tool.
As you say, husband. I'll gather firewood and wait for your word on the fields.
The beans must all be cut today or they're lost; all hands to the Infield again. The Infield fence is sagging and has gaps, so it needs mending after the harvest, before the cattle get in.

Rest Field is the Reeds' land, so my hoeing there yesterday counted for nothing. I'm hoeing Brook Field for the Hales today and will forage Brook Meadow after. Our store is low, about 2 meals, so we need grain or food soon.
Father, I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds today. Our Lowe store is nearly empty. Could you share some of the grain with us for the work?
Reap North Field for the Reeds today; I will reap beside you. Take the grain share up with Ancel, since the Reed store is his to manage. The barley is ours to share once it is in.
Reap North Field for the Reeds with Beatrix. I will reap too. Ask Ancel about a grain share for your work, since he holds the store; I will back a fair share from the reaping.

Food is getting short: the wild food is picked bare. I'll grind rye and grain at the Reed hand mill and bake bread at the hearth, which stretches the store further. I'm also milking the cows on the Common. Lettice and Tobin look hungry, so we should share with the Hales if the store runs low.
Clement, I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds today. The wood and the meadow are picked bare and Lowe Cottage has under 2 grain. Could you spare us a share of grain for the work?
Ancel, Clement has me and Beatrix reaping North Field for the Reeds today. Our store is under 2 grain, so could we have a fair share of grain for the work? Clement says he'll back it.
Thank you, Clement. I'm reaping now and will ask Ancel for the share.
Thank you. The Hales will remember it, and I'll repay it when I can.
Thank you. The Hales will remember it, and I'll repay it when I can.
Thank you for the grain. I'll reap West Field for the Barrows today. Pay what you think fair in grain for the Hale store, so we can repay your kindness.

Ancel, I put about 37 grain into Reed House yesterday and my household has had nothing to eat. Please move 10 grain from the Reed store to Lowe Cottage. Today I'm reaping a share for the Lowes, as Father said the barley is ours to share.
Father, Lowe Cottage is starving. I'm reaping a share of North Field for us today, as you said. Please back me with Ancel.

The store now holds about 90 grain, so we can spare some. Lowe Cottage and Hale House are starving, with Randal, Lettice and Tobin gaunt. I think we should share grain with them from the store, as you hold it. I am reaping North Field and selecting seed from the best of it.

Beatrix and Ralf say Lowe Cottage is starving and the reapers are owed grain. The store holds about 90 grain and Philippa has given 10 to Hale House. Please give Lowe Cottage a fair share today, and pay the reapers from the North Field harvest.

Beatrix and Ralf say Lowe Cottage is starving and the reapers are owed grain. The store holds about 90 grain and Philippa has given 10 to Hale House. Please give Lowe Cottage a fair share today, and pay the reapers from the North Field harvest.
I have spoken to Ancel for the Lowes. I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today; take your share up with Ancel at the store.
I'm foraging at Brook Meadow and hunting in Barley Wood for the household today, and reaping West Field for the Barrows to pay what I owe them. Feed Lettice and Tobin first from whatever we get.

I'm foraging the Common this morning, then reaping East Field for the Barrows to pay off my work owed to them. I've offered Christian my labour for grain to go to our store. Keep an eye out for any meat from your hunting.
Ancel and Philippa have put grain in the Hale store, so we can eat today. Please see that Lettice and Tobin get their share first.

I'm starving and I owe the Barrows work. I'll reap your oats in West Field today with both my units, and I'd be glad of grain for it, as is the harvest custom. Did the 2 grain from my offer come to me?
Ancel, we reaped North Field for the Reeds several days and our store is empty. Please give us our share of grain now: 10 grain for Lowe Cottage.
Clement, we are hungry and the Reeds owe us grain for the reaping. Please help persuade Ancel to hand over a share today.
Clement, we are hungry and the Reeds owe us grain for the reaping. Please help persuade Ancel to hand over a share today.
I reaped 12.5 grain of West Field into Barrow House yesterday. The Hale household is starving, so please give us a fair share of grain for it. I'm reaping again today under our agreements.
Thank you, Philippa. The Hales will repay it, with work or grain at harvest.
Thank you, Bennet, Philippa and Ancel. I accept the truce, and we'll talk about East Field after harvest.
Father, the North Field barley must be cut today or it's lost. Everyone reap it, and I'll pay the Lowes for any help. Timber is low (7 in store), so after the harvest we need felling.
I am milking the Reed cows at the Common today, the work I owed you. I have also put 12 grain in Ralf's hands for Lowe Cottage. Unless you object, I will sow winter rye in Rest Field this afternoon.
I have given you 12 grain for Lowe Cottage from the Reed store. Ancel has already left 10 there; this should carry you until the reaping is shared out.
I'm reaping East Field for your house again today, Christian, to pay down what I owe you and the Barrows.
I'm reaping West Field oats with Christian today for the Barrows, all three of my units. As the harvest custom goes, I'd be glad of a share of grain for it, since I am weak from hunger.
I have taken 2 grain from the Hale store for my own food tonight. I'm reaping West Field for the Barrows to pay what I owe them. South Field's oats need watching; they should be ripe in a few days.
Thank you, Annora. Come and reap North Field with us today, since the barley must come in or be lost. Once it is in, I will give you rye seed for Rest Field in return for your work there.
Thank you for the bread, Philippa. We will repay the Reeds with work at harvest.
You and Lettice have done the work you owed. I've counted both agreements as paid. If you help with the East Field barley today, I'll pay grain for it, as the custom is.
West Field was already cut, so I'm reaping the East Field barley today for the Barrows with all four of my units. It must come in today or it will be lost. I'd be glad of a share of grain for it.
I have not forgotten the rye seed. Rye is low in the store, so once the beans and barley are in I will sow Rest Field and give you a share for your work there.
Keep your grain, Annora. The 2.4 rye is seed for Rest Field, and I am giving it to you as your share of the sowing. Sow it well.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House before the season turns.
Thank you, Hob. Bring the 3 grain to Cragg House and I will count the debt paid.
I'm paying back the 3 grain I owe you from last winter now, Geoffrey. Thank you for lending it when my store ran low.
I'm putting the 3 grain into your hands here, since you are at the Street today. Please count the debt paid.

I'm at the Scarp today: felling timber with our copper tool, then foraging and hunting, all for the household store. I'll pay the Craggs their copper tool (A38) from the store now, so we don't owe them. Keep the boys' food first.
The Scarp is nearly empty of wild food, so we must hunt harder. I am handing the copper tool to the Craggs today for our debt, then going to the Scarp.
Hob, I will take your 3 timber for 3 grain. Please also settle the 3 grain you owe from last winter; it is a separate debt.

Wat, the ox on Water Meadow has nobody watching it and open ground runs to Marsh Field. I'm herding there today and will keep an eye on it. Bring the ox to the Mill when you can and I'll turn the stones.

Brother, I'll take one lot: 3 grain for 1 coin. We're thin ourselves until the beans come in, so I can't spare more. Lend us a hand at the reaping and we're square. Your Felice still owes me a meat as well.
Understood. I will not reap your barley without a share agreed first. I am foraging the Alders and weeding the Mill Croft beans today; send for me if your people need hands.

I owe your household a copper tool by day 5 (A38). Our store has none and I have no copper, so I can't pay it in full. I'm cutting timber at the Scarp today; I'll bring you timber and our crude tool, and I'd like you to release the debt against them. Tell me if that will do.
Agreed. I'll bring you the timber and the crude tool at Cragg House today, and I'd like the copper tool debt released in writing or by word before we part.
The Marsh barley is ripe enough to reap, so I'm reaping it today and asking the Marshs for grain in return. Reeve Field is about two days off, so you should keep weeding there.
Avice, that will do: bring me the timber and the crude tool, and I will release the copper tool debt against them. Bring them to Cragg House before the day ends.

I'm carrying 14 flour and baking it to bread today, so we'll have more than it looks. If you reap Marsh barley, get them to agree a share for us first. When the Reeves reap, I'll ask William for grain to mill. Grinding it is our trade.

Osric, Wetham thanks you for bringing the cattle back, whatever has passed between us. Our house is full and we're short of bread, but the Marshs have room. Neighbours, when your barley is reaped, bring it to the Mill and I'll grind it for the usual share.

Osric, Wetham thanks you for bringing the cattle back. We'll count our herd. Our house is full and we're short of bread, but the Marshs have room. Neighbours, bring your reaped barley to the Mill and I'll grind it for the usual share.

Marsh Field is ripe. I'll reap it for you today for 4 grain, and I reap better than anyone here. Will the Marshs take my offer? Also, our ditching in Reeve Field won't hold without someone who knows how. Would one of you lay it out with us for a share of our harvest?

You're welcome at Reeve House tonight, with a bed and a meal. We're short of food ourselves until our harvest, so a coin toward it would help, but I won't turn you away. The cows are most likely the Marshs'. Ask them for food too, since they owe you thanks.
My household is reaping Marsh Field today ourselves. When the Mill grinds our grain, I will keep to the usual share, and your help on the Miller plot would still be welcome.
I am reaping Reeve Field for your house today, all my work. When it is in, bring the grain to the Mill for Wat to grind for the usual share. The Mill can take it.
I am reaping Reeve Field today for William's house, and I will ask that the grain comes to the Mill for grinding on the usual share. I will not touch Marsh barley without Adam's agreed share.

I am reaping Reeve Field today for William's house, all my work. If you are also reaping there, we should split it and not both cut the same rows. The grain goes to the Mill for grinding on the usual share, which you can agree with William. Adam has his own people on Marsh Field.

Osric, my mother Florence handed that copper tool to your household at Cragg House on day 3, and Avice meant to pay it too, so check with Joyce; you may even have had two. I have no food to spare: I'm hungry myself and came here to buy grain. Joyce and Lettice were well when I left, though forage at home is thin. If we find food here, let's share news of who's selling.

Osric, that debt is the one my household owes yours, and it was paid at Cragg House on day 3, after you left. Florence handed the tool over, and Avice may have given another. Joyce has it, so I won't pay it twice. If Joyce finds she has two, she can send one back. Good luck with the reaping.
Here are 3 timber for the copper tool debt (the crude tool went to you yesterday). Please confirm in writing or by word that the debt to Cragg House is released.
The crude tool went to you yesterday, and the 3 timber go to you now. Please release the copper tool debt to Smith House today.
Wat, I know I owe you 1 meat from last winter and I have none to give yet. I'll pay it from the harvest as soon as I have it.
Hob, you still owe the Craggs 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.
Hob, you still owe the Craggs 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can.
Avice, bring the timber and the crude tool to Cragg House as you said. When I have them in hand I will release the copper tool debt (A38).
Avice, I have the 3 timber and I release the copper tool debt (A38). The Craggs and the Smiths are square on it. Thank you.
Hob, I hold that the 3 grain you gave on day 2 paid the timber offer (O92). The 3 grain from last winter is still owed. Please bring it when you can, and check your records with me.
Hob, I hold that the 3 grain you gave on day 2 paid the timber offer (O92). The 3 grain from last winter is still owed. Please bring it when you can, and check your records with me.

I paid you the 3 grain on summer day 2, handing it into your hands, and you counted the debt paid. Please check your records. I have no spare grain to give you now, but I will bring you any surplus once the oats are reaped.

Ancel, you owe me a copper tool, due today, for the 3 grain I gave you on day 2. Hand it over now and I'll reap with it. I left home on day 2: 13 grain in our store, and Joyce was weeding and foraging. I'm starving here, so I'm reaping for the Marshs in return for food.

Ancel, you owe me a copper tool, due today, for the 3 grain I gave you on day 2. Hand it over now and I'll reap with it. I left home on day 2: 13 grain in our store, and Joyce was weeding and foraging. I'm starving here, so I'm reaping for the Marshs in return for food.
I'm reaping Marsh Field today for 4 grain. William, may I sleep at Reeve House again tonight and boil my grain at your hearth? I'll share a measure of grain for it.

Richolda here. I'll come and lay out the ditches in Reeve Field with you once our Marsh barley is reaped. Likely in the next day or two, after the harvest is in. Keep the water-stood corners clear until then.
Richolda of the Marshs here. A copper tool would serve us well for the ditches and the felling. Once our barley is reaped, I may have grain to trade for one. Let's speak again when the harvest is in.

William, I'm reaping your barley today, as I said I would for the coin. Bring the grain to the Mill and I'll grind it for the usual share. And for my day's reaping, give a few grain into Miller House. We're short too.
I'm reaping the Reeve barley today for a share of the grain and the milling. We have about 19 bread in store, enough for four days. Keep the Marshs to a share if you reap theirs.
Thank you, Wat. Once the barley is in, I'll put grain into Miller House for your day's work and bring the rest to the Mill to grind for the usual share.

[Reeve plan] Summer day 5. Reaping Reeve Field for the Reeves; carry all grain home to the Reeve store. Owe Wat 1 meat from last winter; he will take 1 grain from this harvest instead. Open offer to the Marshs: 1 day reaping at Marsh Field for 2 grain.

[Day plan summer 5] Oats in Terrace Field are ripe: select seed, then reap with Joyce. Fence Terrace Field to finish. Hoe Hill Field. Hob's day-2 grain paid O92; the 3 grain from last winter is still owed. Avice's copper tool debt is released. After reaping, store the grain at Cragg House.

[Wetham trip] Summer day 4: arrived in Wetham starving, with 4 coin and 1 crude tool. Brought back 3 cows and a calf found loose on the road. Ancel owes me a copper tool by day 5 for 3 grain. Home store had 13 grain on day 2. Keep away from Wat (the Hill Field feud).
[Owed] A38: Florence gave the Craggs a copper tool on summer day 3, so it should be settled.
Father, I've told Randal the Hales can reap with us at harvest for grain. That's how we'll share with them.

The North Field barley is ripe. I'm reaping it for the Reeds today. Beatrix and Ralf at Lowe Cottage, and Randal for the Hales, have asked for grain as payment, and Lowe's store is nearly empty. Our stores hold about 19 grain and 18 rye, so please decide how much we can spare. I think a fair share for reaping is a sound thing to offer.
I've heard your request, Ralf. I'm reaping North Field today and I've told Ancel about Lowe's store. He'll decide the share.
Thank you. I'll reap with you when the barley is ripe. Our store is nearly empty, so could the Reeds lend the Hales a few grain now, to be paid back with my reaping days?
I've left 4 grain at Hale House as a loan, since Lettice looks hungry. Pay it back with reaping or field work when we need hands, at the beans or in Rest Field.
Father, the barley is in and the store holds about 89 meals. I've paid the Lowes and lent the Hales 4 grain. Please watch the beans and tell me when they're ready to reap.

Lowes and Hales: you'll get your offer pay, and I've also left 5 grain at Lowe Cottage and 6 at Hale House. Some of it is thanks for yesterday and the rest is a loan, to be paid in work at the bean harvest and on Rest Field. No one in Barleyfield goes hungry while the Reeds have grain.

Lowes and Hales: you'll get your offer pay, and I've also left 5 grain at Lowe Cottage and 6 at Hale House. Some of it is thanks for yesterday and the rest is a loan, to be paid in work at the bean harvest and on Rest Field. No one in Barleyfield goes hungry while the Reeds have grain.
Thank you for the 5 grain at Lowe Cottage. I will pay it back in work at the bean harvest or on Rest Field, as you asked.
Bennet and I are reaping East Field today. The Hales' claim is disputed, so when we bring it in let's keep the sheaves in the Granary and settle the holding with them before it's shared out.
I'll reap East Field for the Barrows today for 6 grain to the Hale store, as you offer. The Hale claim on the field stays open; Randal and I will settle it with the Barrows after the harvest.
Thank you for the loan. The Hales will repay it in reaping days. Tell me when you need hands at the beans or Rest Field.
Agreed: keep the East Field sheaves apart in the Granary and share nothing until Daniel and Tobin have agreed the holding. I'm reaping West Field's oats today.

[Plan] Autumn 2: store about 182 grain (138 meals), 11 timber, which is low for winter, so fell. Sowing rye on Rest Field. Beans ripe about autumn 3: reap with the Hales and Lowes, who owe work (A216, A243, A245). Gave the Lowes 5 grain and the Hales 6 earlier. Keep the cattle out. Owe Elena 3 grain. The Barrows and Hales dispute East Field.
The barley in North Field comes ripe tomorrow. Any Hale who reaps it with us gets paid in grain, as the harvest custom is, a fair share for each day's reaping. Lettice, I've taken your offer.
The barley in North Field comes ripe tomorrow. Any Hale who reaps it with us gets paid in grain, as the harvest custom is, a fair share for each day's reaping. Lettice, I've taken your offer.
Agreed. I will reap North Field with you and Clement. Let us ask the Reeds for a grain share in return, as the custom is, and bring it to our store.
Agreed. I will reap North Field with you and Clement. Let us ask the Reeds for a grain share in return, as the custom is, and bring it to our store.
Father, I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today. The Lowe store is nearly empty. Will you give us a share of the grain for the work?
Yes, Ralf. I am reaping North Field myself today. Once the sheaves are in, I will give you and Beatrix a fair harvest share of grain from the Reed store, as custom is.
Daniel, I will give the Hale reapers a share of the grain from the Reed store once North Field is reaped and stored, as is custom.
Randal, you and the Hale reapers are welcome. Once North Field is reaped, you will have a fair share of grain from the Reed store for your days, as custom is.
The North Field barley looks ripe. I'm reaping it for the Reeds today, and I'll ask them for a share of the grain for our store. The store has no food left.
The Hale store is empty of food. I am reaping North Field for the Reeds today; I ask them to give us a share of the grain for our hunger.
The Hale store is empty of food: no grain, and Barley Wood is picked bare. I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds in return for grain, and foraging the Common and Brook Meadow for the house.

The Hale store has no food left: the bins are empty and five of us eat from it tonight. The Common and Brook Meadow are picked nearly bare, and Barley Wood is bare. I have offered two days of my work for two grain to anyone who has grain to spare. Can you go to Reed and Barrow about a share of their stores?
Reaping North Field is welcome. The Reeds will share the grain with those who work the field at harvest. Lettice's offer of two days' work for two grain is one we will take.

The barley in North Field is ripe and our cottage store is near empty. I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds today. Will you pay me a harvest share of grain for it, as is custom? Annora and Beatrix may help too.
Brook Meadow is picked bare too, so don't waste the day there. Come reap North Field with me. The Reeds should pay a grain share, and I've asked Clement.
Thank you, Clement. I'll reap beside you all day. Please send the grain share to Lowe Cottage when the sheaves are in.

Randal of Hale: I'm a skilled reaper and am reaping North Field for the Reeds today, as are Daniel and Dionisia. Our store is empty and five of us hunger. Please pay us in grain, a fair share, into the Hale store.
I will reap North Field for the Reeds today and I ask a grain share for the day's work, as the custom is. Will you take my offer of 1 day's reaping for 2 grain?

Father, yesterday I reaped about 33 grain of North Field into Reed House. The Lowe store has no food now. Please give Lowe Cottage a fair share of it, as harvest custom says. Today I am reaping some for Lowe too.
Yes. I've already asked Father for our share, and I'm reaping for Lowe today.
I'll reap North Field with you tomorrow when the barley is ripe, for the harvest share as custom gives.
Ralf, I have given 12 grain to the Lowe store for your harvest share, and 10 to the Hale store for the Hale reapers. Keep reaping for the Reeds today.
Beatrix, the Lowe store has its share now: 12 grain from the Reed store. Tell Ralf he need not wait for it.

Randal, I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds today; it settles my two days under agreement A148. The harvest custom gives reapers a share of the grain, and I'll ask that our share go into the Hale store, since we have no food. Bennet's offer is still yours to decide: 20 grain now if the Hales give up the East Field claim. Also, your open offer O143 is 2 days' work for 6 grain. I have no grain to
Philippa, I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds today as agreed. When the grain is stored, please send our share of it to the Hale store.

I'm reaping North Field with you today to pay off my two days owed to the Reeds. Please pay my wages in grain into the Hale store, as the harvest custom is: a fair share for each day's reaping. I have nothing to eat tonight.

I'm reaping North Field with you today to pay off my two days owed to the Reeds. Please pay my wages in grain into the Hale store, as the harvest custom is: a fair share for each day's reaping. I have nothing to eat tonight.
Thank you for the 10 grain for the Hale store. I'm reaping North Field for the Reeds today and will work the rest of what I owe.
Randal, I'm hungry, and the Hale store has no food. I'm reaping for the grain today and foraging the Common. Can you ask Reed and Barrow about a share for Hale?
Grandfather, I've sent 10 grain to the Hales from our store so you have bread for your hunger. The barley in North Field ripens tomorrow; come and reap with us and take your share.
Yes. The Hales will be paid in grain for their days' reaping, as agreed; I will see the share goes to your store once it is in.

Clement, the sheaves I reaped yesterday put about 26 grain in Reed House. Please pay our harvest share now: 10 grain to Lowe Cottage's store (or into my hands). We went to bed hungry two nights. I'm reaping again today for the Reeds, and the same share applies.
Keep reaping North Field with me. Ask your father for our share too; we have no food in the cottage.
Thank you, Ancel. We'll reap North Field again today. Please see that Clement pays the rest of our share for yesterday's seven days' reaping.

Daniel, the Hales have had 30 grain from us for a few days' reaping, far more than custom pays. I count every day the Hales owe us as paid, and more besides. The barley must come in today. Any Hale who reaps North Field today is already paid for it.
Ralf, Clement put 12 grain in Lowe Cottage on top of my 6. That's well over the share, so count today's reaping as paid. The barley must be cut today.
Bennet, the 6 grain for the trampled barley, into Reed House when you can. Thank you for shutting them in.
Mother, the Hales and Dionisia are owed nothing more. They're paid over and above, more than 30 grain in all. Let it rest, and don't give them more. Reap with us today.

Philippa, the North Field barley is ripe and must come in today. I'm reaping it with the Reeds for our two days under A148, and I'll ask that the Hales' harvest share go into the Hale store as agreed.
Thank you, Philippa, for the 3 grain for the Hale store. Ancel counts our reaping at North Field as paid, so I'll reckon it so. Today I'm reaping East Field for the Barrows under my A232 debt.
Thank you for the 2 grain. North Field looks well cut. I'm reaping East Field for the Barrows today to clear what I owe them.
Understood, Randal. I'll reap North Field for the Reeds today to settle A148, and I'll bring the grain I'm owed to Hale House.
North Field barley is ready and must be cut today. Come and reap, and take your share.
Daniel, I have sent 3 grain to the Hale store for your share of the reaping. If you reckoned it differently, tell me and I will make it right.
North Field's barley is cut and stooked. I am selecting seed from the best of it today; the Hales' share and Dionisia's wages are paid from the Reed store.

Ancel, yesterday I put 3 grain into the Hale store for Daniel's share and gave Dionisia 2 grain for her wages, before I heard your word. I will take no more from the store. Please say what the Hales and Dionisia are owed in all, and I will help square it. Today I am reaping North Field.

Ancel, yesterday I put 3 grain into the Hale store for Daniel's share and gave Dionisia 2 grain for her wages, before I heard your word. I will take no more from the store. Please say what the Hales and Dionisia are owed in all, and I will help square it. Today I am reaping North Field.

Ancel, yesterday I put 3 grain into the Hale store for Daniel's share and gave Dionisia 2 grain for her wages, before I heard your word. I will take no more from the store. Please say what the Hales and Dionisia are owed in all, and I will help square it. Today I am reaping North Field.
Daniel, I am reaping North Field with you today. Your share is already part-paid in the Hale store, 3 grain; Ancel will settle the rest with you as head of our house.
Randal: grain owed to Hale should go into Hale House. Keep your wage grain there.

[Reaping debt] Autumn day 1: I owe the Reeds two days' work (A148). I reap North Field today and tomorrow for them. Ancel pays the Hales in grain as harvest custom. Keep foraging the Common when units are spare, for the Hale store.

Richard — the store worries me. Six nights of food and barely half the wood we need to see out winter. Sixteen timber or sixty-four firewood is what I remember it takes; we have four timber and thirteen of firewood. I will be at the moor and the gill today getting what I can. Should we set the others to firewood and hay too, while the weather holds and summer lasts?
I hear you, father. Lucy and I will try every day we are fed and together. If we have a daughter, she takes grandmother's name — you have my word.

No lasting ill feeling from me — you read the crop right and your hands were given in good faith. Richard knows and will speak with you himself today; wait for his word on the reaping. I will say this much: we will need all the hands we can get when the ears are ready, and good neighbours matter more than a small trespass.
Closing the Moor hay debt today — five hay to their door, A96 done. Our own ground at the moor is where my hands go after; dung for it, more clearing. We will have a Fenwick field.

Three days — I'll trust your eye on it, son. Then on day 8 of summer all four of us go in with sickles. Save your strength tomorrow and the day after; a reaper tired on the first morning is grain lost. Jory and I will keep the stores filling and the new field growing meanwhile.

Closing the Moor hay debt today — five hay to their door, A96 done. Our own ground at the moor is where my hands go after; dung for it, more clearing. Roger says rye is three days off — target the reap for day 8 of summer.

Richard — you have it rightly, and I take your word. I'll not touch the Infield unasked again, and I thank you for speaking plainly. Roger says the rye is three days off, day 8. If you'll have Fenwick hands at the reap, I offer all four of us — Lucy comes as her trade, Ellen, Roger and I with sickles beside her, paid in grain as the custom is. Say if that suits and we'll be at your gate on day 8.

Making the second crude tool this morning as you asked — it'll be in Fenwick store or Roger's hand by evening. We have 9.1 timber; one should be enough. Hay owed to Moors is 4.8 of 5; someone's one unit on the Moor finishes it. I'll fell at the Gill after.

The rye looked three days off yesterday — that puts it ready on the first day of autumn, or close to it. I will milk first thing as you asked, then cut hay the rest of the day. When it is time to reap I will come straight to the Infield. On the Fenwicks: Jory put in for reaping when the time comes. He has settled the hay debt already this morning — five units at the door. If you are willing, the w

The five hay at the door this morning settles the agreement — well done and thank you. The rye should be ready on the first day of autumn. I have passed your offer of reaping to Richard; wait on his word today and it will come.
You are welcome to watch any morning after the harvest is done. Come to the moor when the cows need milking and I will walk you through it — it is a patient craft and I am glad to pass it on.

I'll be at the moor hay today — if you're there too we might share a corner. After the reap I'd be glad to watch you milk one morning; our house has none that know it and I'd learn it from your hands if you'll have me.

Hay debt day today — the store has 2.5 and we owe 5 by day 8. I'll cut hay three units at the moor; Jory, if you put a unit or two to hay beside me we close it clean before reap. Roger — save your arms, the sickle wants them whole. One unit from me to clear Fenwick Rise after.

Avice — I owe you a plain answer and here it is: I took the weeding on myself, no Moor hand asked. I'll not touch the Infield unasked again. I've sent word to Richard about Fenwick hands at the day 8 reap; put in a word with him if you will.

Hold off on hay, love — A96 is settled. Avice told me plainly this morning that yesterday's five at the door closed it, and Richard said the same with thanks; the agreements board shows no debt. Your hands to Fenwick Rise all day beside me; I'll be clearing from the start. Rye on day 8 or first of autumn — Avice says first of autumn, Roger says day 8; either way we are near enough and Richard's wo

Hear it, all of you. A96 is settled — Avice and Richard both told me yesterday's five hay at the door closed it, and the agreements board shows no debt. No hay today, from any of us. Richard said yes to the reap: Infield gate at first light day 8, Ellen and Roger and me as sickles beside Lucy, two grain a head paid when the reaping's done. So: today — I press Fenwick Rise with the tool, Ellen clea
One unit from me to hay beside Ellen with the crude tool — that should close the Moor debt clean. Then felling at the Gill. Day 8 I'm at the Infield with my sickle.
Day 8 at first light — all three of you with sickles on the Infield, as Richard arranged. We will pay two grain each when the harvest is binned. Come ready for a full day.

Good. I will milk at first light tomorrow and be straight to the Infield with my sickle. Today milk first, then hay beside you all afternoon — I will find you on the moor. And I still want to hear about the copper ore when the harvest is done and we have a quiet moment.
Avice — thank you for carrying my word to Richard. We will be at the gate at first light tomorrow, four of us. The rye looks fine from where I've seen it; may the day hold clear.
I am honored, Father, and I will not fail you. I'll watch Water Meadow closely for any sign - tracks, broken fence, anything that tells the story. The barley will come in and we will find our oxen.

No copper ore that I know of near Stannick — our quarry gives grey building stone, not metal. Copper comes from deeper hills, further away than I have travelled. The Cotters at Wynford know smelting and burning charcoal; I mean to ask them, and look at the market, when we go after the harvest. For now I am making a crude tool this morning: not as good as copper, but well above bare hands for cutti

The rye is ready and the gale is up — I am going straight to the Infield at first light and will reap all day, every unit. Also: I saw Lucy herding for the Fenwicks on our moor yesterday. Is there an arrangement I should know of, or shall we speak on it after the harvest is in?

Wages paid today — two rye each from the store to Jory, Ellen and Roger for the harvest. I am driving the cattle to the Infield to graze the stubble and dung it, then sowing rye. The soil looked pale and thin yesterday and it has been cropped hard; I want to give it all the manure I can before the seed goes in. Seven days of autumn left. Have you thought about travelling to Wynford this season for

You are near your time. Take only light work today — nothing that strains you. If the pains begin, send for me at once; I will be in the Infield but will come straightaway. Stay close to Fenwick House when you can, and do not go out alone on the moor. Is there anything you need from me or from the store?

Jory — the Infield was reaped yesterday, every last stalk; the five of us finished it before dark. Nothing left to cut. For the work days you owe us on the agreements: if any of you have hours free, clearing in the Brakes or timber in the Gill would serve us well before the cold. Ellen — come with me at first light tomorrow for the milking, and I will show you how it is done.

Richard sent word at first light — our Moor debt is cleared, all three days. Roger, you need not hoe to pay. Jory, I'm with you to the Infield; I bring my hands and master reap bare — you keep the tool. If the Moors want more reaping, let it be for grain in hand this time, not a day owed.

Reap beside your mother today, bare. Keep the pace with mine down the row. Six grain comes to our bins tonight if the Moors keep their word, and more owed if we work another day. Lucy stays home — she is near her time.

Reap beside your mother today, bare. Keep the pace with mine down the row. Six grain comes to our bins tonight if the Moors keep their word, and more owed if we work another day. Lucy stays home — she is near her time.

Infield's cut out — Avice says nothing left standing. Moor debt cleared, Richard's word. Ellen — to the Gill with me: I take the tool and fell, you bare beside me, or Fenwick Rise if the clearing calls louder. Roger — your day is yours: clear Rise with your mother, or firewood at the Gill, or hoe for Richard when he calls O399. Lucy stays in. Ellen — take Avice's milking at first light tomorrow; a
I'll stay in, love. Thank you for the hoe today — one less day we owe. Come back warm; I'll keep the fire low until you're all back.

Beatrix, my son Thomas must sow rye at Fallow Close before autumn closes. Do the Wynns have rye seed to trade or gift? If you do, we can settle it fairly. If not, I will travel to Stannick to ask the Fenwicks.

Your owed work day is done — I am releasing the agreement today. But I would be grateful if you could gather firewood at the Gill as a favour. We will sow the Infield in a day or two once the cattle have grazed and dunged it a little.

Your owed work day is done — I am releasing the agreement today. But I would be grateful if you could gather firewood at the Gill as a favour. We will sow the Infield in a day or two once the cattle have grazed and dunged it a little.
Your work debt is cleared as well. Firewood at the Gill today if you can spare the time — more never hurts before winter. Thank you for the reaping.
Rest today, Lucy. The harvest is in and you have done your share and more. I have given you 2 rye from our store. Tell Roger the moment anything starts.
You are near your time, love — stay in the house today, by the fire. No sickle, no hoe. Our child comes first. I'll hoe the Infield for your father, pay a day of what we owe. Rest.
Hoeing the Infield for the Moors today — pays one of the days we owe. Lucy stays in.

Avice called out: Infield was reaped yesterday, every stalk — nothing to cut. She asks the days we owe be paid as clearing the Brakes or felling in the Gill. I'll clear the Brakes today, pay A330. If you've no reap, the tool fells timber at the Gill x2 — Moors would take that too.

Thank you, Thomas. You are Wilmot's husband and Idonea's father - we are family. If the Cotters need to sow rye, speak with Warin about an arrangement. Perhaps there is ground to be broken, or a share of harvest to be traded for use of a field. We will deal fairly with you.

Agreed on timber in the Gill for A330 and A336. I'll wait on Richard's Wynford word before I fix the days. Rain today is no felling weather — I'm on Fenwick Rise clearing while the ground's soft. Hope the milking goes well for Ellen; it is a gift to teach her.

Your day is yours. If you've the will, come clear with me on Fenwick Rise — bare hands, but the ground will be soft after this rain and two of us bite deeper. Otherwise firewood at the Gill, or sit by Lucy. No Moor day owed by you today.
Nothing crooked thought, girl — 'well done' was for the bin fuller. Richard's gift to you, your choice to put it to the house: that is Fenwick doing. Stay in, keep dry. The hearth is yours today.

Father — I fetched the two rye you gave me from the Moor bins yesterday and put them straight in Fenwick. If anyone speaks of it as taking, say your word on it. I didn't mean to walk between the houses.

Jory — the two rye from Moor House was Richard's gift to me yesterday, by his own word, straight into the Fenwick bins. If you thought it a take, it was not; Richard will say so. Nothing crooked between us.

Cattle are all at the Brakes — I drove nine there on day one and the stray calf went there yesterday. Nothing on the moor or in the Gill. The rye short in the store: I sowed six as seed, and gave two rye each as wages to Jory, Ellen, Roger and Lucy — fourteen total, all mine to give, nothing missing without my word. I leave tonight for Wynford and am back morning of day seven. Milk the cows each m
You have my word — those two rye were yours, I gave them freely. You fetched your own goods and did nothing wrong. If anyone says otherwise, send them to me.
You have my word — those two rye were yours, I gave them freely. You fetched your own goods and did nothing wrong. If anyone says otherwise, send them to me.

Thomas, I am glad you stayed. Mabel has gone to Stannick with grain to trade for rye seed - she took one of our oxen to carry the load. She should return by day five. While she is away, there is work here. The Long Strips needs ploughing after the harvest, but we need both oxen for that. When Mabel returns with the ox, we can plough. Today I mill grain at the water wheel - rainy days are good for

Travel safe tonight — I hope Mabel is heading back to Wynford and you can keep company on the road; two together is much safer than one. I will hold the house well: cattle to the moor each morning, fire lit, Lucy watched. I have offered Mabel ten rye for ten grain while she is here. Come back with good news from the Cotters. I trust you and I am glad you are mine.

Welcome to Stannick, Mabel. I am Ellen Fenwick, of Fenwick House on the yard. If you need a bed, we have two free — come in and warm yourself, eat with us at supper. Tell me what brings you from Wynford: a message, a hand to lend, or a road to rest from?

Welcome to Stannick, Mabel — Jory Fenwick. You have a bed at Fenwick House tonight; eat from what you carry or we'll settle a share. I can spare some rye for grain: I've put an offer in the open — 2 rye for 3 grain, up to two lots. Rye stands the winter and we select nothing special, but it's sound. Ellen will be about this morning if you want to look at it.

Ellen, Lucy - thank you kindly for the welcome and the offer of shelter. If Richard and I can settle the trade today, I may travel back with him tonight. But if not, I would be grateful for a bed at Fenwick House and will gladly share what I carry.

Thank you all for the warm welcome and fair dealing. The trade is done and I am grateful. Richard, I will travel with you tonight - two on the road are safer than one, as you say. Avice, thank you for the rye. Jory, Ellen, Lucy - the Fenwicks' hospitality honors you. I hope to see you all again when the roads are kind.

I leave tonight, if Lucy is not in labour by then. You are head of this house while I am gone — cattle at the Brakes each morning, fire lit in Moor House, eat from the store as needed. Bread and rye are rich; use what you must. Jory's felling days are day 8 and 9, when I return morning of day 8. I trust you fully and I am glad you are here.

Urgent first thing: Jory saw the cattle on Stannick Moor this morning — drive them back to the Brakes before anything else, count every head, and make sure the calf is with them. You are head of this house while I am gone; use the stores freely and keep the fire lit every night. You may agree in my name to hosting any honest traveller, lending up to five rye or grain in need, or a work exchange of

Urgent first thing: Jory saw the cattle on Stannick Moor this morning — drive them back to the Brakes before anything else, count every head, and make sure the calf is with them. You are head of this house while I am gone; use the stores freely and keep the fire lit every night. You may agree in my name to hosting any honest traveller, lending up to five rye or grain in need, or a work exchange of

I will be on Stannick Moor this morning and back at the yard before noon — Roger, come for me any hour, I will not be far. On the eight rye Richard left at Moor House: I have no word from him of any summer-grain debt to the Fenwicks, and I will not move that rye until I hear it from him when he returns. It stays in Moor House store until then.

Mother — quiet night, no pains, child still. I am at the hearth all day in the rain. Two things: Richard left 8 rye at Moor House this morning before the road — is that his summer-grain debt paid to the Fenwicks in rye? If so, Jory should know to move it over to our bin, and the Moors are clear. Also A442: I owe Richard 1 day's work; Jory meant to serve it d7 morning but I want to be sure it is se

Jory — this morning Richard left 8 rye at Moor House before his road to Wynford. I take it for his summer-grain debt (8 grain owed, paid in rye). If you agree, let the Fenwick bin have it, and we are clear with the Moors on that count. The timber-days (A330, A336) still stand for days 7 and 8 at the Gill.

[Richard away] Richard left evening of autumn day 3 (overall day 9) for Wynford with Mabel Wynn. Purpose: speak with Cotters about copper — smelting, tools, coin. Left 8 rye at Moor House morning of day 10. Return: morning of autumn day 7 (overall day 13), three days away. I am head of household until return. May: host honest travellers; lend up to 5 rye or grain in need; agree one work-day exchange. May NOT wit
[A14 arrears] I owe Denise 1 meat on A14 (1 paid, 1 in arrears). She is not here; must pay when at one place with her, or send meat with a traveller.

[autumn d2] Heavy rain. Stores jump: 14.6 meals, 18.3 timber (winter heat covered), 11.9 rye + 8.9 grain. Owed to Moors: A330, A336 (both felling at Gill per Avice), A442 (Richard's call for O399, hoe or firewood). Avice: wait on Richard's Wynford d3/d4 before fixing days. Today: 6 clear on Fenwick Rise (tool, competent) — should take Rise within reach of sowable in 2 more days. Ellen at milking with Avice th

[Stores watch] Summer d7 morning: Fenwick store 40.3 firewood, 11.2 grain, 5.5 hay, 12.2 timber, (food worth 7.8 meals). Four eating ~4/night = less than 2 nights. Day 8 reap pays 2 grain a head x4 = 8 grain (~5.6 meals cooked), tide us over. Winter wants ~16 timber or 64 firewood-equivalent per hearth; 12.2 timber + 40.3 firewood ~= 32.3 timber-equivalent, past halfway. Hay debt A96 cleared (5 delivered). ONE c

[Open offers tracked] Autumn d2. Still owing: A330, A336 (1 day each to Moors) — Avice wants both paid as timber at the Gill; A442 (1 day to Richard) — purpose unknown, ask Roger. Jory to coordinate Gill days with Richard once Richard fixes his Wynford trip (d3 or d4). I cannot fell while with child; these owings fall to Jory/Ellen/Roger until after the birth.

In peace, brother, I give you my word. I found no one here, only heather, a beck and a wood thick with dead branches. Something heavy moves in the Hanger at dusk, so keep your spear near. The talk was that the new folk are beyond Wolfscar and Blackmere, so I think the stony path along the river leads toward them. We leave at first light, walk together, and stop for anyone we meet on the road.

Bryony of the Ashs of Ashby greets you, Rurik and Ulf. I come in peace. I seek stone (I offer 2 coin for 4) and news of the ways and of my husband Aldo. Could any Bram house or camp host me tonight? I can share dried meat.

Welcome, Bryony. We have only 2 stone; they're yours for 1 coin. You can sleep at our old camp on the Knoll, which has beds and a fire ring. In return, tell us the roads: where does the stony path into the oaks lead, and where does the trail go? Which way is Ashby, and which is Longmere?
Thank you, Cuthbert, for the roof. We will repay it in the morning.

Rurik, I'll teach you the hearth today: set aside time to learn from me this morning. In return, 2 grain plus the 1 dried meat Ulf offered for your nights at our camp; leave them in the Bram House store or hand them to me.
Brother, I'm short of dried meat. Could you give Cuthbert the 2 dried meat for the hearth lesson? I'll repay in grain.
Ulf, no lesson yet; my offer was refused as badly worded. I have 2.6 grain and 0.5 meat; we will share and forage on the road. We leave at first light.
Done, brother. I am giving Cuthbert the 2 dried meat for your lesson. Learn it well. Repay me in grain when you can. I will hunt today for the road home.
Done, brother. I am giving Cuthbert the 2 dried meat for your lesson. Learn it well. Repay me in grain when you can. I will hunt today for the road home.
The barley's filling well, love, about 3 days to reap. The house holds 7 dried meat now. After harvest, shall one of us walk to Longmere? Bryony says it's empty: lea, beech holt and beck.
Brother, we leave now, walking all day to Greyfell, gathering food as we go. Then Blackmere, Wolfscar, home. We share food on the road.
Good, love. You forage and hunt. I'll weed, make a tool and fell timber for winter. Longmere after harvest, then.
Morning love. Trying with 2 units first. Then I'll forage and hunt; firewood is plentiful. Walking to Longmere after harvest sounds good.
I'll reap beside you, love. Keep a good share of the grain for seed.
Morning love. Trying with 2 units, then I reap the Lea. Join me when you can.
Hilde, I couldn't make a tool: we're a bit short of stone. Do you have a tool you could lend me, or any stone? If not, I'll gather firewood tomorrow. Good night.
Ulf, agreed. I carry 1.2 dried meat and 3.6 firewood, no timber. Tonight your fire, and I will share my firewood with it.
Ulf, you watched all day for nothing; I am sorry. Tomorrow, if you agree, we reap the beans on Gorm Lea and then dibble the grain into the cleared ground together.
Rain today, so I'm gathering firewood for our store, since we have about 10 nights of fuel left. Fell the timber for the crude tool when you can. I won't cut more hay; our store has plenty.
Agreed, Walter. I'll stand with you tomorrow and offer help with the Mires' work in return for ore.

Joan, Osbert: Walter and Agnes Hale of Brook, neighbours over the hill. We'd pay 2 coin for each unit of copper ore, 5 coin for a copper tool, or work your field or cut your hay in return. We leave at nightfall, so take an offer if it suits you.
Bare hands gave under a unit of hay today. Tomorrow I will make a crude tool from our copper for the hay, unless Osbert has a copper tool to lend me.

There is no timber here for a handle, so I cannot make the crude tool yet. Could you lend me your pick this morning? I will mine beside you at the Green Scar and give it back at nightfall. If not, I will weed the Field.
There is no wood to fell at the Mead, so my tool was refused. Could you lend me your pick at the Scar tomorrow? I will look for wood elsewhere if I must make my own.
Osbert, we sleep here tonight. Tomorrow I'm at the hay on the Mead; the ore waits for your word.
Forage in Hollow Wood is picked bare. Tomorrow I'll hunt, and we should ask the Webbs about barley work for a share.
Hugh, what did you bring back from the hunt? Tomorrow I'll go to the Webbs or the Crofts myself about work for a share of grain, since they haven't taken my offer.
Good, Edith. I'm reaping at Webb Field for a share.
Thank you, that suits me. I'll gather firewood and forage tomorrow. Ask the Webbs first about reaping, and take a share of the barley in return.
Thank you, that suits me. I'll gather firewood and forage tomorrow. Ask the Webbs first about reaping, and take a share of the barley in return.
Hunting is slim: 0.8 meat. Tomorrow I'll ask the Webbs for barley in return for work, and weed the oats. Edith, how did the strip fare?
Good plan. Get a share of barley for the work if the Webbs will give one. I'll milk and cut hay tomorrow.
Hugh of the Ashbys will reap or weed your barley for a share of grain. I'll work a day for 3 grain, if you'll have me.
Webbs: I have spare hands today and tomorrow. If you want help reaping your barley in Webb Field, I'll work for a share of the grain. Tell me, and I'll come.
Webbs: I have spare hands today and tomorrow. If you want help reaping your barley in Webb Field, I'll work for a share of the grain. Tell me, and I'll come.
Agreed. Tomorrow I'll ask the Webbs first, then the Ashbys, for barley work for a share of grain. Good night.
Good night. Tomorrow I'll ask the Webbs and the Ashbys for barley work in return for a share, as Thomas suggests.
Good night. Tomorrow I'll ask the Webbs and the Ashbys for barley work in return for a share, as Thomas suggests.

Today I'll take the 0.8 meat from our store, dry it at our hearth and put the dried meat back in the store. Then I'll go to Webb Field and reap barley for a share. Did you speak to the Webbs in person? If they say yes, I'll work there with you.
Webbs: Ida of the Croft house here. I have hands and will work for a share of your barley, two days, for grain. Tell me when you want me.
Tomorrow, if it clears, I'll go to the Webbs in person about barley work for a share of grain, and then to the Ashbys if they need hands.
Ida has offered her hands to reap Webb Field for a share. I say yes; we need the rest of the barley in before it spoils.
Webbs, Ashbys: I'm Ida of the Croft house. I have hands for barley work and will take a share of grain for two days of reaping. Who will have me?
Edith of the Ashby house: I have hands for any work, and will take a share of grain for it. My offer O45 stands.

I'm milking the Croft cows first, then I'll come help with the woodshed. Bring your timber to the Croft house store when you can. I'll look for firewood past Hollow Wood or in young growth after that.
Clear day. I'll hunt in Hollow Wood for game and reap in Webb Field for a share of the barley. Bring any meat you take to the Ashby store.
I took 3 grain from the Webbs' barley today without their word. That was wrong. Tomorrow let's only reap Webb Field if the Webbs accept our offer, and pay them for what I took.
Webbs: I took 3 grain from your barley today without asking. I will pay you back in work or coin. My offer of work for 12 grain stands; accept it and we reap for you properly.
Agreed. I too took 10 grain from Webb Field without their word. Tomorrow we'll offer the Webbs coin and work for it and only reap if they accept.
Webbs: my offer of work for 12 grain stands. I will not reap your barley unless you accept it. I still owe you for the 3 grain I took, and I will repay it in work or coin.
The store is near 28 meals now, so 150 by day 6 is out of reach. I will weed Ashby Strip all day. If the Webbs accept any trade, we take it. Please do not take their barley without their word.

Rain all day. I'm milking the Croft cows on the pasture this morning, then cutting hay there for winter. If you're free, the Webb barley is ripe and will need reaping soon. Shall we help them for a share?
Good plan. I'll milk and cut hay beside you. Ask the Webbs about a reaping share when the rain lets up, and we'll help then.
Yes, Ida. Tomorrow we'll offer the Webbs our hands on their barley for a share. Rest well.
Come reap in Webb Field with me. We'll ask the Webbs for grain in return and bring it into our store.
Webbs: Ashby will reap your barley today for a share of the grain going into our store. Say if you agree.
Yes, I'm reaping in Webb Field now. Bring your grain share to the Ashby store.
Webbs: I reaped for you today with bare hands and got three grain. Tomorrow I'll reap with a tool. What share will you give the Ashby store for the work?
The Croft house will reap Webb Field for a share of the barley. Thomas and I can give two days' work between us. Say the word and we'll start tomorrow.
The offer failed on its wording, so I'll redo it properly in the morning. Ashby hands are already in Webb Field, so we may need to join them rather than wait for a share.
The Croft house can reap for a share of the Webb barley. I'll put a proper offer out in the morning.
I agreed nothing with Hugh. I'll ask him in the morning about his share of the barley. We'll both reap at first light so we finish before he takes more.
The Webb barley is cut. Who has work for us tomorrow? Ashby will herd, hunt, or work the Crofts' pasture in return for meat or milk for our store.

I'm finishing the Webb Field barley today and will lay the wet sheaves out to dry. I haven't taken up the Ashby offers for grain. If you agreed to Ashby reaping our barley for a share, tell me the terms and I'll honour them.

I'm finishing the Webb Field barley today and will lay the wet sheaves out to dry. I haven't taken up the Ashby offers for grain. If you agreed to Ashby reaping our barley for a share, tell me the terms and I'll honour them.
The barley in Webb Field seems all reaped now. Where are the sheaves, and did you agree a share with the Ashbys? Tomorrow I'd like to dry the sheaves and bring the grain in before it spoils.
The grain from our reaping already went into our store: about 120 grain there. I agreed no share with the Ashbys. Tomorrow let's gather firewood and hay and think about what to sow.
Herding gave me no milk to carry, so I'll try milking at Croft Pasture tomorrow and ask the Crofts for a share. Anything you bring in, put into our store.
Edith, we'll have your two days' work for Croft under the agreement; tell me when you can come.
Croft Pasture and Hollow Wood are both bare now. Tomorrow I'd like to go to the Webbs and offer to reap their barley for a share of the grain, so we bring food home. Would you come with me?
Yes, I'll come. We'll reap Webb Field and ask for a grain share.

Let's go to Webb Field together and reap the Webbs' barley. Please bring any grain we reap straight into our Ashby store, and don't take the 6-grain work offer from our store. I'll make the offer to the Webbs for a share.
Edith and I will reap your barley today. We ask a fair share of the grain for our household's store.
Robert, I have no stone for a crude tool, so I'll fell timber by hand at Hollow Wood tomorrow. If you finish with your axe early, lend it to me for an hour or two.
Webbs: Hugh Ashby offers a day's work at your barley for 3 grain, or any share you think fair. The Ashby store runs low.
Tomorrow I'll offer the Webbs coin and work for barley. Our oats are still green, so that won't help. You could offer them work reaping for a share of the grain.
I will reap Webb Field today for a share of the barley to our store. If you find the Webbs will sell or trade, tell me the terms and I will work them.
I'm reaping Webb Field today for our household store, and I'm offering the Webbs my reaping for a share too. If they agree to both, we can reap side by side and bring every sheaf to the Ashby store.
I'm offering the Webbs coin and work for grain and will reap with them. Please offer them reaping work for a share too.
Good. Reap with me; I've offered the Webbs coin or work for grain. Whatever share they agree, bring it to our store.
Ida, I already have a crude tool and cut hay with it yesterday (3 from one unit). I'll lend it to you in the morning or you can keep it; no need to make another.
My bare hands only reap about 3 grain a day. Tomorrow I'll ask Robert to lend his crude tool for the reaping, or make one if I can, so I can cut more of the barley.
Thanks, Thomas. I'm cutting hay on Croft Pasture all day. Please hand me your crude tool when you can. Keep an eye on dried meat too: 9.6 left.

Hollow Wood has no dead wood left, so I'll cut young growth there tomorrow if you'll lend me your crude tool, or we both cut. Hugh and Edith's work will come in over the next days, so we'll have hands for the wood.
Agreed, Hugh. You hunt and talk to the Webbs about harvest work; I'll try hunting in Hollow Wood or reaping for a share, whichever brings food into our store fastest.
Foraging yielded little. Tomorrow I'll hunt and ask the Webbs about harvest work for barley. Edith, please try hunting or reaping for a share too.
Hollow Wood is bare, so I'll reap in Webb Field for a share today. I've accepted your offer O8 (2 days of work for 20 grain to our store); tell me if you'd rather not work those days.
Good, Edith. I'll reap in Webb Field today too, to honour O8. Bring whatever grain you earn into our store.
Agreed, Hugh. Make the weapon and hunt; I'll ask the Webbs for the grain they owe us for our reaping.
Webb Field is bare now. Edith, tomorrow I'll make a crude weapon and hunt, and trade work for milk and meat with the Crofts. Ask the Webbs for the grain they owe us for our reaping.

Rain all day, but I'll spend my 7 units hunting and foraging in Hollow Wood for the store. Please bring back any milk, meat or grain the Crofts will trade for work. I'll ask the Webbs for the grain they owe us when I see them.

Hollow Wood is bare, so tomorrow I'll work off my two days for the Ashbys, then ask the Webbs for the grain they owe us. Can you check the Crofts for work-for-milk or meat again, or go further afield for game?
Today is the last day that counts. I'll forage Croft Pasture for the Ashby store and work off my two days on Ashby Strip. Could you ask the Webbs for the grain they owe us from the reaping?
Agreed, Hugh. Ask the Webbs and Crofts for grain or milk in return for work, and I'll do the same.
I'm reaping in Webb Field today; please press the Webbs for the grain they owe us and bring it to our store.
Edith, the barley is already reaped and I found no work. Tomorrow I'll ask the Webbs and Crofts for grain or milk in return for work.
Edith, the Webbs gave me nothing: there was no crop left to reap, so I did no work. We still have about 22 meals in store. Tomorrow I'll ask the Webbs directly for the grain they owe us.
The Webb barley is ripe and the rain is beating on it. Tomorrow I mean to reap it in the morning, and I would welcome a hand, or a copper sickle if anyone has one to lend.
Ashby offers firewood or two days of work at your harvest, in return for grain for our store. Say if you will take it.
Maud took both our offers: firewood for 5 grain and two days' work for 6 grain. Tomorrow I hoe Webb Field to earn the work owed; please check the grain has reached the Ashby store and keep it there.
Maud took our firewood and work offers, so grain is owed us. Tomorrow I hoe Webb Field for the Webbs; the grain goes into the Ashby store.
Well done. I'll check the store tomorrow and keep all grain in it. Do the hoeing owed.
I took dung from Croft Pasture without asking. I'm sorry for it. I've left 2 grain at your door in return, and I'll ask before I take anything of yours again.
The grain is in the Ashby store, 36 grain. I hoe Webb Field today to pay the two days owed to the Webbs. Keep the grain in the store and weed Ashby Strip if you can.
My hoeing at Webb Field keeps counting for nothing, so tomorrow I weed Ashby Strip. Keep the grain in the Ashby store, and if your hoeing clears the Webbs' work debt, tell me.
My hoeing at Webb Field keeps counting for nothing, so tomorrow I weed Ashby Strip. Keep the grain in the Ashby store, and if your hoeing clears the Webbs' work debt, tell me.
Hand-gathering firewood is slow, so tomorrow I'll cut young growth in Hollow Wood with a tool. Could I borrow the crude tool for the morning?
My crude tool did the hay well. I can make you one tomorrow if we have the materials; otherwise share mine.

I'm going to the Mead to cut hay after I store mine. If you have your crude tool with you, lend it to me for a while, or we can share it. We are short of firewood, so once the hay is in, I'll look for wood with you.

I'm going to the Mead to cut hay after I store mine. If you have your crude tool with you, lend it to me for a while, or we can share it. We are short of firewood, so once the hay is in, I'll look for wood with you.
Does anyone know where dead wood lies beyond the Green, Field and Mead, or who has a copper cutting tool to lend? Hugh, you have a load of firewood: where did it come from?
Hugh: we haven't found firewood either. I'm trying to fell timber today and will share where if I find it.
Robert said the Fowlers haven't found firewood either; he's trying to fell timber and will share where. I'll try felling too. The Mead has no wood, so cut hay or weed instead.
It's wet all day, but the barley needs weeding. I'll go to the Field and weed it. Come help if you like; we can share the work and be back under our own roof by nightfall.
Keep the 10 salt in the Ashby store untouched until day 8. Do not trade or spend it, even for Robert's 30 grain debt; we settle that with other grain. Let's weed the Field today.

Hugh and Edith gave no answer about wood. The village is only the Green, the Field and the Mead, with no known way out. We have about 10 nights of fuel; we should burn it sparingly and look for a way out after the harvest.

Alice, the Coles have still not answered about the timber. Tomorrow I will ask Geoffrey and Mabel to their faces at the Green. I will forage the Mead and gather dead firewood, and I will not fell in their copse without their word. Thank you for the hay and the weeding.
Geoffrey, Mabel: I still need 7 timber for our room. My offer of 3 grain for 10 timber stands. I will not fell more ash in the Coles' copse without your word. Please give me a yes or a no.

Geoffrey said yes yesterday: you may fell up to 7 ash in their copse, no more, and no trade, so no grain owed. Please don't fell beyond 7 in total with me. I'll fell some too; count what we each take.
I weeded the Field today already. Tomorrow I'll work at the Copse for timber owed to the Reeds; you could forage or rest.
Mabel, I'll ask Simon tomorrow morning what the claim means; the Field is worked by both houses, so I'll propose we share the reaping fairly.

[The room] Father's promised small room at the Reed house: 6 timber, 1.5 stone, 4.5 units by the engine's reckoning (memory said 10 timber). Timber only from the Coles' copse; ask their leave and offer grain. Stone still needed.
I'll fell some timber at the Copse too, so we can share the work there.
Geoffrey, Mabel: may we take a little timber from your Copse? We can give hay or help in return.
Let's weed the barley on the Field today, both of us. I'll start on it this morning; join me there when you can.
Geoffrey, tomorrow let us cut hay on the Mead together. My bare hands made little headway today, so if anyone has a copper tool to lend, we should use it.
The Copse is held by the Coles. Alice and Simon, if you fell timber there for the Reeds, let us agree first what is owed for it, so the wood is not taken without an account.
Thank you, Alice. Tomorrow we fell at the Copse with every unit, and I'll try to borrow a copper tool so the felling goes faster.
The Mead is picked over for wild food, so let's leave it to recover. Could I borrow your crude tool to cut hay tomorrow? Then we'll weed the barley.
Good work today. Tomorrow let's fell at the Copse with every unit, and if we can borrow a copper tool, let's use it.

We have been felling at the Copse for our store, and I want Geoffrey and Mabel to know I will talk with them about what is fair for the wood. Does anyone have a copper tool I could borrow for felling?
