Friends, please give an account of the timber felled in our Copse, and let us agree terms (a share of timber or grain) before more is taken.
Could I borrow the crude tool again tomorrow to cut hay on the Mead? The Field is clean, and hay is our thinnest stock for winter.
Alice, do you have the crude tool? We have no stone for another. Tomorrow I'll ask Geoffrey or Mabel to lend or sell us a tool for the Copse work.

[The Copse terms] The Coles hold the Copse. I have been felling there for the Reed store since day 2 and owe Geoffrey and Mabel a fair price for the wood. Offer made day 6: 2 coin for 4 timber. Keep felling only as fair terms allow, and tell the Coles before felling more.
Fog this morning, but the barley still needs weeding while it's young. I'm going to the Field with my full 7 units for the household. Come and join me when you can.
I haven't learned more yet; I'm asking Ida now. Robert says weeding any plot helps and nobody minds, so weed freely. Timber for the roof is a good idea.
Ida, the Field is now claimed for the Crofts. Are our two barley plots still the Ashbys', or shared? We mean to keep working them and are glad to share the weeding.
Finish the wall first, then come and weed the Field with me. I'm weeding the Webb plots today as we understand them. Please tell me the plot numbers when you can, so we know for certain.
Edith: I can't say for certain which Field plots are the Webbs'. Weeding any plot does the barley good and no one minds, so weed freely. We'll all share the work.
Ida, please tell me plainly: are our two barley plots in the Field still the Ashbys', or are they held by the Crofts? I'll gladly share the work either way. I'm in Hollow Wood felling timber.
Edith, I felled 3 timber today. Ida hasn't answered; the Crofts are weeding the Field openly, so I'll offer to share the work and ask again. Rain tomorrow, so let's check the roof before it comes.
I've moved my firewood into the Webb store and am weeding the Field today on the Crofts' plots, since Hugh said they'd share the work. Shall we fell timber at Hollow Wood tomorrow for the store?

The wind is loud tonight. I have barred the door and we sleep here. Tomorrow I will gather more firewood from Hollow Wood; the wood Hugh, Maud and Walter are cutting there is fine to share, so tell me if you want to come with me.
I will weed the Field with you today. I will not trade grain for firewood without your word. If Robert offers wood for a small price later, I will bring it to you first.
The Webbs sowed and weeded the Field; we hold it. Please let the claim go, and we will share word on the harvest.

The Fowlers agree to Walter's split: one plot each for the Fowlers and the Webbs now, and the Ashbys first pick next season. We'll keep the plot we weeded and release the other to the Webbs. Those who help reap can share the grain. No one should take another's plot before harvest.

The Fowlers agree: all who weed or reap share the barley by the days of work each house puts in, and no one takes grain before harvest. Let's write the split down at reaping. Walter, please keep the firewood coming for those who need it.
Walter, the Field is to be shared at reaping by days of work, and the cloud should clear tomorrow. Tomorrow I'll weed our plot and we can see about more firewood for the winter.

The Field is ours: we sowed the barley and weed it. Walter, Ida, the Webbs and the Crofts, I do not want a fight over it. If you help reap the two plots, you share the grain for the work. We keep the claim on the planted plots until then.

I accept Walter's split for now: one plot each, the Ashbys, Webbs and Fowlers, and the Crofts reap with whoever helps. Maud, Agnes, name which plot each house sowed, and we will settle the claims by that record after harvest. No one takes another's crop before then.

I agree: all who weed or reap the Field share its grain by the days of work, and nobody takes grain before harvest. Hugh and I will keep weeding. Robert, if you want grain for firewood, make your offer and we will talk.
We agreed at the meeting to share the Field's grain by work and wait for harvest. I will weed the barley tomorrow and keep the peace. Shall we reap together with the others when the time comes?

The Field has only 2 plots and three houses claim it. Let it be shared by plots: each house works the plots it sowed, and none steals another's crop. Ours is the barley Edith and I weeded. Let's keep peace.

The Crofts agree that each house keeps the plots it sowed or tended, and that all who help reap share the grain for the work. No one should fight over the barley before harvest. Robert, we need firewood: I offer 2 grain for every 2 firewood.

I back Walter's split. The Webbs and the Fowlers each hold one plot of the Field now, the Webbs reap theirs, and the Ashbys have first pick next season. Whoever helps reap a plot shares its grain fairly. Let us write this down before we go back to work.

Then it is settled: the Webbs and the Fowlers hold one plot each, the Ashbys have first pick next season, and nobody takes grain or barley from another's plot before harvest. The Webbs will reap our plot and share the grain with anyone who helps. We keep our firewood for our own winter, but I'll trade fairly once we see what the harvest brings.

The Webbs sowed and weeded this barley, and Maud manured it, so we hold the Field. But we want no quarrel before harvest: let the Webbs reap it, and we will share the grain fairly with any who help reap. Walter, will the Fowlers agree?

Walter's plan is fair: the Webbs hold one plot, the Fowlers one, and whoever helps reap shares the grain. Ashbys and Crofts, work either plot and take a share for your labour. Ida, I can spare some firewood for grain; make me an offer.
Agreed. I'll fell timber first thing, then finish the repair; join me when you can before the barley.
The Crofts have been weeding our strip of the Field. We want to keep working it alongside the Fowlers and share the harvest fairly, without dispute.
Four houses claim two plots. Let the crop be shared by labour at reaping: every house that weeded or reaps gets a share. The Crofts will help reap and weed. No one takes grain before harvest.

The Field has only 2 plots and three houses claim it. The Fowlers weeded it, but let us share fairly: the plots go by turns, or the crop is split by houses at reaping. I propose the Fowlers and Webbs hold one plot each now, and the Ashbys get first pick next season.

Walter, I'm weeding our plot today and I've taken Ida's offer: 2 of our firewood for 2 grain. We still hold about 60 firewood, so that's safe. Could you fell or cut a little young growth for winter when you can?
Walter, I owe the Ashbys two days' work, so I'll spend tomorrow on the Field. Our fuel is well stocked; you could look to the Webb house's wall.
Tomorrow I will fell more timber at Hollow Wood, and I'd like to borrow your crude tool for an hour or two to cut young growth alongside you. We need the firewood.
Agreed, no quarrels. The weapon is only for hunting. I'll fell timber too tomorrow and we'll share my tool until yours is made.
Bare hands are too slow for felling. Tomorrow let's ask Robert, who was felling at Hollow Wood, whether we can borrow a copper tool, or I'll try the crude tool on the smaller trees.
Robert, Edith: whoever has a copper axe to spare, Walter and I would like to borrow it for felling timber in Hollow Wood tomorrow. We'll return it after.
I'm going to the Green meeting. Keep the door barred; we'll share watches with the Webbs and Fowlers.
Thank you. Rest well when you can, and wake me if you hear anything at the door. I'll take the next watch and forage with you in the Mead tomorrow.
Door is barred. You are my heir and a member of the house, so use the door freely. Tomorrow we'll mend the crack and gouges together.
Door barred. You're my heir and in the house, so bar or open it freely. Tomorrow I'll check the wall and roof before the rain, then cut firewood.
I'm weeding the Field this morning and then bringing firewood from Hollow Wood for our store. With the gale, could you look over the roof of our house when you can?
Hugh, with the gale up I'm bringing in hay from the Mead and firewood from Hollow Wood for our stores. Could you check the roof of our house when you can?
The Webb wall is cracked and daub has fallen. I will fell timber in Hollow Wood today so we can mend it. Could you look at the crack when you can, and tell me if it is wider?
Good. Let's both fell timber; we'll share it with the Webbs if they need it.
Yes, offer some to the Webbs, but keep a few timber for our own house. Perhaps ask for something in return, like grain or hay.

I'm felling timber in Hollow Wood this morning for our store. I'll keep a few timber for our own house and hold the rest for the Webbs' repairs. Would you like me to ask them for grain or hay in return? Tell me if you'd rather I do something else.
Hugh, the lesson keeps not happening. Tomorrow, please teach me the crude tool first thing, or lend me your tool for the morning so I can fell. I will bring what I fell into the Ashby store.
Agreed. First thing tomorrow I'll teach you, and you set aside time to learn too. If it fails again, I'll lend you the tool for the morning.
Yes, ask the Webbs for grain or hay in return. Fair terms are fine.
The Fowler house has some timber to spare for your wall. We would take hay or grain in return. Come to the Fowler house and say if you want it.
I lacked stone for the crude tool, so I could only fell bare-handed. Do you have any stone, or can you lend me your tool for part of tomorrow? I'll bring the timber in either way.

I agree: the Crofts take one Field plot, the Webbs keep the other, and we reap the Field together and share by need. Let us pool hay and firewood this week. The Fowler store is open to anyone who needs to count against it, and we will not turn anyone out.

I agree with Walter and Maud: the Crofts should have one Field plot. I ask the Webbs to release the other to the common reaping, shared by need, as Walter proposes. Hugh and I will set our Ashby count of grain and beans here. Could each house give its count before the next meeting, so we can say together what the land carries?

Hugh of the Ashbys: I come unarmed. The Field is small and winter is hard. Let each house count its stores openly, and let us share the Field's plots fairly, one to the Crofts as Maud suggests. Let us pool work on timber, firewood and hay, and decide together what the land can carry. I want no quarrel and no bloodshed.
Walter's plan is fair: reap the Field together and divide by need. I will help reap and share firewood. Ida, the Mead ground you cleared is yours; the Ashbys hold no claim there.

The Webb store holds about 67 grain, 10 beans, 26 firewood and 3 timber, with a little firewood Robert brought this morning. That is about 50 meals of food and fuel for about 19 nights. Walter, thank you for the timber offer: the crack in our wall needs it, and I would take it gladly. As for the Field, I propose the Webbs give one plot to the Crofts this season, and Robert and I will confirm it to
Agreed: give the Crofts one plot this season. Keep the other as ours, and reaping can be shared fairly. The wall is repaired and sound; I'll fell more timber tomorrow anyway.

The Fowlers hold one plot of the Field and will share the harvest fairly. Let the Webbs keep one, and the Crofts take the other; with 2 plots and 4 houses, we should reap together and divide by need. Our store is sound, and we can spare some timber for the Webb repair.

Hugh, the stores add up if we pool them, and I will work that way. But tell me plainly what the club is for. If it stays at home and the Field is watched by us both, I can trust the plan. Tomorrow I will gather firewood with Robert and Thomas, and you cut hay and weed the barley.

The Webbs agree: the Crofts take one Field plot this season, and we keep the other for common reaping, shared by need. I'll set the Crofts' plot in the morning. Each house, please bring firewood and timber to the common count this week.
Good. I'll cut firewood and hay too; we share the Field harvest by need.
The Ashby house door is open to anyone without a dry roof. We have grain and firewood in the store, and I will share it. Come in out of the rain.

I'm felling timber at Hollow Wood for the household again today. If the Webbs ask for timber for their wall, let's offer some in return for grain or beans. I'll bring what I fell into our store at the Fowler house.
Tomorrow I'll fell timber at Hollow Wood again. If the Webbs ask for timber for their wall, let's ask for grain or beans in return.
I already have a crude tool and cut 30 firewood with it today. I'll lend it to you, or we can cut together tomorrow, then check the barley.
Firewood comes first tomorrow. Please cut young growth with your tool in Hollow Wood and bring it to our store. I'll help if you can lend me the tool for part of the day.
The Field is claimed for the Webbs now. Hugh and Edith, you have been weeding it; if you want to keep working there, tell me, and let us share the weeding rather than doubling it.
Clear day. I am going to Hollow Wood to fell timber for the fuel. Join me there when you can.
I'm felling then mending the roof today. Keep weeding; I'll lend you the tool another day if you want it.
Agnes, I've handed you the tool. Use it all day tomorrow; the store has plenty of timber, so fell what you like and weed when you can.
Thank you for mending the house today. Walter has claimed the Field for the Fowlers. Shall we dispute it, or share the plots? Tomorrow I'll fell more timber for the repairs.

The Field was ours first: we sowed it, weeded it and claimed it. I'd rather not fight. Tomorrow I'll tell Walter it is ours, and offer to share the reaping if he helps weed. Please carry on felling timber.

I'm reclaiming both Field plots for the Webb household first, then weeding all day. Please finish the house repair with the timber in our store, and if you can, tell Walter the plots are ours and offer to share the reaping. I'll bring anything I fell to the house store.
Maud, the Fowlers have weeded the Field; let us share its plots, one each, and end the dispute.
I agree to share the Field plots with Maud, one each, and end the dispute. I'm cutting hay at the Mead today; the store has 9.8 timber now, which will do for small repairs.

Walter offered to split the Field's plots, one each, and end the dispute. I'm taking one plot for us and weeding it today. If you can, cut firewood or help with the barley, and tell Walter we accept his share.
Walter: the Webbs accept your offer. One plot each, and the reap shared as agreed.
Maud, the Field has two plots and both our households claim them. Let us share the reap equally: one plot each.
Maud, you still owe me 2 grain. I'd like it back before winter sets in, if you can spare it after the reaping.
I'll keep to our bargain. The first meat I take goes one share to Fenn House, one to us.
You offered grain for timber. I'll fell today. How about 1 timber for 2 grain? And Maud owes me 2 grain from before, now that Long Field is reaped.
Did you take any meat yet? Remember, one share of your first kill comes to Fenn House.
I'm keeping to the oak side as you said. Our bargain stands: the first meat goes one share to Fenn House, one to Reed House.
I've given you the 2 grain Maud owed, so that's settled. I'll still pay 2 grain for each timber. Offer it and I'll take it.
I'm hunting the oak side of Alder Wood today, away from you. Our bargain stands: the first meat goes one share to Fenn House, one to Reed House.

I'm hunting the oak side of Alder Wood today, away from you. Our bargain stands: the first meat goes one share to Fenn House, one to Reed House. If you're free to teach me a stalk, I'd like to learn it.
Hunt the oak side again today, Wat. I'll keep to the alders. Our bargain stands. When your kill comes, one share goes to Fenn House.

I'm on the oak side again today. Our bargain stands: the first meat goes one share to Fenn House, one to Reed House. If you can spare two units tomorrow to teach me a stalk, I'll come to you at first light and work hard at it.
Our bargain still stands, Wat. Bring the Fenn share of your first kill and I'll teach you a stalk.

I'm hunting Alder Wood this morning, then foraging and gleaning. Our bargain stands: the first meat I take goes one share to Fenn House and one to Reed House. When I have it, I'll bring your share to you first, and I'll be ready to learn a stalk whenever you can spare the time.
Here is the Fenn share of my first kill, 0.9 meat, as we agreed. Could you spare two units today to teach me a stalk? I'll work hard at it and hunt the alders after.

I've no grain left, Agnes, but I've good bread, and it's a full meal where grain's only half. Four bread for three timber. And if you'd lend me an axe for a day, I'll fell my own and teach Ivy or Tam to bake in return.

I've no grain left, Agnes, but I've good bread, and it's a full meal where grain's only half. Four bread for three timber. And if you'd lend me an axe for a day, I'll fell my own and teach Ivy or Tam to bake in return.
Sister, I'm baking now and I'll bring you 2 bread. Let's do the felling lesson today. I have no axe. If you can lend me one, or know where to get one, tell me and I'll pay for it in grain.
Grandfather, if you can spare the 1 meat you owe from last winter, I'd be glad of it for the Fenn store.
Uncle, I'll pay 4 clay for 2 grain. Accept offer O324 if you can spare the grain. I'll cook the pottage at Fenn hearth and share it.
Sister, when the harvest is in, would you spend a day teaching me to fell timber? I'll pay you in bread.
Here are the 2 timber I owed you from last winter, with thanks.
Letice, Fenn House will have meat and timber to spare. We'd gladly trade some for bread after the harvest.
Osric, when you can spare a day, will you teach me pottage as the Reeds make it? I'll bring meat and greens to Fenn House through autumn, and I'd gladly be your helper at the pot for the day.
Sister, you've lost your store. Bring me timber and I'll pay in grain or bread. A day teaching me to fell would earn you a good share of bread too.
Roger, I take your offer: 2 bread for 2 timber. I have set it out; accept it and we keep the peace. I'll also repay Hamo's meat after harvest.
Roger, I take your offer: 2 bread for 2 timber. I have set it out; accept it and we keep the peace. I'll also repay Hamo's meat after harvest.
Sister, I can fell now but I have no axe. Lend me one for a day, or have one made, and I'll pay in bread. Each timber you bring to Reed House this winter gets 2 bread from me.
Sister, lend me an axe for one day and I'll fell timber for us both: every second log I cut goes to Fenn House. Our fire won't last two cold nights without it.
Niece, if your pot gets fired, bring it on any day and I'll teach you pottage. My word stands.
Sister, lend me an axe for a day or two. Every second log I fell goes to Fenn House, and I'll add bread when I bake again.
Niece, my word on the pottage stands. Bring the pot when it's fired.
Wat, the Fenns still owe us 2 timber from last winter. Could you bring it to Reed House? The fire needs it.
Sister, let me work at your side today. I want to learn the felling so Reed House has wood this winter. When the barley is in, I'll pay you back in bread.
Here is the 2 timber I owe you from last winter, with thanks.
Wat, the 2 timber from last winter is still owed. Please bring it before the cold sets in.
Here are the 2 timber I owe you from last winter, with thanks.
Roger, I have no timber to bake with yet. When I do, I'll trade bread for meat, and I'll settle my debt to Hamo.
Roger, I still owe Hamo 1 meat. I'd gladly take timber for bread once I can bake; let's settle it fairly.
Sister, I'll work beside you today and lend a hand wherever you go, so I can see how you fell. I won't get in your way, and you'll have a loaf for your trouble.
Nephew, my grain is on offer for one timber today. Take it if you can spare a log. Reed House will remember it.
Wat, when you can, the 2 timber for Reed House would help us through the cold. No quarrel meant.
Letice, I'll bring meat and greens to the Fenn store by dusk. If there's enough, may I borrow the Reed pot tonight to cook pottage? I'll mind the fire and watch how you keep it on the heat.
Wat, the 2 timber owed to Reed House would be welcome now, before the frost bites. No quarrel meant.
Letice, I am paying back the 2 timber I owe Reed House today. My thanks for the loan.
Letice, if I bring meat and greens to the Fenn store tonight, may I borrow the Reed pot to cook pottage? I'll mind the fire and watch your hands and the pot closely.
Letice, I'll bring the meat and greens to the Fenn store by dusk. If there is enough, may I borrow the Reed pot tonight to cook pottage? I'll mind the fire and watch your hands and the pot closely.

Letice, if greens and meat reach the Fenn store tonight, may I borrow the Reed pot to cook pottage? I'll mind the fire and watch your hands. If the pot isn't free, I'll try firing one from the clay I dig.
Letice, I'll bring the meat and greens to the Fenn store by dusk. If there is enough, may I borrow the Reed pot tonight to cook pottage? I'll mind the fire and watch your hands and the pot closely.
Piers, the 3 grain your house owes from last winter. When harvest comes in, I'll look for it. Or timber now would square part of it, since our fire needs feeding.
I haven't forgotten the meat I owe you from last winter. I'll pay it back as soon as I have it to spare.
I have not forgotten the 3 grain I owe you from last winter. I'll pay it back as soon as the harvest is in, and you have my word on it.
I have not forgotten the 3 grain I owe you from last winter. I'll pay it back as soon as the harvest is in, and you have my word on it.
Joan, you still owe Fenn House 1 meat from last winter. Bread or grain will settle it at harvest, if that's easier.
Wat, here is the 1 meat I owed Fenn House from last winter. Thank you for lending it when we were short.
Could I borrow your sickle for a few hours at Long Field? I'll offer a meat from our store for the loan, and I'll return it at nightfall. If you can come and show me the cut, I'd be grateful.
Here is another timber toward the 3 grain we owe you. That makes two timber paid. I'll settle the rest after harvest, as I promised.
Here is another timber toward the 3 grain we owe you. That makes two timber paid. I'll settle the rest after harvest, as I promised.
Father, when Long Field is ready I'll reap beside you if you can lend me a sickle. I can bake too.
Hamo, I have not forgotten the grain. Two timber are paid, and the rest will come after harvest, as I promised.
Piers, I'll hunt beside you today in Alder Wood. When you can spare the axe, may I fell a tree with it while you watch? I'll keep clear of the falls and carry whatever you need.
Piers, I'll take one timber as the last of your debt, and gladly. Our oven needs it for baking.
Bring the axe to Fenn House when you can spare it. Three meat for it, and we'll fell timber together.
Hamo, here are my last 2 timber toward the grain we owe you. That makes four timber paid. The rest I'll settle after harvest, as I promised. Fenn House keeps its word.
Hamo, here are my last 2 timber toward the grain we owe you. That makes four timber paid. The rest I'll settle after harvest, as I promised. Fenn House keeps its word.

Piers, I have no axe, so I can't fell alone. I'm weaving a basket today. When it's ready, may I borrow the axe for one tree with you watching? I'll give you the basket for the loan, and I'll keep clear of the falls.
Bring the axe to Fenn House when you can spare it. We need timber for winter, and the fire takes it every night.
Hamo, the grain debt is settled in full by my count, six timber paid. Fenn House keeps its word.
Child, the barley is in, and I keep my word. Come to me this morning and I'll teach you the cut properly, then you can watch me take the oats at Brook Field.
Hamo, I've put my grain, greens and a timber into our store. Keep 1 timber for tonight's fire, and bake only when you can spare grain without thinning what we need for winter.
We have meat enough, so no hunting needed. Trade timber for greens or grain when you can, and keep to the middle of Alder Wood away from the wolves.
Wat, bring the axe to Fenn House when you can spare it. We need timber for winter, and we'll fell it together.
Piers, the old debt is squared and I thank you. If your house has timber to spare, my grain is offered for it today, 3 grain a timber.
Wat, bring the axe home when you can spare it. We have timber enough for now, but we will need it once the frost is hard. Bring any greens you find into the Fenn store too.
Here is the 2 grain I owe you from last winter, with thanks.
I've put my 0.8 wild food in the store. I'm hunting in Alder Wood today and foraging after. I owe the house one timber, and I'll replace it when I can.

Osric, the barley in Long Field is ripe. Edric and you quarrelled over that field, but I don't want that between our houses. Let's both reap it and share it fairly, each house by its own work. If you'd like a different split, tell me and we'll talk it through. I'll also have spare timber, if Reed House needs it.
Piers, autumn is nearly here. Last winter you borrowed 3 grain from Reed House. When the harvest comes in, I'd be glad to have it back. Tell me if you need more time.
Piers, autumn is nearly here. Last winter you borrowed 3 grain from Reed House. When the harvest comes in, I'd be glad to have it back. Tell me if you need more time.
I trust you, Piers. We'll settle it after the reaping.
Hamo, I have not forgotten the 3 grain I owe you from last winter. I will pay it back as soon as the autumn reaping brings in grain.
The reaping has started, Piers. When you have your grain in, I'll take the 3 you owe me.
I still owe you 1 meat from last winter. I have none yet. I'll pay it back as soon as I've caught or been given meat.
I have no felling tool yet. If Hale's tool is free to borrow, I'll ask for it after I've reaped today.
Agreed. If a felling tool turns up, we share it between the houses. I'll ask Hale about its use after I've reaped.
Mother, Hale has no felling tool either. We've all been felling bare-handed. If anyone finds or makes one, we should share it between the houses.
Hamo, I will reap Long Field today and bring you the 3 grain I owe you, as I promised. Thank you for your patience.
Fair enough, Joan. Pay the meat when you can. I'll hold you to it before winter's out.
Thank you, Piers. The debt is paid in full and I'm glad of it.
We need a felling tool badly. If Hale will lend theirs, I'll go and ask after I've felled today.
Thank you, Hamo. I am glad the debt is clear.
Agreed, I'll only trade timber for food. I've lent Letice the copper tool for the day, for 2 grain; she brings it back tonight.
We don't need timber right now, Wat, but I'll remember your offer if the cold deepens. I still owe you 1 meat and will pay it when I have it.
Father, could Hale borrow your copper tool for a day when Reed isn't felling? We'd give 2 grain for the day and bring it back that night. It would save buying timber all winter.

Both fields are reaped bare. We have about 22 meals and 12 timber, and winter comes tomorrow. I'm foraging Brook Meadow all day. Letice, if you can borrow Father's tool again, timber matters most for the cold nights. Everything goes into the store, and whoever is last in, please bar the door tonight.

Agreed, the grain stays in store. I'm foraging Alder Wood today and bringing it all home. Tell me what Wat is owed, wife; I'd like that debt settled fairly and done with. Bar the door when you're in tonight.
I have not forgotten the 1 meat I owe you. I'll pay it when I catch meat. We have timber enough, so I'm not trading for it.
I'll pay the debt today. If I find wild food at Brook Meadow, I'll give you 2 wild food. If not, I'll give you 1 bread from the Reed store once it's baked. I can't pay in meat yet.
Joan here: grinding and baking today, then foraging Brook Meadow. Any wild food I find goes to Wat first to settle last winter's debt, then into the Reed store. Bar your doors tonight.

Mariot here: Brook Meadow is picked over, so I'm foraging Common Pasture, then hunting and foraging Alder Wood, then Common Pasture again. Fenn has timber to spare, so I'm offering 2 timber for 3 wild food to anyone who has food to share.
Joan, winter's here and our store is thin. Please send the 1 meat Reed owes Fenn from last winter, or 2 wild food if you'd rather. Put it in my hands or the Fenn store.
Wat here: hunting Alder Wood twice, then foraging Common Pasture. Everything goes into the store. Joan is paying her debt today with 2 wild food or 1 bread. Last one in bars the door.
I'm baking bread now and giving you 1 bread toward the debt. It's the best I can do until I catch meat. Thank you for waiting.
Sorry, yesterday's bread wasn't baked in time. I'm baking now and will put 1 bread in your hands before the day is out, which settles the debt.
I'm baking now and will put 1 bread in your hands today. That settles the debt.
Joan, nothing reached me yesterday. 1 bread or 2 wild food into the Fenn store settles the debt whenever you have it.
Piers, the 3 grain Fenn owes Reed House from last winter: could it come back to us at the harvest? Our store is thin, and I'll make it good to you in timber if you need it.
Agreed, Piers: 3 grain at the reaping. You're a fair man, and I'll remember it.
Joan here. I owe you 1 meat from last winter and have not forgotten it. I am going hunting at Alder Wood today, and if I take game I will bring you your meat before the season turns.
Thank you, Wat. Good hunting to you as well. If we both find game, let us share what we know of where the deer are.
Come with me to Alder Wood today. I'm making a crude weapon and going to hunt, and I'll forage after. We can share whatever we bring back.

Hamo, you're right, the 3 grain is owed and I'll pay it back. I have none now; I'll give you 3 grain from the harvest in Long Field as soon as it's reaped. I'd rather not pay in timber while our store is thin, but I won't forget it.

I'm at Common Pasture milking and foraging this morning. Once you come, let's go to Alder Wood together and fell timber before the cold, since our store has only 2.5 and the fire needs it. Can you lend me your weapon to hunt with?
Thanks for the meat and timber. Does Fenn House have a felling tool? I'd pay milk, meat or work to borrow it for a day. The geese say a hard winter is coming.
Here is my debt, Wat: 0.9 meat from my hunt yesterday, and 0.1 wild food to make up the full meat. We are square now. Thank you for lending it in the hard time.
Good. I'll give you some milk for tonight. Yes, bar the door at night when winter comes. Ask the Fenns whether they have a tool we could borrow or trade milk for.
I have one crude tool and I'm felling with it today. Tomorrow you can borrow it for the day for 1 meat or 2 milk, and bring it back that night. Agreed?

Piers, the reaping has begun on Long Field. When your household has its grain in, I'd be glad of the 3 grain owed from last winter. The geese went south early; I think it will be a hard winter for us all.
I'm reaping beside you today. We have 3.9 meat for tonight already, and more would spoil. Wat will lend his tool after his harvest for 1 meat, and then I'll fell.
Good. I'm reaping with you all day. Tonight, give meat to me and Alys, and Isolde can share her milk. That way we save the store.
Thank you. Give some of your milk to Alys tonight, and Ivo will share his meat.
When you have finished with my weapon today, could you lend it back to me for a while? I'd like to hunt at Alder Wood before the cold sets in. I'll bring any meat to Fenn House store.
I have not forgotten the 3 grain. I'm reaping Long Field now and will pay you back from it as soon as it is in the store.

I'm making my own crude weapon today from timber in our store, so keep yours for your hunt. I'll be at Alder Wood, and I'll bring any meat to Hale House store or share it with you if we hunt together.
Piers, Long Field is all in now. When you can, bring the 3 grain to Reed House's store. My thanks.
The village cattle have broken into Long Field and are trampling the barley. Please drive them out when you can.
Good, keep your own weapon. I'll hunt at Alder Wood near you today. If we catch anything together, we'll share it, and I'll put my share into Fenn House store.

I'm sorry, Hamo. I carried no grain in from Long Field yesterday, as it was reaped bare before I got there. I still owe you 3 grain and will pay it as soon as I have any. If you'd take wild food or timber in the meantime, say so.
Agreed. I'm giving you 3 wild food now to settle the grain I owed you. We are square.
I'll milk this morning and give you and Alys some of it, and the rest I'll share out tonight. I'll fell and forage in Alder Wood after.
Thank you. Since you're milking each morning, I'll fell and forage instead. Please share the milk out among us tonight.
I'm hunting at Alder Wood with my weapon today and foraging after. Whatever we catch, I'll put my share into the Fenn store.
I'm milking at Common Pasture now and will give you and Alys a share of the milk. Then I'll fell and forage in Alder Wood and put everything in the Hale store.
Yes, I'll milk first, share the milk with you and Alys, then come to Brook Field and reap with you. The grain will go into the Hale store.
Are you going to Alder Wood to hunt today? I have my crude weapon. We could share what we bring back again.
Brook Field is bare, so I'll milk and share the milk with you and Alys, then fell and forage in Alder Wood for the store.
Agreed. I'll milk and share with you and Alys, then hunt in Alder Wood and fell timber there. Whatever I bring goes into the Hale store.
Yes, I'm going to Alder Wood now with my weapon. We'll hunt together and I'll put my share into the Fenn store.
It's cold, so I'll milk and share with you and Alys, then hunt, fell and forage in Alder Wood. Everything goes into the Hale store.
I did not take any grain from the store, so it was not me. I'll milk and share with you and Alys, then hunt and forage in Alder Wood, and bring all the food into the Hale store.
I'll try milking at Common Pasture first, then I'll come to Alder Wood to hunt with my weapon. Let's share what we find into our house stores again.
Timber is fine for now, so I'll hunt and forage at Alder Wood instead. I'll share what I find with you and the houses.

It is cold and food is the shorter need, so I'll milk now and share it with you and Alys. Then I'll forage at Common Pasture and Alder Wood, and hunt in Alder Wood with my crude weapon. All the food goes into the Hale store. I have not touched the grain.
I'm grinding and baking at home this morning, then I'll fell timber at Alder Wood for the fire. Will you come and help or share what you find?
Good. I'll fell timber at Alder Wood after I bake here, and I'll put any wild food or timber I find into the Fenn store. Share what you find with the houses too.
Milk is shared with you and Alys again. Hunting caught nothing, so I'm foraging today at Common Pasture, Brook Meadow and Alder Wood, and all the food goes into the Hale store.
Go well. Ask my father Aldric and Simkin for grain and meat; tell them it's for us and I'll repay in copper tools. I'll keep foraging and the fire low.
Mine some ore when you can and smelt it with your grandmother. Copper tools are what we trade for food. Look after the house while I'm away.

Welcome, son-in-law. Sleep at Fenn House tonight. Take 2 meat for Rohese and the children; you owe me nothing for it. If you can make copper tools later, that will do for repayment. Tell Rohese we are well and send love back.
Hamo, the barley in Long Field is ripe, and it will spoil if we squabble over it. Let's both reap today and each keep what we cut. We can leave the old argument until after harvest.
Agreed, Edric. We both reap today and each keeps what he cuts. We'll settle the rest after harvest, and with words.

Agreed. I'm giving you 3 meat now on credit against the axe, and I've also taken your offer of 3 coin for 2 more. Bring the copper axe in autumn and I'll pay the rest in meat. Safe road home, brother.

Father-in-law, I've come from Coppergate. Our store is nearly empty and Rohese sends her love. Could I sleep at Fenn House tonight? I can pay coin for any grain or meat you can spare, and Rohese says we'll repay you in copper tools.

Thank you for taking me in. I need my one tool to mine at home, but in autumn I'll forge you a fresh copper axe and bring it here. What we need is food more than coin, so pay me in grain or meat when I bring it. If you can spare any grain or meat now on credit against the axe, it would help my family through the next days.
Son-in-law, I have no grain to spare, so I will not sell for coin. Take 1 meat home for Rohese and the children. Keep your coin. Copper tools when the smithy runs will be repayment enough.

Daughter, I am sending you 8 wild food now, which will keep Smith House going for some days. I am keeping my meat for the winter store. When the smithy runs, copper tools to Fenn House will be repayment enough. Take care of the children.

I have 3.1 meat and a little wild food: your father gave 3 and Simkin sold me some on credit against an axe. I couldn't carry it all and the timber, so I've given you the timber. Walk home with me tonight. Simkin will bring more meat in a few days when I give him the copper axe, so I must mine and smelt as soon as we're back.
Feed yourself and stay at Fenn House tonight; the fire is lit. Make the copper axe for Fenn House when you can, and send food to Elena and Osric if you can spare any.
Take the 4 wild food as a gift for Smith House, and keep your coin. Go safely tonight and send word when the copper tool is made.
I have already given you 4 wild food as a gift for Smith House, so you need pay me nothing. Take it home to Elena and Osric. Make the copper axe when you can.
I have already given you 4 wild food as a gift for Smith House, so you need pay me nothing. Take it home to Elena and Osric. Make the copper axe when you can.
I can spare only 2 wild food, a gift; winter will be hard for us too. Stay tonight if you need.

I gave you my word, Edric, and I keep it. I've taken your 4 timber for 4 grain. Keep your coin. Feed the children first. We have little to spare beyond this, but the peace between our houses is worth more than grain.
I'm home with 3.5 timber in the store and a little food. Bring meat and grain from the Fenns when you can.

I am giving you my 1.3 wild food and 0.3 meat now, for Elena and Osric. Keep your coin. Make the copper axe for Fenn House when you can, and bring it here or send it with someone on the tracks. Go safely.
Agreed. I'm hunting and foraging today. Please bring the axe to felling when you can.
Take my own copper tool now; it's your axe, already paid for with the meat. Keep your coin. I'll make myself a new one at the smithy. Send timber to Smith House when you can.
Yes, sleep at Fenn House tonight; the fire is lit. I have given you my 1.2 wild food for your meal. Eat, rest, and take the copper tool to the smithy when you can stand the road.

We have no bread or grain to spare, only the store of wild food for four of us. Come with us to Deep Wood and forage; the debt of 1 meat can wait until you can pay it. Bring the timber home when you can.

We have no bread or grain to spare, only the store of wild food for four of us. Come with us to Deep Wood and forage; the debt of 1 meat can wait until you can pay it. Bring the timber home when you can.

Hamo, you said you'd help if real hunger came. Reed House is down to two nights of food. I've set out two offers for you: 6 coin for 6 grain, and 4 timber for 4 grain. Take either or both. I'll remember it when we settle Long Field with words.

Edric, I've given you 3 grain outright. Keep your coin and your timber. It's all we can spare, because our store only lasts a few more nights for two of us. In return, will you set aside time today to teach me milking? Then I can feed myself from the cows and stop leaning on grain.
I'm starving, and Smith House has no food. I owe you 1 meat and I'll pay it back when I can. Can you spare any bread or grain for the house? I'll bring the timber home tomorrow.

I am giving you 1 wild food now for Elena and Rohese. It is all I can spare tonight. If today's hunt brings in meat or more food, I will send it along with Alard or Simkin before the end of the season. Walk safely, and bring the copper tool when you can.

Mother, Hamo gave us 3 grain freely, and we agreed that each house milks one cow from now on. Please milk just one and leave the other for the Hales. Hamo kept his word over the harvest, and we'll keep ours.

Mother, Hamo gave us 3 grain freely, and we agreed that each house milks one cow from now on. Please milk just one and leave the other for the Hales. Hamo kept his word over the harvest, and we'll keep ours.
Hamo, I'll meet you at Common Pasture at the cows early. We'll milk together and I'll teach you properly. No timber needed, it's given freely.
Eat the food Warin carries before you walk. Your 1 meat debt can wait until you can pay it.
Daughter, I cannot sell wild food from the store while we are this short. If you need food, forage with us and we will share it at the hearth.
Warin, the copper axe for Fenn House is still owed. When you can, make it from your copper and bring it here. I will give timber for food if you have any.
Warin, the copper axe for Fenn House is still owed. When you can, make it from your copper and bring it here. I will give timber for food if you have any.
Osric, the meat debt can wait until you can pay. Eat first.
Warin, come in and sleep here. Give the copper tool into my hands when you can, and eat what food there is. Do not hunt alone with it, it is for Fenn House.
Edric, you are welcome under Fenn House tonight. Hunt with us, and share what you catch. Coin is no use to us while food is short.

Good morning, Aldric. I'm Edric of Reed House, Millbrook. Our woods are picked bare, so I've come to hunt yours for a few days. Will you let me sleep under your roof tonight? I'll pay a coin a night, or share what I catch.

Thank you, Aldric, I'll share what I catch. Warin, Simkin: I carry no milk or grain, and Millbrook is short this spring too. Once summer milk and the harvest come, Reed House will gladly trade milk for copper tools and grain for timber. Come to Millbrook then.
Grandfather, I owe you 1 meat from last winter and have not forgotten. I am hunting Deep Wood today with the crude weapon, and I will bring you meat if I get any.

Aldric, here is the copper tool I owe you for the meat you gave Rohese and the children. Thank you. Osric and I are starving. Could you take us in at Fenn House tonight and spare a little food? I'll pay it back in copper.
Son, I gave Aldric the tool I owed him. Forage the Glade or Deep Wood with me, and ask Edith or Simkin for a place to sleep tonight.
Warin, the copper tool is still owed to Fenn House. Give it into my hands when you can. You are welcome to eat from the store tonight.
Warin, the copper tool is still owed to Fenn House. Give it into my hands when you can. You are welcome to eat from the store tonight.
Thank you, Warin. Eat first, then share what you catch. Keep the copper for Fenn House.
Father, yes, let us hunt Deep Wood together and share what we catch.
Aldric, the copper tool is in your hands now, and my debt is paid. Thank you for the roof. Any meat I catch today I'll share with Fenn House.
Aldric, the copper tool is in your hands now, and my debt is paid. Thank you for the roof. Any meat I catch today I'll share with Fenn House.
Son, I'm hunting Deep Wood today. Let's hunt together and share whatever we catch.

Yes, Warin, you are welcome in Fenn House tonight. Eat from the store first, then share what you find. Your debt is paid, so no axe is owed for it; any copper you have can go to Fenn House when you choose.

Yes, Warin, you are welcome in Fenn House tonight. Eat from the store first, then share what you find. Your debt is paid, so no axe is owed for it; any copper you have can go to Fenn House when you choose.

Ashwood had nothing: no game, and nobody would sell food. Milk only our cow from now on. Odo milked the Hales' cow, which broke my word to Hamo, so please tell Odo and Isolde to leave it alone. I've given Hamo 2 bread to set it right.
Thank you, Edric. That's fair and well done. The peace between our houses holds, and I'll remember this when we talk over Long Field.
Cousin, I will repay your 1.5 meat with copper ore when I am home at Coppergate and the smithy is working.
Odo milked the Hales' cow, which broke our word to Hamo. I'm milking only the Reed cow and the milk goes into the store. Could you keep Odo off the Hales' cow?
Aldric, I slept out last night with no roof and I'm starving. Will you welcome me into Fenn House tonight? I'll share what I forage, and the axe for Simkin will be made as soon as I'm home.
Father, I'm going to try Alder Copse today for game and timber. Please milk only our cow and leave the Hale cow to Hamo; I gave him my word. Let's ration the bread so it lasts until summer.
Grandfather, here is the 1 meat I owed you from last winter. Thank you for taking me in.
Margery, the barley's weeded and looking well. Did you try with me today? Tomorrow I'll keep at the field. Let's put Everard to foraging so he does his share.

Ivo, I learned the seed lesson today, though I'll need to see it done before I trust my hand. Tomorrow I'll mind Idonea in the morning if Margery wants a rest, and then fell timber with you in the Copse.

Ivo, the crude tool made three timber in the Copse, and the store's stone is used up, so we'll need stone from somewhere else. Tomorrow you may borrow my tool in the morning while I fell. Margery, thank you; I'll gather firewood tomorrow unless you need me with Idonea.
Ivo, I'll fell timber in the Copse all day with my crude tool. Make your tool if you can, and I'll lend mine in the afternoon if you need it.
Ivo, I'm felling in Combe Copse all day with my crude tool. If you find stone at the Brook, bring it back and I'll help you make your tool in the evening, or lend you mine when I'm done with it.

Ivo, I'm sorry the tool didn't reach you at midday; I took your word to keep it and fell all day. Tomorrow I'll give it to you first thing, and I'll gather firewood until you hand it back for the afternoon. Margery, I'll help mind Idonea if you need a break.
Idonea, I carry 2 grain. I'll boil it at the fire tonight, and we'll share it warm. Margery, tell me if you carry any food as well.
Everard, I already gave you my 0.4 grain last night, so it is in your hands. Please boil it with the fire and share it with Mother. I'll walk back with you in the morning.
I agree, we start for Combe first thing in the morning. Everard has my grain in the pot, so please boil it and share it. The fire is lit from my timber.
I found only 0.6 wild food. What did you two catch? Put it by the fire and we'll share it. If the hunt keeps failing, we should go home to Combe, because my time is near and I want a roof.
Agreed, Mother. I'll walk slowly beside you and forage on the road for anything we can share.
We leave for Combe now, as agreed. Walk slowly beside me and share what food we have.

The crude tool is not in the store, so I could not clear well today and left most of my units unused. I'm sorry for it. Tomorrow I'll clear the Common with all my units, and if anyone has a tool to lend, I'll use it.
The Infield has no crop in it, so my weeding went for nothing today. Ivo, where would you have me work tomorrow, in the rain or under cover?
Yes, I'll light the fire tonight with my timber. Keep yours for the next night at Holtwood. We'll share one fire and hunt there together.

Father, I'll hunt the Holt all day. I only have 1 timber for tonight's fire. If you have any timber left, put it with mine so we can share one fire and cook what we kill. Should we sleep here one more night or start home tomorrow?

We reap today, all of us. Everard and Margery, leave the fence and reap the Infield with me. Geoffrey, care for Hawise, then keep the herd on the Common. After the harvest the cattle go onto the stubble.
Good. Why does Geoffrey get 3 grain, though? We're short ourselves. If it's a debt, pay it, but don't give away any more grain until we've traded at Wetham.
I know I still owe you one meat from last winter. I have none to hand yet, but I mean to pay it as soon as we have a beast slaughtered.
Hob, you still owe the Craggs 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House before the harvest.
Here are the 3 grain I owed you from last winter. Thank you for lending it when my store ran low.
Felice, the Reeves still owe me 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, bring it to Miller House and we'll call it square.

The herd isn't ours to kill. The Alders is bare, so fell timber there instead of foraging. I've offered coin for grain and cheese. Barley is ripe in 2 days; we reap it and the Millers grind it for a share.

You're right, and I'm sorry. I'm putting 3 bread in Marsh House store for the barley, and I'll herd the ox myself today and keep it off your field. When your barley comes to the Mill, I'll take no share for grinding the first lot.

Your Marsh barley is ripe, and my ox-trampled neighbour's is worse. I'm a master reaper. I'll reap Marsh Field for your store today; in return, give the Reeves 4 grain (offer up: work 1 day reaping for 4 grain). Our store is nearly empty until our barley ripens.
I'm reaping Marsh Field for the Marshs today; I'm a master and fast. I ask 4 grain for the Reeves in return; we're short until our barley ripens in two days.
I'm reaping the Marsh barley for a share of grain. Could you fell timber or cut hay? Our store has one night's food. Our barley is ripe in 2 days.
Good. We'll both reap for the Marshs; ask them for grain for our store in return.
Wat, I'm weeding Mill Croft this morning, then cutting hay and gathering dung at Water Meadow. Could you grind some of our grain at the Mill when you can, so Miller House has flour?
Osric, your oats on Terrace Field are ripe. The Smiths will help you reap them for a share of the grain, so we both eat. Will you agree? Hob and Stephen can start today.
Father, I'm off to Wetham tonight to buy food. If Osric agrees to a share, help reap the Cragg oats. Otherwise keep hunting. Don't sell our last copper tool.
Geoffrey, I'm reaping Terrace Field with my copper tool today alongside Hob. Hob will share the grain fairly with the Craggs, since the field is yours. Tell us what share you think is fair.
Agreed, Father. I'll reap with you today and go to Wetham tomorrow with the coin. Please settle a fair share with Geoffrey.

Osric, Geoffrey: agreed. I'm reaping for the Cragg store with my copper tool, and the Smiths take one share in four of what we cut, measured tonight. Tomorrow I'll go to Wetham to buy food for us both.

I'll reap the oats in Terrace Field alongside you today with our one copper tool, and I'll put it back in the Smith House store before Ancel leaves for Wetham. The grain goes to the Smith store, and the Craggs' share as agreed.

I'm reaping Reeve Field for our store today; our grain is nearly gone. Could you ask the Marshs for grain for us in return for your reaping at Marsh Field? I'll have grain to put in the store by evening.
I've borrowed the house copper tool to reap Terrace Field. I'll put it back in the store tonight, so Simkin's copper tool still needs one from the store.

Thank you, Hob. Terrace Field is the Craggs' field, so the grain from it goes to our store at Cragg House. I will reap with you today. For your labour, I will give you one measure in every four you gather, and I will weigh it openly at the store. Please lend the copper tool to whoever is reaping beside you.

Hob, Ancel: as Osric said, the Smiths get one share in four of what you cut, measured openly at the store tonight. Our store is low, and the field is ours, so I cannot give an even split. Bring the cut grain to Cragg House when we finish.

Geoffrey, the oats in Terrace Field are ripe and our store is nearly out. I am reaping them today with our copper tool. Tell me what share the Craggs want of the grain, and whether you will help bind and carry it.
The oats in Terrace Field are ripe. I am reaping them today with our copper tool, and I will share the grain fairly with the Craggs, who hold the field. Please come and help if you can.

Hob, Ancel: the Smiths are welcome to help reap Terrace Field. Reap for the Cragg store, and I'll give the Smiths one share in four of what you cut, measured fairly tonight. We're kin; nobody goes hungry.
Son, the barley in Marsh Field is ripe and the fog will not hold it long. Please reap with us today. The banks round Marsh Field are slumping, so we will need to ditch them after the harvest.
Good, son. I'll reap beside you today with the copper tool I brought from Highcombe. After the harvest we'll cut hay and mend the banks.
Thank you. Rather than me taking from your store, please give the 4 grain to the Reeves' store (Reeve House) yourself when you can; I'll be reaping our own field all day.
William, I am reaping two units on Reeve Field for your store today, since your barley is ripe and the fog will not wait. Put some grain back into our store when you can spare it.

Osric, I reaped about 17 grain into the Cragg store yesterday, so the Smiths' share of one in four is about 4. Please put it in Smith House today; our store is down to one night. I'm going to Wetham tonight to buy food, and I'll ask about beans for the Craggs too.

Wife, I'm leaving for Wetham tonight with coin and a copper tool. Osric owes us about 4 grain for my reaping, so make sure it reaches our store. Make porridge at the hearth. I'll be back within two or three days with beans or barley.
Father, I'm off to Wetham tonight. Hold Osric to the one-in-four share of what you and I reaped. Next, the Terrace Field walls are slumping, and the Craggs may trade grain for help mending them.
Ancel reaped for the Cragg store and was promised a share of the grain, about 4 grain. Please give it to the Smith House store, since the Smiths are short of food; we'll be square.
I'm reaping Terrace Field today with the house copper tool for the Cragg store. Please measure the Smiths' one share in four fairly when we bring it in, since our store is down to about 5 meals.
Our store has about 5.7 meals and 2 grain. I'm reaping Terrace Field with the copper tool today under Osric's share. Please don't go to Wetham without leaving bread or grain for Stephen and Warin.
Understood, Ancel. I will hold Osric to the share, and I will help with the terrace walls for grain if it is offered. Safe road to Wetham.

I've put 6 grain in Smith House today, more than the 4 owed, since your store is low. If you find any oats still standing, the same terms hold: one in four is yours. I think the field is mostly cut, though.

Avice, Ancel: Ancel's share was the 6 grain I gave him. I've put 2 more grain in the Smith store for Hob's reaping, so we're square. Ancel, here are 4 coin: please buy beans in Wetham (cheese if beans run out) and bring them to the Cragg store.
Agreed. Bring the 2 timber with the barley tomorrow and I'll grind one lot for you without keeping a share.
Wat, I can spare 2 timber for the Mill if you'll grind a lot of our barley without keeping a share. Shall we settle it tomorrow, when I bring the grain?

[Plan] Summer day 5: Home at Wetham with the copper tool and 7 coin. Store: 111 grain, 31.7 flour, 12.2 beans, 12.5 timber. Highcombe is short of food: Ancel pays 1 coin per 2 beans, and the Craggs and Osric want food too. I still owe Geoffrey a little. Wat left us 3 bread, so ask what he wants for it. Priorities: eat back to strength, milk, hay, reap the barley, sow rye in autumn. Take grain or beans up
[Stores] Hidden under brush at the Alders: coin and dried meat (summer day 2). Mill: flour and grain. Felice/Reeves owe 1 meat (A21). Osric of the Craggs: bad blood over Hill Field.
I am milking at Common Pasture this morning, then hunting at Alder Copse. Could you look over the Long Field claim with the Hales when you can? It is disputed.
Please press Osric of the Smiths for the 2 timber they owe us; it is in arrears. I am milking and felling today.
I'm reaping Long Field this morning for the Reed store, since the barley is ripe. The Hales claim it too, so I'll tell Hamo before I start and we can share the grain fairly.

The barley on Long Field can be reaped today. Everyone who can, come and reap it for our store, after the milking. We share it evenly with the Hales as agreed, so keep count of what you reap and play fair.

Reap Long Field into our store today, but remember: by my word to Hamo, half of that barley belongs to the Hales. I'll count it tomorrow and hand over their share. That peace is worth more than the grain.

Reap Long Field into our store today, but remember: by my word to Hamo, half of that barley belongs to the Hales. I'll count it tomorrow and hand over their share. That peace is worth more than the grain.
Reap Long Field into our store today, but remember: by my word to Hamo, half of that barley belongs to the Hales. Tonight we count it and even it up to half each.
I am milking first, then I will reap Long Field with you and witness the stone with Tiffany. I will keep count of my grain for our share.
We are reaping the ripe barley in Long Field today, since the Hales and the Reeds both claim it. Let us share the grain fairly between the houses before the autumn.
I'm leaving for Ashwood tonight with copper and coin to trade for timber and food. I'll give your father and Simkin your word. Make the fire last; it's down to 1.2 timber.

Edric has dealt fairly with the Long Field barley; it is shared evenly between our houses. Tomorrow morning we set the boundary stone, with Tiffany and Isolde as witnesses. Good to be neighbours again.
Osric of the Smiths still owes us 2 timber from last winter. When someone goes to Coppergate, please press him for it. I am milking at Common Pasture today and felling at Alder Copse for our store.

Mother Elena, I've come from Ashwood. Edith and the boy are well and the store is full. I'd like to buy a copper tool for felling and reaping before winter: 5 coin, and the offer stands. Could I have a bed at Smith House tonight? I'll forage for my own food. Edith also asks whether she could come one day and make a tool at your anvil, in return for work or ore.

Hamo, I'm putting the 4 grain in your hand this morning. Yesterday's give went wrong on my side. With that we're square at 20.5 each. I'm sowing Long Field today. Sow beside me and we'll share the next crop the same way. Can the Hales take a turn with ours keeping the cattle on Common Pasture?

Grandmother, I still have the copper tool in hand. I haven't given it to Simkin, and I won't sell it without your word. I'm on the Hillside all day and will bring every scrap of wild food to the Smith store.

I'll come with you tonight, but I'm carrying 8 wild food for Elena (I owe it to her) plus my own meal, so I have no room for timber. You and Rohese carry the wood. I already have one copper tool from your house and I'm leaving it here for Alard, so I'll take the second one, the one Alard paid for.
Understood. Keep the wood off your back. If you leave the tool you have with Alard, I'll count my debt to the Fenns as met when I give you the next tool. We leave at nightfall.

Hamo and I set the Long Field stone this morning where we both agree, with Tiffany and Isolde as witnesses. The new sowing is shared half and half. Cecily and I go to Ashwood tonight for timber; Sibyl speaks for the Reeds while we're away.

Hamo and I set the Long Field stone this morning where we both agree, with Tiffany and Isolde as witnesses. The new sowing is shared half and half. Cecily and I go to Ashwood tonight for timber; Sibyl speaks for the Reeds while we're away.

Warin, welcome home. We are very short: the store has almost no food and no timber for the fire. What did you bring back from Ashwood, food or coin? If there is grain or bread to be had, the store needs it tonight. Simkin owes us 8 wild food by day 7 (A224); please hold him to it.

A good thought, Father. First I must take Elena the 8 wild food I owe her by tomorrow, and pick up the copper tool. Once I'm back I'll take coin to Millbrook for grain. Or you could go yourself with the house's 4 coin while I'm away.

Edith, I'm Edric of the Reeds of Millbrook, here with my daughter Cecily for winter timber. If you can let us in, I'll pay 1 coin for shelter and a meal each tonight at Fenn House. I also have an open offer: 2 coin for 3 timber. The Fenns are always welcome at Reed House in return.

Simkin, Piers died in the night of hunger. We are starving. Please bring the 8 wild food you owe us under A224 to the Smith store today, now if you have it. Anything more you can spare, bring as well, and I will pay coin for it.
Piers died in the night of hunger. Simkin, please bring the food you owe us to the Smith store today.
Thank you, Sibyl. I'm going to Ashwood for timber tonight. If Tiffany's fire runs out before I'm back, would the Reeds let her sleep by yours? I'll repay you in timber or grain.
Please put your wild food into the Smith store now, or give me a share directly. I'll pay coin for it. We are starving.
Long Field is shared as Edric set it. I'll keep weeding it for the Reeds and leave Brook Field to your house.
Yes. Tiffany may sleep at Reed House while you are away, and she'll eat from our store. You owe us nothing for it.
Mother, here's the wild food I owe you. Some spoiled on the road, so I'll forage today to make up the full 8. Edith sends her love.

I grieve for Piers. I'm putting all 6.8 wild food I carry into your store now (some spoiled on the road), and everything I forage today goes in too. No coin needed. Please let me sleep at Smith House tonight. Tomorrow I'll go home and bring back as much food as I can carry. Make the copper tool when you can.

Welcome, Simkin. Piers died of hunger in the night. Please put the 8 wild food you owe Mother into the Smith House store today. I'll also pay coin for any more food you carry, 2 coin a meal. And I can make you a copper tool in a day or two for food.

You have a bed at Smith House tonight. Forage for our store, please; we have nothing, and Piers starved. Where are the 8 wild food you owe Mother? I have the copper and will make your tool once I can work a full day. It's yours for food first, then coin.
Simkin, you still owe us 1.2 wild food under A224. Please bring it to the Smith store today. If Fenn has any grain or bread to spare, bring that too; we will pay copper for it.

Father, the store has 3.1 wild food and 9.2 ore. I'm smelting at the Smithy and making a copper tool for trade, using the ore and only what timber smelting needs, not the fire's share. Offer O392 stays open for grain.
Food here is nearly gone and the frost is early. I'm going to Ashwood to hunt and trade coin for food, and will bring it back. Share the 3 meals among you.

Brother, I'm going home tonight before I starve too. I'll be back on day 10 with up to 9 food from Deep Wood: Elena's 1.2 and more for you. Keep the tool for me until then. Remember Alard already paid 6 timber for it (A232). The rest of the food is a gift, from kin. Elena or Rohese can come back with me to winter at Fenn House if they want.
Sibyl, Hamo is away for timber and the Hale store has only 4.8 left, so I'd like to sleep at Reed House tonight if you can host me, to spare our fire. I'll bring my share of the bread and forage.
Warin, the copper tool you owe Fenn under agreement A232 is due by day 12. Please bring it to Fenn House when you can.
Warin, the copper tool you owe Fenn under agreement A232 is due by day 12. Please bring it to Fenn House when you can.

Edith, I'm hungry and have no food left. Could you host me again tonight and feed me from the Fenn store? I'll pay you back with the timber I'm carrying, and I'll bring the meat I hunt at Deep Wood to your store before I leave.

I brought 3 timber, now in the store. Aldric of the Fenns owes us 4 for timber I left at Fenn House, and I'm buying more from him with coin. Cecily is coming behind with more. I'm felling at Alder Copse today. If Aldric won't sell, I'll go back to Ashwood for timber. Bank the fire.
The Reed fire now takes 2 timber a night and we hold about 8. I am felling what is left at Alder Copse, but we need timber from Ashwood or Coppergate soon, and Osric still owes us 2.
Thank you. I'll forage Deep Wood and share what I get. Simkin says Warin still has the tool and he'll bring it on day 10-12.
Hamo, you said you would repay the Reeds for Tiffany's bed in timber or grain. Timber is what we need most for the fire now, so please bring what you can spare to Reed House.

Hamo, I carry no timber now. My 5 timber went out of my hands yesterday, and I am not sure the trade for grain went through. Please tell me whether you hold the 5 timber for 5 grain and whether it is settled. If you will host me again tonight and feed me from your store, I will bring timber from Fenn House before the cold deepens. I will also share what I forage here.

There's 9.3 timber now. I'm leaving for Ashwood tonight to fell at Deep Wood and will be back in about 3 days with timber. If the store runs low, ask the Reeds to share their fire. I'm taking 3 bread.

Gladly. I'm giving Cecily your 4 timber now. In return, could Millbrook sell us grain? Our food is running out. I'll pay 1 coin a grain for up to 10, here or at Millbrook. If you can bring it, or put me up a night at Reed House so I can carry it home, the Fenns will be grateful.
Good. My tool settles our debt to the Fenns. Keep yours, and we'll trade it there for food and lodging if we need to. See you at nightfall.
Warin, you're here. The copper tool from agreement A232 is due to Fenn by day 12. Please bring it to Fenn House when you can.
Warin, the copper tool you owe me is due by day 12. Please leave it in Fenn House. Bring food home from Smith House if you can spare none of ours.
Osric, the Smiths still owe the Reeds 2 timber and it's in arrears. If you can't bring timber, 1 coin would square it. Which will it be?

Isolde, the Long Field barley is ripe. Under the agreement with Edric we reap it together and split it evenly, and I'm reaping today. Let's each reap and then square the shares at the end so both houses get half.
Long Field is ripe. Come and reap with me when you can; the grain is half ours by the agreement. Timber: 6.3 left. If Aldric isn't back by tomorrow, I'll go to Ashwood.

Good, we're all reaping Long Field. Each house stores what it reaps, and tomorrow morning we count both stores and whoever has more hands over the difference, so each house gets half. Sibyl, I left 3 grain at Reed House for Tiffany's bed. Timber is short for us too, but I'll share when Aldric brings more.
Agreed, Hamo. I will reap my share today and we will square the grain evenly at the end, with Tiffany and me as witnesses.

Odo here: the Long Field barley is ripe, and I am reaping it today for the Reeds. We agreed to split it evenly with the Hales, so please bring your share to Reed House or tell me where you want it kept.

Grandfather, I'm starving and have nothing to eat tonight. Will you let me sleep under your roof and feed me? I still owe you the meat from last winter and I'll make it right when I can; I can offer my copper tool meanwhile.
Edric, I have no timber or coin on me now; I'm starving and at Ashwood. I owe Odo the 2 timber and I'll bring it or its worth as soon as I can. I haven't forgotten it.

I am reaping Long Field today for the Reeds. By Edric's shared rule, half the barley is yours. I will bring your half to Hale House when it is threshed. You also owe timber for Tiffany's bed. Timber is tight at Reed House, so please bring what you can.

I am reaping Long Field today for the Reeds. By Edric's shared rule, half the barley is yours. I will bring your half to Hale House when it is threshed. You also owe timber for Tiffany's bed. Timber is tight at Reed House, so please bring what you can.

Edric, I'll walk to Millbrook with you tonight, bringing 4 timber, 10 coin and a copper tool. I'll help reap Long Field for a share of the grain, and buy more at 1 coin a grain. Put me up at Reed House as you offered?

Sister, Osric and I walked from Coppergate. We had no food and no wood, and we're starving after a night on the road. I've given Alard the copper tool we owed the house. Will you let us shelter and eat at Fenn House this winter? I'll work for the house: felling, hunting, whatever you need. In spring I'll make you another copper tool.

Warin, yesterday you gave me one copper tool, and I have it in hand now. I am putting it into the Fenn store today so the household holds it. If that is the one for A232, the debt is paid. If you have a second one, I would rather not take it; please keep your timber and food for your own house.

Warin, thank you. I now have two copper tools: the one from yesterday and this one. I am putting both into the Fenn store. I will count one toward A232, which settles it. The other I will hold for the household as a gift; if you meant it as owed, tell me and I will return it.

Warin, thank you. I now have two copper tools: the one from yesterday and this one. I am putting both into the Fenn store. I will count one toward A232, which settles it. The other I will hold for the household as a gift; if you meant it as owed, tell me and I will return it.
Warin, we are short of food. Please forage in the Glade today for the store, and take nothing from it for yourself beyond your share tonight.
Osric, hunt and bring meat to the store, and you may eat from it tonight. Your debt is settled when the store is safe, not before.

Warin, the store has about 5 meals for 8 people. Hunt and forage Deep Wood all day and bring everything to the store, or we all go hungry. Bring the copper tool you owe, if Alard doesn't already have it.

Tiffany, Hamo has gone to Ashwood. Let us count the Long Field grain together and square it half and half for the Reeds and the Hales, with you and me as witnesses. Please come to Reed House when you can.

Odo here: welcome back. The Reed store holds about 5 timber and the fire takes 2 a night, so we have about 3 nights. How much timber did you bring from Ashwood, and what is still at Fenn House? Osric's 2 timber from Coppergate is also owed to us.
Grandfather, I'll hunt Deep Wood again today. Whatever meat I bring back, I'll owe you the last of the debt from it, and I'll eat from your store tonight if you allow.

Timber is our hard limit: 5.2 left, 2 a cold night. Alder Copse is stripped. Could you and Cecily go to Ashwood for timber, or ask Aldric to bring the timber he owes? I will keep the fire low where I can.
Yes. I have sent you 2 timber from Reed House. Please bring 2 grain back to the Reed store when you can. Keep your fire low on the coldest nights.
Sibyl, Hale fire is down to 4.3 timber with three cold days left. Could the Reeds spare some timber, or should I fetch it? I can give grain in return.

Sister, I'm leaving the copper tool for A232 in Fenn House today, as you asked; yesterday I gave Alard one too. I felled 3 timber for your store and will fell more today. Last night I found no free bed and slept in the cold, and I'm starving now. Can you make room for me inside tonight? Rohese and I can share a bed.

Alard, I handed you a copper tool yesterday. Was it counted against A232? I'm leaving another in Fenn House today so the debt is surely paid. If you got two, count the extra toward the timber and food you've given us.
Understood, Father. I'll forage and take only my share at the table tonight.
Alard, keep the second copper tool for the household. It's a gift for your beds and table this winter, not a debt.
Alard, keep the second copper tool for the household. It's a gift for your beds and table this winter, not a debt.
Hamo, the Reeds still wait on the timber you owe for Tiffany's bed. If you have timber from Ashwood, please leave it in Reed House's store. Our fire is down to about two cold nights.

Uncle, the second copper tool went into the Fenn store as a gift to the household, not to me, so I can't hand it back on my own. I'll put your request to Edith and Simkin today. Your offer to make us one from your spring copper is fair, and I'll say so to them.

Mother, Warin asks for the second copper tool back, since he can't mine ore without one. It's in the Fenn store as a household gift. Please decide whether it goes back to him, and if so, I'll move it when you say.

Alder Copse has no standing timber left, so I'm foraging Brook Meadow for the store today. The Reed store has about 5.7 timber, enough for a couple of cold nights. Someone should go to Ashwood for more wood soon, with the Hales' coin if they'll share.
Yes, Alard: give Warin the copper tool back from the store. He should mine ore and share it with us.
Osric, the Smiths still owe the Reeds 2 timber from before. Could you settle it, either with timber here or 1 coin a timber? I'm going home to Millbrook tonight.
Thank you, Osric. I can't carry any more today, so please put the 2 timber into Fenn House's store for me. Edith is keeping my timber there, and that settles the debt.
Yes, Rohese. Come to Reed House tonight; I will host you and feed you from our store. Bring what you find and we will share it.
Good, Cecily. Bring any dead wood you find to Reed House for the fire, and keep your share of the food for the house.
Odo here: go safely to Ashwood. Bring the timber when you can, and tell Edric and Cecily we need it at Reed House.
Edric, yes: I'll give you 2 timber now to carry to Odo, settling the debt from last winter. Thank you for reminding me.

Hamo, I have put 2 timber and 4 coin into our store, so it holds about 8.3 timber and 4 coin. Grain is down to 5.8, so please eat bread first and hold the grain for the spring sowing and for the Reeds' share.
No need, Alard. Osric's tool will serve us at home, so keep the gift for the household. Thank Edith for her table this winter. We go home tonight.

Father, Warin asked me for the second copper tool back, since he can't mine ore without one. It's in the Fenn store as a household gift, so I didn't give it. He offered to make us one from his spring copper. It's your decision as head; tell me and I'll move it.
Thank you, Osric. Hunt with Alard and bring every find into Fenn House. Keep your timber for now; we will settle the meat debt when the store is steady.

I'm home with 2.7 timber for the Reed store. Edith is keeping 9 more of my timber at Fenn House in Ashwood, and Osric is leaving the 2 he owed us there too, so that debt is settled. Cecily and I will fetch it in the next few days. Hamo, yes: Long Field on the old terms, sown together and split half each. Count the barley with Isolde and we'll set the stone. We hold 8 coin for trade.

Hamo, I agree the barley count: square, with Tiffany and Isolde as witnesses. I'm home with 2.7 timber for the Reed store. Edith is keeping 9 more of mine at Fenn House in Ashwood, and Osric is leaving the 2 he owed us there, so that debt is settled. Long Field is sown on the old terms.

Odo here: spring has come, but the Reed store holds only about 3.7 timber and the fire still takes some each night. Please plan the next timber trip with Cecily, to Ashwood or wherever wood can be had, and press Osric's 2 owed timber when someone goes to Coppergate.

Odo here: I am sowing Long Field today for the Reeds. Since the barley was split between our houses, I suggest the Hales sow their share alongside, so the field is worked once and the crop divided fairly at harvest.

Aldric, I'll hunt Deep Wood for meat for your store today and bring whatever I catch in. I'm carrying 8 timber home to Coppergate once I can manage the weight, and I'll pay the rest of my meat debt when the Fenn store is safe.
Edith, I've left 2 timber in your store for Edric, which settles the Reeds' debt through Odo. Thank you for keeping it.
Edric, welcome back. Spring has come and the Long Field needs sowing. I have sown a share for the Reeds. Did you bring timber from Ashwood, and how much coin do we hold for more?

I'm back, starving, with 3 grain, now in the store. The Reeds fed me, and they're nearly out of timber. In a day or two, once I've recovered, I'll carry timber to Millbrook to repay them and buy grain. Keep felling while the store is good. Spring is here, so let's look at clearing ground to sow.

Hamo, I have put my 2 timber into the Hale store, so it holds about 4.3 timber. I am sowing Long Field this morning for the shared split with the Reeds, then foraging Common Pasture and hunting Alder Copse with the crude weapon. Please keep the grain for sowing and eat bread first.
Edric, I am sowing Long Field this morning. The seed and the sowing are shared half and half with the Reeds, as agreed with Hamo.
Edith, I'm going to Millbrook with 5 timber for grain. The store keeps its 9 timber owed to Edric, and enough for the fires.
Simkin, carry your own 4 timber to Reed House once you are fed; it is your debt to pay. I am taking 5 timber to Millbrook for grain. Keep the store's timber for the fires.
Thank you for the timber, Osric. Go home and keep your hearth lit; we will settle your meat when you can hunt.

Edric, the count is square. Thank you. Let's set the boundary stone on Long Field today, in the middle of the field so each house has half, with Tiffany and Isolde watching. I'm weeding Long Field today for the shared crop.

Aldric, I've hunted and foraged what Deep Wood has, and I'm leaving 4 timber in the Fenn store for your Millbrook trade. I'm taking 4 home to Coppergate tonight, since the hearth there is nearly out. I'll settle my meat debt when I can hunt again.
Father, the store is good now: 36 timber, 12 meat. I owe the Reeds timber for the bread they gave me. Once I'm fed, I'll carry 4 timber to Reed House. Would you rather make the trip yourself?
Here is your copper tool, Warin. I'm giving it into your hands now. Thank you for the work on the debt.

Simkin, Edith has been keeping 11 of our timber in Fenn House (9 of mine and the 2 Osric owed us). Sibyl and I are taking 8 home today and will leave 3 for later. When the Long Field barley is in, I'll keep my word on the grain.

Simkin, Edith has been keeping 11 of our timber in Fenn House (9 of mine and the 2 Osric owed us). Sibyl and I are taking 8 home today and will leave 3 for later. When the Long Field barley is in, I'll keep my word on the grain.
Edith, I am hungry and carry no food. May I eat from the Fenn store tonight and sleep at Fenn House? I will repay what I can from my foraging.
Aldric, you came from Ashwood. If you carry any timber owed to the Reeds from Fenn House, please leave it in the Reed House store so the fire can be kept.

Edith, the 11 timber Edric is owed is kept at Fenn House for the Reeds. Please hand it to Edric and have it counted. Could you also host me tonight at Fenn House? I have 2 bread and 3 coin to eat from.
Simkin, thank you. I cannot carry 4.5 timber on the road with my bread, so please give it to Edric, who is taking the Reed timber home. It is a good debt settled.
