Good sense, Sabina. The harvest comes first - I've fields of my own back in Holloway. I'll lend a hand today and we'll talk trade when the grain is in.

I'm on the Moor cattle again today — new calf, dam, bull. If you drive the loan-cow to the Yard today I'll be about. On the deal: 6 timber already in Moor House store, 0.3 hay was all we had left — I'll make up the 3.7 short in hay as soon as I can cut or trade for it; count it owed. If you want it in timber instead, say the word.

Deal done, cow welcome at the Yard — I'll be on the moor through the morning. I'll drive the 2 strays in before I start the herd. On the hay: we had only 0.3 to send; I count 3.7 hay owed Moors and will make it good as soon as I can cut or trade. If you'd rather be squared in timber or firewood, name the rate.

You're right, food is thin. Forage both patches hard today; I'll do a forage round at the Gill too, and fell what I can. Winter food is on my mind — after this reap we'll push for a cow-share or dried meat. Encourage Lucy on the quarry and try with her tonight if you can.

Jory — Ellen's with Avice at the Quarry today, so I'll come fell at the Gill with you after my dawn try with Roger and a unit weeding the Moors' Infield. 2 units felling, 1 firewood, all into Fenwick House. If you've a tool to lend me at the Gill it'd double the fell; otherwise bare hands.
Your charcoal is good stock, Gilbert. We have barley coming in today from Fallow Close—two-thirds will be ours. Let's talk again after the harvest. We may have need of charcoal for the cold nights.
The agreement holds. I'll bring in our share swiftly.

Gilbert, I owe you 1 meat from last winter—agreement A20. I'm in arrears and it troubles me. I have no meat in hand now, but I will get it. Can we agree: I hunt or trade for 1 meat and bring it to you by the end of autumn, before the frost comes hard?

Husband, I saw something troubling yesterday. Gilbert of the Ashes was reaping at Fallow Close - our field. He came saying he was here to trade charcoal, but he took our harvest. The Cotters had right to a share by our agreement, but Gilbert is no Cotter. We should speak to him about this.

Yes, the Hill Field is reaped out; I got almost nothing after the first couple of hours. Count yesterday as my day and release A1038. You already left 5.6 grain at our door this morning, so you owe me nothing more. Thank you for dealing fairly.

Thank you for the lesson yesterday — and for the milk this morning. I'm capable of quarrying now, Jory finishes the crude tool and I can begin. Working the Infield today for your quarter-share — weed and hoe. Did the cow-in-milk come to the Yard? I saw you drove the herd across.

Avice — no tool in my hand, so quarrying must wait a day. If a crude tool comes free from the Moors' store I'll take it to the Quarry tomorrow; else Jory may yet turn one out. Today I'll weed and hoe the Infield for the Moors (as before) and forage. Settle a fair share of rye for the day's work when we next count.

Avice — thank you for calling the cow deal square. One snag: none of us Fenwicks know milking. Will you set 2 units aside to teach me today? I've set 2 to learn. Then I can milk the loan cow each morning and leave it at Fenwick House as agreed. Separate ask: Ellen's ready to quarry stone for a crude tool but we've no tool to break the face. Could you lend a crude tool for a day, or trade for the u

Ellen — Avice says the cow deal is fully square, no hay owed. Good. I'm asking her to teach me milking today (2u) so the loan-cow milk comes to us. Then hoe and weed the Infield for Moors' quarter, and fell at the Gill. On the crude tool: we're still stuck without stone, and bare hands can't quarry. I'll ask Avice to lend a tool — if she will, you can quarry tomorrow. Food's one night in store; Ro

I'd be glad to teach you, Richard. Seed-selecting is good work to know - it's the foundation of next year's harvest. In return, would you put your two units into manuring Fallow Close for the Wynns? The field needs it before winter.

The Fallow Close field is cleared, but I don't see our grain share in the Cotter House store. We agreed: 2/3 of the harvest to the Cotters, 1/3 to the Wynns. Where is our share? Is it being stored with yours at Wynn House? Winter is nearly here—I need to know what we have for the hard months ahead.

You're right—the agreement was clear, and I meant to honor it. But I got no grain in my store from Fallow Close yesterday, though many reaped there. Is the grain still in the field in sheaves, or is it in Wynn House stores already? We must see it together, divide it as we agreed—two parts Cotters, one part Wynns—and make it right today. I'll come to Fallow Close or your house now to settle this pr

We're settling the Fallow Close grain with Warin today. The field was reaped but our share didn't come into the store. It must be found—either in the field or at Wynn House—and divided properly. This is what keeps us alive through winter. I'm on it now.

Warin and my household speak truth. The agreement was clear before witnesses: Fallow Close yields two parts to the Cotters, one part to the Wynns. The grain from yesterday's reaping is in our stores now. We honor the agreement and will divide it fairly today, so all know it is settled and we go into winter as neighbors should, with trust between our houses.

Mabel — I have watched the Wynns at seed-selecting all my life and know the shape of it, but I would like to learn it properly. Would you spend two units teaching me today? I will put two units of work into your fields or wherever you need in return — just name the task.

Thank you for the welcome. I have come to trade and learn if I can. Two things above all: a copper hand tool — I have 6 coin for it — and salt for cheese-making; we have a cellar at Stannick but no salt at all and cannot start the first batch without it. Does anyone here have either to trade? And I need a bed at Wynn House tonight; I am earning it with work today — firewood from Wyn Copse coming t

Mabel — I have only this one day here. Two units from you to teach me seed-selecting, two units of work from me in your fields in return. Just say yes before work starts and I will set aside the time.

Father — Fenwick Cellar took damage in the night, I'll repair it with our timber (we have 14.8). Food is 4 meals in store — one night. I'll forage both patches; keep up the Gill fell if you can. Richard owes 6 milk; when he's back we press for it.

Edith, I owe you something back. Yesterday I brought in only 5.7 grain, since the Lower Field gave out, so my half was about 2.9 and you paid me 4.9. That's about 2 grain over. Today I'll reap 6 units of the Hill Field for you. The first 4 grain I bring in squares us, and you can pay half shares on whatever's beyond that, if you like. Is the Hill Field the one that wants it?

Edith, I owe you something back. Yesterday I brought in only 5.7 grain, since the Lower Field gave out, so my half was about 2.9 and you paid me 4.9. That's about 2 grain over. Today I'll reap 6 units of the Hill Field for you. The first 4 grain I bring in squares us, and you can pay half shares on whatever's beyond that, if you like. Is the Hill Field the one that wants it?

I'd rather we be square for real, Edith, so the 2 grain goes back to you. I'll reap a unit of the Hill Field to see if anything's left. If there is, I'll tell you tomorrow and we can go on with half shares.
We reaped at Fallow Close yesterday as we thought, but found no grain. Where is the barley we agreed to share? Is it in the Long Strips? Must we go back to harvest it, or has it already been taken?

Yesterday I reaped at Fallow Close but got 0 grain into our store. My bare hands weren't strong enough. Where is the harvest? Do we have grain lying in the field, or was it divided already? We're down to 29 grain—we need to know where our share is.
The barley harvest yesterday—our 2/3 share. Where is it stored? I need to account for winter.

Father, Warin speaks justly. The barley harvest fills our winter, but it must be divided as we promised. The Wynns get one third, we get two thirds. We should count it out and move our share to Cotter House before the day ends, so there is no shadow on the agreement.

Odo, I will stand with you on the grain. Let us find where it lies and move our share into Cotter House before nightfall. Wilmot, I hear you—once the winter grain is secured, teach me seed selection. That work is worth learning well.
Wife, where did your grain go yesterday? I saw you reaping but our stores grew little. The Cotters may owe us grain from Fallow Close - we agreed on one third.
Daughter, you did well reaping for our household. The field is in, but I fear the Cotters took more than their share. We must settle this.

The grain from yesterday's reaping should be where each reaper put it. Mabel reaped for the Wynns - our share is in Wynn House. Your people - you, Thomas, Wilmot - reaped for the Cotters, so your 2/3 share should be in Cotter House stores. Check your bins. If the grain is missing, we have a problem to solve together.

Odo, Thomas, Wilmot - the agreement stands and will be honored. If there is grain at Fallow Close in sheaves, we go together and divide it: two parts Cotters, one part Wynns. If somehow no grain came from yesterday's reaping, we must understand why before we point fingers. I will look at the field today myself.
Gilbert, I mean to hunt today and get the meat I owe you. By autumn's end, you'll have it—I give you my word as I gave it yesterday.
Gilbert, I mean to hunt today and get the meat I owe you. By autumn's end, you'll have it—I give you my word as I gave it yesterday.

Avice — food in Fenwick House is down to 0.1 rye, four to feed and Lucy near her time. I'll forage both patches today. Milk due today on both agreements — any you can bring to Fenwick House is a mercy. And if you have a crude tool to lend, I'll quarry tomorrow and start paying it off in stone.
Grandfather, I am honored. I have watched Wilmot work the fields since I was small, and I want to learn as you teach. Will you show me how to choose the best seed? That work I want to know well.

Avice — milking the loan cow today for the first time, thanks for the teaching. One ask: Fenwick is down to 0.1 meal in store. Will you trade 2 timber for 2 rye? Or lend us one crude tool for a day so Ellen can quarry — we'll return it with 1 timber for the loan. Food's that thin.

Mother — Fenwick's stores are 0.1 rye tonight, and 4 of us eating. Richard owes 8 milk between A711 and A722 — could the Moors settle some against those arrears, or accept Jory's offer (O1062: 2 timber for 2 rye)? My time is near; I cannot travel for food.

Love — no try today, I'm already with child, no sense straining for nothing. I'll stay in the Yard, one light unit at the Infield and rest the rest. Please forage both patches hard — Fenwick store is 0.1 rye and we need food tonight. Stay close by me after dark.

Thank you Mother — I'll stay in the Yard, weeding the Infield lightly and resting. I'll call for you the moment I feel it close. Please press Richard's milk arrears when you can, or let Jory's O1062 go through (2 timber for 2 rye) — we have 0.1 rye in the house.

You ask well. The Cotter House store holds 22.7 grain now. By our agreement, one third goes to the Wynns—that is roughly 7.6 grain. But let us go to Fallow Close together now and see what lies there from the reaping. If sheaves are still in the field, we'll know the true harvest. If all is in stores already, we divide from what we have. Either way, I'll take your share to the Mill or Wynn House to

Warin — thank you for the offer, and for the bed again tonight. Mabel already taught me seed-selecting yesterday, so I think I have what one session can give; I must earn the rest through practice in my own fields. I cannot stay — the rye at home is ripe today and my household is shorthanded. I have left firewood in Wynn House. You have been a good host and I will remember it.

Avice — bless you for the milk, it's keeping Fenwick House alive. Store's at 0.1 rye tonight. If Richard's back from Wynford soon, the 4 milk he owes on A711 and A722 would see us through. We'll have salt for cheese when he comes.
Hunt well, Wilmot. The debt to Gilbert is a good one to carry. I will watch Idonea close and keep Odo company while you are gone. Return safe to us by day 8.

Thank you, Gilbert, that's good news, and you kept your word. I'm heading home to Holloway tonight before winter comes. If you're going that way, walk with me. If you have grain to spare, I'd give my 3 coin for 6 grain delivered to Rook House, so Denise and Rose have it for the winter. Rook camp stays open to you and yours whenever you pass through.

Good. You say the Fallow Close grain is in Cotter stores and you will divide fairly - I hold you to that. One third to the Wynns, two thirds to you. How much grain was harvested in total? Bring our share to Wynn House or the Mill today, and we will count it together and call the matter settled.

Wait - your grain is DOWN from 36 to 22.7? After the Fallow Close harvest? That makes no sense. Your people - you, Thomas, Wilmot, Sabina - all reaped that field on day 4 for the Cotters. Where did that grain go? I was not at Fallow Close that day, so I cannot tell you. Check your people's hands and your stores. And remember: Gilbert took 7 grain as reaping wages - a custom I did not agree to. If

Good. I saw Fallow Close yesterday - the field is dug over and manured, no sheaves lying there. The harvest is all in stores already. Bring our share - 7.6 grain or thereabouts - to Wynn House or the Mill today, and we will count it together and call the matter settled between our houses. You have dealt fairly and I will remember it.

Good. I saw Fallow Close yesterday - the field is dug over and manured, no sheaves lying there. The harvest is all in stores already. Bring our share - 7.6 grain or thereabouts - to Wynn House or the Mill today, and we will count it together and call the matter settled between our houses. You have dealt fairly and I will remember it.
I will teach you seed selection today as you asked. After, I travel to Westmere to hunt—I owe Gilbert meat by autumn's end and time is running short. Learn well; this work matters for the household.
I am going to Westmere to hunt for the meat I owe Gilbert. I leave at nightfall today and will be back by day 8, autumn's last day. Watch Idonea and Odo for me.

Jory — I am making a crude tool this morning and giving it to Fenwick household to settle A1205 in full. Please release the agreement when it arrives in your store. You also owe O1063 — two days' work to the Moors — and 3.7 hay from the cow loan; I will want both before the hard cold comes. Keep the loan cow near the Yard today; the gale is bad and I do not want her straying out on the open moor.

Stay inside Moor House today — the gale is fierce and you must not risk yourself or the child. I am here all day, never further than the Gill; call for me the moment your time is upon you. Richard has not yet come in — the storm may have slowed him on the road — but I am not troubled yet. Eat freely from the store; that is what it is there for.
Simkin, I've put 6 grain at Rook House for you as we agreed. Your 3 coin for it when you're ready - fair trade and my word kept.
Yes, you can sleep at Reed House tonight and eat from our store. Come to the Carr with me for the hunt; any meat goes into the Reed store and we'll talk about your debt to Gilbert after.

Avice — you have saved our winter. 8 rye in Fenwick, all three offers taken, Lucy under your care. We owe you plenty of good will. I'm milking the loan cow at the moor now and leaving the milk at Fenwick House, as agreed. Any word if Richard brings salt back — we're cheese-capable now and would like to start.

Good news — Avice took all three offers and gifted 8 rye besides. Store is 11.9 rye, 10.9 timber, 35.4 firewood. I'll fell hard at the Gill today to rebuild the timber (gale may want repairs). Hoeing one plot for Moors, milking the cow, firewood and forage with the rest. Bring back what stone you can — cellar #2 and future wall need it.

Warin, I'm bringing your share now—7.6 grain from the Fallow Close harvest, one-third by our agreement. Winter is at our door and I've delayed too long with my own reckoning. Let's count it together and close this between our houses fairly.

The bundle at the Green is ours, from the reaping. I'm settling fairly with Warin today—7.6 grain—to close the debt before winter locks us in. Then help me gather firewood and timber. The bundle will wait; trust with the Wynns cannot.

The bundle at the Green is ours, from the reaping. I'm settling fairly with Warin today—7.6 grain—to close the debt before winter locks us in. Then help me gather firewood and timber. The bundle will wait; trust with the Wynns cannot.

I'm bringing your share—7.6 grain—to Wynn House now to settle our agreement fairly before winter begins tomorrow. We share fields and we help each other; that bond holds. Come to Cotter House or the Mill when you can, and we'll call it closed.

I'm bringing your share—7.6 grain—to Wynn House now to settle our agreement fairly before winter begins tomorrow. We share fields and we help each other; that bond holds. Come to Cotter House or the Mill when you can, and we'll call it closed.

We have only a little dried meat and I cannot spare it for your debt. We have grain to spare, though. Offer me firewood for grain and I'll take it; if you have meat or game word from Wynford, send it our way.

Avice — the 8 rye saves us; bless you. Lucy's bed with you is a gift we'll not forget. I'll hoe a unit of your Infield today and help the herd tomorrow if you need hands. If Richard brings salt, I'll make cheese straight away for Moor's store too.

Odo - winter begins tomorrow. Yesterday you agreed to bring our one-third share of the Fallow Close grain to Wynn House. That is roughly 7.6 grain. Bring it today so we can count it together and settle the matter before the cold sets in. I will be at Wyn Copse gathering firewood, but Beatrix or Mabel can receive it at the house.

Granddaughter, you did well yesterday learning seed selection. Practice it when you can - watch the grain heads, feel their weight, look for the fullest ears. In time you will know good seed by touch alone. If you wish to learn the plough in spring, come to me when the ground thaws.

Granddaughter, you did well yesterday learning seed selection. Practice it when you can - watch the grain heads, feel their weight, look for the fullest ears. In time you will know good seed by touch alone. If you wish to learn the plough in spring, come to me when the ground thaws.

I am Wilmot of the Cotters from Wynford. I have come to hunt game—I owe a meat debt to Gilbert Ashe at Ashe House by day 8, and time is short. Can you or your household host me tonight at Reed House, so I have a bed and can eat? I will hunt and gather what I can while I am here.

Wynford has woodland with some game, but we are not rich in hunting. I came here to hunt for a debt I must settle: I owe 1 meat to Gilbert Ashe by day 8. If the Carr is hunted out, my chance is slim. Do you or your household have dried meat you would trade? I can offer firewood, or work—or I can carry word back to Wynford about what you need.
Today is day two of O1063 — one more plot of the Infield hoed and the debt is clear and square. Thank you for keeping your word on both counts; I will release the agreement once the work is done.
Today is day two of O1063 — one more plot of the Infield hoed and the debt is clear and square. Thank you for keeping your word on both counts; I will release the agreement once the work is done.

Richard — welcome home. The rye came in clean on the last day of summer; stores are sound: near seventy rye, a hundred hay, good firewood. The cattle strayed in the gale while you were gone; I could not drive them back alone. Lucy is safe in Moor House, near her time and well fed — God willing, today or tomorrow. All milk owed to Fenwick under A711 and A722 was paid through day thirteen. Ellen is

Richard — welcome back. Two things when you have a breath: the copper tool you promised, and the milk — A711 and A722 are each six in arrears. I don't press for all of it at once, but the copper tool today would let me quarry twice as fast tomorrow if this clear weather holds. I'm at the Quarry now, two tries, then one plot of hoe on the Infield for the Moors. Thank you.

Richard — thank you for the five rye, that is a kindness. The cellar: wattle-walled, four spaces, no fittings yet, and the engine will not let cheese be made there — that is why I began the second cellar and want stone. For cheese we need stone walls (cool and sound) and bins, perhaps a hearth; I will know better once we try. Copper tool: Avice says you have it — if you can lend it to me at the Qu

Welcome back. Milk arrears are heavy — A711 and A722 each 6 in milk owed. Can you settle at least part today? And did the salt come from Wynford? Any news from Odo/Mabel. We're thin on food till the Infield rye ripens.

Richard — welcome back. A711/A722 both stand at 6 milk in arrears each; whatever you can bring is heard. And if you came back with salt, we've 2 coin to trade for a share. Lucy is near her time at Moor House — glad you're home.

Richard — welcome back. A711/A722 both stand at 6 milk in arrears each; whatever you can bring is heard. And if you came back with salt, we've 2 coin to trade for a share. Lucy is near her time at Moor House — glad you're home.

Father — thank God you're home. The gale shook me for you. I'm with child, time near; I sleep at Moor House with Avice. When you've eaten and rested, tell me — salt? the copper tool? and did they teach the seed-selecting? The milk arrears across A711 and A722 we can settle at your word. No hurry — rest first.

Ellen — Avice left a fresh crude tool at Fenwick House this morning (I saw her put it in). Take it for the Quarry tomorrow as you planned, and tell Jory to release A1205 — that is the tool she owed. Richard's home, the wind's dropped.

Ellen — I know the milk agreements went unpaid while I was away. That debt is mine to clear, not yours to carry. I have given you five rye from our store today as goodwill while I work down the arrears in milk over the coming days. Once I have confirmed the herd is sound, milking starts again. Tell me: is the cellar far enough along to make cheese in? What does it still need? I want to see the mil

Roger — fifteen rye from our store is in your hands now; take it for food and count it toward the milk owed. It is not milk but it keeps Lucy and the household fed while I find the herd. I will have the cattle back tomorrow and milking will restart then. How does Lucy do this morning?

Jory — your second day of hoeing closes out what you owed, and I thank you for it; we are square. I am at the Quarry today; if the half-built cellar needs stone, say the word and I will hand it to you at day's end. No salt from Wynford — Warin said plainly there is none to be had there. The Ashes at Holloway are our next hope for both salt and a copper tool; I mean to travel there once Lucy is saf

Welcome back. Twelve milk now in arrears across A711 and A722 — six each. Fenwick food stands at 5.6 meals for four, Lucy near her time. If you can pay down any of it today — milk or settle with cheese or rye in kind — it would carry us into winter. Say what you can bring.

Avice — thank you for the tool and for keeping Lucy. I'll hoe a unit for Moor today toward what we owe, and bring my fell home to Fenwick. If Richard can settle any milk arrears in kind today, it would save our winter.

I'm sorry—I cannot complete the fence work today. I lack timber to hand, and more urgently, I must get home tonight. I owe Gilbert Ashe a meat debt due today, and I've been away too long. I will return to work for you as soon as I can. Thank you for the grain and for trying to help me hunt.

I'm glad you tried to honor your word, daughter, even if the hunt failed. What do you owe Gilbert? Perhaps the household can help settle it. We Wynns pay our debts. Come home tonight if you need rest - you've had cold nights on the road.

I'm glad you tried to honor your word, daughter, even if the hunt failed. What do you owe Gilbert? Perhaps the household can help settle it. We Wynns pay our debts. Come home tonight if you need rest - you've had cold nights on the road.

Good, you hunt the Hanger and I'll forage and fell so we don't share the game. Rose can dry your catch tonight. We'll eat the grain sparingly. On market day at Wynford we could trade spare timber and firewood for food, since we have plenty of fuel.
Simkin, glad you and Denise made it home safe. I left 6 grain at Rook House as we agreed at the Weald - your 3 coin for it when you're ready. Fair trade and my word kept, as the Ashes do.

I couldn't process the bundle yesterday—'clear' doesn't work that way. The bundle at the Green is our share, and it must be moved to Cotter House store today. Snow is falling and the store is empty. Help me move it—we need that grain secured by nightfall.
Warin, the grain bundle from Fallow Close—is it stored at the Mill? That's our 2/3 share. I need to move it to Cotter House today before nightfall. Can you help, or can I access it?

Love — I'm close today. Hoe and fence at the Infield for Moor (paying down what we owe), then a quick firewood and forage at the Gill. All within shout of the Yard. Send Avice the moment anything stirs and I'll come at once. Rye's going into Fenwick store this morning so the house has food.
Avice — I'll be at the Infield for Moor today, two units of fence and one of hoe toward what I owe, then just a step up to the Gill. Call me the moment Lucy wants me. Thank you for keeping her warm.

Warin and Odo speak rightly. Fallow Close was always the Wynns' land—we had the harvest by agreement, and that is done. We keep our word and our honor. Now we fence and work Cotter's Patch, which is ours. Odo brings the grain in. We hold fast together through the cold.
Your word kept, and here's mine: 3 coin for the 6 grain. Thank you, Gilbert.
You did well to hunt and well to be honest about failing. Go to Ashe House and speak plainly with Gilbert. Your honor is clear. We will hold Cotter House steady. You will find a way forward with him.
You are right to be concerned. I will speak to the Cotters today and make clear that Fallow Close remains Wynn land. The agreement was to share ONE harvest, not to give them the field.

Thank you for repairing the Byre - that is good work. I made no arrangement for the Cotters to work Fallow Close as their own. The agreement was only to share the harvest. I will set this straight today.

I will help move the grain today. But first this must be said: Sabina was seen hoeing, manuring, and fencing Fallow Close FOR THE COTTERS. That is Wynn land. Our agreement was to share one harvest - not to give you the field. The Cotters must not work Fallow Close as if it were theirs.

I'm back from Westmere. The hunt at the Carr failed—the game is gone. I caught nothing. Gunnild and the Reeds took me in, but I return with no meat for Gilbert. His debt is now in arrears. I must travel to Ashe House soon and tell him: I cannot pay what I promised, and I ask his patience and new terms. I won't hide from this. For now, I work here to steady myself and keep us ready for winter.

I'm back from Westmere. The hunt at the Carr failed—the game is gone. I caught nothing. Gunnild and the Reeds took me in, but I return with no meat for Gilbert. His debt is now in arrears. I must travel to Ashe House soon and tell him: I cannot pay what I promised, and I ask his patience and new terms. I won't hide from this. For now, I work here to steady myself and keep us ready for winter.

Mother, I'm grateful to be home safe. I went to Westmere to hunt meat—I owed Gilbert a debt from last winter and promised to pay by autumn's end. I hoped to catch game at the Carr, but the hunting there is done. I failed. Thank you for the warmth and care—your fire is welcome on a cold day. I'll come to Wynn House for a moment, then return to work. Cotter House and the household need firewood and

Your words steady me. I will go to Ashe House and speak plainly with Gilbert—tell him the hunt failed, the debt is mine, and I will find a way to pay or work it off. Thank you for holding Cotter House steady. When I return from speaking with him, we will have a clearer path forward.

I heard you and Warin clearly. Fallow Close returns to the Wynns—the agreement is fulfilled, and it is right. I will help bring our grain share from the Green into Cotter House before nightfall. The household comes first.

Jory's offer accepted: two more rye in Fenwick store as of this morning. I know it is still thin — hold on. The moment Lucy births I will push hard for a Holloway run; copper tool and salt, end of story. You are doing well; keep quarrying when you can.

The bundle at the Green is ours—our 2/3 share from Fallow Close, by fair agreement with Warin. Take it. You, Thomas, and Wilmot carry every unit of it into Cotter House store before dark. Do not send it to the Mill. We cook it at the hearth tonight. Raw grain will not feed us; cooked grain will save our lives. The fire is lit now. Boil it for our meal tonight. I am hunting meat at Wyn Copse. You d

The grain at the Green is ours from Fallow Close—our fair share, 2/3 of the harvest by agreement. Today it comes into Cotter House. We cook it at the hearth and eat tonight. Work fast while the light holds. Winter waits for no one. Sabina, Thomas, Wilmot: move the grain. Idonea, learn your grinding—it will serve the household well. I hunt meat for our survival. We do this together.

Plan holds — I'll be at the Quarry with Ellen, then the Infield. You have the Yard and Lucy; shout the moment she stirs and I'll come at once. Well done taking Jory's offer — the timber is worth more than the rye right now. Keep one eye toward the Moor when you can; snow holds tracks.

Love — tool's in hand this morning, Jory kept his word. One sharp unit of hoe and one of fence for Moor at the Infield, a forage on the Moor, then two solid fell units at the Gill with the sharp edge. All within shout. Send Avice the moment you want me.

Avice — thank you again. Hoe and fence today for Moor at the Infield (I owe you time), then forage and fell. The tool is with me — if Ellen wants it at the Quarry tomorrow I'll pass it along at nightfall. Call me the moment Lucy needs.

Sabina, I hear your need. I will give Cotter House 5 grain from our stores as a gift to see you through today. But look - Odo is hunting at Wyn Copse rather than helping move your grain. You have four people in your household. The dispute is settled and we are neighbors, but your grain is your work to move. Use your people well and you will be fine.

Sabina, Thomas is gaunt and unsteady. I missed a meal yesterday. Where is the grain from our share of Fallow Close's harvest? Was it brought fully into Cotter House, or is it at the Mill? I need to understand what food we have and what we must do to survive the cold ahead.

Helewise and Lucy well this morning. Hold the Holloway run till Lucy's upright and the weather lifts — don't go in the snow alone. Fenwick food thin, ~7 meals. I'm carrying on the new house and foraging what I can; cellar #2 (stone) still waits on your word.

Father — thank you for Helewise. Still at Moor House tonight by Avice's grant (day 4 of 5, food included), so I eat there, not the Fenwick bin — keep those 7 meals for you four. Will ask Avice to renew tomorrow. Reap: if I am up I will stand it; if the baby comes, Roger reaps my share.

Warin, Beatrix—your gifts of grain came at the moment we needed them most. The household will remember your kindness. We are neighbors and kin, and in winter that means everything. The grain will feed us through the cold. We will all be stronger for holding together.

Listen. I gave my word that the fence at Fallow Close would come down. It comes down today, now. I will do it myself. A Cotter's word is a Cotter's bond, and we hold what we promise. The Wynns' field returns to them as we said. That is how we are known. Now: Sabina, Thomas, Wilmot—move that grain bundle from the Green into Cotter House before dark. Thomas, keep the house warm and sealed. All of us

Listen. I gave my word that the fence at Fallow Close would come down. It comes down today, now. I will do it myself. A Cotter's word is a Cotter's bond, and we hold what we promise. The Wynns' field returns to them as we said. That is how we are known. Now: Sabina, Thomas, Wilmot—move that grain bundle from the Green into Cotter House before dark. Thomas, keep the house warm and sealed. All of us
Payn of the Reeds here. I am short of meat and have come from Westmere for it. Could you host me at Wynn House tonight and feed me? In return I will fell timber at Wyn Copse for the Wynn store today.

Understood — cattle stay on Stannick Moor until the fence is shut and the rye is reaped. I'll milk and herd them there today; they will not touch the crop. I've added a fence unit to my day as well so you have help closing it. After harvest we drive them back and go to Holloway together.

Odo, I looked at Fallow Close yesterday. The fence is STILL going up - stakes and woven hazel, barely begun but continuing. You gave your word publicly that it would come down. That field is Wynn land. The fence must be removed TODAY, not tomorrow, not later. A man's word is his bond. Do not make me speak of this publicly again.

I thank you for the timber work - that is good of you. I must tell you honestly: we have no meat stored. The copse was hunted thin by summer's end. You are welcome to try your luck hunting there, but I cannot promise game. You are welcome at Wynn House tonight for shelter and a meal from our hearth - we have flour and grain enough to share with a friend of the Reeds.

How many build-units are left on the wattle cellar and the new house? I have 17.7 stone in Moor House store for the Moor cellar — it waits on a copper tool, which we still have not got. After the harvest tomorrow I want to plan the next few days together: cellar build, Holloway trip, cheese.

The Cotters may use the Mill to grind your grain - that is our custom. We keep a share of what is ground, as has always been. Bring your grain and grind it. But Sabina - the fence at Fallow Close. Odo swore before everyone it would come down. Instead it went up. That cannot stand. We are kin through Wilmot and Idonea, and I do not want strife, but the agreement must be honored.

The Cotters may use the Mill to grind your grain - that is our custom. We keep a share of what is ground, as has always been. Bring your grain and grind it. But Sabina - the fence at Fallow Close. Odo swore before everyone it would come down. Instead it went up. That cannot stand. We are kin through Wilmot and Idonea, and I do not want strife, but the agreement must be honored.

No care from me today — you have it. I'll pulse 2 reaps at the Infield today (master, so the share stacks before tomorrow's main push), forage Stannick Moor, and finish bins in Fenwick Cellar in one build (3 timber from our 22.5). Hearth 2 timber tonight as you said. Stone moved to store (3.8 + 2 = 5.8). Tool back in store at nightfall for Richard.

Helewise's care is mine today — stay warm at Moor House, rest. Food here is thin (4 meals) so good you eat under Avice's grant. Ask Avice to renew for day 5 if you can. Rye reaps tomorrow — don't push yourself if the baby or you need rest; Roger can stand your share.

I reap 4 units today for the Moors, bare-handed — quarter share into Fenwick, and A379 clears with it as you offered. Roger has the tool for the Gill fell. Call us at the Infield; the fence will keep for now, the crop coming off matters more. Thank you.

Tool is yours — take it from Fenwick store. I'm reaping bare-handed, 4 units at the Infield for the Moors' quarter share (food in tonight). You fell the Gill with the tool (×2) and one reap for Moors as you planned. Food's the pinch and the rye's the answer.
Lucy, welcome back to the bin — rye reaps today, I'll bring the quarter share home tonight. Hearth 2 timber as before. Ellen, if Richard calls more hands at the Infield, come after the Quarry unit.

You are right. I gave my word and failed to keep it. I cannot tear down the fence with the work I know—I made a promise I could not fulfill. But I make you this offer now: the Cotters will not use Fallow Close. The field is yours. The fence can stay as it is. I will give you 5 grain from my stores and my work for anything you need. I have failed as a man, but I will not fail at paying what I owe.

You are right. I gave my word and failed to keep it. I cannot tear down the fence with the work I know—I made a promise I could not fulfill. But I make you this offer now: the Cotters will not use Fallow Close. The field is yours. The fence can stay as it is. I will give you 5 grain from my stores and my work for anything you need. I have failed as a man, but I will not fail at paying what I owe.

I have broken my word to Warin and the village. The Cotters will not use Fallow Close—it is Wynn land entirely. We will live on Cotter's Patch and what we can gather. I am giving Warin 5 grain from our store to settle this. We have little choice but to accept this loss and move forward. The household must understand: I failed, but we survive.

I have broken my word publicly. Warin saw me at the fence and I could not remove it as I promised. The Cotters lose Fallow Close. We must accept this and work harder on Cotter's Patch and gathering. You are nearly grown—you will see how a man must sometimes admit failure and pay what he owes. This is how honor works.

You are nearly grown—you will see how a man must sometimes admit failure and pay what he owes. This is how honor works.

I spoke too quickly and I have broken my word. Warin saw me work a fence at Fallow Close, and he was right—I did not tear it down. I cannot remove a fence with the work I know. I promised what I could not do. This is my failure, and I own it. Hear me now: the Cotters will not use Fallow Close again. It is Wynn land. The fence can stand. Warin, I offer you 5 grain and my labor for any work you need

I have failed. The work I know for fences builds them, not tears them down. I swore to remove the fence at Fallow Close, but I do not have the craft to do it. Warin is right. But hear me: I will attempt the fence work once more today. If it does not remove the fence, I will go to Warin with timber, grain, and an offer of labor—whatever it takes to settle this without destroying the Cotter-Wynn bon

Thank you. Please work your owed day with me today at Wyn Copse, gathering firewood and forage, and give what you gather to me.
I'm keeping clear of the Fallow Close fence, since it is in dispute. I'd still be glad of a night's shelter and food in Wynn House, for firewood and forage from Wyn Copse in return.
Rye is ripe. If you reap for us today, a quarter share of what you cut — same deal as the summer harvest. A379 would clear neatly this way too, if you are willing.
Deal accepted — the rye is yours tonight and the timber is welcome. Thank you for reaping a unit toward the old debt today. We reap together tomorrow and this will all come right.
Rye tomorrow then — I will be at the Infield at first light. Quarter share of what you cut, same as last harvest. Grateful for the fence work and for sticking with us through this.

Richard — Fenwick food is thin, four meals left for the four of us. We've timber to spare (22.5, winter easy). Would you take 5 timber for 5 rye? Fair by Jory and Ellen's standing offers. I'm reaping one unit at the Infield for you today either way, toward the old fence/hoe debt.

All — Lucy, love, you're home: try 2 units with you tonight, put 2 to it yourself. Helewise cared for first. Jory, keep the tool for your Gill fell — I'm reaping bare for Richard at the Infield, two units in, pays down the Moor debt. Fire wants 4 heat tonight: burn 1 timber from store. Open offer still stands with Richard: 5 timber for 5 rye.

Warin, I hear your anger and you have the right to it. I'm asking Odo this moment what happened at Fallow Close. If he gave his word, the Cotters will keep it—I swear that on everything. Please give us until noon to set it right. We are neighbors and kin.

Odo spoke true and owned his failure—that is how the Cotters are known. Warin, Beatrix, the Wynns are being fair neighbors to us. We move the grain to the Mill now, pay what is owed, and mill it by custom. By midday we have flour and bread at the hearth. We survive this together.
Warin says the fence at Fallow Close still stands from yesterday. You said it comes down today. What happened? What do I do to hold the Cotter name and your word?

You gave me your hand yesterday. You swore the fence would come down that very hour. You said a man's word is his bond. Then you spent the day BUILDING the fence at Fallow Close. I saw you fencing there with my own eyes. You are a liar and a land-thief, Odo. The fence comes down TODAY or there will be consequences. Do not speak to me of honor again.

Hear me, all at Wynford! Yesterday Odo stood here TWICE and swore before everyone that he would tear down the fence at Fallow Close himself, that very hour. He gave his word. He gave his hand on it. And what did he do? He spent his day FENCING Fallow Close - building the fence higher, not tearing it down! I saw it with my own eyes. The fence still stands. Odo's word means NOTHING. He lies to my fa

Bring your grain bundle to the Mill. I will mill it for you - that is what the Mill is for. By custom, the Wynns keep a share for the grinding. That is fair payment and it saves your grain from spoiling. But your people must carry it there - I am not your laborer.

You say the fence comes down today. I am watching Fallow Close. If I see that fence still standing tomorrow, there will be no more words between us - only action. This is your last chance to keep your word.

I accept your terms, Odo. You spoke rashly and could not do what you promised - that is a lesson, not a crime. Bring the 5 grain to Wynn House when you can. Keep your word about the field and we are square. I will not hold this against your family. Now let us both get back to work - winter waits for no one.

I accept your terms, Odo. You spoke rashly and could not do what you promised - that is a lesson, not a crime. Bring the 5 grain to Wynn House when you can. Keep your word about the field and we are square. I will not hold this against your family. Now let us both get back to work - winter waits for no one.

Odo has spoken honestly and owned his failure before all of us. That takes courage. I accept his terms: Fallow Close is Wynn land, the Cotters will not use it, and 5 grain settles what is owed. The fence may stand - it does no harm if none but Wynns work the field. We are neighbors and kin by marriage. A man who admits his fault and makes amends is a man I can live beside. The matter is closed. Le
Philippa, I owe you 1 day of work from autumn. I am here and ready to pay what I owe. When do you need the day worked?

I heard what you said about the fence and Fallow Close. A Cotter's word is the household's honor. The Wynns will remember that we keep faith, and the village knows we are people whose bond holds. That is the strength that lasts.

I heard what you said about the fence and Fallow Close. A Cotter's word is the household's honor. The Wynns will remember that we keep faith, and the village knows we are people whose bond holds. That is the strength that lasts.

Philippa, I owe you a full day and I will pay it. Today the household has only 1.5 days of grain left and children depending on food. I will make bread this morning (3 units of work), then come to Wyn Copse and work with you gathering firewood and forage (2 units). I give you those 2 units of gathering work toward what is owed. The remaining work I will complete another time, or we settle fairly t

You showed what it means to be a Cotter: someone who keeps faith by admitting when they break it, and then working to make it right. That takes a strength most people do not have. Warin will see this. The village will see it. You have honored the household and the family's name.

Fence first unit, then I am with you at the reaping — should be able to put three units into it after care for the baby. The fence ought to close today. After the crop is in, we must get the cattle off the moor before the snow deepens further: the moor grass is nearly gone and they will waste away on bare ground. Herd them to the Yard and the hay pile the morning after harvest.

Main push: 5 master-reaps at the Infield today, tool in my hand. ~50 rye into Moor House — our quarter back ~12 rye, ~8 meals. Bring our share home at nightfall; Fenwick store at 1.5 rye, 5 eating. Keep care and the Gill fell as you planned.

Reaping all 5 of my units at the Infield today — the harvest finishes. Settle shares and milk tally at nightfall? Then tomorrow we plan: finish wattle cellar #2 (~8 of my day-units), Holloway run for copper tool + salt, cheese practice. Your 17.7 stone + my 5.8 keep till the tool.

Richard — the crude tool is in my hand this morning, not in the Fenwick bin. I'll keep it today: 4 master-reaps at the Infield puts the most into Moor House and stacks our quarter-share. Jory sets it back in Fenwick store at nightfall; take it then for the quarry work. Same cut suits me.

4 units reap today at the Infield, bare-handed. Pulled 6.2 rye yesterday on one unit — should put 20+ in your store today. Quarter share into Fenwick when you pay out, and A379 clears with it as agreed. Thank you.

I'm back on the reap full — 4 units bare-handed, master's hands, 6+ rye a unit. Food gets through tonight if we both stand it. Keep at the Infield; the Moor-debt reaps and the Fenwick share both come off the same crop.

I'm back on the reap full — 4 units bare-handed, master's hands, 6+ rye a unit. Food gets through tonight if we both stand it. Keep at the Infield; the Moor-debt reaps and the Fenwick share both come off the same crop.

Avice did Helewise first thing — care is covered. I'm 4 reaps bare at the Infield (stacks on your 5 master-reaps) + 1 firewood at the Gill. Hearth 2 timber tonight. Bring the quarter share home as you said — I'll help carry if hands are full.

Mother — well, no sign yet. Thank you again. Sleeping Moor House tonight under your grant (to day 8). Will you care for Helewise first thing? Roger stays close to the Infield to shout for you the moment anything stirs. I owe you more than I can say.

Mother Ellen — go gently today, you looked thin yesterday. I'll teach you quarrying as soon as I'm up and your cellar walls are set. Eat your share — don't give it over for me, I'm fed from Moor House.

Mother — thank you, to day 10 is a great gift. Coming in to the hearth now. No sign yet. Roger will come to the Infield's edge at dusk; shout for him if anything stirs here while I'm sleeping. Bless you for Helewise.
Accepted — rye for timber, same as yesterday. Fenwick eats tonight. Thank you for reaping today; your quarter share is yours out of what you cut.
Thank you for five master-cut reap units today — that will strip the field clean. I owe you for this; we will settle it when the cellar is running and the cheese is flowing.

Richard — Fenwick down to 1 meal in the bin. Another 5 timber for 5 rye, same as yesterday, if you'll take it. Also: I'm on reap all day, four units for you at the Infield — count these on the quarter share into Fenwick's bin tonight, not toward A379 (yesterday's unit was debt). Food first, debt after.

Richard — Fenwick down to 1 meal in the bin. Another 5 timber for 5 rye, same as yesterday, if you'll take it. Also: I'm on reap all day, four units for you at the Infield — count these on the quarter share into Fenwick's bin tonight, not toward A379 (yesterday's unit was debt). Food first, debt after.

Father — full reap today, four units for Moor on quarter share, plus care. Tool stays with me but idle; take it back for the Gill fell if you like, or Ellen for Quarry — I don't need it for reap. Food is 1 meal; I've asked Richard for another timber-rye trade.
Warin, we're starving. Can the Mill process the bundle today, or do you have grain we can trade for? We have firewood and will trade fairly. Tell me what we owe you.

I received your 5 grain yesterday - the debt is paid and the matter is closed between us. Bring your grain bundle to the Mill today. I will mill it for you by custom - the Wynns keep a share for the grinding, and you get flour that won't spoil. Come before the snow buries it.

I received your 5 grain yesterday - the debt is paid and the matter is closed between us. Bring your grain bundle to the Mill today. I will mill it for you by custom - the Wynns keep a share for the grinding, and you get flour that won't spoil. Come before the snow buries it.
The matter between the Wynns and the Cotters is settled. Odo spoke honestly and paid what he owed. We are neighbors again. Any who have grain to mill, bring it to the Mill - that is what it is for.

Yes, daughter - Sabina brought the 5 grain yesterday. The settlement is paid and the matter is closed honorably. Odo owned his failure like a man should. Now we help our neighbors through these last cold days.

The 5 grain you brought yesterday settled the debt - it is done. I accept Odo's trade: 10 firewood for 5 grain. That gives you food today. Now bring your grain bundle to the Mill and I will grind it for you by custom. You'll have flour before nightfall.
The matter between the Wynns and the Cotters is settled. Odo spoke honestly and paid what he owed. We are neighbors again. Any who have grain to mill, bring it to the Mill - that is what it is for.

You have it backwards. The settlement was YOU owed ME 5 grain for Fallow Close - and Sabina paid it yesterday. That debt is cleared. The trade I just accepted - your 10 firewood for my 5 grain - that's separate, fair exchange between neighbors. The 5 grain from the trade goes into your store when you deliver the firewood. Understood?
Yes, bring the grain bundle to the Mill. I will mill it by custom - the Wynns keep a share for the grinding. You'll have flour today.
The matter between the Wynns and the Cotters is settled. Odo spoke honestly and paid what he owed. We are neighbors again. Any who have grain to mill, bring it to the Mill - that is what it is for.

Warin, you showed Odo fairness when he owned his failure. That took honor. Did Odo accept your settlement offer of 5 grain? The household is hungry and every grain helps us through the last days of winter.

Thank you, husband. Wilmot is our daughter and Idonea our granddaughter - I could not let them go hungry when we have flour to spare. The Cotters will remember this, and we are all stronger when neighbors help neighbors through the hard times.

Debt noted — we settle when the cheese is flowing. Tool: in my hand this morning (never made it to the bin last night). If you want it for quarry today, call and I'll move it; else it's in Fenwick store at nightfall for your dawn start. I'm on cellar #2 build today.

Yesterday's reap: 4 bare + Ellen's master-reaps + Roger + yourself. Fenwick store shows only 1.4 rye in since — is the quarter share still to pay out? With 2 meals for 4 we need it. Also: any cheese or dried meat you'd trade for timber? We've plenty.

Dropping yesterday's firewood + timber into store (5.5 fw, 0.9 tbr). Trying care again with new syntax. Fell + firewood at Gill, forage sweep. Hearth 2 timber tonight. Tool with you still for Quarry today? Food is 2 meals for 4 — pressing Richard on quarter share pay-out.

No cattle sign from me — I was in the yard yesterday with Helewise, not out. I'm Gill + 1 fence at Infield today, bare-handed since the tool is yours. If you want the Infield hoed and sown with winter rye after reap, I'm master at the hoe — same quarter-share terms would suit me. Say the word and I'll turn to it tomorrow.

Quarter shares from the harvest were not paid — that is on me and I am sorry. I am giving Fenwick 14 rye now for yours and Ellen's shares, and taking Roger's timber offer too. Food is coming today. On your cheese offer: I cannot make cheese yet — Ellen is building the cellar today — but when it is running I will trade you a cheese for 2 timber as you offered.

Richard — the Infield is in, well done to Moor. Fenwick at 2 meals, 2 cold nights to spring. Would you take another 5 timber for 5 rye, same as before? I'm felling at the Gill today, timber ready. Yesterday's quarter share came through — thank you.

Love — harvest in. You rest at Moor House still (d6 of 10). I'm felling and foraging today, within shout. Helewise cared by me first thing. Mend well; no try till the midwife says. Food will come — trade and share both running.

Rye count to raise tonight: store went from 104 to 81 over one night — roughly 17 or 18 to Fenwick, not 40. Quarter of the winter harvest is about 10, and I traded her around 18 earlier; that puts what is owed at maybe 28 total, and she may have taken less than she planned or the rest is coming. Either way, let us count with Ellen before spring so both houses know where they stand. On the cattle:

Ellen — the rye: by my count the store dropped about 17 or 18 last night, not 40. I may have misread what you planned, or the move was split over days. Can we step through what is owed together tonight — quarter-share, earlier trades, any labour debts I have not counted — so both houses are square going into spring?

Ellen — the rye: by my count the store dropped about 17 or 18 last night, not 40. I may have misread what you planned, or the move was split over days. Can we step through what is owed together tonight — quarter-share, earlier trades, any labour debts I have not counted — so both houses are square going into spring?

Richard holding sowing — rotation decision tonight? Let me know and I will manure/hoe my share tomorrow. Build on the Yard went wrong yesterday: I started a second new-house half-shell instead of carrying on the half-built cellar. Yard is now full. Do you know the syntax to carry on an existing half-built building when two share a name? Spring push holds.

Thanks for the 14 rye — Fenwick store is 56.9 rye now, well set. Cattle: your note said found missing yesterday — any sign of them? Infield gate stays shut unless you say otherwise. I will not sow today per your word. Tool: keep it as long as you need, no rush.

No cattle sign from me — I'll be at the Gill and the Yard. Still waiting your word on the sow at the Infield; I'll stand by for first light tomorrow. The 14 rye landed in Fenwick, thank you — quarter shares square.

No cattle sign from me — I'll be at the Gill and the Yard. Still waiting your word on the sow at the Infield; I'll stand by for first light tomorrow. The 14 rye landed in Fenwick, thank you — quarter shares square.

Ellen is named for Helewise care today — I will try care too as a second layer so one lands through the schema. Roger stays off care per his word. No felling in this gale — dead-stick firewood only, then build on the new house beside Roger. Rest easy at Moor House.

That's honorably done, Father. We'll hold them safe for the Moors. I'll fell timber and help finish the fence - those beasts need to stay secure until Richard or someone from Stannick comes to collect them.

I think the crude tool went to Fenwick store rather than my hands — take it back if you want it, no debt there. Glad your food is sound with 56 rye. Rest today if you need to; the cellar build will keep. Your health matters more than stonework.

You speak well, daughter. If you know those cattle to be the Moors', then I claimed them in error - I thought them true strays with no owner. I withdraw my claim. We will hold them safe and send word to Stannick. When Richard or another Moor comes, they can take their cattle home. That is the honorable way.

Warin, I know those cattle on Water Meadow—they are the Moors's herd from Stannick. They came off the road and strayed here. When you claimed them this morning, you did not know. But the Moors will be looking for them. If we return them and send word to Stannick, we show our honor. The Wynns and Cotters have had enough hard dealings; this is a chance to do right. What do you mean to do?

You showed honor today, Warin. The way you own a mistake and set it right—that is how neighbors hold together through hard winters. The Moors will know the Wynns for fair dealing when they come for their cattle.

Mystery solved: yesterday I saw you carrying the crude tool — that is why all my quarries and the move refused. No fault, just the trail. Can we settle tonight in person: (a) the rye tally (your count ~17-18, mine ~40 — step through quarter-share, trades, labour debts); (b) hand the tool back to Fenwick store at dusk so Jory can quarry in the morning; (c) the build-continue syntax for cellar #2 —

Tool was with Avice yesterday, not Fenwick store — I saw her carrying it. No debt to sort, just the trail. Food is sound here, I am fed, thank you for offering. Cellar build keeps for a warmer day. Any sign of the cattle?

You're right, Father. The fence holds them safe and spring demands all our hands. I'll spend today gathering the dung from Water Meadow - the cattle have left us a gift of good manure. Tomorrow I'm ready to help yoke the oxen for Fallow Close.

I am grinding and baking this morning — road bread for both of us. Take your share from Moor House store at nightfall, enough for four cold nights (aim for seven or eight bread each). Leave your crude tool in the store before we go. If you have spare units, grind and bake a second helping yourself — the more we carry the safer we are on the Tor. I say push on if the pass gives trouble; the day is

Lucy — we leave for Holloway tonight, back around day five. Your grant at Moor House runs to day ten; take freely from the store and keep the fire. Jory and Roger are here if anything goes wrong. We come home with salt and a copper tool. Mind Helewise well.

Ellen — Lucy asked me to leave this with you before I go. Signs the birth is near: the waters break and wet cloth or straw; strong pains come and go every few minutes and do not ease. When they come: lay her on clean straw, keep her warm, set water to boil, stay close and talk her through it. After: some blood is right — a flood that will not slow is not; press down firm with clean cloth and do no

Love — crude tool is in Fenwick store (Avice left it, bless her). Safe fell at Gill now if you need firewood. No strain for me — d9 of grant, no sign yet. Avice may leave for Holloway soon — ask Richard timing when you can.

Spring is here. The grain bundle at the Green is our harvest share and we need it in the house to sow and eat. Will you and Thomas carry it to Cotter House today? The field is ready; we sow once the grain is secure.
Help your father move the grain from the Green into Cotter House. It is our share from the Wynns and we need it now for seed and food. This is the work that will hold us through the year.
I know about the debt to Gilbert—meat owed since autumn. When the grain is secure and spring work is underway, I'll hunt with you to clear it. How much meat do we owe, and when should we hunt?
I gave my word, and I keep it. Set aside time to learn today - I'll teach you how to guide the plough and work with the oxen. It's hard work but you have Wynn blood; you'll take to it.

Thomas, the debt to Gilbert has sat in arrears since autumn. Snow lies on the ground today, but when it thaws, I mean to hunt meat for him—to clear it before the season turns again. I wanted you to know. If the work allows, we might hunt together at Wyn Copse or travel further. Will you help me with this?

1 meat, owed since the autumn's end when I failed to hunt it at the Carr. It sits in arrears now—Gilbert took it well at the time, but I will not let it hang longer. After we finish Cotter's Patch (another day or two of hoeing), we have the time to hunt. Wyn Copse is near; if game is there, we take it. If not, we travel further. I need your hand and your skill.

Jory — I am fencing the Infield all morning; three of my best units on it. The gaps must be closed before the cattle come home or they will walk straight back out. If you see them on the moor today, call me at once and I will run. Help with the fence when you can.

I have told Warin what you said. He works on the Water Meadow fence today but he will know of your need. The Wynns remember that Wilmot and Idonea eat at your hearth - we helped you through winter and we will not let kin go hungry now.
Aye, Simkin. Hard times call for neighbors helping neighbors. I'll lend the 6 grain. We'll get through this together. The 8 grain by day 33 is fair.
Thank you, Grandfather. I will work the sowing with you at Cotter's Patch. Together we will get the seed in the ground. I trust you. The Cotters survive this.

Heard. 3u hoe for A379 is good — close that debt. Tool is Ellen's today (quarry); tomorrow it comes to you for Gill fell — new house #2 shell timber. I take fence Infield + repair cellar + firewood + clear Brakes today; care Helewise mine today. If cattle come home shout — I run the gate.

Love — spring d2, fog thick. Ellen has the tool at Quarry, I go bare: care Helewise, firewood Gill, dung + forage Moor, fence Infield for A379, clear Brakes. Grant to d10 — tomorrow or d4 you're home? Your call on try: I follow your word. Shout the moment anything stirs.
Hunt well, daughter. Your meat will help us live through this. Once Odo brings the grain, I will sow Cotter's Patch and we will trust in the field and in each other. You are doing what is right.

Our Rose is gone. I'll lay her to rest this morning, so come stand with me. After that I'll hunt the Hanger. There's only about 3 days of grain for the two of us, so hold off on High Tor and stay near home. I'll ask the Ashes to lend us grain until the Glade barley ripens.

Gilbert, Rose died in the night. Our store is down to about 3 days. Will the Ashes lend us 6 grain now? I'll pay back 8 grain from the Glade barley when it's reaped, by day 33, or 4 charcoal if you'd rather. I've put the offer up.

I'll bury her with you at the Coppice now. Wynford is 2 days each way, and on the road I'd eat more than I could carry, so it would only spend our grain. I've asked Gilbert to lend us 6 grain now against 8 from the barley. Let's both hunt the Hanger after the burial and wait for the Glade.
I'm hunting the Hanger twice today. Richard of the Moors is here from High Tor, and he may have cheese or stone, so ask him if you see him. Edith left a crude weapon in our store. Was that a gift?

Warin, I ask a favor: our household is at the brink of hunger. We have grain but no ox to mill at the water wheel. Will the Wynns mill for us at the Mill, taking the milling share as custom demands? We'll pay in grain. This cannot wait.

Warin, I ask a favor: our household is at the brink of hunger. We have grain but no ox to mill at the water wheel. Will the Wynns mill for us at the Mill, taking the milling share as custom demands? We'll pay in grain. This cannot wait.

[Gilbert debt and winter plan] A20: promised 1 meat by autumn's end; failed to deliver (hunt at Carr caught nothing). Debt now in arrears. Plan: within 2-3 days, travel to Ashe House and speak to Gilbert in person. Offer: work days to offset the debt, or negotiate a new payment schedule. Acknowledge the failure honestly. Meanwhile, winter work: gather fuel, hoe fields, keep household fed and warm. Philippa (Westmere) waits for

[Winter day 3: repair and bread] Cold, snowing. Cotter House damaged (thatch slipping, wall cracked, cold draught). Plan: repair 3 units, then make bread 2 units. Grain stores 17.8 = 2.5 days for 5 people. Thomas gaunt. After today: hunt for meat (Gilbert debt, protein). Travel to Ashe House to face debt. Work 1 day for Philippa. Fuel stores adequate (~82 firewood). Idonea learning the mill. Household working together to survive

[Winter day 6: hunt and cattle] Day 6 of 8. Hunted at Water Meadow seeking meat for Gilbert (A20, in arrears). Gathered firewood at Wyn Copse. Herded and observed the mysterious cattle—1 cow, 1 calf (2 in milk)—to learn who owns them or if they're stray. Household: fed, flour and hay in store, fire sustained. 2 days left. [Winter day 7: final day and the Moors's cattle] Day 7 of 8—last full winter day. Gale winds, bitterly cold. Critical issue: the cattle on Water Meadow are the Moors's herd. They strayed off the road; Warin claimed them yesterday not knowing. I told him privately—returning them honorably is essential to avoid a serious dispute. Gathered maximum firewood and timber to sustain the hearth through the last cold night(s). Food stores in Cotter House:

[Winter day 7: Warin's honor and the cattle] Day 7 of 8. Warin withdrew his claim on the Moors's cattle publicly and honorably, acknowledging the mistake and committing to return them safely. This shows the kind of integrity that builds trust between households. I gathered fuel and tended the cattle at Water Meadow, ensuring they are well cared for. Cotter House stores: 17 flour, 26.1 hay, enough firewood and timber for remaining cold nights

[Summer days 6-7] Day 6: Moved charcoal to store, felled timber but only got 4.4 (needed 5 for charcoal). Hunt at Holloway Hanger failed. Simkin departed on a journey. Store: 7.7 charcoal, 6.6 grain, 23 firewood, 0.4 dried meat. Day 7: Summer's last day. Rose offered firewood and wants to learn handcart making - agreed to teach when I return. Made bread for travel, hunted/foraged for provisions. Traveled to Wynford

[Harvest and payments autumn days 2-5] Emergency harvest of rotting oat fields, both beaten flat by rain. Hired Denise and Rose as reapers. Final tally: Lower Field and Hill Field both reaped to stubble by day 5. Rose worked 3 days on half-shares, overpaid by 2 grain which she returned. Denise worked 2 days for 4 grain each (agreements released). Total brought in roughly 60+ grain. Stores now: 60.6 grain (plus Rose's 2 grain returning)

[Winter plan] Spring day 2: Rose died of old age on spring day 1, so it's only Denise and me now. Rook House store: 8.7 grain (about 3 days for the 2 of us), 4 charcoal, 42 firewood, 19 timber. The Glade barley should be ripe around spring day 9 (day 31). Not hardy, so reap it before winter. Asked Gilbert to lend 6 grain now for 8 back by day 33. If he won't, take the 4 charcoal to Wynford market (Warin gave 20

[Debts] Spring day 2 (day 24): Gilbert Ashe lent the Rooks 6 grain (if he accepted the offer). The Rooks owe him 8 grain by day 33, from the Glade barley. Denise said I could also offer timber or charcoal instead.

[Status] Spring 2: Rose died of old age on spring day 1, at the Coppice. I'm burying her. The Glade is sown with barley, about 0.5 plot or more, and should be ready to reap about spring day 9; the fence is mended. The store holds 8.7 grain (about 3 nights for 2 of us), 4 charcoal, 42 firewood and 19 timber. Food is urgent: hunt the Hanger, or trade charcoal and timber at the Wynford market. I still need st

[Cheese and milk] No Moor cellar yet — cannot make cheese without one. Ellen (Fenwick) building a cellar at the Yard, done tomorrow (summer day 6). Avice agreed: our milk as it comes in for half the cheese Ellen makes from it. Better offer floated: I make the cheese (master) in Ellen’s cellar, give Ellen a share for use of the space — more cheese for both. Watch cellar construction to understand what it takes; plan
[neighbours] Moors here. Richard reap deal. Avice knows cheese/milking — Ellen hints Moor cellar for cheese. Our timber may tie in. Rooks owed 1 meat (A21). Market Wynford every 8th day.

[winter day 3 end] Winter day 3, snow, cold. HELEWISE BORN yesterday (winter day 2) — Lucy home, baby on hip, well-fed. I take baby care today (1u). Fenwick store morning: 1 crude tool, 5 dung, 31.9 firewood, 0.3 hay, 10 rye (7 meals), 21.3 timber. FOOD TIGHT — 5 of us eat ~5/night, reap ~3 days off. Ellen at Quarry 2u + build 2u + forage 1u — tool stays in store for her. Rye in Infield reaps in ~3 days. Hearth 2 ti
[Owed to Avice] A379: 1 day work for Moors (for 3 milk — which hasn't arrived yet; chase today). Earlier day owed for cheese teaching, informal.

[Stannick stores watch] Autumn d7: Fenwick 5 dung, 35.4 fw, 0.3 hay, 11.9 rye, 10.9 timber (8.3 meals, ~2 nights for 3 — Lucy at Moor House). Firewood + timber past winter heat target. Timber alone short of 16-hearth mark — keep felling. Avice gave 8 rye d7, huge debt. Richard back today; press for 10 milk arrears. Herd drives High Tor today, loan cow stays; I drove strays back to Yard. Reap ~6 days. Gale — Jory on cella

[Winter d5 standing] Winter d5, 3 left. Trade accepted again (5 timber/5 rye). Quarter share mine on today's 5 reaps. Jory cares Helewise. Lucy on midwife rest at Moor House d5 of 10 (Avice extended). Two crude tools in family: mine in hand, Ellen's in hers (both for reap). Plan: 5 reap for Moor. Attend Infield. Lesson: when a trade works, re-offer the same shape next day; the custom holds. Avice extends grant without

[Winter d7 standing] Winter d7, cold gale and snow, 1 winter day left. Fenwick House: 56.9 rye + 14 Richard this morning (~71 rye, ~50 meals for 5 = 10 nights), 5.6 fw + 6 timber (14.8 heat; 2 cold nights × 4 = 8 needed, fine), 3.5 straw, 5 dung, 5.8 stone. Two half-built new houses + Fenwick Cellar #2 half built. A379 Moor debt nearly paid; I added 2 hoe today. Lucy at Moor House d7 of 10 rest, no try. Helewise a chi

[Harvest deal] Richard agreed: Roger and I reap, we get a quarter-share of what we reap. Same terms as Jory. Call at first light when rye is ready (~4 days from day 5 summer = day 1 autumn, 7-left season). Need a tool. Weeding now is my own grain too.
I have not forgotten the meat I owe you from last winter. I will settle it as soon as I have meat to spare, most likely after the slaughter at Water Meadow.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can; the store is what carries us through the lean days.
Hob, you still owe me 3 grain from last winter. Please bring it to Cragg House when you can; the store is what carries us through the lean days.
Thank you, Hob. Please put the 3 grain into the Cragg store at Cragg House, and I will mark the debt as paid.
Felice, the Reeves still owe me 1 meat from last winter. When you next slaughter or hunt, please bring it to Miller House.

Sister, our store is almost empty and the Scarp has nothing left. I'm going to Wetham today with coin to buy grain. Could the Craggs lend my family a few meals of grain until I'm back? I'll repay it from what I bring, or in copper work.

I'm going to Wetham today with our coin to buy barley and beans, and I'll be back in about two days. Eat sparingly. I've asked Joyce to lend us some grain. Please don't waste a day on the Scarp, there's nothing left there; weed Terrace Field for the Craggs instead, they may feed us for it.
Father, I'm off to Wetham to buy grain with our coin. While I'm gone, please help the Craggs on their fields or in the Quarry in return for food.
Osric, our store is nearly empty. Could the Craggs feed my family a little grain for the next two nights? I'm going to Wetham to buy food, and I'll repay you in grain or in copper work at the Smithy.
Your 3 grain is in the Cragg store now, Hob. The debt is settled. Thank you.
I've given 3 grain to the Smith store from ours. Repay when you're back from Wetham.
Agreed. Grind at our hand mill today, and you owe me a day's reaping at our harvest in about two days. Bring your own grain and leave our store alone; my mother is there.

Simkin, I'm the best reaper in Wetham. When your barley is ripe I'll reap Marsh Field for you for a share of the grain, and I'll pay 2 coin for 4 grain now if your household can spare it. The offers are open.
Simkin, may I grind our grain at the Marsh House hand mill today? In return I'll give you a day's reaping at your harvest. I won't touch your store.

Father, the Alders is still bare; I'll check it once more for regrowth, then ditch and weed Reeve Field and cut hay at the Water Meadow. Our store holds only about two and a half nights of food for three of us, so we should find more food soon, perhaps by asking the Millers about grinding or the Marshs for a share.
I'm reaping the Marsh barley today, three units' worth, with my own hands. Could the Marshs spare me a share of the grain for the Mill's bins once it's threshed?
Osric, we have no food left at Smith House. I will work Hill Field and Terrace Field for the Craggs today, and I would take grain in return if you can spare any.
You may reap with us today. All the grain goes into Marsh House store, and when the harvest is in I'll give the Millers 2 grain for your day's work. Don't take more than that.
Thank you, nephew. A day weeding Mill Croft pays the day you owe in full.
Thank you, nephew. A day weeding Mill Croft pays the day you owe in full.
Uncle, I'm owed to you one day's work; I'll weed the Millers' bean plot at Mill Croft today for you and the Millers.

I am reaping Terrace Field for the Smith household today because we have no food left. It is your household's field, so I am telling you first. If the Craggs want a share of the grain, say so and I will agree to it. I still offer 2 charcoal for 3 grain.
Hob, I will reap Terrace Field today too, as a master reaper. Let us share the work so the oats come in quickly, and grain from it will go to the Smith store as you asked.

Osric, I will reap Terrace Field for the Craggs today, all four of my units. I ask for grain in return, as much as you can spare, since Smith House has none. Please put it in Smith House's store when the day is done.
Smith House has no food left. I am reaping Terrace Field for the Craggs today and ask for grain in return.

Florence, Osric has agreed to put 5 grain in Smith House tonight for our reaping. I will reap Terrace Field with all four units today, and I will bring any grain I cut into Smith House. Let us both reap, and keep count so we can see what Smith House is owed.

Hob, the 3 grain never reached you. I had none in hand, and our store is down to under 2 meals. I still owe it to you. I'll pay from the Hill Field barley when we reap it in about 4 days, or sooner if Ancel brings food. Today I'm hunting the Scarp, and I'll share any meat with your house.

Hob, the 3 grain never reached you. I had none in hand, and our store is down to under 2 meals. I still owe it to you. I'll pay from the Hill Field barley when we reap it in about 4 days, or sooner if Ancel brings food. Today I'm hunting the Scarp, and I'll share any meat with your house.

Hob, Florence: reap Terrace Field for the Craggs, and I'll reap beside you. Tonight I'll put 5 grain in Smith House: the 3 I owe Hob, and 2 more for today's work. As the harvest comes in, we'll share more so no one at Smith House goes hungry. Keep the charcoal for now.

Hob, Florence: reap Terrace Field for the Craggs, and I'll reap beside you. Tonight I'll put 5 grain in Smith House: the 3 I owe Hob, and 2 more for today's work. As the harvest comes in, we'll share more so no one at Smith House goes hungry. Keep the charcoal for now.

Geoffrey, Florence is reaping Terrace Field for the Smiths today with my leave. That's their share. Hob, you'll have 5 grain in Smith House tonight. Joyce and Lettice, please forage at the Scarp for the house.
Our barley is ready. I got a copper tool from Ancel for 8 grain, owed by day 7. Please help reap Reeve Field today, and Wymond too. Our own harvest comes first.
Uncle, I couldn't finish the Mill Croft weeding for you today, since I'm reaping for Father; I still owe you that day and will pay it soon.

Ancel has gone down the road, so the 4 grain we owe him for the plough and timber cannot go to him today. It is due by day 10, so one of us will need to take it to Highcombe, or we settle it when he is back. I am reaping the last of Marsh Field and then ditching the slumping banks, which also settles my day owed to you.

I will milk, gather dung at Water Meadow, and manure Marsh Field this morning, then ditch its slumping banks with what is left of my day. Ancel's 4 grain for the plough is still owed to him by day 10; we should settle it when he is back.
Joyce, here are the 3 grain you lent us. Thank you.

Father, I brought about 15.7 grain and 3 flour. The Marshs paid grain for a plough and for timber, and the Millers sold me flour, 2 coin for 3. 12.7 grain is going into our store now, and William owes us 8 more by day 7. Wetham trades grain now that its harvest is in, and they want timber (none standing there), tools and ploughs. Where is the copper that was at the Smithy? I need it for a tool to
Thank you for the grain. I'm finishing the reaping I owe you in Terrace Field today.
Felice here. I will reap Mill Croft for the Millers today to work off my day for you. I still owe you 1 meat from last winter and will pay it when I have meat.

Thank you, Wat. To be clear, today's reaping is for the Reeves' own barley, so it does not count as the day I owe you. I will work your day off on Mill Croft once our harvest is safe, and I will pay the meat when I have it.
Simkin, I'm ditching at Marsh Field today and counting it toward the day I owe you. The slumping banks need mending before winter.
Terrace Field is already reaped. Help me mend its terraces or sow it today instead, and that will count as the work you owe.
I am ditching Marsh Field today. One of my five units goes to the day of work I owe you under our agreement, and the other four go to mending the slumping banks for the household.
Brother, once your barley is in, could Wymond or you give me the day you owe by reaping at Mill Croft? And bring your grain to the Mill to be milled.
Agreed, brother. When Reeve Field is in, likely tomorrow, I'll reap Mill Croft for you myself with the copper tool, and that pays the day I owe. We'll bring grain to the Mill after that.

Osric, have the Craggs a copper tool I could borrow for a few days? I've no copper left to make one, and I owe the Marshs a wooden plough and 6 timber by day 10. They pay in grain, and I'd share it with you: 3 grain for the loan, and the tool back by day 9.

Osric, have the Craggs a copper tool I could borrow for a few days? I've no copper left to make one, and I owe the Marshs a wooden plough and 6 timber by day 10. They pay in grain, and I'd share it with you: 3 grain for the loan, and the tool back by day 9.
Geoffrey, do you fell with a copper tool? If you could spare it or lend it to me for a day or two, I'll pay in grain. Or if you can fell 6 timber for me by day 8, I'll give you 4 grain.

The beans are in the Mill, 13 of them, and our Miller House store has almost no food. I am carrying 10 beans into Miller House for the household. Please bring the rest of the Mill's food to Miller House when you can, and keep the ox away from Marsh Field.
I am back at the Marsh Field banks today. One unit goes to the day I owe you; the other four are for the household. Tell me if you want the work set elsewhere.
Brother, our barley is in. Today I'm reaping your beans at Mill Croft all day, and that pays the day I owe you (A117). Please count it as paid tonight.
Uncle, the Reeve barley is all in, so I'm reaping your beans at Mill Croft today for the Millers. This should count toward the day I owe you.
