William says he paid your day at Mill Croft himself. I am weeding there for the Millers today in case it is still owed. I have no meat to pay you now. I have offered you 2 flour in place of the meat; if you accept, the debt is clear.
Thank you. I am bringing you 2 flour now, and I will count the meat debt clear once you have it.
Hob, we have 17 grain in Smith House, so eat well from the store. Please see that Stephen and Warin get their share first. I am going to the Scarp to forage, hunt and make charcoal.

Use the mill freely, Hob. I've taken your offer: 3 grain for 2 days. Put the days into reaping Terrace Field with me when the oats ripen, in about 3 days. I don't know where copper came from; it was always your trade.
Yes, Felice, 2 flour in place of the meat is fair, and the debt is clear. Give it to me or leave it at the Mill, and I'll count it paid.
Brother, your beans were reaped before I got to Mill Croft. Will you take 5 grain for the day I owe, or name another task? If grain suits you, say so and I'll give it at once.
Uncle, I'm reaping your beans at Mill Croft today and will leave the grain at Miller House for the Millers. That is my day toward what I owe you.

Osric, your copper tool is back with you, and the 3 grain: A444 is paid. I'm off to Wetham now with your coin and 8 timber. I'll trade 2 of it for your rye seed or beans. You mentioned 2 days of work owed to the Craggs (A506); I'll do them when I'm back.
Yes. I have 11 coin of ours and will buy all the barley and beans I can carry, and William owes us 8 grain. Keep everyone eating flour first and go easy on the grain. Back in 2 or 3 days.
I have given you 2 flour. Please release my meat debt (A18) so it is clear, and tell me if the day's work (A117) is still owed; I will work it at Mill Croft once I know.
Thank you. I have released the meat debt, so we are square.
Released: the meat debt is clear, and the day's work A117 was paid by William. You owe us nothing. Thank you.

Uncle, I'm ditching the wet corners of Reeve Field for two units today, and giving the other two units to gathering dung at Mill Croft for the Millers. That is part of what I owe you under A117; I will settle the rest of the day with work when I can.
Ancel, you owe us the wooden plough and 6 timber under our agreement, due by day 10. Bring them to Marsh House and I will give you the 4 grain for them as we agreed.

Simkin, I've put the 6 timber I owed into Marsh House (A304). Bad news on your plough (A287): there's no copper anywhere in Highcombe, and a wooden plough needs some. If you or anyone here has copper or copper ore, give me 1 and I'll make it straight away. If not, I'll give back your 6 grain, or you can take 3 coin now. Which do you want?

Wymond, William still owes me 8 grain from his harvest (A203). Can you pay it out of Reeve House, or tell me when he'll be back? I'd also pay 1 coin for a bed and supper with you tonight, the same as last time. And do you have rye seed or beans to sell? I'll pay coin.

Felice, the 6 timber I carried was owed to the Marshs, so I have none left today. I have 30 timber at home, though. I'll bring you 4 timber by day 13 for your 10 grain now. That's in my offer to you: take it, and I'll come back with it.
Sister, I am giving 10 grain to the Miller household's store, as a gift, so you need not pay coin for it. Eat well tonight.
I've given you the 4 grain I owe under A287 from our household store. Please bring the 6 timber and the wooden plough you owe us by day 10. We're short of timber for the winter fire.

Yes. I'll teach you ditching and banking at Reeve Field this morning, and I'll ditch there myself after. Be there at the start of the day. Work of your own ground in return is fine, but I'd rather you just come to the Marsh fields when we need hands.
The Mill has no grain to grind. Anyone with spare grain, please bring it to the Mill, and we will keep a fair share for it. The ox is penned on Mill Croft today.

Thank you for going to the Alders. Bring the forage to Miller House's store, and we will share the beans and flour evenly until Wat is back. I am keeping the ox on Mill Croft and weeding Marsh Field today.
I have no coin to trade, but I am giving 3 grain to the Miller House store today as a gift, not for coin. Godiva, thank you for weeding and penning the ox.

Ancel, good to see you in Wetham. The wooden plough and 6 timber are due to us tomorrow. If you've brought them, leave them in Marsh House's store and I'll have the grain we still owe you (2 grain, after the 2 coin I paid) ready to hand over. If you need more time, tell me when you'll have them.
Father, Ancel is here. If he leaves the plough and timber at Marsh House today, give him 2 grain from our store for what we owe. Keep the cattle off Marsh Field and milk as usual.

Warin, I came from Wetham to pay Ancel the 8 grain I owe him (for the copper tool). I've put the 8 grain into Smith House's store this morning. Please tell Ancel it is paid. Could you also let me sleep at Smith House tonight? I'll give 1 coin for a bed.
Stephen, I've left 8 grain in your store to pay Ancel's debt. I'm felling timber on the Scarp today. If the Smiths have timber to sell, I'll pay coin. And I'd pay 1 coin for a bed tonight.

Gervase, please set aside time today to teach me ditching and banking. Yesterday we missed each other, and Reeve Field is still sodden. I'll give you a day's work on your own ground in return, whenever you say.

Ancel, I can't pay your 8 grain from our store. That debt is William's to settle, and he isn't here. I'll tell him you asked and that you want a date or payment. I have no coin for a bed, so I can't offer you one tonight without his word.

Ancel, I can't pay your 8 grain from our store. That debt is William's to settle, and he isn't here. I'll tell him you asked and that you want a date or payment. I have no coin for a bed, so I can't offer you one tonight without his word.
Aunt, I'm sending 3 grain from Reeve House to Miller House as a gift, no coin needed. It's for the Millers' table tonight.

Godiva, Miller House has about four meals and the Mill has almost no food. I'm foraging the Alders today and will herd the ox on Mill Croft. Please tell me if you want the store's food shared out differently. My 2 coin offer for grain is still open.
Agreed, Godiva. I'll put any wild food I find into Miller House's store for the house to share evenly.
I'll dry the meat at our hearth. Bring it into Marsh House and we'll send the Millers a share.

Joyce, I'm home and half-starved. May I use your hand mill today to grind our grain to flour? Flour goes further than porridge. I haven't forgotten the 2 days of work I owe the Craggs (A506); I'll do them once I've eaten.

Good, so William's debt is settled. The Marsh plough is already called off: I gave back their grain and paid 3 coin. Do ask Richolda about ore, though. If we find copper, I can make tools to sell in spring.

William, the Reeve store has only 0.2 timber and the hearth needs about 2 on a cold night. Have you had word from the Smiths in Highcombe about the 4 timber Ancel owes us by day 13? If they cannot spare it, we must find another source before the next cold spell.

Osric, thank you and the Craggs for the grain and flour that kept Smith House fed. I am working two days' repair at Cragg House for you today to settle what I owe under A506. After that I will hunt and forage at the Scarp for our store.

Olive, thank you. Please keep the ox on Mill Croft today and bring what forage you find into Miller House's store. I will forage the Alders too, and we will share the beans and flour evenly until Wat is back.
It is winter and the Millers are short of food. I am foraging the Alders today for our store. Anyone with spare grain, please bring it to the Mill, and we will keep a fair share for it.
Agatha, thank you for foraging and herding. Please bring any wild food into Miller House's store, where we eat, and I will share it out evenly with Olive and the others in the house.
Simkin, thank you for the meat share. The Millers will take our part of it into Miller House's store, and I will see the house's work is returned to Marsh House once Wat is back.
Grandmother, I am going to the Alders to forage, hunt and fell timber for the house. Miller House has no food, so please share the Mill's beans out carefully.

Winter is here and every house is short of food. I'm slaughtering one cow that isn't in milk from the Wetham cattle and drying the meat at Marsh House. The cow in milk, the oxen, the bull and the calf are kept. The Millers will get a share of the meat, since their bins are empty.

Winter is here and every house is short of food. I'm slaughtering one cow that isn't in milk from the Wetham cattle and drying the meat at Marsh House. The cow in milk, the oxen, the bull and the calf are kept. The Millers will get a share of the meat. Gervase, I'll teach you ditching once we have meat put by.

Wife, I've brought 11 timber home and put it in the store, enough for about 5 cold nights. Ancel's debt is paid. Eat well tonight, because we have grain and flour. Tomorrow we need more timber, or we trade grain for it.

I brought 11 timber home from the Scarp on the handcart, and it's in the store now, enough for about 5 cold nights. Ancel's 8 grain is paid. Hob offered 6 more timber for 6 grain. I don't know of any 4 timber Ancel owes us; if he owes it, we'll ask for it when he comes.

Gervase, we missed the ditching lesson twice. Winter fuel is short, so I'm felling at the Alders today. When you can spare the time, teach me ditching at Reeve Field, and I'll come to the Marsh fields when you need hands.
Thank you, sister. The 5 flour means a lot. I'll count it as a debt and pay it back in grain or work when I can.
Wat, my records say your meat debt was released, but I know the Millers are hungry. I am sending 4 grain now, and I am baking bread from our flour to send to your house tonight. Eat well.
Hob, Osric has released our debt under A506: we owe the Craggs nothing more. I am out at the Scarp today for food, then making charcoal for the Smith store.

Wat, you are back. Miller House has no food left and the Mill store has only dung, hay and timber. Please bring any oats or flour you bought into the Mill, and we will share it fairly. The ox must stay penned on Mill Croft.
We will grind the grain in the Mill store today for the Millers' house, and keep a fair share for the Mill as always.

Father, Miller House has no food and the Mill has none either. Did the oats or any grain come back from Highcombe? Simkin is drying meat at Marsh House and promised the Millers a share. Should I keep the ox, or can we kill it for the meat?
Simkin, the Millers have no food at all. When your dried meat is ready, please give the Millers a share, and I will work for it on your fields.
Avice, the work you owe me (A199) is still open. Could you mend Cragg House with me today? It's still damaged.
Thank you, Florence. Your repair work counts, so I've released A506 as paid. Tell Hob he owes us nothing more.
Godiva, here is the Millers' share: 1 dried meat, about 3 meals, into Miller House. It was the calf, not a cow, so there was less meat than I'd hoped.
Felice, the Millers have no food left at all and five of us to feed. You've owed us 1 meat since last winter. If you can pay it now, or in grain or milk instead, it would keep my mother fed tonight.

William, Highcombe wouldn't sell us anything. Our store is empty. I'll mill any grain you bring to the Mill at no share all winter, and pay coin on top, if you can spare us some grain now. I've put an offer up: 4 coin for 5 grain.
Simkin, the Millers are out of food. Will the Marshs sell grain, milk or cheese for coin? I have 10 coin. I'll also mill your grain at the Mill for no share all winter.

Wife, we have about 9 timber, which is 4 cold nights. The Alders give nothing, so tonight I'm taking the handcart to Highcombe. I'll buy Hob's 6 timber with grain, fell more on the Scarp, and ask Ancel about the 4 he owes. I've ground grain into flour and put it in the store. I sold 3 grain to Agatha for 2 coin because the Millers are starving. Bank the fire low, and I'll be back in 3 days.
Wat, I still owe you a full day under A117. Today I'm herding at Mill Croft for the Millers as my payment. Tell me if you'd rather have the grain or the work another day.
Godiva, you owe the Marshs two days' work under our agreement. Please come to Marsh Field and work the banks with me on your days.

William, Felice's offer was never taken up, so there's no debt of 4 timber. But I'll take your offer: 6 timber for 4 coin, out of Smith House. All 6 of our beds are full and we have barely 2 nights of food, so I can't take you in. Cragg House has a spare bed and more food; ask Joyce or Osric, and I'll speak for you.

Son, the Reeve store has 6.2 timber, enough for about 3 cold nights. When you can, fell a little at the Scarp or the Alders, and bank the fire low. I am baking bread and spreading dung on Mill Croft today.

Wat, I am sorry, the Reeve store has under 1 grain left, so I cannot spare the 3 for your milling. We do have flour: I can offer you 4 flour for your household's bread, if you need it. Take it at Reeve House when you can.
Simkin, I am ditching Marsh Field today as I promised, for the share of your dried meat that goes to the Millers.
Godiva, you owe me two days of work under our agreement. The banks of Marsh Field are slumping, so please come and ditch and bank there today or tomorrow.

Ancel, it's William. I've come for timber and I'm half starved from the road. Will you take me in at Smith House tonight and feed me? I'll pay 1 coin a night, as you paid me in the summer. Also, Felice thinks you owe us 4 timber by day 13. Is that right?

Simkin, the Ancel plough deal is called off and his grain and timber are back in our store. A287 still shows the plough in arrears. Please release it or clear it with Ancel, since we will not get the plough. Keep the seed grain for spring; do not sell it to the Mill or to Wat.
Godiva, you still owe the Marshs two days' work under A807. Come to Marsh Field when you can, and we will settle it before spring sowing.
Godiva, you still owe the Marshs two days' work under A807. Come to Marsh Field when you can, and we will settle it before spring sowing.
William, could I borrow your copper tool for a day to fell here? I'd pay 1 coin and give you a share of the timber.
William, could I borrow your copper tool for a day to fell here? I'd pay 1 coin and give you a share of the timber.
William, could I borrow your copper tool for a day to fell here? I'd pay 1 coin and give you a share of the timber.
William, could I borrow your copper tool for a day to fell here? I'd pay 1 coin and give you a share of the timber.
Osric has given us 4 bread, freely, as kin. He says Hob's 3 grain was paid in autumn with the 11 grain he gave Smith House, and A506 is released. We owe the Craggs no grain.
Osric has given us 4 bread, freely, as kin. He says Hob's 3 grain was paid in autumn with the 11 grain he gave Smith House, and A506 is released. We owe the Craggs no grain.
Wat, I am sending 4 flour to Miller House now as a gift; no coin needed. Keep the Reeves' grain in mind, we have only about 1 grain left.
Son, I have seen your word. I will bank the fire low and keep the bread for cold eating if we must.

Osric, the Smith store is down to about two or three days of food for six of us. I have 2 charcoal I can carry to you. My open offer O176 is 2 charcoal for 3 grain. Could the Craggs accept it, or spare grain against my work? I will repair or reap for you in return.
Our agreement A858 has you working 2 days for me, 0 done, due by day 19. Could you come and work at Marsh Field when you can?
You owe me 2 days' work under A807, 1 done so far. I am at Marsh Field ditching today if you want to finish it there.
Gervase, I am working Marsh Field today with Richolda on the banks, for the Marshs. I have no record of owing you work under A807, so I will check with Adam and Richolda before I count anything more.
Osric, you still owe me 3 grain for the reaping at Terrace Field. Please put it into Smith House when you can; the store is thin for the frost.
Osric, you still owe me 3 grain for the reaping at Terrace Field. Please put it into Smith House when you can; the store is thin for the frost.

Ancel, our last 5 grain is spring seed and I can't sell it. I've given Smith House 4 bread, freely, as kin. Keep my 1 coin and spend it on rye or grain seed for us at Wetham. Tell Hob and Florence: I paid Hob's 3 grain in autumn with 11 grain to Smith House, and I released A506. No grain is owed.

Ancel, our last 5 grain is spring seed and I can't sell it. I've given Smith House 4 bread, freely, as kin. Keep my 1 coin and spend it on rye or grain seed for us at Wetham. Tell Hob and Florence: I paid Hob's 3 grain in autumn with 11 grain to Smith House, and I released A506. No grain is owed.

Simkin, I'm working on Marsh Field today, manuring it with dung from the Mill, as the first of my two days. The Millers have about 4 meals for 5 of us. I've put up 4 coin for 2 dried meat; or I'll work more days in spring for a little more flour. Whatever you can do, I'll remember it.
I'm sorry, Ancel. I need the copper tool at home to fell for our fire, and I'm leaving for Wetham tonight. I'll lend it another time.

William, the Reeve store has 0.2 timber and tonight is cold. Ancel of Highcombe owed us 4 timber by day 13 for 10 grain, and that is now overdue. Could you go to Highcombe with the cart and fetch it or any timber you can buy with our grain?

Agatha, I'm telling you first as you asked: Miller House has no food left and nobody will sell grain. I'm going to slaughter the ox today so we don't starve. The meat goes into Miller House. Please dry what you can at the hearth so it keeps. We'll find another beast for the stones after harvest.
Welcome back, brother. Miller House is down to under 1 timber and tonight is cold. I've put up 3 coin for 3 timber; please take it if you can spare it. I'll have ox meat to share too.
Felice, thank you for the flour. I'm slaughtering our ox today; the Reeves will have a share of the meat for your kindness.
I brought 8 timber home. I've put 6 in our store, which is enough for tonight and a few more cold nights. I gave 2 to the Millers. Ancel says he never owed us the 4 timber, so let that go.
Brother, I'm giving Miller House 2 timber and 5 bread as a gift, no coin needed. It's all I can spare: the rest keeps our own fire going. I'd be glad of some ox meat when it's ready.

Richolda, the Reeves have almost no seed grain for Reeve Field. Could the Marshs lend or sell us some grain or beans for seed? In return I will reap for the Marshs at harvest, as my work for 2 days, or I can give bread.

Richolda, the Reeves have almost no seed grain for Reeve Field. Could the Marshs lend or sell us some grain or beans for seed? In return I will reap for the Marshs at harvest, as my work for 2 days, or I can give bread.

Osric, I will mend the fallen terraces of Terrace Field today for the Craggs. I have offered you two days' work for 3 grain. I also still hold charcoal for O176 if you want it. Seed for the spring sowing is the next need; tell me if the Craggs will lend or give seed.
Avice, you owe me 2 days of work. Come to Hill Field today and help hoe it for the Craggs.

Welcome back from Highcombe. Under A287 you still owe us a wooden plough, one in arrears, and under A304 you owe the Marshs 6 timber, due by day 10. Our store is down to about 8 timber with winter not over. Could you bring the timber to Marsh House and the plough when you can?

Welcome back from Highcombe. Under A287 you still owe us a wooden plough, one in arrears, and under A304 you owe the Marshs 6 timber, due by day 10. Our store is down to about 8 timber with winter not over. Could you bring the timber to Marsh House and the plough when you can?

Good day, Florence. I'm Simkin Marsh. Ancel owes us a wooden plough and 6 timber by day 10 (we paid him in grain). Is it ready? I'd carry the plough home myself. Do the Smiths have any oats to spare for seed? I'll pay coin. And could you give me a bed tonight?
Thank you for felling in the Alders. Please bring the timber you cut to Marsh House, as the roof there needs it. Under A304 six timber is owed; if you cannot reach six, pay the rest in coin.
Agreed. I have released A304 on the 5 coin, in place of the timber. Thank you. Please bring the harness when you can find the leather.

Thank you for the bed, Osric. Today I'm weeding your oats on Terrace Field for the Craggs. In return, would you set aside 4 grain of oats for me as seed when you reap? I'm going home to Wetham tonight.
Thank you for the bed, Florence. When Ancel comes back, please tell him the Marshs are still waiting on the plough and 6 timber he owes us. He can bring them to Marsh House.
Richolda, Godiva is ditching the slumping banks of Marsh Field today to pay what she owes us under A807. Please count that ditching toward her days.
Ancel has sold our copper tool, so I have nothing to hoe with. Would you lend me yours for the day at Hill Field? I will give you a loaf for it and still count my reaping toward A199.
Avice, keep hoeing Hill Field with me today. Once your two days are done, the debt under A199 is clear.

Adam, I am ditching the slumping banks of Marsh Field myself today, to pay the days I owe the Marshs under A807. I will leave the ditched ground for the Marshs to sow; tell Richolda it counts toward what I owe.
Osric, you owe me 3 grain for my reaping at Terrace Field. I am weeding Terrace Field today; accept my offer of 2 days' work for 3 grain, and it will settle that debt and feed Smith House.
Avice, thank you for hoeing Hill Field. When the Terrace oats ripen in about 3 days, I'd count a day of reaping there toward the 2 days you owe me (A199).

Hob, the Craggs have no grain at all; every grain went in as seed. You told me in winter that no grain was owed. Still, I've offered you 3 grain from the reaping, by day 22, for 2 days of your work; accept it if that suits you. I've also put 1 timber in Smith House for your fire.

William, I'm home again. The Marshs need seed grain for Marsh Field before spring ends. I'll pay 1 coin a grain for up to 5. Also, you still owe us a day's reaping from last summer. We can take that at this year's harvest.

Highcombe had no seed and no timber; the Scarp is bare too. I still carry 7 coin. I'm trading 5 beans to Wat for 2 dried meat and sowing the rest of the beans in Marsh Field today. I've offered coin for seed grain to anyone. Burn dung in the hearth to save timber. Adam, take the cattle wherever there is grass, even onto Marsh Field's edges once it's sown. Ancel still owes us a plough and 6 timber.
Welcome home. I have no grain at all; I'm short of seed myself. I'll gladly give the day's reaping I owe you at this harvest. How much timber did you bring from Highcombe?

Father, we have food for one night. I've asked Osric to feed us in return for work. If he can't, I'll go to Ashby to my sisters for food, and that would be one mouth fewer here. The children eat first.

Mother, I'm hunting at the Scarp with you this morning. Our debts to the Marshs are settled: the plough was called off and its grain returned, and Gervase released the timber debt for 5 coin. We owe them nothing. I'll keep the grain for seed. I've asked Osric to feed us in return for work.

Mother, I'm hunting at the Scarp with you this morning. Our debts to the Marshs are settled: the plough was called off and its grain returned, and Gervase released the timber debt for 5 coin. We owe them nothing. I'll keep the grain for seed. I've asked Osric to feed us in return for work.
Could you lend me your copper tool for one day at Hill Field? I will hoe the Craggs' ground with it and count the work toward A199. I can give you a loaf of bread for the loan if you want it.

I have no copper tool to hoe with, since Ancel sold ours. I have asked Osric to lend his. Food is short at Smith House, so I am hunting and foraging the Scarp first today, and I will come to Hill Field with a tool if one is lent.

Ancel, the Smith store is down to about six meals of bread, flour and grain for six of us. Please go to the Scarp with me or help us find food. Keep the 2.4 grain for seed when the oats are reaped. The Marshs are still waiting on the plough and 6 timber you owe them; they asked that it come to Marsh House.
Thank you, Ancel. Yes, let us keep the grain for seed and hunt at the Scarp together. Thank you for settling the Marsh debts.
Hob, I owe you 3 grain by day 22 under A1197. I have no grain now, since my last 4 went to Osric's sowing. I will tell you when I have grain or can pay in bread from the Cragg store.

Ancel, do not go to Ashby yet. I am foraging and hunting at the Scarp again today for the Smith store, and the Craggs' oats will be ripe in about two days; I will reap them for the grain they owe us. Keep the children fed first, and bring any food you find into Smith House.

[Food] Day 18: the store holds 6 bread, 7 flour and 0.8 meat (about 16 meals), and 3.7 timber. The barley should be ripe about day 22: reap it with the copper tool, since I'm a master reaper. I owe Simkin 1 day of reaping at harvest. Osric will pay 4 coin for 6 grain by day 20. Simkin pays 1 coin a grain (O1188). The Alders are picked bare. Richolda half-ditched Reeve Field.

[Debts] Day 18: I paid Marsh House 2 bread for Richolda finishing the Reeve Field ditches. I owe Simkin (Marsh) 1 day of reaping at this year's harvest. A203 and A117 are settled. Osric will pay 4 coin for 6 grain by day 20.

[Plan] Day 18: last spring day tomorrow. Tried to dibble the last 5.1 beans into Marsh Field and fell at the Alders with the copper tool. Food: about 48 meals, about 6 nights. Timber 1.3; burn dung. We might slaughter a thin beast for meat. Ancel owes a plough and 6 timber. Wat owes 1 day (A858), Godiva 1 day (A807), William 1 day of reaping. Osric may give 4 oats at harvest.

[Debts] Ancel (Smiths, Highcombe) will bring a wooden plough and 6 timber by day 10. For that we pay 6 grain plus 12 grain at the deal, and 4 grain on delivery; the 2 coin I already paid counts against those 4 grain, so about 2 grain is left to pay. William owes us a day's reaping. Paid the Millers 2 grain for Agatha. Felice was paid 2 grain from my hands for a day's reaping. Wat's 2 bread settled the ox

[Winter food plan] Winter day 4. Smith House holds about 14 meals of bread and flour; six eat about 6 a night. Plan: bake flour into bread at the Smith House hearth, Stephen and Warin eat first. Grain (2.5) kept in store until 8 grain can be ground at the Craggs' hand mill. Osric owes 3 grain for reaping at Terrace Field. Declined William's bread-for-coin offer. Make a harness to trade for grain. Still needed: coppe

[Food] Spring 4: The store has about 10.7 bread after I gave the Smiths 4 (they were out of food), and 9.8 timber, roughly 3.5 days. The oats are ripe around spring 6 (summer 1): REAP with Hob (his 2 days), Avice (A199), Ancel and Lettice, and select seed. I owe Hob 3 grain by day 22 (A1197). Simkin asks for 4 oat seed. Ancel will work our fields in return for food. Wetham sells nothing. I carry 6 coin a

[Plan] Day 18: We owe the Marshs nothing (A304 released, plough called off). Osric gave 4 bread and asks for work in return; the Craggs have about 4 days of food. Their oats will be ripe about day 20; Hob and I will reap and get a share. There's no copper ore known here. The old wood over the scarp is unexplored and might have timber and game. The Scarp is bare. Keep the 2.4 grain for seed. Ashby is the

[Debts] I owe Joyce (Craggs) 3 grain. I hold 1 coin of Osric's to buy beans or barley for the Craggs. O178: I owe Simkin (Marsh) a wooden plough by day 10; he owes 2 more coin on delivery. O182: William (Reeve) owes me 8 grain by day 7 for a copper tool. Sold my other tool to Simkin for 4 coin. Make a new copper tool from the copper at the Smithy, then make the plough.
Yes, the Coles may use the Forge with us today. Bring what ore you have and I'll smelt it with ours. The copper tool will be shared with you and Gilbert, and stone is a fair return.
Keep the store tight. We owe Elena 3 grain at Millford, and I mean to carry it to her before harvest.
Good morning, Wat. I'd like to put some of our grain through your water mill today. Keep the customary share for the grinding, as always. Does that suit you?
Alard, may the Coles use the Forge to smelt and make a copper tool? We'll bring ore and share the tool's use, and can pay in stone.
Yes, Colin, that suits me. Bring your grain to the Mill and the customary share stays with the Millers, as always. Elena will be at the Mill while I am out at Willow Holt.
Thank you for the grinding yesterday, Wat. I've left 4 flour in Miller House as your share, in case Elena didn't keep it at the Mill. Tell me if that's short.
Fair, Nicol. A quarter to the Moors is agreed; I'm mining for the Moor store today as a start. Could we also use the Forge to make a copper tool, with our ore and a share of it for you?
I have made a crude tool and will try the Seam myself today. If you have a spare copper tool, lend it to me when you are done.

Drew, your people are mining our Seam and quarrying our Quarry. We're neighbours and I won't make a fight of it. But let's agree a fair share: say one part of every four you take goes to the Moor store, or you give us charcoal or timber when you have some. What do you say?

Drew, agreed: a quarter to the Moor store. The Coles may use the Forge for tools, with a share of the work or copper coming to us. Bring your own charcoal or timber, though; ours is gone. I'm going to Ashwood soon for charcoal. If you want some too, tell me.
Thank you, Colin. The 4 flour in Miller House is a fair share and I will count it as paid. Nothing is short.

Your North Field barley is ripe. I'm reaping it for the Reeds today; I'm the best reaper in the village. By harvest custom, will you pay me a share in grain? Say a tenth of what I cut, left at Barrow House.
Yes. Reap with us today. You, Beatrix and your mother will have your share of the North Field grain as at harvest.
Yes, Lettice. Reap today and you will have a fair share of the grain for your work, as at harvest.

I'm hungry and our store is empty. I'm foraging, then reaping North Field for the Reeds for a share of grain. If the Reeds will sell us grain for coin, please accept their offer if it is yours to make.
Thanks. I'm giving you 2 ore from today's mining as the Moors' share. I'll bring charcoal/timber from Ashwood when I can and then use the Forge.
I am reaping your barley in North Field today, two units. I would take a share of the grain for the work, as at harvest. Will you give it?
Thank you, Thurstan. That is a real kindness, and the Hales will remember it. I'm reaping for the Reeds to earn more grain, and I'll repay you when I can.
Thank you, Thurstan. That is a real kindness, and the Hales will remember it. I'm reaping for the Reeds to earn more grain, and I'll repay you when I can.
No need to repay me, Randal. Keep your household fed through the autumn and it will be repayment enough.

Reynold, you have my word: go to Coppergate. I've given you our copper tool, 4 coin and a bread. Mine ore or buy copper from the Coles and Moors, and take bread from the store for the road. I'm going to Barleyfield to reap for grain.
Yes, you may sleep here if you give 2 bread, and share your catch.
I'm Alice of the Bells from Millford. Our woods are spent, so I'm hunting and foraging in Deep Wood today. Could I sleep under your roof tonight? I'll share what I find, and I can pay in bread.
Thank you. I'm giving you my 0.8 bread now, and I'll bring you a share of whatever I catch today to make up the rest.

Ralf, we reap North Field together today. Bring any wild food or wood you find to Lowe Cottage. Ask Clement to pay our share in grain for our store, and keep the woodpile by the Granary in mind; it is nearly gone.

Father, I can't work for the Reed store as a Lowe, so I'm reaping North Field for myself and will give the Reeds a fair share of what I bring in. Lowe Cottage has no food; please send grain as you promised.
Thank you, Father. I'll repay it from the reaping.
Ralf, you and Beatrix have grain from the Lowe share now. Eat it before you go to the field.
I'll reap North Field for you today, which settles the day I owe you. I've offered you 1 day of work for 3 grain to take home to Hale House.

Thank you, Alard, we'll gladly stay. If it helps, you can have the handcart I have with me today, against a copper tool you owe me by day 9. I'll come back for it, or you can send it to Ashwood with Nicol.

Gilbert here. Our Cole store holds about 12.7 copper ore, enough to wait for your smelting. I will quarry stone today with the crude tool. When you can, the copper tool for the Seam work would help me most.
I am reaping for you in North Field today, as I owe you my day's work.
Father, I'm reaping North Field for my own household today, as agreed. Please let the grain I cut stay with Lowe Cottage, and send a share of the rest, as we have nothing to eat.

Market has been good for us, but we have no copper left to strike coin or make tools. I'd like to go to Coppergate by the Pass for copper ore: the seam is there, and the Coles and Moors know mining and smelting. Mining needs a copper tool, so I'd need to take one of ours or buy one. Can you spare a copper tool, or should we keep selling them? Tell me before I leave; I won't go without your word.
Understood. I'll mind the house with Cecily and won't go to Coppergate without your word. If copper or ore comes to market I'll buy it with coin.
I never got the copper tool from Adam, so I have only my crude tool. If you have a spare copper tool, lend it to me for the felling.
Our store is thin and the house has one free bed. Forage and hunt, and bring a share; I'll see what I can spare tonight.

Aldric, I have no bread left to pay you, only my labour. I will forage the Glade and hunt in Deep Wood today and bring you a share of whatever I catch before dark. Please let me sleep under your roof tonight on that promise.
Ralf, the beans are the Reeds' and go to the Reed store; the reapers take their fair share of grain or beans as at harvest. Reap Bean Field with care and keep the count with Ancel.
Ralf, I have sent 2 timber from the Reed store to Lowe Cottage for the hearth. Keep the grain you reap for Lowe, and bring the Reeds their fair share.
Alard, I'd like to watch you smelt or work copper at the Forge today, to learn it. I'll pay in ore or a share of copper.
Thank you. Take timber or charcoal back for the house and the Forge, and keep the Moors' share honest. I will keep the house and mine at the Seam.
Father, thank you for the grain. I'm helping reap Bean Field today; tell me how you wish the beans shared.
Ancel, I'm reaping Bean Field today. Please keep the count of what I cut, and I'll take my fair share, plus any spare timber for Lowe's hearth.
I'm reaping North Field today for my own household, since I can't use your store. I'll hand you back the Reeds' share of the barley afterwards, less the 4 grain we agreed for the day's work.

Bennet, this is my first day of the two I owe you. East Field is reaped, so I'm hoeing it ready for the winter sowing unless you'd rather have other work; just say. May I sleep and eat at Barrow House tonight? I have grain but no hearth to boil it.

Aldric, I owe you bread I no longer have. I am starving. Would you let me sleep under your roof tonight in return for two days' work from me, on your fields or in your wood? Whatever I forage today I will give you.

Aldric, I owe you bread I no longer have. I am starving. Would you let me sleep under your roof tonight in return for two days' work from me, on your fields or in your wood? Whatever I forage today I will give you.

Father, thank you for the grain; Lowe Cottage now has plenty but no timber, so the fire is out and we can't boil it. Could the Reeds spare 3 timber for 6 grain? I sent 8 grain to Reed House yesterday as repayment.
Beatrix, I am sending 3 timber from the Reed store to Lowe Cottage for the hearth. No need to repay it in grain; keep your grain for your own household and cook at home.
Our store holds about twenty meals now. Ralf and Beatrix look gaunt and Warin too; I suggest we share some grain with the Lowes at Lowe Cottage.

Well done with the bread. Tell Nicol he can take one handcart from our store as the one I owe the Moors for copper (agreement with Wilmot, due day 14). He can bring the copper when it's smelted. A second handcart only for a copper tool. A bed for Nicol is fine with me if Mother agrees.
Thank you. I will eat from the grain tonight. Bring timber back when you can; the fire takes half a timber a night.
Thank you, Cassandra. I will eat from the Merchant House store tonight and I have put my timber in to repair the house. Bring in your game and I will share what I find.

Aldric, I will hunt and forage in Deep Wood for your store today and sleep under your roof again if I may. I will go to Millford and bring you bread from the Bell to settle what I owe, and I will come back to work for the house.
Elena, here are the 3 grain you lent us last winter, with my thanks. Please count it paid.
Randal, agreed: if Thurstan reaps our oats, he gets a fair grain share from the store. I will reap South Field myself today.
Ancel, I'm here from Millford. Please pay the 3 grain you owe me (A31) today.
Florence, the handcart we owe the Moors under A624 is ready in our store. Will you carry it home today? Copper can come by day 14 as agreed. Has the charcoal reached you yet?
Yes, the cart Nicol gave you is the one owed under A624, so our side is done. Copper by day 14 is fine. If the Moors want a second cart, I'd trade it for a copper tool.
The Cole fire is out and we have only 0.2 timber. Please keep your share of the grain and do not burn the little timber we have on anything but the hearth.
The Coles still owe the Forge timber or charcoal. Drew and Wymarc are at Ashwood for it. I will bring what I can once it is back.
I've put my 1.3 timber into Cole House for tonight's fire. It's a gift, no ore needed. Once Drew and Wymarc are back from Ashwood, please send charcoal to the Forge as Katherine said.
Thank you, Daniel. I'll eat what I can and repay you in grain once our hearth is lit.
Understood, I'll keep my coin. Reap on. If Thurstan reaps our oats, he should be paid a fair grain share from the store.

Bennet of Barrow House paid me 4 grain for 3 coin, so about 1 coin per grain, and Ancel of Reed House gave grain freely. Folk there looked hungry (Beatrix, Lowe), so ask the Reeds and Barrows. Reaping there pays in grain.

Wat of the Millers from Millford. I came for timber, and Cassandra's copper felling tool did not reach me. Could you host me tonight in Ashe House, and if any copper felling tool is spare here, could I borrow it for a day or two? I will bring back timber for the Ashes' hearth or for Miller House, as we agree.

Aldric, the Glade is picked bare, so I will hunt Deep Wood with my crude weapon today instead. Whatever I catch I will bring to your house, and I am starving, so I ask to sleep under your roof tonight, and to eat from your store if you can spare it. I will settle what I owe from my catch.
I'll reap South Field oats today. A share of grain for Lowe Cottage would be welcome.
Thank you, Ysolt. I will eat the bread now. Please host me at Merchant House tonight if you can, and I will pay you back when I can reach home.
Thurstan, thank you for reaping South Field with us. Randal and I agree you will have a fair grain share from the Hale store for your work. Come to Hale House and I will see to it.
The Hales' oats in South Field must be cut today or lost. I'm reaping there for the Hales, and I ask for grain in return.
Good plan. I'll stay, hunt and forage for the children and keep timber up. Remember the Moors are owed a handcart by day 14.
Ysolt here. I have put 2 bread in your hands for nothing; eat it now, and come to Merchant House tonight if you have nowhere warm to sleep.
I am giving you 2 more bread now, for nothing; you need no coin. Come to Merchant House tonight: there is a bed and a meal there for you. Eat the bread today, not later.

Peter, I'm starving. I came back from reaping at Barleyfield with nothing but grain. If you can spare one dried meat, I'll repay you with the first copper tool I make once Reynold brings copper, or in grain now if you'd rather.
Gilbert, I am giving the Coles 10 grain from the Moor cellar for the winter. Bring the copper ore to the Forge when you can.

Aldric, Deep Wood gave me nothing yesterday and the game is thin. Today I will forage Deep Wood and the Glade for whatever wild food is left and bring it to your house. I still owe you for last night, and I ask again to sleep under your roof tonight.
Glad you're home. Keep to 7 meals. I'll reap the rye with Clement, and we can share a little grain with the Lowes from the harvest if you agree.

Thank you, Beatrix and Philippa. But the Barrows have plenty of grain. What we lack is fire: no timber for two nights, so we can't cook it, and Father and I are starving. Clement, Philippa, will you let Thurstan and me sleep at Reed House tonight and cook our own grain at your hearth? Or sell me timber: I have 16 coin, and my offers are open. Anyone hungry may have Barrow grain in return.

Christian is starving, so I've sold two bread for 4 coin, as Peter asked us to share with the hungry. I'm taking a dried meat and going to Deep Wood in Ashwood to hunt, since Willow Holt is bare. I'll bring back any game I catch.
I am going to Ashwood with 3 copper ore for timber and food. Keep the fire small and share the grain store fairly. Ask Alard for help as well.

Alard, thank you for the bed and the meal. My ore still needs fuel to smelt: could you give me 5 timber from the Moor store, or let me take it from the Forge woodpile? In return I'll work two days for the Moors on whatever you need, and I'll smelt my 1 copper ore beside you and Wilmot at the bellows.

Millford: Annora is dead of hunger, and we must not lose anyone else. The Merchant store has bread and dried meat, and I will share it with the hungry, the children and the sick first. Bring whatever game or wild food you find to Merchant House. Speak to me if you are starving.

I cannot sell you bread for coin, Christian. Coin cannot feed anyone now, and our bread goes first to children and the sick. Tell me who in your household is most in need, and bring any game, wild food or timber you find to Merchant House; I will share what we have with them.
Thank you, Elias, but the Merchants have no grain to spare, and we have timber enough. If you bring game or wild food to Merchant House, I will see it is shared out fairly.

Here is one dried meat for you, Adam. Bring your grain to the Merchant store when you can, since winter is near and the stores must hold. The first copper tool you make can come later, once Reynold has the copper.
Father, I'm reaping rye beside you at Rest Field. I'll give you what you need for seed and keep a share for the Lowes, as you promised.

Good news about the grain. I am trading 4 of it to Elias for 3 timber for our winter fire, and I have given Christian one bread from our store. Annora's grain did come into the Smithy, and the Lowes are still owed 2 timber, which I have stored for them.
Agreed: you rest a day, then we go to Coppergate for copper. I gave Christian one bread before I heard your word, so the house store has one less. I will not give more bread away.
Thank you, Philippa. I will sleep by your hearth at Reed House and cook my grain there. Bennet and I will share the cost of the fire with you if the Barrow coin can buy timber.

Yes, you may sleep at Merchant House and eat from our store tonight, for nothing. I have given you one loaf for the road to Barleyfield. Go to Barleyfield, not back to Ashwood, and eat before you walk.

Ysolt here. Merchant House has about 11 grain and 4 beans in its store. Could the Mill grind some of it for us this week, and what share do you keep for the grinding? We will bring the grain to the Mill when you say.
Thank you, Peter. I'll remember the dried meat and repay you with the first copper tool.

Aldric, Florence died in the night, and the wood and the Glade are bare. I will hunt Deep Wood once more today, then go to Millford to take bread from the Bell's store and bring bread back to you to settle my debt. I am sorry I cannot stay to share the work. Thank you for your roof.

Aldric, Florence died in the night, and the wood and the Glade are bare. I will hunt Deep Wood once more today, then go to Millford to take bread from the Bell's store and bring bread back to you to settle my debt. I am sorry I cannot stay to share the work. Thank you for your roof.
Go safe. Take the grain and coin, and bring back as much timber as you can carry, including Bennet's share. Eat the grain only if you can cook it.

Ysolt, it is winter now and I have only 1 bread and 2 coin. Could you host me at Merchant House again tonight and feed me from your store? I will work for Merchant House for two days, in return for the bread, before I leave for Barleyfield. Thank you for everything you have done.
Bennet, I am sorry for Thurstan. I have sent 8 grain to the Barrows. We have no timber to spare; Ancel goes to Millford for timber from the Merchants, and you may pay him your coin for a share.
Dionisia, yes: grind your 8 grain at the Reed hand mill today. You owe nothing back; take the flour to Hale House.

Clement, the Hale store has grain for only about two nights. May I grind 8 grain at your hand mill at Reed House today? I will leave the flour in Hale House's store and pay you back in work after the winter.
Clement, Philippa: Dionisia of the Hales asks leave to grind 8 grain at your hand mill today, for our store. We will pay it back in work.

Aldric, I am Gilbert of the Coles, hungry and without a bed tonight. I have 3 copper ore to offer. Would the Ashes host me for a night and share the fire and food? I will work for it tomorrow if you need hands.
Accepted, Elias: 2 bread for 4 timber. Eat your share tonight, and bring back whatever game you take to Merchant House.

Alard, it is cold and I have had no meal since yesterday. Could you let me sleep at Moor House and feed me from its store tonight? I'll pay you back with work at the Forge, or with my share of the smelting when charcoal comes.

Alard, it is cold and I have had no meal since yesterday. Could you let me sleep at Moor House and feed me from its store tonight? I'll pay you back with work at the Forge, or with my share of the smelting when charcoal comes.
Peter, I'm repairing Merchant House for you today, toward what I owe for the dried meat. If you count it as more than that, a little bread or meat for my house would help, but there's no need.
I'm going to Millford with harness, charcoal and coin to buy bread and flour. Back in two days. Keep the hearth lit and share the grain.
Yes, I'll come home with you tonight. I have no food left, so please let me eat from your share on the road. I'll put my 6 timber on the handcart.
Wat, could the Mill grind our Smith House grain into flour? We have about 12 grain. Tell me your share and I will bring the grain to the Mill.
Good. Here's my last bit of dried meat, and I'll share whatever I forage at the Glade. Load your timber on the cart. At home we'll eat porridge from our grain and mend the house.

Randal, the Hale store has 7.9 meals of flour and no timber, so the fire stays out. Please share the flour carefully: the children first, then the rest of us. I will forage Brook Meadow and ditch Brook Field today.
Daniel, the flour is in Hale House's store. Please take your share each night and tell me if you feel worse.

Go to Millford with your harness and buy what bread and flour you can. I'm holding two harnesses here to trade for bread or grain at Ashwood, so keep yours for Millford. Keep the hearth lit at Ashe House, and share the grain evenly; Alice and the children first.
Elias, eat from the Merchant store tonight; Ysolt will feed you. Don't sell your last food for timber. We will share bread with the hungry first.
Thank you, Adam. The repair counts toward what you owe for the dried meat, so we are square. Keep your own house fed first; I will send bread to the hungry from the batch I bake today.

Wat: our bread is down to about 1 and the grain is 4.9 in Miller House. Please bake from the Mill's flour when you can, and keep the hearth to the cold nights only. I am hunting and foraging today for what I can bring in.

Amice, Wymarc here. The Coles have no timber left and my fire at home is out. Could you let me sleep at Ashe House tonight? I will share the wild food I gather. I will take word of timber back to Coppergate in the morning.

Sibyl, the house grain is all gone and I missed my meal last night. Are you carrying any? We have 1.4 timber left. If we have no grain, I think I should go to Barleyfield. Bennet owes me a bed and I owe him a day's work, and the farms have grain.
Peter, our house store is empty of food and I'm hungry. Can you spare a bread? When Reynold brings copper, I'll give you a copper tool or strike coin for you in return.

Mother says she left 8 grain in the store, but the store now holds no food at all, so I fear someone took it. If either of you has grain in hand, put it back in the store. I'm hunting Willow Holt. If we're still empty tomorrow, I'll go to Barleyfield to work for grain, since Bennet owes me a bed there.

I've put about 13 timber in the house store for the fire, and 1.8 dried meat from the Store (about 5 meals). There's 0.7 bread left in the Store too. Ashwood is bare, and the Millers won't sell grain. I'm hunting the Holt today. Christian owes us 5 grain at Barleyfield, and the Barleyfield farms may sell grain for coin, so one of us should go there soon.
Lettice, the flour is in Hale House's store. Take your share tonight; you are gaunt and must eat. I am foraging the Common today.
Piers, the store holds about 11 meals for us three. Please eat from it tonight and keep the fire lit. Let us share what we find, and I will hunt in Deep Wood with you.

Joyce, I am sending 3 grain to Ashe House from the Fenn store. It is all we can spare, since we have about 11 meals for three of us for the last days. If you find any game or wild food, please bring a share to Fenn House. I need no timber.

The Ashe store has no food left and Amice, Basilia and I are hungry. If the Fenns have any grain, meat or wild food to spare, please bring it to Ashe House. I can give timber in return if you need it.
Thank you for the grain. If I catch anything I'll bring a share to Fenn House as well.
Thank you. I'll take my share of the flour tonight. I'm foraging the Common now and will bring the wild food to the Hale store.

Piers, Nicol Moor here. Elias owes me a handcart (A624, due by day 14). I've already paid the copper into Fenn House. Can you or Rose hand it to me today? My home fire is out and I need the cart to haul timber. I'll also trade my spare copper tool for charcoal or timber.
Rose, Nicol Moor here. The Fenns owe me a handcart for the copper I left in Fenn House. Could you give it to me today? I also have a spare copper tool to trade for timber or charcoal.
Adam, I have given you our last 0.7 bread for your house tonight. Eat it, and repay us when copper or coin comes your way; the repair already counted toward your debt for the dried meat.
Reed House has no fire tonight and 0.2 timber. I'll pay 10 grain for 3 timber, and anyone who brings timber to our hearth gets bread or flour in return.
Rohese here, starving. Store at home under four nights of food. Share any bread you get; I carry 12 timber and a handcart to trade.

Home store was about 13 grain, 1.7 dried meat and 23 timber when I left, so under four nights of food. Jordan and Piers are foraging and hunting and keeping the fire, and Rose is with them. I have 12 timber and a handcart. I'm coming to Barleyfield with you. Please share a little bread if you can, I'm starving.
Sibyl, we go to Barleyfield tonight. Bennet owes me a bed at Barrow House, and we can work for grain and timber there. Leave the house grain for Mother. Come with me at nightfall.
Agreed. We eat at home tonight and leave for Barleyfield together tomorrow at nightfall. We'll ask the Barrows and Reeds for grain and timber, and Bennet owes me a bed.

Bennet, Ysolt told me at Millford she cannot sell timber, since her house needs it for its own fire. I will not walk there for nothing. Ralf has my offer of 6 grain for his 3 timber at Lowe Cottage; I will go to Lowe Cottage for it. I am grinding grain at our hand mill today.

Mother, I'm taking 10 timber and my coin to Barleyfield to buy grain. Christian owes us 5 grain there too. That leaves 11 timber at home, enough for the fire for 5 nights. Please eat the beans and flour sparingly. I'll be back with the cart in two or three days.
Randal, I'm foraging the Common this morning for Hale House, then finishing my hoeing at Rest Field for the Reeds. Eat the flour from the store tonight; we will not refuse Bennet's gift.
I'm foraging the Glade with my two units and will put all the wild food into the Ashe store. Please keep Amice fed first. I'll bring a share to Fenn House as I promised Jordan.
I have no bread or grain on me yet. I'll put what I forage into the Ashe store today. If Ashe House has grain to spare after Jordan's gift, I'll offer you a harness for timber.

Rohese, Nicol Moor here. Elias owes me a handcart (A624, due by day 14). I've already paid the copper. If you've brought one back, please let me have it. I've also put up an offer: my spare copper tool for another handcart, if you'll take it.
I'm giving you the handcart now against Elias's debt A624. Please release it. I'll make another cart soon and we can talk about the copper tool then.
Cecily, Jocelin is starving and the Bell's fire is out. Could you host him at Smith House tonight, and feed him from your store if you can spare it? I will repay what I can when I have food.
Daniel, I'm giving you flour: eat it raw, rest, and share with Lettice.
Smith House is open to anyone who is cold or hungry tonight. I have 6 grain to share, and I need 4 timber for the fire.

Ysolt, I am starving and have no food but 2.9 flour. Could you host me at Merchant House tonight, and feed me from your store if you can? I owe you the two days' work (A1269); I will do what I can of it here before I go home, and I will bring grain for Colin when I next come to Millford.
Agreed, Ysolt. I am foraging Riverside Meadow for the Merchant store today and will count it toward the two days I owe you. Please keep a bed for me tonight if you can.

Ralf, I've traded my timber to Bennet for grain, but I'll pay coin for flour: 3 coin for 2 flour, up to 4 flour. The offer is open now. Also, tell Christian I'll collect the 5 grain he owes me next time.
Bennet, I am going to Millford with my coin to find timber for the Reeds. If I cannot buy any, I will bring back your share of the coin.
Grandfather, I will bring back whatever the Holt gives. Please share the flour with Cassandra and Ysolt first, and take your turn at the fire only if you are warm enough.
Eat your share from the store first tonight, and keep warm by the hearth. I'm hunting and felling in Deep Wood for meat and wood.
Thank you. Any meat either of us catches, we'll share between Ashe and Fenn houses. I'm hunting and felling in Deep Wood now.
Gillian, thank you. Share the flour as Ysolt counts it, and eat first from the store tonight. Bring the Holt's catch to the store, not to your own hands.
Christian, you owe me 2 days of work under our agreement. Please gather forage at Riverside Meadow today and put what you find into the Merchant House store. That pays me, and it feeds the house.

Basilia, yes, come to Moor House tonight and sleep by the hearth; we will feed you from the store. Keep your copper tool for now; the charcoal trade stands, and you can give the copper tool to the household if you wish. Accept my offer when you can.
Thank you. I've given a harness to the Reed household in return, and I'll come to the hearth tonight. I'll bring timber from Ashwood when I can.

Alard, I have no charcoal now. Nicol took that offer yesterday, so I can't accept O1758 and won't take your grain for nothing. I'm starving and have only 1.9 raw grain. Could you host me at Moor House by the hearth tonight so I can boil it? I'll give you my copper tool, and I'll burn charcoal for the Moors once I have timber.

Ysolt, I am foraging Willow Holt for the Merchant store today, toward the two days I owe you. I am starving and have only 2.9 flour of my own. Could you host me at Merchant House tonight and feed me from the store? Tomorrow I will go home to Barleyfield for grain and flour and come back with it.

Colin, I have no grain on me, only 2 coin and 2.9 flour, so I cannot pay you today. The grain is in the Barrow store at home. I will fetch 5 grain from there and leave it at Merchant House, as you asked. I owe you that and will not forget it.
Bennet, yes: you may sleep in Reed House tonight, and eat from our store. Keep your timber and flour for the Barrows' fire. Your 8 grain from me is a gift; pay later only if you can.
Christian, you owe me 5 grain for the 2 timber I gave you. Since you're here in Millford, please give it to me or leave it at Merchant House today. My family is starving.

Mother, I've put it all in the Merchant House store: 12.7 grain, 1.9 flour and 6 timber. That's about 10 meals with the porridge. Please share it out and keep the hearth lit. I also hold 31 coin. Christian owes us 5 grain. Please tell Gillian and Peter.

Mother, I've put it all in the Merchant House store: 12.7 grain, 1.9 flour and 6 timber. That's about 10 meals with the porridge. Please share it out and keep the hearth lit. I also hold 31 coin. Christian owes us 5 grain. Please tell Gillian and Peter.
Thank you for the timber. I'm making a harness from our hide now. It's yours if the Fenns can use it, and I'll keep the offer open in return for any food you can spare.
Thank you, Rohese. I will bring you half of any meat I catch, and I will repay the rest with timber once I am home.

Colin's grain is in the Merchant store: about 12.7 grain, 2.6 flour, about 11 timber. Eat porridge from the grain at the hearth, one meal each, flour for the children first, and count it with me tonight. Christian owes us 5 grain.
Nicol, I have given you 1 copper to pay Elias Fenn of Ashwood for the handcart debt, which is overdue since day 14. Pay him when you go to Ashwood, and bring back timber or charcoal if you can.
Philippa, thank you and Clement for keeping me alive through the winter. Spring is here, so I'll sow our fields now. When the Barrows have a harvest, the Reeds will have a share of it.

Ysolt, I am foraging Riverside Meadow for the Merchant store today toward the two days I owe you. Then I am going home to Barleyfield for grain and flour, and I will bring Colin's grain and come back to work off the rest.

I'm back with flour. 10 of it is in the store now, so feed everyone from it. Barleyfield is starving for timber and has grain. Tomorrow I'll load the handcart with about 14 timber and take it there by way of Millford to trade for grain. Keep at least 8 timber here for the fire. Is there any word from the Moors about the copper they owe us?
Son, while I'm gone, fell timber in Deep Wood when you can. Timber is what feeds us now, because Barleyfield and Millford pay grain and flour for it.
I'm foraging the Glade today, since Deep Wood is bare. Anything I find will be shared with Fenn House as I promised, and I'll bring it to Ashe House first for Amice. Thank you for the timber.
Agreed. Ashe House first for Amice, then I'll share the rest with Fenn House.

Father, that debt is already paid. Elias's copper was paid long ago, Rohese gave me the cart on winter day 4, and nobody owes anything now. I'll use your copper for a tool to trade at Ashwood for timber and charcoal.
Thank you. Bring what you find to Ashe House first, as you planned. I'll share mine with Fenn House.

Alard, our copper debt to Elias Fenn of Ashwood (1 copper, due day 14) is overdue. The Moor store has 2 copper. I will smelt the Forge ore today and we can send one copper with Nicol the next time he goes to Ashwood.

Spring has come. The Merchant store has about 6 grain, 2.6 flour and 7 timber. Anyone of the Bell who is still living, come to Merchant House and eat at the hearth tonight; we will share what we have.
Christian, bring back the grain you owe us, and then we will call the work owed settled.

Mother, Elias is already paid. That debt was settled on winter day 4, so keep your copper to trade. I'm coming to Ashwood with you tonight with the handcart, and we'll fell at Deep Wood together. The cart carries 40 on the track, so we can bring a lot home.
Bennet, thank you. Reap what is ripe at North Field and bring the grain to Reed House; I will take it in and it is yours to share as you agreed.
I have no grain with me, only flour and a little coin. Bring the timber to Lowe Cottage when you can and I'll pay in Barleyfield grain or flour then.
Thank you, Jordan. Yes, let us share what we find. I have a copper tool and will fell timber and forage for both houses as I can. I am starving myself.
Christian, the last timber is gone. Take the handcart, coin and flour to Millford for timber as soon as you can. I'm reaping the Reeds' rye for a tenth share.

Grandmother, Elias says Barleyfield has rye and grain for timber, or some for coin, and that Durand of the Reeds had coin and rye. The store has about 3 timber and 6 coin. I will not send any timber without your word; tell me if you want coin sent with Elias instead, or a little timber.
Basilia, I am sorry about Amice and Joyce. I will repair Ashe House today, and we will share what meat or forage we find between our two houses.
Ralf, I am sorry about Beatrix. She was my daughter and she worked hard for the Lowes to the end. Come to Reed House and eat from our store whenever you need to; the Reeds will share what we have.
Thank you, Bennet. I'll remember it and repay you in grain or flour when I can.
Thank you, Bennet. I'll remember it and repay you in grain or flour when I can.
Thank you, Philippa. I grieve for Beatrix too. I'll come to Reed House if we run short, and I'll repay the Reeds.
Rohese, I am Wilmot of the Moors and I am starving here with nothing in hand. Could the Fenns host me tonight at Fenn House? I will fell timber at Deep Wood for you in return where I can.

Clement, I grieve for Philippa. I've put the 65.7 rye I owed into Reed House. I'll reap the rest of North Field today before it's lost, give you nine tenths tonight and keep my tenth, as Philippa and I agreed.
Ralf, the Lowes are welcome to sleep at Barrow House if your fire is out too. Bring what food you have and we'll share it.

The Store repair needs timber, and I have only 0.4 in Smith House's store. If you bring 2 timber to the Store I will repair it. Otherwise I will count my owed days as foraging or hunting for the Merchants, if you tell me which.
Bennet, thank you. Philippa and I valued your word. Reap North Field, and give the Reeds their nine tenths as agreed.
I'm going home to Millford tonight with the timber to trade it for flour. You're gaunt: come home soon and eat from the store. I'll keep your share safe.

Clement, Bennet has 6 timber and the Reeds get the other 8. I've offered you 8 timber for 16 grain, a cheaper rate. Accept it today and the timber goes straight into the Reed store for your hearth. I'm leaving a crude weapon at Reed House as a gift as well.
Cecily, I have forgiven the two days' work you owed me, so you need not work for it. Come to Merchant House if you are hungry; Ysolt will count what we have.
Grandmother, the store has no food left. I am foraging and hunting at Willow Holt and will bring anything back. Cecily is starving and I have forgiven her debt to me.
Basilia, I have sent you 1 grain. We are baking bread at the Fenn hearth today; I will bring you a share once it is baked.
Cecily, the flour I offered is gone from the store, so I cannot give it. I release you from the work you owed for it. Forage with us if you can, and bring whatever you find to the Merchant store.
Cecily, I will not spend timber on the Store repair, since the fire needs what we have. Your debt to me is released. Forage or hunt for the Merchant store instead, and bring it in at once.

Clement, my gift to the Reeds failed yesterday, so I'm settling it now: 101.4 rye into Reed House. That's your nine tenths of everything I reaped on days 3 and 4. I already used my own tenth to buy timber. If Reed House needs fire, I have a little timber to spare.

Christian, it's good to have you home. Elias sold us timber, so we have about 13 now and the fire is lit. You weed West Field and I'll weed East Field. Settle your debts with Wymarc and Ysolt when you can. The barley should be ripe around day 7.

Christian, it's good to have you home. Elias sold us timber, so we have about 13 now and the fire is lit. You weed West Field and I'll weed East Field. Settle your debts with Wymarc and Ysolt when you can. The barley should be ripe around day 7.

I am back from Millford with no timber; Ysolt and Ralf had none to spare. I will weed West Field today and forage at Brook Meadow for the store. I am eating my flour tonight, and the Barrow store has flour and food enough. I still owe Wymarc 1 meat and Ysolt 2 days' work, and I will go to Coppergate and Millford when I can.

Elias: the Reeds accept your 8 timber for 16 grain. Bring it into the Reed store in Reed House, and the grain is yours when it is in. Bennet, your nine tenths of North Field's reaping are owed to the Reeds.
Bennet, thank you for the rye and for settling the Reeds' share. If you can spare 2 timber, I have offered you my 4 coin for it; please accept it, and put the timber into Reed House for the hearth.

Colin, I won't sell flour for timber or coin. Ashwood has plenty of timber, and coin won't feed anyone right now. I'm giving you 2 flour as a gift so you can eat. I'll take the rest to Fenn House tonight, and Cassandra will share it with my family there.
Grandmother, I will bring every scrap of wild food to the store for your count. I will not take timber or coin out without your word.

Alard, I have put my 2.5 timber into the Moor store for the hearth tonight. Please cook grain at the hearth for the house and eat your share; I am taking a copper tool from the store to mine at the Seam.

[Winter day 5 food count] Merchant store: about 3.6 flour, 0.7 bread (Store), 9.1 timber, 16.2 hay, 3 crude tools, 1 pack. Household eats about 4 meals a night, so food lasts about one night. Fire takes 2 timber a night, so timber lasts about 4 nights. Keep at least 8 timber. Colin is at Barleyfield with the handcart, 10 timber and coin, expected back in 2 or 3 days. Christian owes me 2 days' work (A1269). Riverside Meadow

[Plans] Spring day 5: Home at Millford and starving, carrying 9.8 timber and 31 coin. Offering timber and coin for flour, grain and bread. Cassandra stayed at Fenn House in Ashwood. Ralf pays 2 flour for 1 timber; Durand pays 6 coin or rye for 3 timber. Nicol sells a copper tool for 10 timber, and grain at 5 for 2 bread. Cecily owes me 2 days' work (A2009). Christian owes 5 grain. Deep Wood fells 4.9 timb

[Food] Winter day 4: Sibyl and I left for Barleyfield at nightfall. I took 2 grain, and Cecily keeps about 4 in the store and guards it. Bennet owes me a bed, and I owe him 1 day on A678. We need grain and timber from the Barrows and Reeds. We owe Peter Merchant a copper tool or coin. Reynold is still at Coppergate.

[Lowe timber debt] Annora Lowe gave 4 grain into the Smithy (autumn day 4) for 2 timber; she promised 4 more grain on delivery. Annora has since died. The 2.2 timber I felled at Ashwood is moved into the Smith House store (autumn day 5) for the Lowes to carry back to Lowe Cottage, Barleyfield. Settle with Ralf or Beatrix Lowe when they come; I still owe nothing else.

[Plan] Spring d5: I settled with the Reeds: 101.4 rye (90% of days 3-4), so I owe them nothing on North Field now. Barrow House has about 13 timber and its fire is lit; Christian is home. Elias will bring more timber from Ashwood. East and West Fields are barley, ripe around day 7: reap them then (I'm a master reaper). The Granary holds 11.5 grain. I owe kindness to the Reeds and Elias. Ralf (Lowe) is fe

[Plan] Winter day 3: I was stuck in Millford for a night over the weight limit; each timber weighs 2, so 10 weight means 4 timber at most, less with food. I gave Ralf 3 timber for Lowe Cottage. I'm walking home with 3 timber. Ysolt gives 2 timber for 1 grain. Elias comes to Barleyfield with timber and a handcart: host him and tell Bennet. I still owe the Barrows timber or their 6 coin back. Durand is in

[Debts and timber] Owe Wymarc (Cole) 1 meat, in arrears. Owe Ysolt (Merchant) 2 days' work (A1269). Timber: none to buy at Millford this trip; Colin of the Merchants offered 2 timber for 5 grain earlier. Barrow fire needs timber; Willow Holt has no standing timber.

[Debts and promises] Owed by me: hoe the last 1.5 plots of Brook Field for the Hales; reap South Field for the Hales. Ancel's day is paid. Hale store about 30 grain; giving 4 to the Lowes after the oats, as Randal agreed. Rye seed needed before winter.

[Food plan, spring day 1] Ashe store is nearly empty (0.2 grain, 1.7 hide, 0.8 timber). Deep Wood has given nothing for days. I am foraging the Glade, the nearest ground not yet picked bare. Promised: share food with Fenn House (Jordan, Piers). Owed: a share of any food to Fenn House. Harness needs 2 timber per make; hide 1.7 is enough once timber is in. Keep Amice fed first.

[Plan] Day 20: at Millford with 19.6 flour, 9.1 rye and 3.8 grain on the cart. Home on day 21; share food with the Fenns and the Ashes (Amice is starving). Barleyfield badly wants timber (2 flour a timber), so bring another cartload soon, to Reed House (Clement/Avice: 10 grain for 3 timber). Fenn store has ~23 timber. The Moors (Florence) owe 1 copper (A624).
[Handcart owed] Settled on winter day 4: Rohese gave me the handcart for A624, which I released. I keep the cart (weight 0, 40 on cart tracks). Rohese may make another cart for a copper tool later.

[Autumn plan] Autumn day 2: about 15 meals and 2.7 timber in Cole House. Food is thin; grain (21 lots) is our main store. Timber comes only from Ashwood. Trade copper ore for timber with Elias Fenn, or take 3 ore to Ashwood myself. Christian of the Barrows still owes 1 meat (arrears).

Gorse Bank is bare, so we must find food. Tomorrow I'll offer my work in the Long Field for a share of grain. If the Hearnes say no, we forage at Mill Mead. I'd rather not try for a child until the stores are fuller.
Gorse Bank is picked bare. We newcomers need food. Who in the Long Field will take a day's work from us for a share of grain?
Rob and I agree: tomorrow we seek paid work, hay at Mill Mead or a field share, and keep the grain for food.
Agreed. No child yet. You ask the Hearnes about Long Field work; I'll ask at Mill Mead for hay work, and we'll share what we earn.

Piers worked on the wheel at the Mill House today. My offer to him failed, so tomorrow I'll make a proper deal and pay him 3 grain and 1 coin for today. Mary of the Newcomes was foraging and cutting hay on Mill Mead for her people. Odo, should we let them cut there for a share, or tell them to stop? Odo, what did the wheel need when you looked at it?
Newcomers here: we'll cut hay or reap for a share of grain, a day's work for a fair measure. Ask at Mill Mead or the Long Field.
Mary can cut on Mill Mead for a fair share of grain; I would rather be paid than refuse. I will look at the wheel first thing and tell you exactly what it still needs.

Hugh: I did not see the wheel today. Tomorrow I walk to Mill Garth first and report what it needs. On Mill Mead, I say let the Newcomes cut for a share of grain, as Mary offered; the meadow is ours to lend.

Hugh: I did not see the wheel today. Tomorrow I walk to Mill Garth first and report what it needs. On Mill Mead, I say let the Newcomes cut for a share of grain, as Mary offered; the meadow is ours to lend.
Good, hoe the Long Field. Go easy on the grain; forage when you can.
Night all. Tomorrow I'll cut young growth at Gorse Bank for firewood. Go easy on the grain; forage when you can.
Good, Odo. Tell us what the wheel needs and I will carry timber or lend a hand at Mill Garth tomorrow.

Piers: I've put up an offer of 6 coin and 18 grain. That is 5 more days on the mill wheel, plus pay for the day you already put in. Accept it and carry on. Mary: the Newcomes may cut hay on Mill Mead for a share of grain, but ask me or Odo first.
Weeded all day. Tom is at Holm Wood; we reap soon. Keep the fire in and share what we have. Tomorrow I will seek grain work or help reap.
Good. I'll cut my share on Mill Mead and hand it to the Hall store. Whatever Hugh pays for what's over her two days, we'll put it in the Newcome store.
Put your firewood in the camp store so it's there for the cold nights. Tomorrow I'll take the hay I cut to the Hall, and then we'll ask Hugh whether the debt is square.
I'm at Mill Mead cutting hay too, per Hugh's word. Together we should clear the debt quickly and then ask for grain.

Wat the mason: our cottage roof fell in last night. I need timber and will pay in firewood, cut stone or mason work. Hugh, your hall cracked too. I'll mend it, or lay stone for the leat, in return for shelter and grain. Name your price.
I'm hungry and have nothing to carry, so I'll weed the Long Field today rather than walk to Holm Wood. If you bring back game or wild food, please keep a share for me.
I'm sleeping on the floor by the hearth again. If there's any food left, I'd be grateful for a share in the morning.

Odo, I traded Wat for the stone myself, and it went into the wall. Alys says the Hall is mended and sound, so leave it. Tomorrow go to Mill Garth, check that Piers works the days he owes on A127 and A161, and tell me. Alys, help Piers on the leat, since more hands shorten the work. I'll see to Ellen's day and the hay.
Rob: I have no timber, but I carry 9 firewood. Let's share a fire with it tonight. Tomorrow I'll hunt and fell timber, and can help Wat with the camp.
Rob, Tom, Will: if any of you has timber for a fire tonight, we can share it. Up to four can sleep by one fire. Tomorrow I'll fell timber and build a camp. Anyone who helps can sleep there.

[Mill wheel] Summer day 4: Piers the wright says he knows wheel and leat work. His rate is 3 grain and 1 coin a day, and he asked 15 grain and 5 coin for 5 days. He worked on the wheel at the Mill House on day 4 without a deal; I owe him for that day. The offer format must be plain goods, e.g. give '3 grain' get 'work 1 days', or a fixed total. Mary of the Newcomes cut hay and foraged on Mill Mead (ours) on da

[Plan] Deal with Hugh: 3 grain + 1 coin a day, through O100. A127 and A161 are owed (2 days). Each day I work the wheel at the Mill House: each build is 2 units, so 3 builds a day, with the spare unit for a repair or for speaking. About 130 units were left on day 8, and no materials are needed. Repair Wright's House first whenever it is damaged. Teach the craft only after the wheel turns, for about 10 co

I'd like us to ask the Masons for one stone for a fire ring at the camp, offering a day's work in return rather than grain. Will you come with me to the Quarry once I've foraged? I'll keep my grain for now.
Rob of the Newcomes: I'll work a day for the Masons in return for one stone for our fire ring. Wat, will you take that?
Alys here, near my time and short of food. If either of you has a fire or can spare a bite, I'd be glad of it; I'll share what I forage tomorrow.
Thank you, Rob. I'll gladly share your fire. I have a little wild food to put in. Will, I'll likely walk home with you tomorrow, since my time is near.

Odo, the Hall store had no stone from Wat's 18, only the 3 I bought today. Did O90 go through, or does Wat still owe it? The Hall repair needs 7 stone, so we need about 27 in all. Was Piers working on the Hall today? I didn't agree a wage with him.

The Hall repair needs 7 stone, not timber; we have 20 timber in the store. Please find out whether Wat owes us the 18 stone from O90, and get it to the Mill House. Felling timber at Holm Wood for the wheel is still the best use of your days.
Wat, you have grain: put it in the store and let's cook it at the hearth with the firewood by the door, and share it. Tomorrow I'll ask the Hall or Wright's House for a roof for the birth.
Mary: the stone is in my hands. I'm working today at Gorse Bank, next to the Quarry, to pay Wat the day I owe him under A96. Hold the camp fire for tonight, and we will talk on your return.
I've a fire lit and some meat. Alys, Will, come share it and the warmth.
Yes, Joan, the grain goes in the store and we share it. Tomorrow you ask the Hall or Wright's House to take us in, and I'll get Piers to mend the roof.

Will here: I have 3 firewood and nothing to cook on. Rob, Alys, if you bring any dry sticks we can share a small fire tonight and cook your grain and meat before they spoil. I walk home to Wenbridge in the morning.
Will: thank you, Rob. I'll come to the fire and share the warmth. Alys, I'll sit by you. My three firewood stays with me for home.
Mary of the Newcomes: Wat, I'm here to repair your roof for the day I owe you under our agreement.

Hugh: The Mill House has 3 stone. I accepted O156 for 9 stone at 6 grain, so that is 12 with the 3 you bought; O90 still shows 3 lots (9 stone) open and I am asking Wat whether it is still owed. The Hall needs 7 stone, so we are 15 short of 27 until Wat delivers. I will repair the Hall with you this morning and then leave for Holm Wood tonight to fell timber.

Odo here: Wat, I have taken O156, 9 stone for 6 grain. Please bring it to the Mill House. My O90 still shows 3 lots open; please say whether that stone is still owed to us, because the Mill House has only 3 stone.

Wat: Odo, a trade moves both ways at once or not at all. Piers got 9 stone, Hugh 3. If you got no stone, you paid no grain, so nothing is owed. I've withdrawn those offers and I'm quarrying fresh stone for the mill today, 1 grain a stone.
My tool broke. Have you still got yours? Lend it to me tomorrow and I'll quarry while you rest here.

Hugh, thank you for the beds. My crude tool broke at the Quarry today. If you give me 1 timber, I'll make a new tool and pay you back in stone for the leat: 5 stone for that one timber. I can also patch your wall with stone while I'm here.

Hugh, if Odo paid and the stone never reached the Mill House, I'll make it good: the first 9 stone I quarry go to the Mill House for him, unpaid. After that, every stone is yours at 1 grain each. My tool broke, though, so lend me a tool or a timber in the morning. Alys, thank you.
Will: Holm Wood was mostly dead wood and wild food, no timber without a tool. Rob and Alys shared their fire, and I got home with 3 firewood. Thank you, Kit. I'll take the floor and eat sparingly.
Tom, the barley is ripe, so I will reap with Ellen and Kit in the morning. I owe the household 8 grain from my Holm Wood trip, and I will pay it back in reaping work.
