Hugh: Piers, thank you for owning up. Keep the hay and pay me 3 grain when you can, and good felling at Holm Wood. Wat, I'm taking your 3 stone at 1 grain each, so go and eat. Bring any more stone you cut to the Mill House.

Piers here, Odo. I've come to fell timber for the wheel, at Hugh's 2 grain each. Have you a fire tonight? I'd share it and give you 1 grain for it. How much have you felled, and is there dead wood in the Holm?

Tom: Will, your 8 grain debt is paid by your reaping. Tomorrow Kit and Will eat well and carry the outside grain into hands; we need timber for a granary, so I'll sell some grain for timber from Hugh's people. Ellen and I reap the rest of the barley first, it cannot stand.
Yes, Joan, I've got 6 grain from Hugh. I'll eat it cooked at the Hall, and if you're short I'll share it. Come, let's go.
Tom, I am going to the Long Field to reap for the household with my four units. I'll mark what I cut so you can count it against the 8 grain I owe.
Tom, I reaped four lots for the household today, and I'll count them against the 8 grain I owe. The grain outside the door is at risk, so I'd like to start on bins or a store first thing.

Wat, the copper and the Hall's stone are at the Mill House now. You owe Odo 9 stone. When you've quarried, bring it there, and I'll pay 1 grain a stone for any beyond that. Are you eating enough? How is Joan's baby?

Wat, of course. You, Joan and Margery sleep and eat here tonight and tomorrow night. Keep your coin. The 2 stone count against the 9 you owe Odo. Eat, get strong, and bring stone to the Mill House when you can.

Wat, of course. You, Joan and Margery sleep and eat here tonight and tomorrow night. Keep your coin. The 2 stone count against the 9 you owe Odo. Eat, get strong, and bring stone to the Mill House when you can.

Rob, welcome. You look starved, and I am too. I have only a little wild food and no fire, and I will not burn the wheel timber. Tell me your news from the road: what did you see at Wenbridge, and how did your timber offer stand? Piers, if you have grain to spare, let us share the cooking in the morning.
Tom, I have no units left tonight, so I can't guard formally, but I'll sleep by the door and watch the grain. Tomorrow, if you can lend me a tool, I'll cut young growth with you.

Rob, I have moved our reaped grain into the camp store and am gathering firewood on Gorse Bank so we can cook at the fire ring tonight. I still owe Wat a day under A96 and will pay it when I can reach his work.
I will, Joan. I have 4 stone for Hugh, toward what we owe Odo. Come on, let's go to the Hall and get Margery warm.
Tom, I'll go to Holm Wood with you for timber if nobody sells it tomorrow. I'm not sure I have a copper tool, though; we'd need to fell by hand or borrow one.
Margery is fed and minded. Good work on the stone; go to Holm Wood for timber once the debt is paid.

Hugh, here are the 3 grain I owed you for the hay, so we're square. Sad news: Odo starved at Holm Wood. His 4.5 timber for the wheel lies by his body at the Holm. How much timber is in the Mill House now? I'm ready to lead the wheel at 4 grain a day once the 60 are there. With the Hearnes paying 3 grain a timber, you'll get more brought in if you match them.

Joan, I'm giving Hugh 3.9 stone for Odo, so that's 5.9 of the 9. I'll quarry the rest today. Please mind Margery and rest. Timber sells for 3 grain now, so I may go to Holm Wood to fell some once the debt is paid.

Joan, I quarried 8 stone today. 3 go to finish what we owe Odo, and I'll sell the other 5 to Hugh for grain, so we'll have food of our own. Let's sleep at the Hall again. Hugh said tonight was fine. How are you and Margery?

Hugh: Wat, thank you. 5 grain is yours now for the 5.2 stone, and Odo's 9 are settled. Piers, we have no meal or bread to give. But I leave for the Holm at nightfall with timber for a fire, so come with me and share it: grain cooked at a fire feeds you. I'll pay 2 grain for every timber you bring to the Mill House.

Hugh: I've buried Odo here. Rob, the timber in that heap is Odo's, felled for the Arderns' mill wheel. Please give back what you took, or bring it to the Mill House and I'll pay 2 grain a timber. Piers, are you here to fell? Every timber you bring to the Mill House earns 2 grain. Does either of you have a fire tonight we could share?

Rob, the camp roof has come in and the camp is a ruin. I am reaping at the Long Field for grain and will ask the Arderns for a night in the Ardern Hall. I still owe Wat one day under A96; I will pay it when I can reach him.
Wat: I have not forgotten the day I owe you under A96. I will pay it as soon as I can reach your work; tell me what you need done.

Piers: Yes, Hugh, I'm here to fell for the wheel, at 2 grain a timber at the Mill House as agreed. I have no timber on me tonight, sorry. Tomorrow I'll fell and light a fire, and you're both welcome to share it. God rest Odo.
Rob: Hugh, may I share your fire tonight? Tomorrow I carry timber home to the Mill House.

Piers: Tom, Will, I'm lighting a fire tonight; come and share it and cook your grain. I've felled more timber than I can carry home. I'll sell you some here at your price, 3 grain a timber, paid in grain when we're back in Wenbridge. You carry it home. Take the offer if you want it.
Tom: Thank you, Piers. I'll take timber at 3 grain each, paid in Wenbridge; tomorrow we'll load what we can carry. Will, share the fire with us.
Thank you, Will. I'll share your fire gladly.
Go hunt if you feel strong. I'll mind Randal today. Carry a little food for the night out, and come home when you can.

Piers: Tom, I'm walking home this morning and can't carry it all, so I'm giving you 5.3 timber now, at the 3 grain each you agreed to: 16 grain, paid to me in Wenbridge when you're back. Share it with Will as you like. Thank you.

Tom, Piers offered me 2 timber for 6 grain, paid when we're home. I have only 0.3 grain on me, so I'll owe it from the harvest. I'll fell timber here with bare hands for the room, and carry it home with yours.
Alys, I'm lighting a fire here tonight from the timber Tom gave me. Come and share it. Tomorrow I'll carry the timber and firewood home to the Hearne store.

[Plan] Only carpenter. Food low (10 grain day 1 summer). Forage Gorse Bank; sell carpentry (rooms, beds, bins, repairs) for grain/coin agreed beforehand. Newcomers at the camp may need a room built. Lord holds mill; wheel work possible.

[Plans] Winter day 1: I sold 2 timber to Ellen (O451) for 6 grain. Tom is back and owes me 16 grain; make sure he pays. Rob died, so I'm the only one who knows the wheel. Asked Hugh about the Mill House materials. Firewood ~21.8 is only ~2.7 cold nights (8 a night). I need food and fuel. No firewood at Gorse Bank.
Agreed: Piers owes 3 days in all, the second 12 grain is not to be paid. I'll help with the hay.

Odo, it is three days owed, not six: A18 and A31 are the same 12 grain. Hold him to three, and do not pay twice. Hugh, I'll try with you tonight, and tomorrow I'll fetch firewood or hay with a tool if Piers has one to spare.
Odo, we seem to hold two agreements with Piers, A18 (Alys's) and A31 (yours), each for 3 days. Did we pay twice? If so, that's 6 days of wheel work owed us. Let's hold him to it.

Hugh, we did not clearly pay twice. One 12-grain payment has gone out from the Hall store, and A18 and A31 are two separate 3-day agreements with Piers. So 6 days on the wheel are owed to us, and I'll hold him to both. I'm cutting hay on Mill Mead today for the Ardern store.

Piers here. The Arderns took my offer twice, so I owe you 6 days. I'm working on the mill wheel from today, and I'll take coin for more days after that. I can teach you the wheel as well: 2 units a session, for a price we agree first.
Hugh Ardern here. Piers, keep at the wheel; you did well yesterday. After the days you owe, I'll pay 5 coin a day for more work on the mill wheel. That offer is for Piers, since only he knows it.
Hugh, agreed: it is three days owed in all, one 12-grain payment. If Hugh saw Piers work one day, two remain. I'm back on hay at Mill Mead today for the Ardern store.

I'll repair beside you, which will get it done faster. I'm keeping count of Piers: he worked days 4 and 5 by my eye. If Wat comes asking for a bed, I've offered him floor space in return for mason work, if you agree.
Hugh, I'm repairing the Hall this morning and cutting hay at Mill Mead after. Piers's days on the wheel are still owed to us, so please keep count of what he does each day.

Odo, I've given Wat and Joan shelter in the Hall for 4 nights, and Joan eats from our store. Wat repairs for us in return, and I gave him 1 timber for a tool. If my grant doesn't go through, please host them yourself. I'm repairing beside you today.
Agreed, Tom. I'll take the floor by the hearth tonight and share it with Will in turns. We'll be at the Long Field at first light.
Hugh's day is owed today, so I'm working it. Keep the ring lit; there is firewood at the camp.
Understood. I'm working Hugh's owed day (already paid in coin), and I'll seek grain with the coin after.
Tomorrow we all go to the Long Field at first light and reap if the barley is ripe; if not, weed. Will, cook grain tonight with the firewood in the store. Kit, share the floor with Will in turns.

The Hall is sound. Thank you, Wat, that's your lodging well paid. Joan, you're welcome by our fire until your cottage is up. Odo, tomorrow I'll see Piers about the wheel and pay him coin for his days. Then we should lay in firewood for winter, perhaps with a trip to Holm Wood. Rob still owes us a day.
Yes, Wat, eat with us while you stay. You've earned it today. Bring us some stone when you can, and we'll call it square.
Rob, don't blame yourself. We'll both work tomorrow where it's allowed: I'll look for reaping for grain, and you speak to Hugh about your debt. Sleep well; I'll keep the ring lit with you.
Piers here. My spare bed at Wright's House is yours tonight, as Wat asked. Leave 4 stone at my door when you can. Hugh's Hall still feeds you, so eat there before you come.
I'm off to work the Hall wall for Hugh, to settle my debt. Cook the beans at the ring; we need grain, so keep taking paid work.
I lost the day to a refused plan, Mary. Tomorrow I'll work in a place where it's allowed and speak to Hugh about my debt.

Odo, I've given you 15 coin. Please put up an offer of 5 coin for 'work 1 days' each morning while Piers is near, and withdraw it if anyone else tries to take it. I've asked the Hearnes aloud whether we may reap for a third share. I'll stay for that instead of going to Holm Wood today.

Odo, I saw you chewing raw grain. Was the fire out? Let's keep the hearth fed; we have 31 firewood. Tomorrow I'll reap barley with the village, for a share. Did the Hearnes answer anyone about shares? Did Piers work today, and did you pay him?

The barley in the Long Field is ripe and wants reaping while the rain holds off. It's the Hearnes' field, so please ask them whether we may reap it for a share. I'm cutting firewood on Gorse Bank today.

Alys, Hugh: I'll keep the hearth fed and lit tonight, and I'll cook all grain from now on. I didn't see the fire out, but I should have checked the grain before eating. I didn't see Piers today, so I haven't paid him, and I've had no word from the Hearnes about shares. Tomorrow I'll settle Piers's wheel days first and check on the barley. Alys, I'll come the moment the baby starts.

Piers here. Today is my sixth and last owed day on the wheel (A18 and A31). From tomorrow I'll keep at it on your O97 terms, 5 coin a day, unless you want it otherwise. Will you make that offer again?
Mary, I reaped about 24 grain at the Long Field. It's in the camp store, so cook some tonight at the ring. Tomorrow I'll settle with the Hearnes for their share, then pay Hugh my debt.
Mary, I reaped about 24 grain at the Long Field. It's in the camp store, so cook some tonight at the ring. Tomorrow I'll settle with the Hearnes for their share, then pay Hugh my debt.

Hugh Ardern: Piers, the 5 coin offer for a day's work is for you, on the wheel; nobody else take it, please. Hearnes, your barley will be lost if it isn't cut today, so I'm reaping it for a third share and handing you the rest.

Good, keep your offer up and I'll leave it to you. I'm hosting the Masons tonight for 3 stone. I'm reaping the barley today because it's lost otherwise, and I said aloud yesterday it's for a third share.
Understood, Rob. I'll reap the Long Field and settle my share with the Hearnes. Keep the ring lit and cook grain tonight.
Rob, I've got about 44 grain on me now, enough for us both for a good while. Let's sleep here with the ring lit. Tomorrow I'll ask the Hearnes to settle my reaping share.
I'm working Hugh's day at Mill Mead. Reap at the Long Field and ask the Hearnes for your share; we'll settle with them fairly.

Hugh Ardern: Piers, the 5 coin offer for a day's work is for you, on the mill wheel; nobody else take it, please. Rob, Mill Mead is the Arderns' meadow, so please don't clear it without asking me. You still owe me a day.

Hugh Ardern: Piers, I've paid you 5 coin for yesterday, and today's 5 coin offer for a day's work is up for you, on the mill wheel; nobody else take it, please. Rob, Mill Mead is the Arderns' meadow, so please don't clear it without asking me. You still owe me a day.
Wat, I haven't seen your tool, but I carry one and can lend it to you tomorrow for quarrying. We'll eat our grain here tonight and leave the Hearnes' firewood be.
Rob, I'm reaping the Long Field today for our store. The camp's firewood is low, so please gather firewood when you can, and keep the ring lit tonight. I'll cook grain at the ring this evening.

Alys: I'm keeping the hearth fed and lit tonight. Tomorrow I'll mind Randal in the morning and work the Long Field's stubble after. Piers: I owe you 5 coin for yesterday; I'll pay it when you're here.
Hugh, I cleared Mill Mead yesterday and am clearing again today toward my owed day (A144). Tell me if you want other work.
Sorry Hugh, I'll stop clearing Mill Mead. Name the work you want for my owed day, and where, and I'll do it tomorrow.

Tom, you're chewing raw grain and so am I. Give me 2 timber for my 3 firewood and 2 coin; it's on offer now. I'll light a fire and we can both cook by it. Or light one yourself and I'll share it with you.
Hugh, share my fire tonight; I have firewood. Tomorrow I fell a little more timber and head home.
Hugh, welcome back. The Long Field has no crop left and Gorse Bank no wood. Tomorrow after caring for Randal, what work would help most? Wat looks gaunt; we could share some grain. Good night.

Hugh, Piers has worked the wheel two days (yesterday and today) and says 10 coin is owed tonight. My offer for 5 coin for a day's wheel work was refused as badly worded, so nothing is paid. I have 15 coin. Shall I pay him 10 from it, or will you settle it? Gorse Bank is bare of firewood now, so we need Holm Wood or to buy in.

Hugh, the Hall store has about 40 grain, 29 beans and 40 firewood, and Alys and Randal are eating from it. Piers has not been paid for the wheel since your offer was refused, so 10 coin is owed on his count. Say the word and I'll pay it from my 15 coin tomorrow.

Piers here. I worked the wheel yesterday for Hugh's 5 coin a day and I'm on it again today. That makes 10 coin owed tonight. Please leave it with me or at Wright's House. If it's still unpaid tomorrow, I'll stop until Hugh is back.

I've posted today's offer for Piers myself (5 coin for work 1 days), so don't post one too. Please pay him the 10 owed for the last two days, giving it into his hands. Those grain heaps on the Green belong to someone, so leave them be.
Piers, my offer of 5 coin for a day's work is for you, on the mill wheel today. Odo will pay you the 10 owed for the last two days. Everyone else, please leave the offer to Piers.
Rob, you've made a kill. Could you spare some meat for me and Margery? We are starving. I'll hunt and fell timber with you tomorrow and share what I get.

Rob, we'll light a fire here tonight and set off for Wenbridge at first light. I'm carrying more than my weight, so the firewood is heavy; if you have room, take some of it, or give it to Joan to carry for her family. Joan and Margery are very thin, so I've given Joan a share of the wild food.
Odo: Piers, I've put up 10 coin for your two owed wheel days. Accept it and it's yours. I'm walking to Holm Wood for firewood.

Odo: I'm here with Joan, Mary and Rob. I have one timber and no fire in the open tonight. Tomorrow I'll gather dead wood in the Holm and walk home with what I can carry. Mary, keep to the raw grain only if you must; cook it when you can.
Thank you. Piers is owed 5 coin for day 5, and Odo has the coin at the Holm. Don't pay him in grain. I'll send Odo back with it.

Piers, I'm sorry, I've no coin in hand now; Odo carries the rest and he's at Holm Wood. We owe you 5 for day 5, and I'll see you're paid when he's back. Please don't work today unless you're willing to wait a day or two for that pay too. I'm going to the Holm and will send Odo home with the coin.
We leave for Wenbridge at first light. Joan, Odo, Rob: share the firewood between you so no one is overloaded, and we eat what we carry on the road.

Thanks for the 5, Hugh. Odo's offer of 10 went to Holm Wood with him before I could accept it, so 5 is still owed for day 5. I didn't work yesterday. I'm on the wheel today in good faith. Could you put 10 coin in my hands tonight, 5 for day 5 and 5 for today? Then I'll keep going day by day.

Thanks for the 5, Hugh. Odo's offer of 10 went to Holm Wood with him before I could accept it, so 5 is still owed for day 5. I didn't work yesterday. I'm on the wheel today in good faith. Could you put 10 coin in my hands tonight, 5 for day 5 and 5 for today? Then I'll keep going day by day.
Mother, I've given you 14 grain to keep for the store, since I can only carry 10 weight. Wat has been taking grain and straw from the hut's store. Please keep the door barred when you can.
Will, it's Hugh Ardern. I've no timber for a fire tonight. If you light one, may I sleep by it? I've given you 3 firewood toward it. If either of us takes game tomorrow, let's share it.
I'm sorry, Will. I've less than a meal of raw grain myself, and the firewood I gave you is all I have. Keep it. If I take game tomorrow I'll share it, and either way I'll see you in Wenbridge.
Piers says he is owed 10 for days 5 and 7 and wants 5 more tonight. Hugh's words were 5 for day 5 and 5 for today, so I'll give the 10 now and leave anything beyond that to Hugh.

Welcome home, Odo. Hugh says you carry the wheel coin. I'm owed 10: 5 for day 5 and 5 for day 7, which I worked on Hugh's word. Please put the 10 in my hands now. I'm working the wheel today too, so that's 5 more tonight. About 90 units are left; at this pace it turns within the season.
Hugh, yes, sleep by the fire. Thank you for the firewood. If either of us takes game tomorrow, we'll share it.
Will, have you seen my daughter Margery, a child, here at the Holm? Mary's party left her here on day 7. Do you know where she went? I have a little grain to share if you are hungry.
Thank you, Will. I have no timber, only a little grain, which I'll share. We'll walk home to Wenbridge together in the morning.
Rob, yes. I've put my firewood in the camp store so the ring stays lit. We'll cook what grain I have left at the fire and share it. We'll look for timber and my pack tomorrow.
Firewood is in the store; the fire stays lit tonight. Rob and I share the grain.

Welcome back, Hugh. Piers says he is owed 10 more for the wheel, and that I owe him 5 for autumn day 8. I paid 10 for days 5 and the one you named, so please settle any more with him yourself. Tomorrow what work do you want from me?
Mary, eat your share first; I'll bring my 3 firewood to the camp fire tonight. Margery was left at Holm Wood, Wat is going for her.
Mary, you carry grain and firewood: let's light the fire and cook now, and I'm starving, so please share a meal. Tomorrow I'll find timber for the roof.
Thank you, Mary. We'll eat tonight, then tomorrow work to repay the owners of that grain and look for your pack.
Hugh, I'm foraging the Holm for wild food today. I'll share what I gather with you tonight, as we agreed.
Joan, I'm Will. If you have timber for a fire, I'll give my 3 firewood toward it, and we can share what food we have. I'll walk home to Wenbridge in the morning, if you're going too.
Will, welcome home, and sorrow for Joan's loss. Let Joan share our fire tonight if there is room; we'll sort the missing grain with Tom in the morning.

Piers, by A18 and A31 you owe me 6 days of work, none done yet. I ask you to work them on the mill wheel, starting today; that settles what we owe each other for those days. When they are done, we can talk about paid days again.

Good. Keep the 5 coin for now unless Rob's offer of 5 grain for 5 coin still stands; grain is worth more than coin to us, so take it if it does. Piers will sleep on the Hall floor for a few nights in return for wheel work.

Piers: you owe me 6 days by A18 and A31. I'll count your 10 coin for autumn day 8 and winter day 1 against 2 of those days, so you still owe me 4. Work those 4 on the wheel. I've given you shelter in the stone Hall from tonight for 6 days, on the floor by our hearth; no coin, no timber. Rob: for A144, gather firewood today and put it into the Ardern Hall's store. I have no grain to spare, I'm sorr
I am sorry about Margery. Joan, you are welcome to share our food tonight. Tom, I took nothing from the store, and I'll help find out what happened to the grain.
Hugh, I hold 5 coin and will pay nobody more without your word. I'll forage near home today, and I'll say what I find at nightfall.

Hugh, I've worked the wheel on autumn day 8 and winter day 1 on your 5 coin a day, so 10 is owed. I won't go on until it's paid; pay it and I'll keep at it. My house is cracked and I'm nearly out of fuel. Will you sell me timber at 2 coin each, or give me a bed in the Hall on cold nights? I'd pay with wheel work.
Mary, Hugh is here. I'll ask him for work. Keep the camp fire lit with the store firewood and eat your share of the grain.
Hugh, I owe you a day of work (A144, 5 coin paid). Tell me what to do today. I'm starving; a little grain against it would be a mercy.
Thank you. Piers gave 5 grain for my 5 coin; we have about 10 between us. Cook it at the camp fire tonight and share.
Wat, Margery is dead; I found her body at the Holm. I brought nothing, only a hide, and I am starving. Trade stone for grain and share it with me. When we can, we go together to bury her.

Rob, I have no grain left. I'm offering my 5 firewood for 4 grain to anyone who has some. Keep the camp fire lit from the store, and tell Hugh you'll gather firewood for him if he gives you a share of his grain.

Rob, I have no food left to share tonight, I'm sorry. Before you take the Gorse Bank heap, ask Hugh whether it's his or the Arderns', so it isn't theft. If it's nobody's, take it for his day and bring some to our fire.
Mary, there's a firewood heap at Gorse Bank (T4). Tomorrow I'll take it for Hugh's day and our fire. Share what you have tonight.
Kit, I'm lighting a fire with my timber tonight. Share it, you're welcome. Shall we hunt the Holm together tomorrow and share what we kill? Bring dead wood for tomorrow night's fire.
Ellen gave me 4 grain. I'm walking to the Holm now, as we said. Come if you can. We'll bury Margery, hunt and fell timber there, and I'll share the grain with you.

Rob, I've put my firewood in the camp store so we can keep the fire going tonight. I found no grain at the Green, so I have none to share. Tomorrow I'll look for paid work or grain. What did Hugh give you for your day?
Hugh gave nothing yet; I paid my debt in firewood (A144), as he asked. Tomorrow I'll ask him for grain, and we may go to Holm Wood to hunt.

Thank you for staying, love. Eat your grain tonight, and I'll eat with you if you'll share a little. In the morning I'll gather up the grain heap and the firewood bundle lying on the Green and put them in our store, so we can cook properly. Then we get strong enough for the Holm, and we bury her together.

I'm lighting a fire with my 2 timber; sit close and share it, all of you. Tomorrow I've no wood left. Whoever gathers dead wood for tomorrow night's fire shares it with me, and I'll share any meat cooked at it. Kit, burying Margery takes 6 units, more than I had. If you start it tomorrow, I'll give what I can.

Rob, here's half a meat to cook at the fire. Work your owed day (A144) tomorrow by hunting beside me and sharing the kill. The rest of my meat goes home to my starving household. Kit, I'll help with the burial in the morning, and then I hunt.

Tom, I am at the Holm with Hugh. We are burying Margery this morning, then I forage for food and gather dead wood for tonight's fire. I will hunt with Hugh if I have units left. I have not yet counted the timber, and I owe you the grain account.
Hugh, let's bury Margery now, then forage and hunt together, and share what we find tonight.
Rob, I'm glad you're here. Ask Hugh about the kill in the Holm, and let me have a share for my firewood. Keep the warmth between us tonight.
Rob, yes, we'll bury Margery with Kit and Hugh at first light. I'm offering my 5 firewood to Hugh for a share of the meat, and I'll help dig.

Joan lies dead of hunger in the Masons' cottage. That's a hard thing. Odo, are you going to the Holm now the sky's cleared? My house is cracked and cold, and I'll pay 2 coin for each timber you bring, up to 10. Tomorrow's my last owed day on the wheel; there are about 72 units of work left on it.
Hugh, you have a kill. I'm starving; Mary too. Could you spare some meat against my owed day (A144)? Tomorrow I'll hunt and work for you, and help bury Margery.
Kit, agreed: I'll help bury Margery at first light. Hugh, please give Mary and me a share of the kill; it's my owed day, and I'll work it.
Kit, agreed: I'll help bury Margery at first light. Hugh, please give Mary and me a share of the kill; it's my owed day, and I'll work it.
Alys, I'm back, starving; the Holm gave little. Where is Odo, and how is Randal? Piers, how far is the wheel now, and how many of your owed days have you worked on it?

Will, I have no timber, only about five firewood. Let's put our firewood on Hugh's fire tonight and share what food we have. Tomorrow we bury Margery at first light, then fell and carry timber, or go home.
Piers: I'm sorry for Joan and Wat. I'm going to the Holm this morning and will bring timber back if I can. Please work your owed day on the wheel for the Arderns.

I'm Odo from Wenbridge, looking for Hugh. I have only one timber and no food; if anyone has spare food or wood, I'd share the fire with you. Tomorrow I'll gather dead wood here and bring what I can back to the Hall.
I caught nothing today. Mary and I are starving. If anyone has meat or a fire with wood, we'll gather dead wood tomorrow and share what we find. Hunting together tomorrow may work better.
Kit, I have 2 firewood and 2.5 grain and no timber to light a fire. If you have timber, let's light one together tonight and share the food. Tomorrow I'll fell with you and carry back what we can.
Anyone here with timber to light a fire: I have 2 firewood and 2.5 grain to share at the fire. Tomorrow we fell timber at the Holm.
Will, I'm starving. I'm foraging Holm Glade now with my two units. Share what you find and we'll eat together before the burial.
Agreed, Will. Share the food tonight, dig at first light with all our hands, then we walk for Wenbridge together.

We are all starving and sleeping out at the Holm tonight. Margery is still unburied, so at first light let's all dig together until she is in the ground. I have only 0.2 firewood, which I've given to Rob for the fire. Anyone with wood, wild food or meat, please share it at the fire, and we'll put what we find into the burial and the walk.
I've given Will my one timber for the fire tonight, so we can all share it. Tomorrow I'll help bury Margery with the rest of you, and then we walk home to Wenbridge.

Kit, I have about 0.7 wild food and 4 firewood between us, and no timber for a fire. Let's share the food tonight and dig Margery at first light with all our hands. Then we walk for Wenbridge together.

Margery still lies unburied, and she needs six units of hands. At first light we bury her together, all of us putting in what units we have. I have 2 firewood and about 0.7 wild food; I'll share it tonight with anyone who is starving. There is no timber for a fire, so let's keep close to each other for warmth. After the burial we walk for Wenbridge.
Thank you, Odo. I'll try to light the fire with your timber and my firewood, and we'll share the food round it. At first light we bury Margery together, then walk for Wenbridge.

Will, I'm putting my two units into Margery's grave now. With your four that's six, so she'll be in the ground today. Then I'll forage with anything I have left, and we share whatever we find before we walk for Wenbridge.

Will, I'll put my 5.2 firewood into the fire you light with your timber tonight, so we all share the heat. Tomorrow at first light, let's bury Margery together with all four of us, then walk for Wenbridge. Mary's grave will have to wait until we are back with food.

Tomorrow at first light: all of us dig Margery's grave until she is in the ground, six units in all. Then we walk for Wenbridge. Mary's grave must wait until we are back with food and hands. Tonight, whoever has food, please share it at the fire, and my firewood goes in with yours.
Tomorrow at first light we bury Margery and Mary together, all of us putting in every unit we have. Then we walk for Wenbridge. Keep the fire close, and share whatever food anyone finds tonight.
Mary is dead too. I have 1.2 firewood to put on the fire tonight; share what food you have. Tomorrow I'll help bury Mary and Margery if we can.

Kit, Mary has died too. I'll put my two units into the digging with you, and I'm carrying 4.2 firewood and 1 timber, which I'll share with whoever is still here. I'm starving, so once the burial is done we should walk for Wenbridge together.

Kit, I have only two units today, not four, so with yours we'll have four toward the six the grave takes. I'm putting both into the digging now. I'm carrying 4.2 firewood and 1 timber to share, and then we should walk for Wenbridge.
Odo, I bought 3 grain from Ellen. Hugh is dead and Randal is hungry. Share the fire and the grain tonight. Tomorrow I'll care for Randal and see to Hugh's burial; will you go to the Holm for wood?
Odo, the store holds 3 grain, about 10 timber, hay and a little stone, nothing else. Eat tonight's share; we bury Hugh tomorrow and I'll grind what is left. Randal eats first.

Thank you, Alys. I'll eat my share of the grain and sit by the fire with Randal. I'm too weak to walk to the Holm tomorrow, so I'll help with Hugh's burial and fetch wood from the woodpile here. We count every meal.
Kit, I came to hunt and forage here. If you find game or wild food, I will share what I find.
Kit, I have no food or fuel tonight, only straw. Tomorrow I'll hunt and forage and share what I find.
Alys, I'm at the Holm with nothing to make a fire. Do you have food or a fire to share tonight? Tomorrow I'll forage, then bury Will, Rob, Mary and Margery with whatever hands are here.
Thank you, Alys. I'll share what I find too. Tomorrow I'll forage first, then we bury the dead together.

Odo, you take the hay to the Green; I will offer our copper for grain there, so we do not undercut each other. If you get grain, Alys and I will share it as she has said; you are weaker, so eat first.
Kit, here is a small share of meat, all I can spare. Ellen, I'd rather keep the meat than sell it, but I'll gladly cook by your fire. At first light we bury the three, then walk for Wenbridge.
Alys, I'll pay coin for some of your meat. 3 coin for a share? I have firewood to cook it on, and Kit can share the fire.

Alys, you have a kill, and I am starving with nothing in my hands. Would you share some of the meat tonight? I will pay back with my work once I have eaten. At first light let us bury Will, Rob and Mary together, with all hands, and then walk for Wenbridge with what food we carry.
Ellen, yes, let me share your fire. I carry nothing, so I will work at the Holm tomorrow for whatever you pay for the meat, and I will bury Will, Rob and Mary first thing if you can spare the hands.
Alys, go home safely with your meat, and I am sorry the burying fell to us alone. Ellen, I will share your fire gladly, and I will work off the coin you spend on the meat.

[Mill wheel] Winter day 7: Piers worked his 4 days (winter days 3 to 6), and I released A18 and A31. About 70 units of work are left on the wheel. More days cost 5 coin each, or food, agreed first. He buys timber at 2 coin each (up to 10) and 3 firewood for 1 coin. His house is failing and he is hungry. Heaps of grain (T1, T2) and firewood (T3) lie on the Green, nobody's; I took them on winter day 7.

[Mill wheel] The Mill House wheel and leat (Arderns') has its materials in, about 150 units of work left. Day 1 of summer: I offered my work at 4 grain a day. Don't start work until the pay is agreed.

[Work owed] A18/A31 are PAID IN FULL (wheel days 3 to 6). Wheel work is 5 coin a day, or 3 grain, agreed first. Day 8: one go done for Hugh's 3 grain. Wright's House is a RUIN. I'm starving, with about 18 coin. Raw grain feeds little: the Hall's fire must be lit (it needs timber in the Hall store). Ellen holds a lot of grain; buy from her.

[Lessons] Travel only goes to Holm Wood from here; do not use travel for village places. Put 'at' on the work itself. Walling is only offered at Long Field and Mill Mead, not the Hall Garth. Owe Hugh 1 day (A144); I should tell Hugh and ask him what work. Never leave units unused: fall back on cutting young growth at Gorse Bank.

Piers's terms are 2 grain a day from the Hall store, which is what you called fair. I have put that up as an offer for 5 days of work on the wheel. Please accept your own 15-coin offer so he can start today. I will give no grain beyond 2 a day without your word.
Rob here: I'm felling timber at the Coppice, then raising the woodshed at Gorse Bank. Carry timber when you can.
I'm starting the timber upgrade of the cottage with my 7.8 timber; join me when you can.
The Hall's wall cracked in the night. I'm repairing it today with timber from the store. Piers owes me 5 days on the wheel (A173); please see he gets his 2 grain a day.

Wat: my offer O302 stands, 6 coin for 3 stone, your own price. Please accept it today for the Ardern Hall's wall. Piers: your 5 days on the mill wheel for my 20 coin (A173) are still owed; please work them.

Wat: my offer O302 stands, 6 coin for 3 stone at your own price; please accept it today for the Ardern Hall's wall. Piers: your 5 days on the mill wheel for my 20 coin (A173) are still owed. Mary: yes, the Newcomes may cut hay on Mill Mead for your beds; take what you need.

My 3 stone are in the store now. Alys, please take your 4 coin to Wat for 2 more stone so the wall surely has its 7. The Long Field is the Hearnes', so don't reap it unless they ask us and agree a share. Odo, repair first thing; I'll fell timber for the thatch.

Odo, the Hall grain fell from 120 to 70 in two days. What's draining it? We eat only 3 a night. Please hold back grain payments and count what we owe. I'll forage on Mill Mead for food today. The store has 6.5 stone; I hope that's near enough for the wall.

Mill Mead is picked bare; I got only a little. The grain is going fast, so we need food before winter. Tomorrow I'll offer the Hearnes my reaping for a share of their barley. If they won't, I'll make a weapon and hunt at Holm Wood. Odo, did the wall get repaired? Alys, I have 3 units left and I'm trying with you tonight, if you have any too.

Odo, good that O172 is withdrawn. Joan and Rob took it, so they each owe us days of work; let's set them to reaping, felling or bringing stone. Alys's stone from Joan should make up the wall's half stone. Please count the store tomorrow; I'll go after food.

Hugh, your 3 stone are in the Hall store with the 6.5 there, so the wall has its stone. I'm repairing the Hall now with my six units. Piers is owed his 2 grain for the wheel day; I'll pay him at nightfall from the Hall store.

Hugh, I've withdrawn my open offer O172 (2 grain a day for work) so no more grain goes out while we count. Piers's 10-grain offer O169 and the 2 a day owed beyond it are the likeliest drains, plus the household's meals and whatever was given out. I'll count the store against what is owed this morning and tell you the figure before I pay anyone.
Piers: I'm holding back the grain payments from the Hall store until we have counted what is owed. Hugh's 20 coin for your wheel days stands.

Hugh, my offer O172 was taken twice today (Joan 6 grain, Rob 2 grain) before I could withdraw it, so about 8 grain has gone out of the Hall store today. I've withdrawn it now. Tomorrow I'll count the store against what is owed and bring you the figure before any more is paid.
Hugh, Alys: the wall needs half a stone more than the store holds. Whoever can bring one stone to the Hall, I'll pay in grain from the store once we've counted what is owed.

Odo, I'll put my units into repairing the Hall with you today; the gale is tearing at it. Store shows 59 grain, 7.5 stone. I've offered my work for grain to bring food in. Pay Piers nothing for the A173 days. Joan and Rob each owe us a day (A450, A452); let's set them to work.
Good. I'm with you on the repair after my try with Alys. Hold all grain payments; we're down to 59. I'll hunt at Holm Wood or reap for a barley share soon to bring food in.

The Hall is sound again, well done both of you. Food is our worry now: 59 grain and some beans won't carry three of us through winter. Tomorrow I mean to make a crude weapon and hunt, at Holm Wood if need be, unless the Hearnes take my work for grain. Odo, please set Joan and Rob's owed days to reaping or bringing food. The gale brought branches down in the Coppice if anyone wants firewood. Alys,

Odo, Alys: I finished the mending this afternoon, and the Hall is sound now. Check it in the morning, but I think the wall needs no more work. Let's put tomorrow into food: reaping for a barley share, hunting, or setting Joan and Rob's owed days to bring grain in.

Odo, Alys: I finished the mending this afternoon, and the Hall is sound now. Check it in the morning, but I think the wall needs no more work. Let's put tomorrow into food: reaping for a barley share, hunting, or setting Joan and Rob's owed days to bring grain in.

Hugh, the Hall store is at 59.1 grain now, down 10.8 since yesterday, and it holds 7.5 stone, enough for the wall. I'm repairing the wall now. Joan and Rob each owe us one day of work from my taken offer; I'd set them to bringing stone or reaping.

Hugh, agreed: no grain goes to Piers while his ten wheel days are counted, so my earlier promise of 2 grain a day is off. I'm repairing the Hall with my six units now, and I'll hold the store's grain until you and I settle what's owed.
Hugh, Alys: the wall is part mended and needs about 5 more units. I'll finish it first thing tomorrow and keep the grain held until we agree what is owed.
Hugh, Alys: I'll check the wall at first light and finish the last units of it before anything else. Then Joan and Rob's owed days go to reaping or fetching food.

Odo, Alys: I have a crude weapon now. Tomorrow I mean to walk to Holm Wood in the morning, hunt there the next day and bring meat back to dry at our hearth. I'll take 3 grain and some beans for the nights out. Odo, while I'm gone, please set Joan and Rob to the days they owe us: reaping a share or bringing stone. Odo, Alys: I have a crude weapon now. Tomorrow I mean to walk to Holm Wood in the morning, hunt there the next day and bring meat back to dry at our hearth. I'll take 3 grain and some beans for the nights out. Odo, while I'm gone, please set Joan and Rob to the days they owe us: reaping a share or bringing stone. There's a heap of grain and straw lying on the Green (T6). It's likely the Hearnes' b

Alys, yes: I'll try with you first thing tomorrow. Then I'll gather food and wood, and set off for Holm Wood at nightfall so I'm hunting there the day after. Odo, good. Get the Hearnes' barley share, and hold the grain as you say.

Hugh: I'll keep the Hall grain held and pay Piers nothing until his ten wheel days are counted. At first light I'll ask the Hearnes for a barley share for reaping in the Long Field, then bring it home to the Hall store.
I'm off to Holm Wood at nightfall to hunt, taking 6 meal for the road. While I'm away, please call in Joan's and Rob's owed days, and keep holding the grain. We're at 35.

[Plan] Mill wheel: about 104 units left at the end of autumn day 4. 3 builds a day in autumn. Days worked on the wheel so far: about 4.5 (part of summer day 8, autumn days 1 to 4). They go to the 10 paid days: Hugh's 5 (A173) and Odo's 5 (A246). Tell Hugh and Odo my count. After the 10 days, 2 grain a day (O172). Hugh may owe a 10-coin bonus when the wheel turns. Store: about 12 grain, 28 firewood, 13 ti
Odo, the Woods have no ploughland. Would the Holts let us sow a plot of Middle Field? I'm a master at weeding, hoeing and reaping, and I'd work your plots in return.
Agreed, Odo. I'll weed Middle Field when it needs it and help you reap at harvest, for a fair share. We'll talk about plots after harvest.
Agreed, Odo. I'll weed Middle Field when it needs it and help you reap at harvest, for a fair share. We'll talk about plots after harvest.

Daughter, Middle Field is already sown and the barley is up. Hoeing it turns the green corn under. Please don't hoe there any more. If you want work, help me keep the hares and pigeons off it, and we'll share what comes.

Middle Field is already sown with barley on all five plots, so there's no room this season. Help us weed and reap and we'll share the harvest with you. After harvest we can talk of plots for next year.

Middle Field is already sown with barley on all five plots, so there's no room this season. Help us weed and reap and we'll share the harvest with you. After harvest we can talk of plots for next year.
Thank you. Osric or Ancel's father may come to the drive tomorrow; I'll ask Osric. Share the meat fairly.
I understand, Everard. Whoever gets a catch first should share it, and we'll help each other at harvest.

Alys, I can't spare grain just now. Our store at Moor House is only about five nights of food for the four of us, and the barley is not ripe yet. When Broad Field is ready to reap, I'll come and help you reap, and we can settle what you owe then.

Son, our grain fell from 34 to 20 in a day. Was that seed for the Ham, or the rats? I'm shutting the store every night now. Odo says if we help weed and reap Middle Field, the Holts will share the harvest. It's fit to reap in about 4 days.
The Holts will join the drive tomorrow. We'll beat and carry spears; share by heads as you say.
Our store is nearly down to three days of food. Could the Holts spare some grain or beans until the barley is ripe? I'll repay it from the harvest.
Most of it was seed I sowed in the Ham, the rest the household's eating. Good: tell Odo yes, we'll weed and reap Middle Field for a share. I'm weeding there today.
There's a red deer herd using Hazel Copse; I've seen the slots and fraying. Would the Holts join a drive tomorrow, beaters and spears? We'd share the meat by heads.
There's a red deer herd in Hazel Copse. Would the Woods send a beater or two for a drive tomorrow? The meat would be shared fairly among all who come.
Gilbert, the barley in Broad Field is cut green and wet; please hold off until it ripens in a few days, and we will share the harvest fairly.
Here's 2 grain for your weeding; more after the harvest. Thank you.

Neighbours, Broad Field is the Moors' barley, and it won't be ripe for about 3 more days. Cutting it green wastes it for all of us. Please leave it standing. Anyone who helps us reap when it is ripe will get a fair share of the grain.
Thank you, Gilbert. That's neighbourly of you. Come in 3 days and we'll reap together, and you'll have your grain.

Neighbours, Broad Field is the Moors' barley, and it won't be ripe for about 3 more days. Cutting it green wastes it for all of us. Please leave it standing. Anyone who helps us reap when it is ripe will get a fair share of the grain.
The drive is on today at Hazel Copse. The deer keep to the far side by day, so beat from the Leaze side towards me. Meat is shared by heads.
Deer drive at Hazel Copse today with the Holts and me. Come and beat if you can; your household gets a share of the meat by heads.
Matthew, that meat you took at Leven Meadow came from my snares. We are nearly out of food. Will you share some with the Dyers, or give it back in grain or work at harvest?
Son, I'll milk today and keep it for the store. Tomorrow we should all reap Middle Field for our share of the Holts' barley. We only have food for about two days.
Orabel, I am a master reaper. When Broad Field is ripe, I will help the Moors reap it for a fair share of the grain. Tell me the day.

Forgive me, Alys. I had set two lines of my own at Leven Meadow and took it thinking it was from them. It was only a scrap, and it was eaten last night. I will make it right: I'll help reap your barley in Leven Meadow when it is ripe, and you won't owe me for it. I'll leave the Leven Meadow lines alone from now on.
Orabel, I am a master reaper. When Broad Field is ripe, I will help the Moors reap it for a fair share of the grain. Tell me the day.
Thanks for beating yesterday. A wolf is prowling the copse edge, so shut your hens and store up at night. If I get a deer I'll share it by heads as we agreed.
Odo, I'm reaping Middle Field with you today. Our store is down to one night's food. Could we have some of our share of the sheaves tonight?
Good. I'll reap beside you. Paying Denise's share is fair. Keep back the best ears for seed.

Alys, I'm ashamed. I went to check my own lines and took from yours at Leven Meadow again, two scraps of meat. I've left an egg at Dyer House to make up for it, and I still owe you help at your harvest. I won't lift anything at Leven Meadow again.
Yes, reap with us. Once the grain is in I'll give the Woods a fair share for your work; I'll send some grain tonight if I can.
I'm reaping Middle Field now. Denise is helping; we'll pay the Woods a share of the grain.
Orabel, I'm reaping Broad Field today as you asked. I'm a master reaper. A fair share of the grain for the Cotters would be welcome.

Odo, Middle Field is in. Osric and I reaped and weeded it with you, and the Woods have less than one night's food left. Could you give us our share today? Ten grain would carry the six of us a couple of days.
Son, Middle Field is in and our store is nearly empty. I've asked Odo for our share. Today I'll milk and reap what's left in the Ham.
Thank you, Odo. That's a fair share, and we'll gladly work with you again.
Orabel, I'm in Broad Field reaping for you today as we agreed. Every tenth sheaf I cut is ours, so please put that share into Cotter House when we're done.
Here is 20 grain as the Holts' share of Middle Field. We bury Ivy today.
Odo, have you any grain to spare? I'd trade our good deer hide for 5 grain, or a share of the next deer I take. East Field lies bare for want of seed.
[Holt deal] Spring day 3: Odo (Holt) agreed that the Woods help weed and reap Middle Field for a share of the harvest. We talk of plots for next year after harvest.
[Debts] Owe Matthew (Cotters, Brookford) 2 grain from last winter. Bad blood with Everard (Moors) over the pig.
[Drive plan] Spring day 5: deer drive at Hazel Copse with the Holts (Odo agreed) and maybe Osric of the Woods. The meat is to be shared by heads.

[Reaping debts] Spring day 8: Matthew and Sarra (Cotters) and Gilbert (Dyers) reaped Broad Field, each for every tenth sheaf they cut. Matthew asked for the Cotter share to go into Cotter House. Pay fairly from Moor House grain once we know how much each cut.
[Debts] Petronel (Carter, Meadcombe) owes us 2 grain from last winter.

[Promises] Reaped Broad Field for the Moors on spring day 8, about 30 grain into Moor House; our tenth (about 3) is owed. Summer day 1: reaped Leven Meadow for the Dyers to square us with Alys. Set no lines at Leven Meadow. DO NOT use 'take' with 'at'. Milk our cow daily: work milk at North Pasture, thing 'the Cotter cows'. Keep the cows out of Broad Field.
